# Roadmap: prismatic cohomology

**Summary.** Build delta algebra, bounded prisms and their sites, then relative and absolute prismatic cohomology with Hodge–Tate, crystalline, de Rham and étale comparisons. Construct the conjugate and Nygaard filtrations, Breuil–Kisin twists, q-crystalline models and syntomic complexes. The coefficient theory culminates in the equivalence between prismatic F-crystals over a mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring and crystalline integral Galois representations. The logarithmic theory extends the comparisons to saturated charts and semistable geometry, with Laurent F-crystals corresponding to p-Kummer local systems.

## Scope and ownership

This roadmap extends the p-local delta, prism and oriented affine constructions of PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15 to integral delta algebra, general orientable envelopes, nonoriented formal schemes and animated inputs. It owns the relative and absolute prismatic sites, Cartier–Witt geometry, Nygaard filtrations and the prismatic comparison maps in those ranges. It owns the logarithmic delta and prismatic variants, the saturated logarithmic sites, and the log adic and diamond structures specifically required for their Kummer comparisons.

Ordinary algebraic and geometric foundations remain inputs. Mathlib already provides Witt-vector carriers and operations, classical adic completion, divided powers, the divided power algebra, modules, ring localizations, ordinary sites and sheaves, and ordinary derived categories. Their precise declarations are listed below. A divided power algebra is not a divided power envelope; a naive cotangent complex is not the full animated cotangent complex. Stable infinity categories, completed derived tensor products, full cotangent complexes are required from EnhancedDerivedSheaves and DerivedDeRhamCohomology. TauCetiRoadmap.IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants §6.4 supplies ordinary finite-sequence Koszul complexes; DerivedDeRhamCohomology supplies their completed and derived adapters. Formal schemes and their ordinary étale sites belong to SchemeAndStackFoundations; log crystalline and log de Rham theory belong to CrystallineCohomology and DerivedDeRhamCohomology respectively.

TauCetiRoadmap.AlgebraicVectorBundles Layers 0A–0B supply the monoidal sheaf foundations and the affine equivalence between finite projective modules and finite locally free sheaves. We use that equivalence; the new effectivity target here concerns compatible systems over adic quotients. TauCetiRoadmap.AdicSpaces supplies ordinary Huber and adic geometry, including its Layer 6 Fargues–Fontaine adic charts; it does not supply an étale site, Fargues–Fontaine vector-bundle classification or the filtered Frobenius bundle dictionary. Those inputs are distinguished below. Tau Ceti’s arithmetic Frobenius lifts concern local Galois groups, whereas the Frobenius lifts here are endomorphisms of commutative rings. Tau Ceti’s pro-p group predicate is reused for logarithmic inertia.

The current Tau Ceti library supplies `TauCeti.IsAdicComplete.exists_isIdempotentElem_eq` in `TauCeti/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Idempotent.lean` and `TauCeti.exists_projective_quotient_smul_top_linearEquiv` in `TauCeti/Algebra/Module/Projective/Lift.lean`. Reuse their idempotent and finite-projective lifting steps under their adic-completeness hypotheses; the second theorem requires the endomorphism ring of the projective ambient module to be complete. Sections 2.26 and 3.8 additionally require effectivity of an entire compatible inverse system, with functoriality and rank control; lifting one quotient alone does not give that assertion.

PerfectoidQuotients and AInfCohomology, which come before this roadmap in its bundle, supply the companion p-adic theories; PadicHodgeTheory comes after it and only consumes it. Perfectoid rings and almost purity are taken from PerfectoidSpaces, the period rings and period functors from TauCetiRoadmap.PadicPeriodRings and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory, and Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules and the AΩ complex from AInfCohomology; this roadmap constructs the prismatic comparisons with those objects. Semiperfectoid universal perfectoid quotients, prism perfection, the QRSP initial prism and André covers are imported from PerfectoidSpaces §§P4.15.2–P4.15.5. This roadmap owns completed Frobenius perfection for general animated inputs, the perfect-site/arc comparisons and arbitrary-ideal almost purity needed below. PerfectoidQuotients supplies its elementary torsion, cotangent and Tor-independence consequences, not another perfectoid predicate.

## Conventions

Fix a prime p throughout the geometric theory. Rings are unital and may be zero. In Layers 1–8 a prism is bounded unless the target explicitly allows an unbounded prism; the general envelope constructions in [§0.28](#layer-0-general-prismatic-envelope) and [§8.12](#layer-8-prelog-prismatic-envelope) allow unbounded orientable bases and unbounded targets. The elementary delta polynomial identities make sense over any commutative ring; prismatic and log-delta rings are Z_(p)-algebras. In Suggested.lean, the elementary structures are explicitly polynomial generalizations: the prime assumption occurs on the theorems, and they are not substitutes for a complete prism.

The addition correction is the integer polynomial

```text
C_p(x,y) = - Σ_(0<i<p) (binom(p,i)/p) x^i y^(p-i).
φ(x) = x^p + p δ(x).
```

The coefficients are divided in the integers before casting into a ring. No formula cancels p unless multiplication by p is injective. In particular C_2(x,y) = −xy and C_3(x,y) = −xy(x+y). The identity endomorphism of Z reconstructs δ(2)=−1 at p=2, δ(4)=−6 at p=2, and δ(2)=−2 at p=3. An ordinary Frobenius congruence is weaker than delta data in a ring with p-torsion.

Use cohomological indexing. D(A) in a construction of commutative algebra objects means the stable derived infinity category, not merely the homotopy category of complexes. A simplicial commutative ring is animated. Completed tensor products and left Kan extensions are derived; every completion is marked by its ideal. D_comp(A) uses derived (p,I)-completion for a bounded prism (A,I). “Discrete” means concentrated in degree zero. Derived p-completion and classical completion agree only under the hypotheses stated for that comparison.

Nygaard filtrations are decreasing and conjugate filtrations increasing. The relative Nygaard filtration belongs to φ_A^*Δ_(R/A), not to the untwisted complex by an implicit identification. An increasing conjugate graded piece is ∧^i L_(R/(A/I))[−i]{−i}, with derived p-completion. In degree one the shift [−1] and twist {−1} are both retained. Hodge–Tate twists M{i}=M⊗(I/I²)^(⊗i) and absolute prism twists A{i} are separate constructions; an orientation identifies them with an untwisted module but is not part of their canonical definitions.

Sites have arrows opposite to ring maps. A weakly initial prism in algebraic language is a weakly final site object. Covers are finite families jointly completely faithfully flat; the empty family covers the zero prism. Fix a universe cut-off for categories of all bounded prisms, as in ALB23 Remark 3.1.2. On the bounded site the prism ideal of an object over (A,I) is IB by rigidity. Derived completeness is part of every complete-flatness input, including the use of BS22 Lemma 3.7.

For cochain Koszul models with two commuting endomorphisms D₁,D₂, take the complex M→M⊕M→M with d⁰(m)=(D₁m,D₂m) and d¹(a,b)=D₂a−D₁b. Then d¹d⁰=0. On M=Z with D₁(m)=2m and D₂(m)=3m, d¹d⁰(1)=6−6=0; replacing the minus by plus gives 12. Reversing both terms changes the orientation and still defines a complex. The q-integer is Σ_(i<n)q^i, so [0]_q=0, [2]_q=1+q and [n]_1=n. The q-divided power γ is defined only on φ⁻¹([p]_qD), with [p]_q a nonzerodivisor. At q=1 it satisfies pγ(x)=x^p; it is not defined by a 0/0 specialization.

In the F-crystal layer, K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic zero with perfect residue field k, K₀=W(k)[1/p], C the completion of an algebraic closure, and X=Spf(O_K). The period rings, invariant functors, fixed fields and full faithfulness for arbitrary perfect k come from TauCetiRoadmap.PadicPeriodRings §§3–4.3 and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §§R07.3.1–R07.3.3; PadicPeriodRings §§4.2–4.3 and FiniteFlatGroups §R07.3.3 records how they are used here. Set A_inf=W(O_C^♭), θ̃=θ∘φ⁻¹, I=ker θ̃, ξ̃=φ(ξ), μ=[ε]−1. The prism map from W(k)[[u]] is u↦[π^♭]^p, with Frobenius on W(k); the usual Kisin embedding u↦[π^♭] is compatible with θ. The filtration on a filtered Frobenius module uses D⊗_(W(k),φ)K. Normalize HT(χ_cyc)=+1. Thus an effective Kisin module corresponds to a lattice with Hodge–Tate weights ≤0 in the covariant realization; the customary contravariant Kisin functor gives its dual. The rank-one twist realizes Z_p(1).

Log monoids are multiplicative unless a chart is written additively. Every saturation or fs assertion includes integrality. The diagonal N→N^r for a semistable chart gives dlog x₁+⋯+dlog x_r=0; for xy=π, dlog y=−dlog x. A p-divisible chart is not an all-integer uniquely divisible chart. Corrected Laurent realizations land in p-Kummer local systems: prime-to-p boundary inertia is a negative control, not part of the essential image. KYcorr Theorem 7 replaces KY arXiv-v1 Theorems 7.36–7.37 (published Theorems 7.35–7.36); the proper pushforward result KY v1 Proposition 7.38 (published Proposition 7.37) is retained.

## Exact supplier contracts

The contracts identify the ordinary library inputs, lower-layer mathematical suppliers and the three companion roadmaps. They do not assert that an additional input has already been constructed. The additional inputs below are necessary targets before the stated general comparisons can be concluded; narrower versions are stated explicitly at their point of use.

### From Mathlib and Tau Ceti

The ordinary carriers and algebraic operations below are inputs. Their stated provisions do not include the prismatic constructions of this roadmap.

- Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Under` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Comma/Over/Basic.lean): The category of objects under X, the target of the functor F in BS22 Lemma 7.8
- Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Shapes/IsTerminal.lean): Terminal objects, together with the dual notion IsInitial that the same declaration generates through the to_dual attribute; initial objects are the conclusion of BS22 Lemma 7.8
- Mathlib `Module.Projective` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Projective.lean): Projective modules, for the descent of finite projective modules
- Mathlib `Module.Finite` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Defs.lean): Finitely generated modules, for the descent of finite projective modules
- Mathlib `IsAdicComplete` (Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Basic.lean): Classical I-adic completeness (Hausdorff and precomplete), the form of p-completeness available for rings with bounded p^∞-torsion
- Mathlib `Ideal.comap` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean): the preimage of an ideal under a ring map; the Nygaard ideal Fil^i_N B is the comap of J^i under the Frobenius
- Mathlib `Ideal.mem_comap` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean): x ∈ comap f K ↔ f x ∈ K, the membership criterion for the Nygaard ideals
- Mathlib `Ideal.map` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean): the ideal generated by the image of an ideal; the ideals (φ^r)^*(I) = φ^r(I)A of a transversal prism
- Mathlib `Ideal.toCotangent` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean): the linear surjection I → I/I², used to state the transition maps of the twist
- Mathlib `ModuleCat.extendScalars` (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/ChangeOfRings.lean): extension of scalars along a ring map as a functor of module categories; base change and Frobenius pullback of the twist
- Mathlib `Module.Dual` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dual/Defs.lean): the dual module; I^{-1} = Hom_A(I, A) in the target of the Frobenius of the twist
- Mathlib `Ideal.Quotient.factor` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Defs.lean): the ring map R/S → R/T for S ≤ T; the transition maps of the tower B/Fil^i_N B
- Mathlib `CochainComplex.mappingCone` (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/HomotopyCategory/MappingCone.lean): the mapping cone of a map of cochain complexes; the fibre of φ − 1 and of φ_n − can is its shift by −1
- Mathlib `DerivedCategory.Q` (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/Basic.lean): the localisation functor from cochain complexes, used to regard mapping cones as objects of D(Λ)
- Mathlib `frobenius` (Mathlib/Algebra/CharP/Lemmas.lean): the Frobenius x ↦ x^p of a ring of characteristic p, the endomorphism σ of B in Lemma 9.2
- Mathlib `rootsOfUnity` (Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/Basic.lean): the groups μ_{p^k}(R) whose inverse limit is the Tate module T_p(R^×)
- Mathlib `Units` (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean): the unit group A^×, containing the rank-one units on which the prismatic logarithm is defined
- Mathlib `CommRing.Pic` (Mathlib/RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean): the Picard group of a commutative ring, for Lemma 9.6 and Corollary 9.7
- Mathlib `WittVector.frobenius_eq_map_frobenius` (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Frobenius.lean): In characteristic p, F = W(Frobenius of R); used for the Frobenius of WCart over F_p-algebras.
- Mathlib `WittVector.verschiebung` (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Verschiebung.lean): The Verschiebung V : W(R) → W(R), an additive map shifting coordinates; V(1) is the point η.
- Mathlib `WittVector.verschiebung_mul_frobenius` (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Identities.lean): V(x F(y)) = V(x) y; gives u V(1) = V(F(u)) and (1 + [ε]) V(y) = V(y).
- Mathlib `Polynomial.cyclotomic_prime_mul_X_sub_one` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean): cyclotomic p R * (X − 1) = X^p − 1; gives φ(q−1) = (q−1)[p]_q.
- Mathlib `geom_sum_mul` (Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/GeomSum.lean): (Σ_{i<n} x^i)(x − 1) = x^n − 1 in any ring; the identity behind [n]_q (q−1) = q^n − 1.
- Mathlib `LinearMap.lTensor` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Map.lean): the map A[1/I] ⊗ f induced by a morphism f of F-crystals
- Mathlib `Localization.Away` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/MonoidLocalization/Away.lean): A[1/d] for an oriented prism, and A[1/p]
- Mathlib `Ideal.smul_top_eq_map` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean): I • ⊤ = (I.map (algebraMap R S)).restrictScalars R: the scalar-extension submodule is the extended ideal
- Mathlib `Ideal.map_pow` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean): map f (I ^ n) = (map f I) ^ n for ideals of commutative semirings
- Mathlib `RingHom.FaithfullyFlat` (Mathlib/RingTheory/RingHom/FaithfullyFlat.lean): Faithful flatness of a ring map is Module.FaithfullyFlat for its induced algebra; stable under base change.
- Mathlib `comonadicExtendScalars` (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Descent.lean): Extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring homomorphism is a comonadic left adjoint; effectivity in IsStack form is a TODO in this source.
- Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent/IsStack.lean): Stack predicate extending IsPrestack and requiring essential surjectivity of covering-sieve descent functors.
- Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.DescentData` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Descent/DescentData.lean): Descent objects for a pseudofunctor and a covering family, with pullback maps and the self/composition coherences.
- Mathlib `MonoidAlgebra` (Mathlib/Algebra/MonoidAlgebra/Defs.lean): The monoid algebra R[M] of a monoid over a semiring; used for Z_(p)[M], A[P] and the chart rings A⟨P⟩ before completion.
- Mathlib `Algebra.GrothendieckGroup` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/MonoidLocalization/GrothendieckGroup.lean): The group completion M^gp of a commutative monoid as the localization at ⊤, with of: M →* M^gp injective for cancellative M (of_injective).
- Mathlib `Perfection` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean): The perfection {f : ℕ → α // f (n+1)^p = f n} of a monoid (with a CommMonoid instance via Perfection.submonoid); it is the tilt M♭ = lim_{m ↦ m^p} M of KY Definition 2.18.
- Mathlib `CategoryTheory.CosimplicialObject` (Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialObject/Basic.lean): Cosimplicial objects SimplexCategory ⥤ C; carriers of Čech–Alexander nerves C^• and of the cosimplicial algebras of Appendix B.
- Mathlib `TruncatedWittVector.mk` (Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/Truncated.lean): Length-two Witt coordinate carrier and constructor, used with coeff to state the δ_log Witt section contract.
- Mathlib `PadicInt.toZModPow` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/RingHoms.lean): Ring homomorphism Z_p→Z/p^n; the coefficient reductions in finite-level inertia representations.
- Mathlib `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Defs.lean): A ring homomorphism induces a group homomorphism on invertible matrices; reduces inertia actions coefficientwise.
- Mathlib `IsPGroup` (Mathlib/GroupTheory/PGroup.lean): Every group element is killed by some p-power; for finite groups and prime p, iff_card identifies this with p-power cardinality.
- Mathlib `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory` (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/ObjectProperty/FullSubcategory.lean): An object satisfying a fixed predicate and the inherited full morphism category; realizes the p-Kummer essential-image category.
- Tau Ceti `TauCeti.IsProP` (TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/ProP/Basic.lean): Every quotient by an open normal subgroup is a p-group. This existing pinned predicate, rather than a second pro-p group theory, expresses local inertia.

### From lower layers and the p-adic comparison bundle

These are mathematical interfaces, not assertions that the suppliers have already been formalized. Completed and enhanced operations retain their indicated hypotheses. A supplier’s narrower theorem is used only in its range; the extra local targets are linked in the last column.

### Additional mathematical inputs and their ranges

The comparison theorems use the following foundation targets in their stated ranges. The local constructions below give their prerequisite chains; a narrower supplier statement is used only within its hypotheses.

**Integral delta and Witt algebra.** [Limits, colimits and Witt vectors](#layer-0-delta-ring-category) constructs the higher integral polynomials for the cofree delta structure, its unit and both adjunction identities, including rings with p-torsion. [PerfectoidQuotients §0.0](#pq-delta-etale) includes algebraization and the length-two Witt étale base-change theorem, with the two ghost factors and relative Frobenius. Neither conclusion follows from the first two coordinates or from derived completion alone. The additional commutative algebra is Hesselholt Lemma 1.1, pp.6–7, and Borger Propositions 8.1, 8.3, Theorem 9.2 and Corollary 9.4, pp.35–40.

**Complete-flat p-torsion control.** [Syntomic H⁰ torsion-freeness](#layer-1-p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic) holds when A is p-torsion-free and A/p has bounded I-power torsion, including crystalline, transversal, perfect and noetherian prisms. Its proof applies the one-element complete-flat module criterion to B/p. The square-zero completed étale localisation in [§1.23](#layer-1-p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic) shows that arbitrary p-torsion-free bounded prisms do not satisfy the unqualified assertion of ALB23 Lemma 5.1.6. The corrected hypothesis is retained at every use.

**Enhanced derived operations.** [Coconnectivity of perfectoidizations](#layer-2-perfectoidization-coconnective) constructs the operation P⁰ on E_∞-F_p-algebras from the cyclic norm and Tate construction; it is not an ordinary ring Frobenius. [Multiplicative Beilinson cover and décalage](#layer-3-filtered-multiplicative-enhancement) supplies the lax monoidal connective cover and E_∞ Bockstein enhancement using DD.1's filtered category, Day tensor and Beilinson heart. Its invertible-ideal filtration includes negative tensor powers and takes the underlying colimit toward −∞. E5:abstract supplies descendability, module descent and uniform-index colimits separately.

**Adic module effectivity.** [Finite projective descent](#layer-2-finite-projective-modules-p-complete) uses compatible idempotents and complete Hom modules to construct the inverse limit of a compatible finite-projective tower. Stacks Tag 0D4B supplies this adic statement. TauCetiRoadmap.AlgebraicVectorBundles Layer 0B supplies the ordinary affine vector-bundle dictionary, which is a different input.

**Formal geometry and generic fibres.** [Bounded formal sites](#layer-1-bounded-formal-sites) combines SF.4's bounded formal carriers and étale gluing with DD.5's quasisyntomic basis; arbitrary bounded rings are treated by animated extension and étale sheafification. [Pre-adic specialization](#layer-6-preadic-specialization) supplies the generic-fibre comparison beyond H1's type-(S) range, using Huber Corollary 3.2.2 and Theorem 3.2.9, pp.174, 180. [Formal covers and lisse v-descent](#layer-6-formal-generic-v-descent) combines D6's diamondification of arbitrary Huber pairs with the valuative cover argument and C2's enhanced v-descent. It includes nonsheafy pre-adic generic fibres. The perfectoid Spec/Spa finite-étale equivalence is imported from P3; the lisse comparison uses its cohomology as well.

**Global scheme deformation.** [Conjugate splittings and liftings](#layer-2-conjugate-splitting-and-lifting) constructs the scheme Ext² obstruction, the Ext¹ torsor of lifts and their Ext⁰ automorphisms from affine deformation theory and étale descent. DD.0 supplies the affine calculation; ALB23 Proposition 3.2.2, p.20, gives the global range. An affine obstruction class alone does not construct the scheme lifting groupoid.

**Perfect-site, arc and integral comparisons.** [Perfect-site comparison and arc excision](#layer-2-perfect-site-arc-comparison) supplies base independence and dependence on π₀, using BS22 Proposition 8.5 and Corollaries 8.11–8.12, pp.64–69. [Integral perfectoidization](#layer-2-integral-perfectoidization) adds discreteness and almost purity for completed integral maps, including nonprincipal idempotent ideals, using BS22 §10, pp.78–83. These consume PerfectoidSpaces §§P4.15.2–P4.15.5; they are not consequences of the fixed-base definition alone. The local arc foundation supplies the topologies, valuative refinements and torsion étale descent needed for the formal and log applications.

**Arbitrary principal Artin–Schreier localization.** [The perfectoid étale comparison](#layer-6-etale-comparison) first removes the chosen pseudouniformizer-power torsion and then applies tilting to the unchanged localization. It treats zero divisors and the zero ring as well as the regular case; t=0 gives a zero fixed-point complex. No extension of P3's regular-localization theorem is presumed.

**Flat G_m cohomology and syntomic rigidity.** [Animated flat continuity](#layer-6-flat-cohomology-continuity) specifies p-adic continuity, reduction Čech descent, Laurent-polynomial extension and the animated multiplicative fracture square using Česnavičius–Scholze Theorem 5.3.5 and Lemma 5.4.2, pp.59–66, and BL22 §7.2. [Nygaard continuity and internal weights](#layer-6-syntomic-connectivity) gives a prismatic route through finite conjugate stages and finite Nygaard quotients. Internal weights are distinguished from filtration indices, and divided Frobenius multiplies internal weights by p. The rigidity step requires the stated continuity proof, rather than the name of a grading or the THH result of AMMN Theorem 5.2.

**Derived crystalline comparison.** [Derived crystalline cohomology](#layer-2-derived-crystalline-comparison) imports the completed polynomial extension, its discrete A_crys identification on quasiregular semiperfect rings and semiperfect Čech descent from CrystallineCohomology CR.4, then constructs their prismatic comparison adapter. These are the ranges of BMS2 Propositions 8.12–8.13, Theorem 8.14, pp.59–61, and BL22 Appendix F. Ordinary de Rham cohomology over W(k) alone does not supply the imported construction.

**Trace and Fargues–Fontaine inputs.** [The trace comparison and Beilinson square](#layer-7-beilinson-square-foundations) identifies AI.7.2’s absolute trace sheaf with the Nygaard-completed prism, constructs the rational trace square with uniform denominator bounds, and passes from its graded pieces to the uncompleted de Rham square. The separate relative sphere-polynomial comparison is imported from AI.7.3. [The Fargues–Fontaine dictionary](#layer-7-ff-dictionary) constructs the schematic curve and its GAGA comparison from AdicSpaces’s interval charts, imports Robba slopes from FiniteFlatGroups R07.4 and Fargues classification from AInfCohomology AI.2.3, and matches their filtered modification to [§7.18](#layer-7-filtered-phi-module-to-crystal).

**Almost Galois descent and period theory.** [Almost sections of the Galois product](#layer-7-almost-galois-functions) uses perfectoidization, product-diamond v-acyclicity and the Witt filtration to identify the completed period functions; it then removes the almost error after I-inversion and p-completion. [PadicPeriodRings §§4.2–4.3 and FiniteFlatGroups §R07.3.3](#period-functors) uses the arbitrary perfect-residue-field period functors of PadicPeriodRings §§4.2–4.3 and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory §R07.3.3. The [integral Kisin dictionary](#layer-7-kisin-functor-comparison) uses R07.4's arbitrary-weight rational restriction theorem, compatible Tate twists and the integral comparison over 𝒪̂_{ℰ^ur}. Changing a height normalization is kept distinct from tensoring with a Tate line.

**Full algebraic Witt–Frobenius correspondence.** [Algebraic Witt–Frobenius modules](#layer-8-algebraic-witt-frobenius) supplies algebraic modules and their bounded derived category, all bounded étale Z/p^n-sheaves and extension by zero, as used in KY Lemma 8.5, pp.86–88. These objects need not be perfect ring modules. The perfect/lisse correspondence is used only in its smaller range.

**Multiplicative q-comparison and log chart maps.** [The q-Poincaré comparison](#layer-5-q-poincare-lemma) constructs the skew differential graded algebra and an E₁ zigzag using Čech cofaces. The labelled-family construction in [§5.22](#layer-5-ainf-omega-comparison-map) supplies arbitrary naturality; its contractible category is not assumed filtered. [Log q-de Rham complexes](#layer-8-log-q-de-rham-complex) uses free prelog presentations for arbitrary integral charts and q-dependent Koszul maps for coordinate identifications. The chart N=2N at p=2 and the merging map X₀,X₁↦X test the integral lattice and the failure of ordinary differential pullback. No missing coordinate or lattice index is inverted.

**Further logarithmic ranges.** [Completed untilt sheaves and profinite coefficients](#layer-8-untilt-coefficients) constructs the marked structure sheaves and continuous Z_p coefficients from D6, D2 and C0. [Formal integral charts](#layer-8-formal-log-charts), [smooth formal log geometry](#layer-8-formal-log-smoothness), [completed log cotangent sheaves](#layer-8-formal-log-cotangent) and [completed log PD sites](#layer-8-completed-log-pd) combine CR.5/DD.6 with formal étale descent, retaining the relative finiteness and nilideal-lifting hypotheses of Koshikawa's Appendix A. [Log PD deformation and Frobenius rigidity](#layer-8-log-pd-rigidity) constructs the arbitrary-fs-chart common base and the uniform factorial contraction, proves rational effectivity, and supplies the proper Cartier-type O_C comparison in [§8.47](#layer-8-log-hyodo-kato-isomorphism). Its special-fibre finiteness and Cartier inverse use Kato Theorem 6.10 and Hyodo–Kato Proposition 2.24 in their general log-smooth integral ranges; the semistable-DVR comparison alone would have a narrower range. AI.1/DD.1 supplies the commuting-endomorphism cochain Koszul convention; the fs log adic foundations are constructed in Layer 8.


## How to read the build

Layers 0–3 construct the delta and prismatic algebra, smooth and animated cohomology, and Nygaard structures. Layer 4 supplies the absolute Cartier–Witt description and Layer 5 the q-de Rham models. Their comparisons feed the étale and syntomic targets of Layer 6, followed by F-crystals in Layer 7 and logarithmic geometry in Layer 8. Within a layer the explicit prerequisite links determine the construction order. The prismatic theory is stated in the README; Suggested.lean keeps only elementary polynomial data over existing carriers.

The full comparisons require five additional arguments: the absolute trace/prismatic comparison; schematic Fargues–Fontaine GAGA and its specific filtered/prismatic modification match; pointwise formal QCoh effectivity outside the regular-ideal range; decay for arbitrary infinitely presented q-PD/log data; and trace/syntomic together with integral derived-de-Rham matching. Their exact ranges and consumers are stated in [§7.0](#layer-7-beilinson-square-foundations), [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh), and [§5.0](#layer-5-framing-foundations). The regular formal and finite-coordinate decay arguments supplied there do not establish these general assertions.

## Layer 0: Delta algebra and prisms

Start with integral polynomials on the existing ring carrier. The Witt-section description then constructs the localization and completion operations without cancelling p. Delta ideals and free/animated delta algebras lead to PD envelopes, distinguished elements, bounded prisms and their regular envelopes. The key distinction is between the ordinary Frobenius function, its congruence modulo p, and the extra delta operation.

### 0.1 Integral delta algebra and the Frobenius dictionary

For every prime p define the integral polynomial C_p(x,y)=−Σ_(1≤i<p)(binom(p,i)/p)x^iy^(p−i), with exact coefficient division in Z before evaluation. On a fixed commutative unital ring R, `Delta.Structure p R` is a function δ satisfying δ(0)=δ(1)=0, δ(x+y)=δ(x)+δ(y)+C_p(x,y) and δ(xy)=x^pδ(y)+y^pδ(x)+pδ(x)δ(y). Delta maps are unital ring maps commuting with the operation. This integral prefix includes zero rings and p-torsion; PerfectoidSpaces owns its p-local restriction.

Prove pC_p=x^p+y^p−(x+y)^p and naturality of the fixed polynomial. The function `Delta.associatedFrobenius` is φ(x)=x^p+pδ(x); `Delta.associatedFrobenius_isLift` gives its ring laws and Frobenius congruence. An ordinary `Delta.FrobeniusLift` is a ring endomorphism with this congruence, with no chosen division or derived homotopy. If multiplication by p is injective, the equation uniquely reconstructs δ (`Delta.reconstruction`), and Frobenius-commuting ring maps are delta maps; without that injectivity neither assertion is inferred.

Define `Delta.integerDelta p a=(a−a^p)/p` in Z and prove `Delta.integerDelta_structure`; its Frobenius is the identity. Naturality along Z→R gives δ(n)=(n−n^p)/p with the quotient evaluated in Z, especially `Delta.delta_prime`: δ(p)=1−p^(p−1). A nonzero characteristic-p ring therefore has no delta structure (`Delta.no_delta_structure`). A quotient R/J admits a unique compatible delta operation exactly when J is delta-stable (`Delta.quotient_structure_iff`); Frobenius stability alone does not suffice.

**API.**

- `Delta.addCorrection_map`: Every ring map carries C_p(x,y) to C_p of the images.
- `Delta.addCorrection_zero`: C_p(x,0)=0.
- `Delta.addCorrection_symm`: C_p(x,y)=C_p(y,x).
- `Delta.Structure.ext`: Pointwise equality of delta gives equality of structures.
- `Delta.Structure.delta_neg`: delta(-x)=-delta(x)-C_p(x,-x).
- `Delta.Structure.delta_two`: delta(1+1)=C_p(1,1).
- `Delta.FrobeniusLift.ext`: Equality of underlying maps gives equality of lifts.
- `Delta.FrobeniusLift.mod_p`: f(x) and x^p have equal images modulo (p).
- `Delta.FrobeniusLift.congruence_iff`: The witness condition is equivalent to the quotient equality for all x.
- `Delta.toFrobenius_apply`: Evaluation is x^p+p delta(x).
- `Delta.toFrobenius_rank_one`: delta(x)=0 implies phi(x)=x^p.
- `Delta.toFrobenius_map`: Delta-compatible ring maps commute with associated Frobenius.
- `Delta.frobeniusEquiv_apply`: The forward map is toFrobenius.
- `Delta.frobeniusEquiv_symm_spec`: The inverse satisfies p delta(x)=f(x)-x^p.
- `Delta.frobeniusEquiv_symm_toFrobenius`: Reconstruction from the associated lift returns the original structure.
- `Delta.intDelta_apply`: delta(a)=(a-a^p)/p in Z.
- `Delta.intDelta_frobenius`: Associated Frobenius is RingHom.id Z.
- `Delta.intDelta_prime`: delta(p)=1-p^(p-1).

**Proof route.** Expand the integral binomial identity to verify the associated ring map; reconstruct in the p-torsion-free case by cancelling only after the polynomial identities are established. Integer Fermat divisibility gives integerDelta and the universal integer-cast identities. For quotient descent use the addition correction to prove representative independence, then surjectivity of the quotient map for all axioms and uniqueness.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 2.1; p. 13.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 2.1; opening p-local convention; p. 13.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remarks 2.2 and 2.5; pp. 13, 14.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.2; p. 13.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.2 and Definition 2.1; p. 13.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 2.6; p. 14.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 2.9; p. 15.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 2.1: integral addition polynomial; existing addCorrection_map API; p. 13.)

**Checks.**

- `correction_dyadic`: Over Z, C_2(x,y)=-xy.
- `correction_cubic`: Over Z, C_3(x,y)=-xy(x+y).
- `correction_zero_argument`: C_p(x,0)=0 in every ring.
- `delta_two_forced`: Every 2-delta structure on Z sends 2 to -1.
- `delta_zero_operation_rejected`: No 2-delta structure on Z has identically zero delta.
- `delta_zero_ring`: The zero ring admits a delta structure.
- `delta_product_rule_integers`: Every 2-δ-structure on Z has δ(4) = −6 = 2²·δ(2) + 2²·δ(2) + 2·δ(2)² with δ(2) = −1: the product rule with its term p·δ(x)·δ(y).
- `lift_on_integers`: The identity on Z is a lift.
- `lift_in_characteristic_p`: The identity on F_p is a lift.
- `power_not_ring_map`: No lift on Z at p=2 has underlying function x->x^2.
- `phi_rank_one`: A delta-zero element has phi(x)=x^p.
- `phi_integer_two`: For the canonical operation on Z at p=2, phi(2)=2, not 4.
- `phi_zero_ring`: Any two structures on the zero ring give the same lift.
- `reconstruction_integer_value`: At p=2 the identity on Z reconstructs delta(2)=-1.
- `reconstruction_rejects_characteristic_p`: Multiplication by p is not injective on F_p.
- `reconstruction_zero_ring`: Multiplication by p is injective on the zero ring.
- `integer_negative_dyadic`: D_2(-1)=-1.
- `integer_cubic_value`: D_3(2)=-2.
- `integer_zero`: D_p(0)=0.

**Further checks and examples.**

- C_2=-xy and C_3=-xy(x+y). The formula evaluates when p is zero or a zero divisor in R.
- The identity holds in characteristic p, although it cannot recover C_p there.
- The zero operation on Z is not a delta structure. A delta structure alone is not a prism: no ideal or completion is supplied.
- The identity on F_p is a lift although F_p has no delta structure. A map of sets such as x->x^p on Z is not substituted for a ring map.
- No converse without a cancellation hypothesis is asserted.
- The zero ring meets the injectivity condition vacuously. A characteristic-zero ring with a p-torsion ideal need not meet it.
- Without target cancellation the identity map between the two square-zero structures is a counterexample.
- D_2(-1)=-1, whereas at odd p it is zero.
- I=0 returns the original operation and I=R gives the zero ring. The ideal (p) in canonical Z is Frobenius-stable but not delta-stable, since delta(p)=1-p^(p-1).
- Reduction to characteristic p retains the correction polynomial.
- This does not rule out some p-torsion in a mixed-characteristic ring. Retain the dyadic negative-scalar value.

### 0.2 Square-zero delta structures and the torsion boundary

On the existing central square-zero extension B⊕F_p of a delta ring equipped with B→F_p, construct δ_λ(a,b)=(δ_B(a),(λ−ā^(p−1))b) for each λ∈F_p. The associated Frobenius is (a,b)↦(φ_B(a),0), independently of λ, although δ_λ(0,1)=λ(0,1). Thus distinct delta structures can have identical ordinary Frobenius. Calculate the second coordinate of C_p((a,b),(c,d)) by the existing square-zero power formula; at p=2 it is −(ad+cb). The scalar action on F_p is the specified central one, and neither a new ring carrier nor p-torsion cancellation is used.

**API.**

- `Delta.squareZeroDelta_fst`: The first coordinate is delta_B(a).
- `Delta.squareZeroDelta_snd`: The second coordinate is (lambda-abar^(p-1))*b.
- `Delta.squareZeroDelta_frobenius`: Frobenius is inl(phi_B(a)), independent of lambda.

**Proof route.** Check the four delta axioms coordinatewise: the addition correction supplies the mixed second-coordinate terms, while x^p has zero second coordinate over F_p. Use ā^p=ā for multiplication and compute φ explicitly. Evaluation at (0,1) separates parameters, also at p=2.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 2.1; authored square-zero acceptance calculation; p. 13; [PIN-square](#ref-pin-square), snd_mul and snd_pow.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.2 torsion boundary; authored example; p. 13; [PIN-square](#ref-pin-square), TrivSqZeroExt and central-action CommRing structure.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remarks 2.2-2.3 and Example 2.6; authored witness; pp. 13, 14.)

**Checks.**

- `square_zero_parameter`: For B=Z and epsilon=(0,1), delta_lambda(epsilon)=lambda*epsilon.
- `square_zero_addition_correction`: delta_lambda(1+epsilon)=(lambda-1)*epsilon; omitting the correction fails.
- `square_zero_base_compatibility`: Restriction along inl is the canonical integer delta.

**Further checks and examples.**

- At p=2 the result is -cbar*b-abar*d, the second coordinate of -xy.
- The proof works at p=2. B=Z supplies integer tests; B=Z_(p) with its canonical delta supplies a source-compatible p-local example.
- The identity between the two structures is Frobenius-compatible but not delta-compatible. For lambda=1, phi(epsilon)=epsilon^p=0 while delta(epsilon)=epsilon is nonzero, rejecting the rank-one converse.

### 0.3 Length-two Witt sections

Use Mathlib’s actual length-two p-typical Witt ring W₂(R), never the pointwise product ring. Its coordinate-one addition and multiplication are

```text
(x+y)₁=x₁+y₁+C_p(x₀,y₀),
(xy)₁=x₀^py₁+y₀^px₁+p x₁y₁.
```

Construct the coefficientwise ring map `Delta.witt2Map` using infinite Witt functoriality and surjective truncation, and prove both coordinate evaluation laws. A vector z is a unit exactly when z₀ and z₀^p+pz₁ are units; this is a coordinate/ghost criterion, not injectivity of the ghost map. Construct `Delta.wittSectionEquiv`: delta structures correspond to first-coordinate ring sections s:R→W₂(R), with s(x)=(x,δ(x)); the first ghost expression is the associated Frobenius. This works with p-torsion and distinguishes sections that have the same ghost composite.

**API.**

- `Delta.wittSectionEquiv_apply`: The section has coordinates (x,delta(x)).
- `Delta.wittSectionEquiv_symm_apply`: The inverse recovers coordinate one.
- `Delta.wittSectionEquiv_ghost_one`: s(x)_0^p+p*s(x)_1 equals phi_delta(x).
- `Delta.witt2Map_coeff`: The jth coordinate of witt2Map(f)(z) equals f(z_j); the separate lemma target supplies this API.

### 0.4 Localization of integral delta data

Let i:A→B exhibit the existing localization S⁻¹A. A delta structure extends compatibly and uniquely exactly when i(φ(s)) is a unit for every s∈S, equivalently φ(s) divides an element of S. Literal φ(S)⊆S is sufficient but unnecessary. No injectivity of i or p-torsion-freeness is required. The extension has the delta-map universal property into every delta ring C in which the images of S are units, and is independent of all unit witnesses. For z=i(a)/i(s), its value is characterized without p-division by

```text
i(s)^p i(φ(s)) δ(z)=i(s)^p i(δ(a))−i(a)^p i(δ(s)).
```

For any ring map f:A→C with p∈Jac(C), f(φ(x)) is a unit iff f(x) is a unit, even if C has no delta structure. Consequently W₂(C) units are detected by coordinate zero and every localization with p in its target Jacobson radical admits the unique compatible delta structure. The map must commute with delta, not merely with Frobenius.

**API.**

- `Delta.localize_algebraMap`: delta_B(i(a))=i(delta_A(a)); supplied by Compatibility with the localization map.
- `Delta.localize_unique`: Every delta structure on B compatible with i equals localize; supplied by Uniqueness of localized delta data.
- `Delta.localize_fraction`: For z=a/s, i(s)^p*i(phi(s))*delta_B(z)=i(s)^p*i(delta(a))-i(a)^p*i(delta(s)); supplied by Delta of a fraction.
- `Delta.localizeJacobson_algebraMap`: The operation on i(a) is i(delta_A(a)).
- `Delta.localizeJacobson_unique`: Every compatible delta structure equals localizeJacobson.
- `Delta.localizeJacobson_eq_localize`: For any proof of the original Frobenius image-unit condition, localizeJacobson equals localize with that proof.

**Proof route.** Compose the Witt section with W₂(i); the two-coordinate unit criterion permits the existing localization lift, and localization extensionality makes its zeroth coordinate the identity. Conversely a compatible extension makes φ(i(s)) a unit; the multiplication axiom gives the displayed fraction formula and the delta universal property. In radical targets reduce φ(x)=x^p+pδ(x) modulo maximal ideals to obtain the unit equivalence.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 2.15 and proof; p. 16.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.16, printed; associated Frobenius formula of Remark 2.2; pp. 13, 17.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.4; Remark 2.16; pp. 13, 17.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.16, printed; Lemma 2.15; pp. 16, 17.)

**Checks.**

- `delta_localization_identity`: The identity localization recovers the original delta structure.
- `delta_localization_zero`: A zero localization has the unique zero delta operation.
- `delta_localization_rational_value`: Localizing the canonical 2-delta structure on Z in Q gives delta(1/3)=1/9.
- `delta_localization_torsion_survives`: In the localization of Z plus F_2*epsilon at powers of (3,1), the lambda=1 operation extends, epsilon remains nonzero, and delta(epsilon)=epsilon. A p-torsionfree-quotient substitute fails.
- `jacobson_localization_identity`: An identity localization with p in the radical recovers d.
- `jacobson_localization_zero`: On a zero localization the operation is zero.
- `jacobson_localization_dyadic`: At p=2 the localized operation sends the integer scalar 2 to -1, including in a target with torsion.

**Further checks and examples.**

- The result is a delta structure on the given B, not a new localization ring or a p-torsionfree quotient.
- No global section, completion or flat base-change theorem enters.
- Coincidence of associated Frobenius alone is not used; it would be insufficient on p-torsion.
- In A=Z_(p)[X] with phi(X)=X^p+p, the localization A[X^-1] has no compatible delta structure: X^p+p is not a Laurent unit. For p=2 on Z plus F_2*epsilon and s=(3,1), phi(s)=(3,0) divides s^2 but is not a power of s. Literal stability is not necessary.
- Identity and composite maps are compatible by the unique extension property. This proof works even when different delta structures can have the same Frobenius.
- the canonical integer structure at p=2, delta(1/3)=1/9. For phi(X)=X^p+p in the rational function field, delta(X^-1)=-1/(X^p*(X^p+p)); replacing the second denominator by X^p is false.

### 0.5 Delta continuity and the actual adic completion

For any ideal J, y∈J implies C_p(x,y)∈J. If p∈I, prove δ(I^(n+1))⊆I^n and x−y∈I^(n+1) ⇒ δ(x)−δ(y)∈I^n for every n≥0, without finite generation or separation. Define the shifted **function** q_n:A/I^(n+1)→A/I^n by [a]↦[δ(a)]; it is not an additive/ring map or a delta structure on either quotient. Prove evaluation and compatibility with all quotient transitions.

On Mathlib’s existing inverse-limit ring AdicCompletion I A define δ̂ by ρ_n(δ̂x)=q_n(ρ_(n+1)x). Coordinate extensionality proves the axioms, compatibility with A→AdicCompletion and the explicit n+1 continuity modulus for the quotient-kernel topology. For finite I, the existing kernel/power equality identifies that topology with the extended-ideal topology and proves uniqueness among **all** compatible delta structures. No noetherianity, p-torsion-freeness or injectivity of the completion map is imposed; without finite generation do not infer extended-ideal completeness or unrestricted uniqueness.

- `Delta.shiftedQuotient_transition`: For m<=n, reduction from n to m after q_n equals q_m after reduction from n+1 to m+1.

**Proof route.** Use product-ideal induction and the delta addition/multiplication laws for the one-power loss, then quotient descent for q_n. Compatible coordinates define δ̂ on the actual limit; checking one higher coordinate verifies each axiom and the completion-map identity. With I finite, approximate at level n+1 and apply the same congruence to any competing operation; the kernel/power equality and separatedness force equality.

### 0.6 The initial p-local integer delta ring

On the existing Localization.AtPrime of (p)⊂Z construct the canonical delta structure from `Delta.integerDelta`. Its associated Frobenius is the identity and pδ(x)=x−x^p; this uses exact division in the p-local domain, not a field-division definition. The canonical integer map commutes with delta. For every delta ring B in which each integer prime to p is a unit, including p-torsion and zero rings, there is exactly one delta-compatible unital map Z_(p)→B. Keep that unit hypothesis explicit.

- `Delta.intAtPrime_algebraMap`: Delta of the image of a in Z equals the image of intDelta(a).
- `Delta.intAtPrime_frobenius`: The associated ring endomorphism is the identity.
- `Delta.intAtPrime_spec`: For every x, p*delta(x)=x-x^p.

**Proof route.** The identity Frobenius preserves the integers prime to p, so the localization construction applies to the actual AtPrime carrier. Its fraction formula proves the displayed operation and compatibility with integerDelta. Integer-map uniqueness and the delta localization universal property give initiality without cancelling p in B.

### 0.7 Delta-stable ideals and universal quotients

An ideal generated by S is delta-stable iff δ(s) belongs to it for every s∈S. Define `Delta.idealClosure d I` as the ordinary ideal span of δ^n(a), n≥0 and a∈I, with δ^0 the identity; it is the least delta-stable ideal containing I. Prove stability, monotonicity, extensivity and idempotence, and that kernels of delta maps are stable. These assertions require no finite generation, p-locality or p-torsion-freeness.

On the existing quotient Q=A/idealClosure(I), construct the unique delta operation δ_Q(q(a))=q(δ(a)). This is the universal delta A-algebra annihilating I: every delta-compatible f:A→B killing I factors uniquely through q by the ordinary quotient lift, and the factor remains delta-compatible. Include both its evaluation and uniqueness as ring maps. In particular `Delta.idealClosure_prime` gives idealClosure((p))=⊤, since p and δ(p)=1−p^(p−1) generate the unit ideal.

**API.**

- `Delta.idealClosure_eq_span`: C_d(I) is exactly the ideal span of the set of all delta^n(a) with n nonnegative and a in I.
- `Delta.le_idealClosure`: I is contained in C_d(I), by the zeroth iterate.
- `Delta.idealClosure_stable`: For x in C_d(I), delta(x) is in C_d(I); the separate stability lemma supplies this API.
- `Delta.idealClosure_le`: For a delta-stable ideal J, C_d(I) is contained in J if and only if I is contained in J; the separate minimality lemma supplies this API.
- `Delta.idealClosure_idem`: C_d(C_d(I))=C_d(I).
- `Delta.idealClosure_mono`: If I is contained in J, then C_d(I) is contained in C_d(J).
- `Delta.quotientByIdealClosure_mk`: The quotient delta operation sends q(a) to q(delta(a)); this is also a separate projection lemma.
- `Delta.quotientByIdealClosure_unique`: Every delta structure on A/C_d(I) compatible with q equals the constructed one.
- `Delta.quotientByIdealClosure_kills`: For a in I, the existing quotient projection q sends a to zero.

**Proof route.** Span induction uses the correction-ideal identity and the product law, rather than additivity of delta. Each closure generator maps under delta to the next one, while stable ideals contain all iterates; these give minimality and the closure laws. Apply stable-quotient descent, then factor through the stable kernel of f and use surjectivity of q for compatibility and uniqueness.

<a id="layer-0-delta-ring-category"></a>

### 0.9 Limits, colimits and Witt vectors of δ-rings

The category of δ-rings (objects: commutative rings with a δ-structure; morphisms: ring maps commuting with δ) has all limits and colimits, and the forgetful functor to commutative rings preserves both. In particular products, equalizers, tensor products A ⊗_C B along δ-maps and filtered colimits of δ-rings carry unique δ-structures making the structure maps δ-maps. The forgetful functor has a left adjoint (free δ-rings) and a right adjoint, the p-typical Witt vector functor W: for a ring R, W(R) carries the δ-structure whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius, and for a δ-ring A there is a natural δ-map w_A : A → W(A), the unit, whose first two Witt coordinates are (x, δ(x)).

The δ-structure on W(R) is constructed by integral universal polynomials and then proved cofree. For R with p-torsion, neither cancellation of p nor injectivity of the ghost map is used.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.7 (Limits and colimits of δ-rings, and Witt vectors); Remark 2.13; pp. 14, 16.)

- `Prismatic.IsDeltaHom`: For δ-structures d on A and e on B, a ring map f : A → B is a map of δ-rings when f(d(x)) = e(f(x)) for all x; the identity is one, composites of such maps are such maps, and such a map commutes with the associated Frobenius endomorphisms.
- `Delta.Structure.prod`: The coordinatewise δ-structure on A × B.
- `Delta.Structure.tensorProduct`: For δ-maps C → A and C → B, the unique δ-structure on A ⊗_C B for which both inclusions are δ-maps.
- `Delta.witt`: The δ-structure on W(R) whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius.
- `Delta.witt_frobenius`: The Frobenius of the δ-structure on W(R) equals WittVector.frobenius.
- `Delta.wittUnit`: For a δ-ring A, the δ-map w_A : A → W(A).
- `Delta.wittUnit_coeff_zero`: The 0-th Witt coordinate of w_A(x) is x.
- `Delta.wittUnit_coeff_one`: The first Witt coordinate of w_A(x) is δ(x).
- `Delta.wittUnit_ghost`: The n-th ghost component of w_A(x) is φ^n(x).
- `Delta.wittUnit_isDeltaHom`: The unit w_A:A→W(A) commutes with δ, including when A has p-torsion.
- `Delta.wittUnit_counit`: The unit and constantCoeff counit obey both adjunction triangles, naturally in the δ-ring and the ring.

Over Z[X₀,X₁,…], the p-typical Dwork criterion applied to b_n=(w_(n+1)−w_n^p)/p constructs integral coordinate polynomials D_n with p^nD_n=b_n−Σ_(i<n)p^iD_i^(p^(n−i)), D₀=X₁ and D_n=X_(n+1) plus lower coordinates; universal torsion-free ghost calculations prove their delta identities before specialization to arbitrary R, including torsion (Hesselholt Lemmas 1.1 and 1.18, pp.6–7,16). Applying the criterion to φ^n(x) in the free delta ring gives the natural unit with Q₀=x,Q₁=δx, while the triangular D_n recover every coordinate from iterated delta and constantCoeff, proving uniqueness of W(f)∘w_A and both adjunction triangles without ghost injectivity. - `delta_prod_fst`: The first projection A × B → A commutes with δ for the product structure.

- `witt_torsion_polynomial`: At p=2 on W(F₂), δ_W([1])=0 and δ_W(V([1])) has zeroth coordinate 1. The latter detects an operation lost by trying to cancel p in F₂.

<a id="layer-0-delta-radical-localization"></a>

### 0.10 p-local localization of a δ-ring

Let A be a δ-ring and S ⊂ A a multiplicative subset. Let T be the multiplicative subset generated by S, φ(S), φ^2(S), …. Then (S^{-1}A)_(p) := the localization of S^{-1}A along V(p) (inverting 1 + p·a for all a) coincides with (T^{-1}A)_(p); it carries a unique δ-structure compatible with the one on A, has p in its Jacobson radical, and A → (S^{-1}A)_(p) is the initial δ-A-algebra B with p ∈ rad(B) in which every element of S is invertible. The same holds for the localization along V(p, I) for an ideal I, which is the form used for prisms.

A is a δ-ring; S is a submonoid of A. An arbitrary localization S^{-1}A need not carry a compatible δ-structure; the statement concerns its p-localization.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.16 (Localizations in the p-local world); p. 17.)

*Needs:* [§0.4](#layer-0-delta-localization-phi-stable), [§0.4](#layer-0-delta-localization-universal), [§0.4](#layer-0-frobenius-image-unit-jacobson), [§0.4](#layer-0-delta-localization-jacobson), Mathlib `IsLocalization`, Mathlib `Ideal.jacobson`.

- `Delta.frobeniusSaturation_stable`: φ maps T into T, and S ≤ T.
- `Delta.radicalSaturation`: The submonoid of elements of A that become units modulo p in T^{-1}A; the localization of A at it is (S^{-1}A)_(p).
- `Delta.localizeRadical_p_mem_jacobson`: In the localization B of A at the radical saturation, p lies in the Jacobson radical and every element of S is a unit.
- `Delta.localizeRadical`: The unique δ-structure on the localization B of A at the radical saturation that is compatible with A → B.
- `Delta.localizeRadical_unique`: Any δ-A-algebra C with p ∈ rad(C) in which S is invertible receives a unique δ-A-algebra map from B.

**Proof route.** Invert the Frobenius-stable closure T of the denominators, then 1+pT⁻¹A, using the localization theorem. In every target with p in its Jacobson radical, an invertible f has invertible φ(f), so the second localization preserves precisely the original mapping problem. Compare with the ordinary p-local localization by their identical universal properties (BS22 Remark 2.16).

**Checks.**

- `frobenius_saturation_phi_stable_already`: If φ(S) ⊂ S then the Frobenius saturation of S is S.
- `frobenius_saturation_int`: For A = Z with its canonical δ-structure (φ = id) the Frobenius saturation of any submonoid is itself.
- `frobenius_saturation_free_strict`: In the free δ-ring on one generator x_0, the Frobenius saturation of the powers of x_0 contains x_0^p + p·x_1, which is not a power of x_0.
- `radical_localization_dyadic`: For A=Z, p=2 and S generated by 3, the result is Z_(2), with δ(2)=−1; in particular 5 is a unit. The ordinary localization Z[1/3] fails the last assertion.
- `radical_localization_inverts_prime`: For A=Z and S generated by p, the p-localization is the zero ring: after p is inverted, 1+p·(−1/p)=0 is among the elements inverted.
- `radical_localization_empty_generators`: With S={1} and A=Z, the result is Z_(p), rather than Z; every integer prime to p becomes a unit.

- A = Z and S generated by 3 with p = 2: the result is Z_(2) with its canonical δ-structure. For A = Z{x} and S = {x^n}: T contains φ(x) = x^p + p δ(x), which is not a unit of Z{x}[1/x] but is a unit of its p-localization.

<a id="layer-0-witt2-derived-pullback-square"></a>

### 0.11 The pullback square for W_2 of a simplicial commutative ring

(1) For a p-torsion-free ring R the square of rings formed by the restriction W_2(R) → R, (x, y) ↦ x, the Witt vector Frobenius F : W_2(R) → R, (x, y) ↦ x^p + p·y, the projection R → R/p and the composite R → R/p → R/p of the projection with the Frobenius of R/p is a pullback square: W_2(R) ≅ {(a, b) ∈ R × R : b ≡ a^p modulo p}. (2) For every simplicial commutative ring B there is a pullback square of simplicial commutative rings, functorial in B, with the same two maps out of W_2(B) (W_2 applied levelwise) and with R/p replaced by B ⊗^L_Z F_p. In particular, for a cosimplicial simplicial ring B^• with discrete colim lim, colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ W_2(B^•) is W_2 of colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ B^•.

In (1) R is p-torsion-free; in (2) B is any simplicial commutative ring (an animated ring, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation). W_2 is the ring of length-two p-typical Witt vectors with the addition and multiplication of [§0.3](#layer-0-witt-section-coordinates) and [§0.3](#layer-0-witt-section-coordinates). This target constructs the square; the equivalence with coherent derived Frobenius-lift data is outside its statement.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 2.5 (the two squares) and the proof of Lemma 7.7 (1); pp. 14, 57.)

**Proof route.** Over a p-torsion-free ring the two ghost coordinates embed W₂(R) as the pairs (a,b) with b≡a^p mod p. Extend this identification from finite polynomial rings to animated rings by sifted-colimit extension, with R/p replaced by R⊗^L_ZF_p. On underlying spectra the resulting finite pullback is preserved by the indicated exact limits/realizations; discreteness identifies the final object with ordinary W₂.

- R = Z: W_2(Z) ≅ {(a, b) ∈ Z × Z : b ≡ a^p mod p}; the pair (p, 0) is the image of the Witt vector (p, −p^{p−1}), and (1, 0) is not in the image. R = F_p (not p-torsion-free): the underived square fails, W_2(F_p) = Z/p² is not F_p ×_{F_p} F_p = F_p; the derived square holds with F_p ⊗^L_Z F_p in the corner.

<a id="layer-0-animated-delta-rings"></a>

### 0.12 Simplicial commutative δ-rings

A simplicial commutative δ-ring is a simplicial object in the category of δ-rings; the ∞-category of animated δ-rings is obtained from these by inverting weak equivalences of underlying simplicial sets, equivalently it is the animation (sifted-colimit completion) of the category of free δ-rings on finite sets. The forgetful functor to animated commutative rings preserves all limits and colimits; in particular a derived pushout of animated δ-rings is computed as the derived pushout of the underlying animated rings. Free adjunction: for an animated δ-ring A and a chosen point x of its underlying animated ring (with its class in π_0(A)), the animated δ-A-algebra A{x/p} is the derived pushout of A ← Z{t} → Z{s} (t ↦ x, t ↦ p·s); similarly A{J/I} for I = (d) and J = (d, x_1,…,x_r) is the derived pushout of A ← A{t_1,…,t_r} → A{s_1,…,s_r} (free δ-A-algebras) along t_i ↦ x_i and t_i ↦ d·s_i, using chosen points representing d and the x_i. The pushout depends on this diagram, not merely on the names of its π_0-classes. For a finitely generated ideal I containing a power of p the derived I-complete animated δ-rings form a full subcategory, with derived I-completion left adjoint to the inclusion.

Animated commutative rings, sifted left Kan extension and derived pushouts are supplied by EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation; derived completion by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1. Several constructions require this ∞-category (Corollary 2.39, Corollary 2.44, the proof of Proposition 3.13, Construction 6.1); this construction supplies the definition those uses need.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Corollary 2.39 (statement: the derived pushout square in simplicial commutative δ-rings); Remark 2.37; Corollary 2.44; proof of Proposition 3.13; pp. 24, 25, 27, 33.)

*Needs:* [§0.9](#layer-0-delta-ring-category), [§0.8](#layer-0-free-delta-ring), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/nonabelian-derived-category`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject`, [PerfectoidQuotients §0.0](#pq-delta-etale).

- `Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.const`: The constant simplicial δ-ring on a δ-ring.
- `Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.frobenius`: The levelwise Frobenius φ, an endomorphism of the underlying simplicial ring.
- `Delta.SimplicialDeltaRing.frobenius_app`: In each degree n the Frobenius is x ↦ x^p + p·δ_n(x).

The displayed pushouts therefore have the stated underlying derived tensors, so the regular PD calculation applies. Derived completion uses the W₂ pullback description and its limit compatibility, with the unique delta extension imported from PerfectoidQuotients §0.0.

- `simplicial_delta_const_frobenius`: The levelwise Frobenius of the constant simplicial δ-ring on A is the Frobenius of A in every degree.
- `simplicial_delta_face_commutes`: Every simplicial operator of a simplicial δ-ring commutes with the levelwise Frobenius.

### 0.14 Distinguished elements, perfect delta rings and torsion

**Factors of distinguished elements.** Let A be a δ-ring. (1) If d ∈ A is distinguished, u ∈ A is a unit and d, p ∈ rad(A), then u·d is distinguished. (2) If d = f·h is distinguished with f, p ∈ rad(A), then f is distinguished and h is a unit.

A is a δ-ring; rad(A) is the Jacobson radical. For (1): d, p ∈ rad(A). For (2): f, p ∈ rad(A).

**Local distinguished generators of a prism ideal.** Let A be a δ-ring. (a) (Lemma 2.25) If d, p ∈ rad(A), then d is distinguished if and only if p ∈ (d, φ(d)); in particular distinguishedness depends only on the ideal (d). (b) (Lemma 3.1) Let I ⊂ A be a locally principal ideal with p, I ⊂ rad(A). The following are equivalent: (1) p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A; (2) p ∈ I + φ(I)A; (3) one can choose a δ-map A→A′, obtained as an ind-Zariski localization and faithfully flat, for which IA′=(d), δ(d) is a unit, and both d and p lie in rad(A′).

A is a δ-ring; in (a) d, p ∈ rad(A); in (b) I is locally principal and p, I ⊂ rad(A). No global generator of I is assumed in (b).

**p-torsion in δ-rings.** A δ-ring A is p-torsion-free if its Frobenius φ is injective (for instance if A is perfect), and also if A is reduced. Neither hypothesis implies the other: A = Z_p[x]/(x^p − 1) with φ(x) = x^p is reduced and φ(x − 1) = 0; B = Z_p[x]/(x^2) with φ(x) = p·x is not reduced and φ is injective.

A is any δ-ring. (The source assumes Z_(p)-algebras and uses that δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1} is a unit; this is not needed, because p·x = 0 gives p^{p−1}φ(x) = φ(p^{p−1}x) = 0 and δ(p)φ(x) = 0, hence φ(x) = 0.)

**Perfect δ-rings and Witt vectors of perfect rings.** A δ-ring A is perfect if φ is an isomorphism. The following categories are equivalent: (1) perfect p-complete δ-rings; (2) p-adically complete, p-torsion-free rings A with A/p perfect; (3) perfect F_p-algebras. The functor (1) → (2) forgets δ; in particular every ring map between perfect p-complete δ-rings is a δ-map. The functors between (2) and (3) are A ↦ A/p and R ↦ W(R); in particular W(R) has exactly one δ-structure for R perfect of characteristic p. The inclusion of perfect δ-rings into δ-rings has the left adjoint A ↦ colim_φ A and the right adjoint A ↦ lim_φ A.

"p-complete" in (1) and (2) is classical p-adic completeness; for perfect δ-rings it agrees with derived p-completeness because they are p-torsion-free.

**Perfect elements have rank one.** Let A be a δ-ring and x ∈ A. Then δ(x^{p^n}) ∈ p^n A for all n ≥ 0. In particular, if A is p-adically separated and y ∈ A admits a p^n-th root for every n, then δ(y) = 0 (y has rank 1); in particular φ(y) = y^p (the converse needs A p-torsion-free).

A is a δ-ring; for the second statement A is p-adically separated.

**Distinguished elements of perfect δ-rings.** Let A be a perfect p-complete δ-ring, so A = W(R) with R = A/p perfect, and let d = Σ_{i≥0} [a_i] p^i be the Teichmüller expansion of d ∈ A. Then d is distinguished if and only if a_1 is a unit of R. Moreover (Lemma 2.34) if A is a p-torsion-free, p-adically separated δ-ring with A/p reduced and d ∈ A is distinguished, then d is a nonzerodivisor and R = A/d satisfies R[p^∞] = R[p].

First statement: A perfect and p-complete. Second statement: A p-torsion-free, p-adically separated, A/p reduced (for example A perfect and p-complete); d distinguished.

**Proof route.** Expand the delta product law and reduce modulo maximal ideals for the distinguished-factor and prism-generator criteria. Use p·x=0 ⇒ φ(x)=0 and Frobenius iteration/reducedness for the torsion controls; Witt lifting of perfect mod-p rings gives the category equivalences. Teichmüller expansions and the p-adic estimate for δ(x^(p^n)) give rank-one and distinguished coefficient tests, with the separatedness and reduced-mod-p hypotheses retained.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemmas 2.23 and 2.24 with proofs; p. 19.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 2.25 and Lemma 3.1 with proofs; pp. 19, 28.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 2.28 (p-torsion in δ-rings) with proof; Remark 2.29; p. 20.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 2.26, Remark 2.27, Corollary 2.31 with proof; p. 20.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 2.32 (Perfect elements have rank 1) with proof; p. 21.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 2.33 (Distinguished elements in perfect δ-rings) and Lemma 2.34, with proofs; p. 21.)

**Further checks and examples.**

- In Z_(p): p = p·1 and (−p) = (−1)·p are distinguished. The hypothesis f ∈ rad(A) in (2) is needed: in Z_(p), p = 1·p with f = 1 ∉ rad; f is not distinguished (δ(1) = 0) and h = p is not a unit.
- A = Z_p[[q − 1]] and I = ([p]_q): p ∈ (I, φ(I)) because φ([p]_q) = [p]_{q^p} ≡ p modulo [p]_q. For I = (p^2) ⊂ Z_p: p ∉ I + φ(I)A, consistent with p^2 not being distinguished.
- Z ⊕ F_2·ε with the λ = 1 structure of Delta structures on a square-zero extension has 2-torsion and is neither reduced nor has injective Frobenius. The two examples of Remark 2.29.
- W(F_p) = Z_p with φ = id is perfect; Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p is not (x is not in the image of φ). For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}], W(R) is the p-completion of Z_p[x^{1/p^∞}] with φ(x^{1/p^n}) = x^{1/p^{n−1}}.
- In W(R) for R perfect, the Teichmüller representatives [a] have rank 1: φ([a]) = [a]^p. q ∈ Z_p[[q − 1]] with δ(q) = 0 has rank 1 without having p-power roots: the converse of the lemma fails.
- In W(F_p) = Z_p: d = p has a_0 = 0, a_1 = 1; d = p^2 has a_1 = 0 and is not distinguished. ξ = p − [p^♭] ∈ A_inf(O_C) has unit coefficient of p in its Teichmüller expansion and is distinguished; A_inf/ξ = O_C is p-torsion-free.
