### 0.16 PD envelopes of regular sequences are δ-envelopes

(1) (Lemma 2.38) Let B be a p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebra and f_1,…,f_r ∈ B a Koszul-regular sequence on B/p. The derived pushout D′ of D_(x)(Z_(p)[x_1,…,x_r]) ← Z_(p)[x_1,…,x_r] → B (x_i ↦ f_i) in animated rings is discrete, p-torsion-free and equal to the PD envelope D_(f_1,…,f_r)(B); its formation commutes with base change B → B′ to p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebras in which the f_i stay Koszul-regular modulo p. (2) (Corollary 2.39) Let A be a p-torsion-free δ-Z_(p)-algebra and f_1,…,f_r ∈ A a regular sequence in A/p. The animated δ-ring A{φ(f_1)/p,…,φ(f_r)/p} (Simplicial commutative δ-rings) is discrete, p-torsion-free and equal to D_I(A), I = (f_1,…,f_r); so D_I(A) is a δ-ring, finitely presented as a δ-A-algebra. (3) (Remark 2.40) D_I(A) is the φ-pullback of A{f_1/p,…,f_r/p}, which depends only on I and is the universal p-torsion-free δ-A-algebra in which p divides I. (4) (Warning 2.41) The Frobenius twist cannot be removed: for A = Z_(p)[x], f = x, the subrings A{x/p} ⊂ A[1/p] for the δ-structures with φ(x) = x^p and φ(x) = x^p + p are not comparable.

B and A are p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebras; the f_i are Koszul-regular on B/p (respectively regular in A/p). The specified structure maps make the polynomial pushout a Z_(p)-algebra construction. PD envelopes and their universal property are supplied by CrystallineCohomology:CR.0. The misprints in the proofs in the cited sources do not affect the statements.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 2.38, Corollary 2.39 with proofs; Remark 2.40; Warning 2.41; pp. 24, 25.)

*Needs:* [§0.15](#layer-0-free-delta-pd-envelope), [§0.12](#layer-0-animated-delta-rings), [§0.8](#layer-0-free-delta-ring), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`, Mathlib `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`, Mathlib `DividedPowers`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Proof route.** The characteristic-p free PD module over F_p[x]/(x_i^p) makes the derived PD pushout discrete and p-torsion-free under Koszul regularity; the PD universal map and pushout map are inverse on generators. Apply this after the free-delta flat base change for the delta-envelope identification. The two universal extensions of x/p then give the stated distinction by 1/p.

**Checks.**

- A = Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p, f = x: A{x^p/p} is the divided power polynomial algebra on x over Z_p. Warning 2.41: δ_1(x/p) = (x^p/p^{p+1})(p^{p−1} − 1) and δ_2(x/p) = δ_1(x/p) + 1/p.

<a id="layer-0-complete-regular-sequence"></a>

### 0.17 Complete regularity over animated bases

Extend the ordinary regular-envelope input to an animated base A and a finite ideal I=(f_1,…,f_n)⊂π_0A. For a derived I-complete animated A-algebra B, a finite sequence x in π_0B is I-completely regular relative to A when Kos(B;x) is I-completely flat over A. Equivalently Kos(A;f)→Kos(B;f,x) is flat as a map of animated rings; reduction along π_0A/I shows that this definition is independent of the generators f. Here complete flatness itself is detected after derived reduction; completeness is a separate condition on B. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 2.42, p.26.)

The API `Prismatic.IsRelativelyRegular` uses this animated predicate and supplies `nil`, `polynomial` and `baseChange`. The empty case asks that B be I-completely flat, and base change uses derived tensor followed by completion. When A,B are discrete and the selected generators f are regular on both, it can be checked by weak regularity of x modulo I and flatness over A/I of the successive quotients; this is only a sufficient discrete test in that range, not a replacement definition on arbitrary animated rings. For I=0, it requires Koszul regularity and A-flatness of B/(x).

**Checks.**

- `relatively_regular_variable`: x in Z_p⟨x⟩ over Z_p is p-completely relatively regular; its quotient modulo p is F_p.
- `relatively_regular_empty_self`: the empty sequence for B=A gives the identity derived quotient.
- `relatively_regular_p_fails`: p in Z_p over Z_p is not p-completely regular; Kos(Z_p;p,p) has nonzero first homotopy over F_p.
- `relatively_regular_non_flat_quotient`: px is regular in Z[x], but Z[x]/(px) is not Z-flat, so it fails relative regularity for I=0.

*Needs:* [ordinary regular-envelope interface](#ps-prisms), DD.1 complete flatness and derived Koszul reduction, E5:animation, Mathlib `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular` and `Module.Flat`.

<a id="layer-0-pd-envelope-complete-flatness"></a>

### 0.18 Complete flatness of PD envelopes and of p-adic δ-envelopes

(1) (Lemma 2.43) Let A be an animated ring and B a p-complete animated A-algebra with x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) such that x_1^p,…,x_r^p is p-completely regular relative to A. Let D be the pushout of D_(y)(Z_p[y_1,…,y_r])^∧ ← Z_p[y_1,…,y_r]^∧ → B (y_i ↦ x_i) in derived p-complete animated rings. Then A → D is p-completely flat. (2) (Corollary 2.44) Let A be a p-complete animated δ-ring, B a p-complete animated δ-A-algebra and x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) p-completely regular relative to A. Then C = B{x_1/p,…,x_r/p}^∧, the pushout of Z_p{z_i}^∧ ← Z_p{x_i}^∧ → B (x_i ↦ p·z_i), is p-completely flat over A.

Derived p-completion and p-complete flatness are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1. In (1) the hypothesis is on the p-th powers x_i^p; in (2) on the x_i themselves.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 2.43 and Corollary 2.44 with proofs; pp. 26, 27.)

*Needs:* [§0.17](#layer-0-complete-regular-sequence), [§0.16](#layer-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), [§0.8](#layer-0-free-delta-ring), [§0.12](#layer-0-animated-delta-rings), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`.

For the proof, (1) Reduce modulo p: D_(y)(F_p[y]) is free over F_p[y]/(y_i^p), so D ⊗^L F_p is a free module over Kos(B ⊗^L F_p; x_i^p), which is flat over A ⊗^L F_p by hypothesis. (2) Apply Frobenius: by PD envelopes of regular sequences are δ-envelopes (Remark 2.40) the φ-pullback of B{x_i/p} is the PD envelope of (x_i), to which (1) applies after noting that φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p; then descend complete flatness along the p-completely faithfully flat Frobenius of the free δ-ring (Free δ-rings), as in the source.

**Checks.**

- A = Z_p, B = Z_p⟨x⟩: C = Z_p{x, x/p}^∧ is p-completely flat over Z_p. The hypothesis is not automatic: for B = A = Z_p the sequence (p) is not p-completely regular relative to A (Completely regular sequences relative to a base), and the corollary does not apply to B{p/p}^∧.

<a id="layer-0-prism-category"></a>

### 0.19 Complete-flat maps and their coherent category

Equip the supplied prism category with (p,I)-completely flat and completely faithfully flat morphisms, retaining derived completeness of the target as part of every use here. Prove stability under identity, composition and completed base change, and the compatibility of those operations with the underlying ring maps. The API is `Prismatic.Prism.Hom.id`, `comp`, `ext`, `IsCompletelyFlat` and `IsCompletelyFaithfullyFlat`; extensionality says that equal ring maps give equal prism morphisms. This adds the complete-flat categorical interface to the supplied prism predicates. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 3.2, p.28, and §1.2, pp.11–12.)

**Checks.**

- `prism_hom_id_toRingHom`: the underlying map of an identity is the ring identity, and it is completely faithfully flat.
- `prism_hom_map_phi`: every transition commutes with Frobenius, including after composition.
- The map Z_p→Z_p×Z_p, with ideal (p), is completely faithfully flat and retains both factors under base change; a projection Z_p×Z_p→Z_p is completely flat but not faithfully so.
- `prism_bounded_of_torsionfree_quotient`: p-torsion-free A/I is bounded; `prism_perfect_frobenius_injective` excludes a noninjective Frobenius from perfectness. These check the imported predicates used by this interface.

*Needs:* [prism morphisms, predicates and rigidity](#ps-prisms), DD.1 complete flatness, Mathlib `Module.FaithfullyFlat`.

<a id="layer-0-crystalline-prism"></a>

### 0.20 Crystalline prisms

For every p-torsion-free, p-adically complete δ-ring A, the pair (A, (p)) is a crystalline prism, and every crystalline prism is of this form. Examples: (Z_p, (p)) with φ = id; (W(k), (p)) for a perfect field (or perfect F_p-algebra) k with the Witt vector Frobenius; (Z_p⟨x⟩, (p)) with φ(x) = x^p.


([BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 3.3; Example 2.20 (1); pp. 18, 29.)

*Needs:* [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [§0.1](#layer-0-integer-delta), [§0.14](#layer-0-perfect-delta-rings), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, Mathlib `PadicInt`, Mathlib `WittVector`, Mathlib `WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Prism.crystalline`: The prism (A, (p)) of a δ-ring A in which p is a nonzerodivisor (and which is p-adically complete).
- `Prismatic.Prism.crystalline_I`: Its ideal is (p).
- `Prismatic.Prism.crystalline_isCrystalline`: It is crystalline.
- `Prismatic.Prism.padicInt`: The prism (Z_p, (p)).
- `Prismatic.Prism.witt`: The prism (W(k), (p)) of a perfect ring k of characteristic p.
- `Prismatic.Prism.padicInt_I`: The ideal of the Z_p crystalline prism is precisely (p).
- `Prismatic.Prism.witt_I`: The ideal of the W(k) crystalline prism for perfect k of characteristic p is precisely (p).

For the proof, (p) is invertible because p is a nonzerodivisor; A is derived p-complete because it is classically complete and p-torsion-free (DD.1); p ∈ (p). Conversely if (A, (p)) is a prism then (p) invertible forces p to be a nonzerodivisor, and derived p-completeness with p-torsion-freeness gives classical completeness.

**Checks.**

- `crystalline_prism_padic_phi`: The Frobenius of the prism (Z_p, (p)) is the identity.
- `crystalline_prism_padic_perfect`: The prism (Z_p, (p)) is perfect and bounded.
- `crystalline_prism_witt_phi`: The Frobenius of the prism (W(k), (p)) is the Witt vector Frobenius.
- `crystalline_prism_bar`: The reduction of (Z_p, (p)) has p = 0 and exactly p elements.

- (Z_p, (p)): δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}, a unit, so p is distinguished. (F_p, (0)) is not a prism: (0) is not invertible; (Z/p^2, (p)) is not a prism: p is a zero divisor.

<a id="layer-0-ainf-prism"></a>

### 0.21 Fontaine generator normalizations

For the supplied perfect prism of an integral perfectoid ring, record the explicit orientations needed by the comparisons. If C is a characteristic-zero perfectoid field with compatible p-power roots p^♭ of p, then ξ=p−[p^♭] generates ker θ. For the completed cyclotomic extension and ε=(1,ζ_p,ζ_(p²),…), ξ=[p]_[ε^(1/p)], while ξ̃=φ(ξ) generates ker(θ∘φ^(−1)). The comparison formulas `Prismatic.Prism.ainf_I`, `ainf_phi` and `ainf_bar_equiv` express these orientations using the supplied A_inf prism, its Witt Frobenius and θ-induced quotient isomorphism; they do not construct another perfect-prism functor. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 2.20(3), p.18, and Theorem 3.10, p.32.)

**Checks.**

- `ainf_prism_theta_teichmuller`: θ([x])=x^♯; θ(ξ)=p−p=0 in the compatible-root example.
- For the cyclotomic orientation, θ(ξ)=1+ζ_p+⋯+ζ_p^(p−1)=0, whereas θ([ε]−1)=0 has a different generator factor; retain ξ=( [ε]−1 )/( [ε^(1/p)]−1 ).
- `ainf_prism_kernel_not_p`: if p≠0 in R, (p) is not ker θ.
- In characteristic p with R perfect, A_inf=W(R), ker θ=(p), and the dictionary gives the crystalline orientation. `ainf_prism_perfect_bounded` checks boundedness against this special case.

*Needs:* [integral perfectoids, θ and its kernel](#ps-integral), [perfect prism equivalence](#ps-prisms), Mathlib `WittVector.fontaineTheta`, `WittVector.teichmuller`.

<a id="layer-0-breuil-kisin-prism"></a>

### 0.22 The Breuil–Kisin prism

Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, W = W(k), π a uniformizer of O_K and E(u) ∈ W[u] its Eisenstein minimal polynomial over W[1/p]. Then A = W[[u]] with the δ-structure extending the canonical one on W and satisfying φ(u) = u^p, and I = (E(u)), is a bounded, oriented, non-perfect prism with A/I ≅ O_K via u ↦ π. Every generator of the kernel of A → O_K is distinguished.

k perfect of characteristic p; K finite totally ramified over W[1/p]; E Eisenstein of degree e = [K : W[1/p]]. The perfect residue-field hypothesis identifies the unramified coefficient ring with W(k); the source’s shorter description omits that hypothesis.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 2.20 (4); p. 18.)

*Needs:* [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [§0.1](#layer-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence), [§0.13](#layer-0-distinguished-element), [§0.20](#layer-0-crystalline-prism), Mathlib `PowerSeries`, Mathlib `WittVector`, Mathlib `Polynomial.IsEisensteinAt`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin`: For a power-series δ-ring W[[u]] with φ(u) = u^p over a crystalline base and E ∈ W[u] Eisenstein at p: the prism (W[[u]], (E)). Require E to be monic with positive degree; Mathlib’s IsEisensteinAt alone permits E=1 and is insufficient.
- `Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_I`: Its ideal is generated by E(u).
- `Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_phi_X`: φ(u) = u^p.
- `Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_isBounded`: It is a bounded, orientable prism.
- `Prismatic.Prism.breuilKisin_bar`: For E the positive-degree monic Eisenstein minimal polynomial of the uniformizer π, W(k)[[u]]/(E) ≃ O_K via u↦π, respecting W(k). This map supplies the structure map of the Breuil–Kisin object in the absolute site.

**Proof route.** Reconstruct delta from the torsion-free lifted Frobenius; E≡u^e mod p identifies the (p,E)-topology with (p,u), and E is regular. The map u↦0 carries E to p times a unit, so u-adic unit detection makes δ(E) a unit. The quotient is O_K, hence p-torsion-free and bounded; u is outside the Frobenius image.

**Checks.**

- `breuil_kisin_not_perfect`: The Breuil–Kisin prism is not perfect: u is not in the image of φ.
- `breuil_kisin_not_crystalline`: For E = u − p over Z_p the ideal (E) is not (p).
- `breuil_kisin_linear_reduction`: For E = u − p over Z_p, the quotient Z_p[[u]]/(u − p) is Z_p via u ↦ p.

- K = Q_p, π = p: A = Z_p[[u]], E = u − p, δ(u − p) = δ(−p) + (correction) is a unit congruent to δ(−p) modulo u. K = Q_p(p^{1/2}), p odd: E = u^2 − p.

<a id="layer-0-q-de-rham-prism"></a>

### 0.23 The q-de Rham prism

A = Z_p[[q − 1]] with the δ-structure determined by φ(q) = q^p (equivalently δ(q) = 0), and I = ([p]_q), where [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1} is the p-th cyclotomic polynomial evaluated at q. Then (A, I) is a bounded, oriented, non-perfect prism with A/I = Z_p[ζ_p]. The ideal of the prism is ([p]_q), not (q − 1): (A, (q − 1)) is not a prism.


([BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 2.20 (2); Notation 16.1; Example 1.3; pp. 2, 18, 106.)

*Needs:* [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [§0.1](#layer-0-torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence), [§0.13](#layer-0-distinguished-element), [§0.14](#layer-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators), Mathlib `PowerSeries`, Mathlib `PadicInt`, Mathlib `Polynomial.cyclotomic`, Mathlib `Polynomial.cyclotomic_prime`, Mathlib `Polynomial.eval_one_cyclotomic_prime`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.qAnalog`: The q-analogue [n]_q = 1 + q + … + q^{n−1} in a ring with a chosen element q.
- `Prismatic.qAnalog_mul_sub_one`: (q − 1)·[n]_q = q^n − 1.
- `Prismatic.qAnalog_one_eq`: At q = 1, [n]_q = n.
- `Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham`: The prism (Z_p[[q − 1]], ([p]_q)).
- `Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham_I`: Its ideal is generated by [p]_q.
- `Prismatic.Prism.qDeRham_phi_q`: φ(q) = q^p.

**Proof route.** Reconstruct delta from φ(q)=q^p; [p]_q≡(q−1)^(p−1) mod p gives the required cofinal completion topology. Reduction modulo q−1 gives δ([p]_q)≡δ(p), a unit; regularity and the p-torsion-free quotient Z_p[ζ_p] prove boundedness. The ideal (q−1) fails the prism relation because (q−1,q^p−1)=(q−1) does not contain p.

**Checks.**

- `q_analog_two`: [2]_q = 1 + q.
- `q_analog_prime_cyclotomic`: In Z[X] with q = X, [p]_q is the p-th cyclotomic polynomial.
- `q_de_rham_ideal_not_q_minus_one`: In Z_p[[q − 1]] the ideals ([p]_q) and (q − 1) are different.
- `q_de_rham_p_mem`: p ∈ ([p]_q, [p]_{q^p}) in Z_p[[q − 1]].

- [p]_q evaluated at q = 1 is p; φ([p]_q) = [p]_{q^p} ≡ p modulo [p]_q. p = 2: [2]_q = 1 + q, δ(1 + q) = δ(1) + δ(q) − q = −q, a unit.

<a id="layer-0-universal-oriented-prism"></a>

### 0.24 The universal oriented prism

Let A_0 = Z_(p){d, δ(d)^{-1}} be the localization of the free δ-ring on d at the multiplicative set generated by δ(d), φ(δ(d)), φ^2(δ(d)), …; it is the initial δ-ring over Z_(p) with a distinguished element, and d is a nonzerodivisor modulo p. Let A be the (p, d)-completion of A_0 and I = (d). Then (A, I) is a bounded prism oriented by d, and it is the universal oriented prism: for every prism (B, J) with a chosen generator e of J there is a unique map of prisms A → B with d ↦ e. In A the sequence (p, d) is regular and the Frobenius of A/p is d-completely flat.

It is universal among oriented prisms, not among orientable ones. The flatness of Frobenius here is weaker than the faithful-flatness input needed for Construction 6.1. Layer 1 proves the precise Frobenius-twisted flatness used there.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 2.21; Example 3.4; pp. 18, 29.)

*Needs:* [§0.8](#layer-0-free-delta-ring), [§0.4](#layer-0-delta-localization-phi-stable), [§0.10](#layer-0-delta-radical-localization), [§0.5](#layer-0-delta-classical-completion), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [§0.14](#layer-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators).

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Prism.Oriented`: An oriented prism: a prism with a chosen generator of its ideal.
- `Prismatic.Prism.Oriented.isDistinguished`: The chosen generator is distinguished.
- `Prismatic.Prism.Oriented.generator_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: The chosen generator is a nonzerodivisor.
- `Prismatic.Prism.Oriented.isOrientable`: The underlying prism is orientable.
- `Prismatic.Prism.universalOriented`: The derived (p,d)-completion of the free δ-Z_(p)-algebra on d with all Frobenius iterates of δ(d) inverted is an oriented bounded prism; regularity makes this completion classical as well.
- `Prismatic.Prism.universalOriented_lift`: For an oriented prism (B,J,e), there is exactly one prism map from the universal oriented prism sending d to e. Its δ-ring restriction is the free lift; completeness extends it uniquely.
- `Prismatic.Prism.universalOriented_lift_generator`: The universal lift carries its chosen orientation d to the target orientation e; replacing e by a unit multiple changes the lift accordingly.

**Proof route.** Localize the free p-local delta ring at δ(d) and its Frobenius iterates, then complete at (p,d). The polynomial regular sequence remains regular after completion, giving the transversal universal prism. Every orientation maps d to a distinguished generator and inverts the designated elements; its complete target therefore gives the unique extension.

**Checks.**

- `oriented_padic`: The prism (Z_p, (p)) is oriented by p, and δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}.
- `oriented_generator_unique_up_to_unit`: Two orientations of the same prism differ by a unit.
- `oriented_not_unit`: If A is nonzero, the generator of an oriented prism is not a unit.

- The map to (Z_p, (p)) with d ↦ p, and the map to (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) with d ↦ [p]_q. There is no map from the universal oriented prism to (Z_p, (p)) sending d to p^2.

<a id="layer-0-rigidity-prism-ideal"></a>

### 0.25 The torsion criterion for extending a prism

Extend the supplied rigidity theorem by its converse criterion. If (A,I) is a prism and B is a delta-A-algebra that is derived (p,I)-complete, then (B,IB) is a prism exactly when I⊗_A B→B is injective, denoted B[I]=0. Indeed injectivity makes IB an invertible ideal and the prism relation is inherited from A; the reverse direction follows from rigidity. No boundedness of either prism is required. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 1.5, p.3, and Lemma 3.5, p.29.)

For I=(d), this is precisely absence of d-torsion. The zero ring satisfies the criterion; a nonzero derived-complete delta algebra with nonzero d-torsion fails it. Under the cyclotomic specialization q↦1, [p]_q↦p, and the resulting ideal is the crystalline ideal, fixing the direction of the imported rigidity map.

*Needs:* [rigidity and prism morphisms](#ps-prisms), DD.1 derived completeness, Mathlib `Module.Invertible`.

<a id="layer-0-prism-frobenius-ideal-principal"></a>

### 0.26 The Frobenius pullback of a prism ideal is principal

Let (A, I) be a prism. Then φ(I)A is a principal ideal and each of its generators is a distinguished element. Both φ^*I=I⊗_{A,φ}A and the ideal I^p are free A-modules of rank one.

(A, I) is a prism.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 3.6 with proof; p. 29.)

*Needs:* [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.14](#layer-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators), [§0.14](#layer-0-distinguished-factor-rigidity), [§0.14](#layer-0-distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings), [§0.14](#layer-0-perfect-delta-rings).

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Prism.exists_distinguished_generator_map`: For a prism (A,I), there exists a distinguished d∈A with φ(I)A=(d). The stronger assertion about every generator is part of the target theorem.

**Proof route.** On a distinguished local orientation write p=xd^p+yφ(d); the distinguished-factor criterion shows y is a unit, so its φ(I)-component gives a global generator. Modulo p, φ^*I≃I^p, and Jacobson descent gives the global isomorphism. Check the generator map after p-completed perfection, where distinguished elements are nonzerodivisors (BS22 Lemma 3.6, whose “Proposition 3.1” reference means Lemma 3.1).

**Checks.**

- (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)): φ(I)A = ([p]_{q^p}). For a perfect prism the lemma gives that I itself is principal.

<a id="layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness"></a>

### 0.27 Properties of bounded prisms

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (1) A is classically (p, I)-complete. (2) If M ∈ D(A) is derived (p, I)-complete and (p, I)-completely flat, then M is discrete and classically (p, I)-complete; for every n ≥ 0, M[I^n] = 0 and M/I^n M has bounded p^∞-torsion. (3) The functor B ↦ (B, IB) is an equivalence from (p, I)-completely (faithfully) flat, derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebras to (faithfully) flat maps of prisms (A, I) → (B, J). (4) There is a (p, I)-completely faithfully flat map A → B of δ-rings, the derived (p, I)-completion of an ind-Zariski localization, with IB = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d; so (A, I) → (B, (d)) is a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms.

(A, I) is bounded: A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion. In (2) and (3) derived (p, I)-completeness of M and of B is a hypothesis: the printed statement of Lemma 3.7(2)–(3) omits it, its proof uses it, and without it the statement is false.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 3.7 (Properties of bounded prisms) with proof; p. 30.)

*Needs:* [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.14](#layer-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators), [PerfectoidQuotients §0.0](#pq-delta-etale), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Proof route.** Use the invertible-ideal quotients A/I^n, whose p-torsion is bounded by dévissage from A/I, and apply DD.1’s bounded-torsion complete-flat criterion to every reduction of M. Their inverse limit is discrete, classically complete and I-torsion-free. Rigidity gives the prism assertion; completing a faithfully flat orientation cover gives local distinguished generators.

**Checks.**

- M = A: recovers (1). For the q-de Rham prism, A/[p]_q^n is p-torsion-free for all n. For a (p,f)-complete ring R with f a nonzerodivisor, bounded p^∞-torsion of R/f does not give bounded p^∞-torsion of R (A (p,f)-complete ring with bounded torsion modulo f and unbounded torsion; that ring is not claimed to be a prism).

<a id="layer-0-general-prismatic-envelope"></a>

### 0.28 General envelopes over orientable prisms

For an orientable prism (A,I=(d)), a delta-A-algebra B and any ideal J⊇IB, construct `Prism.generalEnvelope(B,J)`: a prism (C,IC) with a delta map B→C sending J into IC, initial among such maps to prisms over A. Neither the base nor the targets need be bounded. The input B and J need not be complete, flat, finitely generated or regular; the output is not asserted bounded or completely flat. `Prism.generalEnvelope.liftEquiv` identifies maps C→T over A with delta-A-maps B→T carrying J into IT, for every target prism T. The remaining API is `Prism.generalEnvelope.map`, respecting identities and composition, `Prism.generalEnvelope.orientationIndependent`, the unique isomorphism for two generators of I, and `Prism.generalEnvelope.regularComparison`, agreement with the supplied regular envelope only under all its regularity and complete-flatness hypotheses. ([K1](#ref-k1), Propositions 3.1–3.2, p.13; [Bhatt, Lecture V](https://www.math.ias.edu/~bhatt/teaching/prismatic-columbia/lecture5-prismatic-site.pdf), Lemma 5.1, p.6, has a bounded-base convention on p.1.)

Here is a construction that does not assume an animated completion is discrete. In a target T, d is injective by rigidity, and derived (p,d)-completeness says that each sequence operator Δ_f:T^N→T^N, (x_n)↦(x_n−f x_(n+1)), is bijective for f=p,d; use its inverse-coordinate operations S_(f,n). These operations are preserved by A-maps by uniqueness. Choose κ=max(ℵ_0,|A|,|B|) and λ=κ^ℵ_0, and close the image of B together with the unique d-quotients of J under ring operations, δ and every S_(f,n) for ω_1 stages: each stage has size at most λ, every countable tuple occurs at a common earlier stage, and the resulting small subring remains d-injective and complete. Take the product of representatives of all such small admissible targets, including the zero target, and perform the same closure inside that product; this gives C, and projections to a small factor give existence of its maps to arbitrary targets, while preservation of the generating operations proves uniqueness by transfinite induction. The prism relation comes from A; the argument uses choice and a larger ambient universe for the product. (The telescope and finite-generator criteria are [Stacks, Tags 091P, 091Q and 091S](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/091P), More on Algebra §93, Lemmas 93.1–93.2 and Definition 93.4, pp.261–263; the solution-set argument here supplies the indicated generality.)

**Checks.**

- `generalEnvelope_identity`: if (B,IB) is already a prism and J=IB, the result and its structure map are B and the identity.
- `generalEnvelope_unitIdeal`: J=B gives zero, since d invertible and derived d-completeness force a target to vanish.
- `generalEnvelope_regularAgreement`: for the completed free delta algebra on x and J=(d,x), agreement with the regular envelope requires checking its complete flatness and relative regularity first.
- `generalEnvelope_nonregularInput`: the ordinary free delta algebra on x,y with J=(d,x²,xy,y²) is an allowed input, without a regular presentation or prior completion; its universal map does not imply flatness.
- `generalEnvelope_unboundedIdentity`: B=A,J=I gives A even if A/I has unbounded p-power torsion. Imposing bounded output would fail this test.
- `generalEnvelope_telescopeZero`: for f=0 on Z, Δ_f is the identity and its inverse coordinates add no elements.
- `generalEnvelope_telescopeUnit`: for f=1 on Z, both constant sequences 0 and 1 have image zero, so Z fails derived completeness for the unit ideal.
- `generalEnvelope_telescopeSign`: for f=2, the constant sequence −1 solves Δ_f(x)=1; a plus sign would give −3.

*Needs:* [prism rigidity](#ps-prisms), integral delta algebra, DD.1 derived completeness and its telescope criterion, E0 products and universe conventions.

### 0.29 Regularity, envelope coordinates and torsion controls

**Regular sequences in a transversal prism.** Let (A, I) be a prism and d ∈ I a distinguished element. If (p, d) is a regular sequence in A, then for all r, s ≥ 0 with r ≠ s the sequences (p, φ^r(d)) and (φ^r(d), φ^s(d)) are regular.

(A, I) prism; d ∈ I distinguished; (p, d) regular (the prism is transversal: A/I is p-torsion-free). The proof uses that p lies in the Jacobson radical and that A is p-adically separated, both consequences of derived (p, I)-completeness with p-torsion-freeness.

**Presentation of a prismatic envelope for a rank-one element.** Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, d ∈ A a distinguished element and x ∈ A an element of rank 1 (δ(x) = 0). Then for every n ≥ 0 there are elements z_n ∈ A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)}, natural in (A, x), with φ^n(d)·φ^{n−1}(d)^p ⋯ d^{p^n}·z_n = x^{p^n}; and δ^n(x/d) lies in the subring A[z_0,…,z_n] of A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)}.

(A, I) bounded prism; d distinguished; δ(x) = 0. A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} is the derived (p, d)-completed δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining x/d.

**A (p,f)-complete ring with bounded torsion modulo f and unbounded torsion.** Let R be the (p, f)-adic completion of Z[f, x_{i,j} : i ≥ 0, 0 ≤ j ≤ i]/J_0, where J_0 is generated by the elements p·x_{i,j} − f·x_{i,j+1} (with x_{i,i+1} := 0) and by all products x_{i,j}·x_{k,l}. (The source omits the products; without them f·x_{1,1}^2 = 0 and x_{1,1}^2 ≠ 0, so f is a zero divisor and x_{1,1}^2 is (p,f)-torsion. With them R/f is the p-adic completion of Z ⊕ ⊕ (Z/p)·x_{i,j}.) Then R is classically (p, f)-complete (it is a completion), f is a nonzerodivisor of R (use the module model and the uniform filtration estimate in the proof below), all p^∞-torsion of R/f is killed by p, yet p^i·x_{i,0} = p^{i−1}·f·x_{i,1} = … = f^i·x_{i,i} ≠ 0 and p^{i+1}·x_{i,0} = f^i·p·x_{i,i} = 0, so R has unbounded p^∞-torsion. The (p, f)^∞-torsion of R is zero.

The displayed chain is the corrected one: the source prints p^i·f·x_{i,1} for its second term.

**Fpqc local surjectivity of Frobenius.** For a δ-ring A and x∈A there is a faithfully flat δ-map A→B and y∈B with φ_B(y)=x. The ring B is the pushout of Z{t}→A, t↦x, and Z{t}→Z{s}, t↦φ(s).

no p-torsion-freeness or completion of A is assumed.

**δ and prime power nilpotence.** On Z_(p), if v_p(a)=n>0 then v_p(δ(a))=n−1. In particular δ^n(p^n) is a unit. No nonzero δ-ring has p^n=0 for any n>0.

the valuation formula concerns Z_(p), while the nilpotence conclusion concerns all δ-rings.

**Joyal operations and Witt-coordinate identities.** For a δ-ring A, define δ_n(x) as the n-th Witt coordinate of the canonical δ-map w_A:A→W(A). Then δ_0(x)=x, δ_1(x)=δ(x), and φ^n(x)=∑_(i=0)^n p^iδ_i(x)^(p^(n−i)). In the free δ-ring δ_n(x) equals δ^n(x) plus a polynomial in the previous iterates. Thus the free δ-ring is also the polynomial ring on the δ_n(x).

The cofree Witt δ-ring and its canonical unit are those of Limits, colimits and Witt vectors of δ-rings; its integral construction and adjunction are proved there before the coordinate operations are used. The identity is polynomial and therefore valid with p-torsion; division by p^n is used only in the universal torsion-free ring.

**Worked torsion counterexample.** the relations give p·x_{i,j} = f·x_{i,j+1}, hence p^k·x_{i,0} = f^k·x_{i,k} for k ≤ i by induction on k, and p·x_{i,i} = f·x_{i,i+1} = 0, hence p^{i+1}·x_{i,0} = 0. R/f is the p-adic completion of Z ⊕ ⊕_{i,j} (Z/p)·x_{i,j} (square-zero), whose p-power torsion is killed by p. Nonvanishing: the ring map from R to the square-zero extension T ⊕ ε·T, T = (Z/p^{i+1})[f]/(f^{i+1}), sending x_{i,j} to ε·p^j·f^{i−j} and every other x_{k,l} to 0, respects the relations (p·p^j f^{i−j} = f·p^{j+1} f^{i−j−1}, and p·p^i = 0 in T) and is defined on the completion because T is (p, f)-adically discrete; it sends f^i·x_{i,i} to ε·p^i·f^i ≠ 0. This verification is supplied here; the source asserts the nonvanishing without proof. Put A = Z[f] and K = (p,f). The square-zero module with generators x_{i,0},…,x_{i,i} identifies with M_i = (K^i + (p^{i+1}))/(p^{i+1}) ⊂ A/(p^{i+1}), by x_{i,j} ↦ p^j f^{i−j}. To verify the presentation, reduce a relation modulo p: its first coefficient is divisible by p; subtract a multiple of p x_{i,0} − f x_{i,1}, divide by p, and induct on i. Its K-adic completion is the corresponding monomial ideal in (Z/p^{i+1})[[f]], where f is injective. The completed direct sum of the M_i injects into their product: at each finite K-adic level an element has finite support and is detected by its coordinates. Thus f remains injective in R. In each M_i the monomial description gives (K^n M_i : f) ⊂ K^{n−1} M_i for n ≥ 1, uniformly in i. Division by f therefore preserves the restricted-product convergence condition; the quotient of the completed direct sum by f is ⊕ M_i/fM_i, a direct sum of F_p-vector spaces. Together with the base summand Z_p, this proves the description of R/f and its bounded p-torsion. Since f is injective, no nonzero element is killed by a power of K.

**API.**

- `Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.Rel`: In the polynomial ring Z[f, x_{i,j}], the ideal generated by the elements p·x_{i,j} − f·x_{i,j+1} (with x_{i,j} = 0 for j > i) and by all products x_{i,j}·x_{k,l}.
- `Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.Ring`: The quotient of Z[f, x_{i,j}] by Rel: the uncompleted model of R.
- `Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.p_pow_mul_x`: p^k·x_{i,0} = f^k·x_{i,k} for k ≤ i.
- `Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.p_pow_succ_mul_x`: p^{i+1}·x_{i,0} = 0.
- `Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.Completion`: The (p,f)-adic completion of Ring, the corrected square-zero ring R.
- `Prismatic.UnboundedTorsion.f_nonzerodivisor`: Multiplication by the image of f in Completion is injective.
- `Delta.joyalDelta`: Define δ_n(x)=(w_A(x))_n, with δ_0=id and δ_1=δ.
- `Delta.joyalDelta_ghost`: φ^n(x)=∑_(i=0)^n p^iδ_i(x)^(p^(n−i)), naturally under δ-ring maps.
- `Delta.joyalDelta_free_generators`: The δ_n(x) freely generate the underlying polynomial algebra of the free δ-ring; the change from iterated δ is integral and triangular.

**Proof route.** For transversal regularity reduce modulo p and use φ^r(d)≡d^(p^r), then distinguish iterates using the distinguished relation; for the rank-one envelope iterate its delta relation and the p,d-adic recurrence. Free integral delta Frobenius is faithfully flat, so its pushout gives fpqc local Frobenius surjectivity; valuation descent proves the nilpotence control. The cofree Witt unit gives Joyal coordinates, with polynomial identities established in the universal torsion-free ring before evaluation.

([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Lemma 2.1.7 (arXiv numbering; Lemma 2.7 in the published version) with proof; p. 13.) ([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Lemma 4.9.4 (arXiv numbering; Lemma 4.89 in the published version) with proof, and the sentence before the proof; p. 72.) ([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Appendix A, Example A.4; p. 95.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Corollary 2.12, §2; p. 16.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 2.6, §2; p. 14.) ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remarks 2.13–2.14, §2.1; p. 16.)

**Checks.**

- `unbounded_torsion_order_two`: p^2·x_{1,0} = 0 in the uncompleted model.
- `unbounded_torsion_nonzero`: p·x_{1,0} ≠ 0 in the uncompleted model: the torsion is not killed by p.
- `unbounded_torsion_no_bound`: For every n there is an element killed by a power of p and not by p^n.
- `pr0_joyal_zero`: δ_0(0)=0 and δ_1(0)=0.
- `pr0_joyal_first`: δ_0(x)=x and δ_1(x)=δ(x).
- `pr0_joyal_second_not_iterate`: At p=2 in Z_(2), δ(2)=−1, δ²(2)=−1, whereas δ_2(2)=−4 from 2=2⁴+2(−1)²+4δ_2(2). Higher Witt coordinates are not iterated δ.

**Further checks and examples.**

- q-de Rham prism: ([p]_q, [p]_{q^p}) is a regular sequence in Z_p[[q−1]]; so is (p, [p]_{q^{p^r}}). In a crystalline prism d = p and (p, d) is not regular: the hypothesis excludes it.
- n = 0: d·z_0 = x. n = 1: φ(d)·d^p·z_1 = x^p. For d = p (so φ(d) = p) and x of rank one: z_1 = x^p/p^{p+1} and δ(x/p) = (φ(x/p) − (x/p)^p)/p = p^{p−1}·z_1 − z_1 ∈ A[z_0, z_1].
- i = 1: p·x_{1,0} = f·x_{1,1} ≠ 0 and p^2·x_{1,0} = f·p·x_{1,1} = 0: an element of exact p-torsion order 2. For (p,f)-complete rings, bounded p^∞-torsion of R/f is not inherited by R; R is not claimed to carry a δ-structure.
- x=p in Z_(p), the construction adjoins a Frobenius preimage without requiring one in Z_(p). This is a local surjectivity assertion, not surjectivity of φ on every δ-ring.
- p=2, δ(4)=−6 has valuation one and δ²(4)=−21 is odd. The assertion rules out nonzero rings Z/p^n, including n>1.
- The n=0 and n=1 identities recover x and δ(x). At p=2,n=2, φ²(x)=x⁴+2δ(x)²+4δ_2(x); δ_2 need not equal δ∘δ.

### Examples

At p=2 on Z, δ(a)=(a−a²)/2 gives δ(2)=−1 and δ(4)=−6. Its associated Frobenius is the identity. The product rule on 2·2 computes 4(−1)+4(−1)+2(−1)²=−6, so omitting the final pδ(x)δ(y) term is detected. The ideal (2) is Frobenius-stable but not delta-stable; its delta closure is the unit ideal. On Z_(2), 2 is distinguished and 4 is not. On the nonzero ring F₂, the identity is an ordinary Frobenius lift but there is no delta structure. These examples force both the integral division convention and the no-torsion hypothesis of reconstruction.

## Layer 1: Relative prismatic cohomology and smooth comparisons

Construct the bounded-prism site with finite jointly faithful covers, then its relative slices and structure sheaves. The Čech–Alexander model makes the Frobenius and Bockstein explicit. Smooth Hodge–Tate comparison removes the preliminary complete Tor-amplitude restriction on base change. The early de Rham comparison has its Witt torsion hypothesis; the general version is in Layer 3.

### 1.0 Bounded formal sites and restriction from the quasisyntomic basis

Prove `Prismatic.Formal.boundedSite_gluing`. On the bounded p-adic formal schemes of SF.4, affine completed fibre products and completely étale localization define the small formal étale site. A complete-derived-category-valued affine functor satisfying completely étale descent extends uniquely to these formal schemes by affine-open descent. For a formal scheme with quasisyntomic affine charts, restriction of a quasisyntomic sheaf is computed by the right Kan extension from the QRSP basis of DD.5, and this restriction agrees on overlaps with affine-open descent. Prove `Prismatic.Formal.qsyn_rightKan`: on a quasisyntomic affine Spf B the right Kan limit over its QRSP objects is its original value, with all Čech, coefficient and filtered compatibilities. Arbitrary bounded B is allowed for affine animated prismatic cohomology and its étale sheafification; the QRSP-basis assertion has the additional quasisyntomic hypothesis. ([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Definitions 4.10, 4.20, Lemmas 4.28–4.30, pp.21–25, Remark 10.4, §10; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 7.4.1 and Proposition 7.4.7, pp.177–179.)

*Needs:* `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/formal-spectrum`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/formal-scheme`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5` (quasisyntomic sites, QRSP unfolding, formal étale realization), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`.

Use the underlying formal carriers of SF.4. Bounded p-power torsion identifies the ordinary affine completion with derived completion where the morphism is completely flat. For an étale chart, the Jacobian lifting property gives unique compatible étale lifts through B/p^n; their limit is completely étale. A finite jointly covering chart family is completely faithfully flat, and its completed Čech nerve computes descent, degreewise modulo p^n and then by inverse limit. This proves restriction and gluing using an affine hypercover. For the quasisyntomic statement apply DD.5's QRSP-basis equivalence on every such chart. Two root covers have a common completed tensor-product refinement; unfolding identifies their totalizations. The affine-open and QRSP limits commute, so the resulting restriction agrees on overlaps and retains filtered and coefficient maps. This establishes the bridge between the two existing suppliers without imposing the QRSP-basis claim on a non-quasisyntomic ring.

**Checks.** On Spf B the identity affine chart recovers F(B). For B=O_C⟨x⟩ the compatible-root Čech nerve computes the same value as formal restriction. A disjoint union of two affine charts gives a product, including the empty formal scheme with terminal value. A single proper principal open is not a cover of Spf B; its value cannot replace the chart limit. A ring with unbounded p-power torsion does not qualify as a bounded chart.
