### 1.1 The site of all bounded prisms and its structure sheaves

Let Prism_bdd be the category of bounded prisms (B,J) and maps of prisms. A map (B,J) → (C,JC) is a flat cover when C is (p,J)-completely faithfully flat over B. (1) The opposite category Prism_bdd^op, with the flat topology: the Grothendieck topology generated by the finite families {(B,J) -> (C_s,JC_s)}_{s in S} of maps of bounded prisms for which B -> prod_s C_s is (p,J)-completely faithfully flat (Bhatt-Lurie Remarks 4.1.2 and 4.4.28; S may be empty, covering the zero prism; one flat cover is the case |S|=1), is a site: isomorphisms are covers, covers compose, and a cover (A,I) → (B,IB) has a pushout along every map (A,I) → (C,IC) of bounded prisms, namely (D,ID) with D the derived (p,I)-completion of B ⊗^L_A C, and (C,IC) → (D,ID) is again a flat cover. (2) The presheaves O : (B,J) ↦ B and Ō : (B,J) ↦ B/J are sheaves. (3) For a flat cover (A,I) → (B,IB) with Čech nerve (B^•,IB^•) in bounded prisms (B^n is the derived (p,I)-completion of the (n+1)-fold derived tensor power of B over A, and is discrete), the augmented cosimplicial objects A → B^• and A/I → B^•/IB^• are limit diagrams in D(A); so the Čech complex of O (and of Ō) for every flat cover is exact in positive degrees, and H^i((A,I),O) = H^i((A,I),Ō) = 0 for i > 0 on every object.

Every object is a bounded prism: A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion. Without boundedness the completed pushout need not be discrete, and the statement is not made. Complete (faithful) flatness is taken in the sense of Bhatt–Scholze §1.2: M ⊗^L_A N is concentrated in degree 0 for every (p,I)-torsion module N (and M ⊗^L_A A/(p,I) is faithfully flat over A/(p,I)). Covers are in addition derived (p,I)-complete, which is automatic for prisms. Variance: morphisms of the site go opposite to ring maps; the final object of a slice (∗/A)_Δ is (A,I). Set theory: the category of all bounded prisms is large; a cut-off cardinal κ is fixed as in Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.2, and no statement depends on κ.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Corollary 3.12 and its proof; p. 33; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Corollary 3.12, proof, second paragraph; p. 33; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Remark 3.1.2 and Proposition 3.1.3; p. 16.)

*Needs:* [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness), [§0.9](#layer-0-delta-ring-category), [§0.12](#layer-0-animated-delta-rings), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism`: The type of bounded prisms (B,J), a category in which a morphism (C,K) → (B,J) is a map of prisms (B,J) → (C,K); so it is the site category Prism_bdd^op.
- `Prismatic.Site.IsFlatCover`: A map of prisms f : (B,J) → (C,JC) is a flat cover iff C is (p,J)-completely faithfully flat over B; in particular B/(p,J) → C/(p,J) is faithfully flat.
- `Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.flatTopology`: The Grothendieck topology on Prism_bdd^op generated by the finite families {(B,J) → (C_s,JC_s)} with B → ∏_s C_s (p,J)-completely faithfully flat; every flat cover generates a covering sieve, the projections of a finite product of bounded prisms generate a covering sieve, and the empty sieve covers the zero prism.
- `Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.pushout`: For a flat cover (A,I) → (B,IB) and a map (A,I) → (C,IC), the bounded prism (D,ID), D = (B ⊗^L_A C)^∧, the pushout in bounded prisms; (C,IC) → (D,ID) is a flat cover.
- `Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.structurePresheaf`: O : (B,J) ↦ B, a presheaf of commutative rings on the site.
- `Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.reducedStructurePresheaf`: Ō : (B,J) ↦ B/J, a presheaf of commutative rings on the site, with the reduction map O → Ō.
- `Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.structurePresheaf_isSheaf`: O and Ō are sheaves for the flat topology.
- `Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.cechComplex`: For a map f : (A,I) → (B,IB) of bounded prisms, the Čech complex B → B^1 → B^2 → … of A-modules, B^n the completed (n+1)-fold tensor power.
- `Prismatic.Site.BoundedPrism.cechComplex_exact`: If f is a flat cover the Čech complex is exact in positive degrees and its H^0 is A; the same holds after − ⊗_A A/I.

**Proof route.** Rigidity reduces pushouts along covers to completed derived tensors; DD.1 complete faithful flatness and the bounded-prism discreteness criterion make these bounded prisms. Koszul reductions of their Čech nerves are limit diagrams by complete-flat descent, and taking the completion limit gives A≃Tot B^•. Perfect base change by A/I gives the reduced assertion; Cartan’s Čech acyclicity criterion then gives higher-cohomology vanishing on every object.

**Checks.**

- `pr1_structure_presheaf_obj`: O(B,J) = B and Ō(B,J) = B/J for every bounded prism (B,J).
- `pr1_flat_cover_id`: The identity of a bounded prism is a flat cover, and the Čech complex of the identity cover has H^0 = B and no higher cohomology.
- `pr1_flat_cover_base_change`: For a flat cover (A,I) → (B,IB) and any map (A,I) → (C,IC) of bounded prisms, the projection from the pushout (C,IC) → (D,ID) is a flat cover.
- `pr1_non_flat_not_cover`: The map of crystalline prisms (Z_p⟨x⟩,(p)) → (Z_p,(p)), x ↦ 0 (with φ(x) = x^p), is not a flat cover, because F_p[x] → F_p is not flat; in general a map of bounded prisms whose reduction modulo (p,J) is not flat is not a cover.
- `pr1_product_projection_family_covers`: For two nonzero bounded prisms, the two projection maps from their product are jointly completely faithfully flat, so their arrows generate a covering sieve. Neither projection by itself is faithfully flat; a topology defined by a single cover in each covering sieve fails this test.
- `pr1_empty_cover_zero_prism`: The empty family covers the zero prism, hence its empty sieve is covering. Every sheaf of rings takes the zero prism to the one-element ring.

- (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) and the cover Z_p → W(F̄_p), the Čech complex W(F̄_p) → W(F̄_p ⊗ F̄_p) → … is exact in positive degrees with H^0 = Z_p. The variance of the opposite category and the explicit structure maps of O and Ō are checked on a composite of two covers. Ordinary site cohomology of a singular X is not identified here with the derived theory of Layer 2.

<a id="layer-1-relative-prismatic-site"></a>

### 1.2 The relative prismatic site (X/A)_Δ

Fix a bounded prism (A,I) and a p-adic formal scheme X over Spf(A/I). The prismatic site (X/A)_Δ has as objects the triples (B, g, f): a bounded prism (B,IB) with a map of prisms g : (A,I) → (B,IB), and a map f : Spf(B/IB) → X over Spf(A/I). A morphism (C,g',f') → (B,g,f) is a map of prisms (B,IB) → (C,IC) under (A,I) whose reduction Spf(C/IC) → Spf(B/IB) commutes with the maps to X. It is a flat cover when (B,IB) → (C,IC) is a faithfully flat map of prisms. The topology is the flat topology generated by the finite families {(B,g,f) ← (C_s,g_s,f_s)} with B → ∏_s C_s (p,I)-completely faithfully flat (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.1.2). The structure sheaf O_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B is a sheaf of δ-A-algebras; the reduced structure sheaf Ō_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B/IB is a sheaf of O(X)-algebras, and Ō_Δ = O_Δ ⊗_A A/I. For X = Spf(R) one writes (R/A)_Δ, with objects (B → B/IB ← R). Equivalently, with (∗/A)_Δ the slice of the site of all bounded prisms over (A,I) and h_X the presheaf (B,IB) ↦ Hom_{A/I}(Spf(B/IB), X) on it, h_X is a sheaf and (X/A)_Δ is the category of pairs ((B,IB), η ∈ h_X(B,IB)) with the induced topology, so Shv((X/A)_Δ) = Shv((∗/A)_Δ)_{/h_X}. A map X → Y of p-adic formal schemes over A/I induces h_X → h_Y and hence a morphism of topoi Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv((Y/A)_Δ).

(A,I) is a bounded prism; formal schemes over A/I carry the p-adic topology. The definition is made for every p-adic formal scheme X over A/I; the comparison theorems of this layer assume X smooth over A/I (Remark 4.2), and for general X the cohomology of this site is not the derived theory of Layer 2. By rigidity (PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2) the prism ideal of every object is IB, so only B, g and f are data. In the affine case the algebraic language of Notation 4.16 is used: an object mapping to every other object of (R/A)_Δ, viewed as rings, is called weakly initial (it is weakly final in the site). Use the formal spectrum and R=A/I in the base case of Notation 4.16.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 4.1; p. 36; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 4.3; p. 37; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Definition 3.1.1; p. 16.)

*Needs:* [§1.1](#layer-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.over`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism`: An object of (R/A)_Δ: a bounded prism (B,J), a map of prisms g : (A,I) → (B,J) and a ring map R → B/J compatible with A/I → B/J; morphisms are taken in the site direction (ring maps go backwards).
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.ideal_eq_map`: For every object, J = IB (rigidity of the prism ideal).
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.flatTopology`: The Grothendieck topology on (R/A)_Δ generated by flat covers; a morphism whose underlying map of prisms is a flat cover generates a covering sieve.
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.structureSheaf`: O_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B as a presheaf of commutative rings, with O_Δ(B) an A-algebra through g.
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.reducedStructureSheaf`: Ō_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B/IB as a presheaf of commutative rings, with Ō_Δ(B) an R-algebra through f.
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.structureSheaf_isSheaf`: O_Δ and Ō_Δ are sheaves for the flat topology.
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.forget`: The category-of-elements projection (R/A)_Δ→(∗/A)_Δ forgets only the map f:R→B/IB and retains the base-prism map g:(A,I)→(B,IB). Its composite with (∗/A)_Δ→Prism_bdd^op also forgets g. Both preserve covering families.
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.restrict`: For an A/I-algebra map R → S, the functor (S/A)_Δ → (R/A)_Δ, (B, S → B/IB) ↦ (B, R → S → B/IB); it preserves covers and commutes with O_Δ and Ō_Δ.
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.base`: For R = A/I, the object (A, id, id) of ((A/I)/A)_Δ; it is final in the site (initial in the algebraic language).

**Proof route.** Pushouts and sheaves are inherited from bounded prisms, while SF.4 completely faithfully flat descent makes the formal-point presheaf h_X a sheaf. Its category of elements is the relative site, so its sheaf topos is the slice over h_X. Composition of formal maps gives the indicated functoriality and affine ring-map direction.

**Checks.**

- `pr1_relative_site_base_terminal`: For R = A/I the object (A, id, id) is a final object of the site ((A/I)/A)_Δ.
- `pr1_relative_site_sheaf_obj`: O_Δ(B,g,f) = B and Ō_Δ(B,g,f) = B/IB.
- `pr1_relative_site_ideal_rigid`: A δ-A-algebra B with an ideal J strictly containing IB such that (B,J) is a prism receiving a map of prisms from (A,I) does not exist: for every map of prisms (A,I) → (B,J) one has J = IB.
- `pr1_relative_site_restrict_id`: Restriction along the identity R → R is the identity functor of (R/A)_Δ, and restriction is compatible with the forgetful functors to Prism_bdd^op.

- X = Spf(A/I) the site is the slice (∗/A)_Δ of all bounded prisms over (A,I), with final object (A,I). For a perfect prism (A,I) and X = Spf(A/I⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) the object given by the perfect prism of the perfectoid ring A/I⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ lies in the site. A triple with prism ideal J ≠ IB does not occur, by rigidity.

<a id="layer-1-prismatic-to-etale-morphism"></a>

### 1.3 The morphism from the prismatic topos to the étale topos

Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I and let fSch_{/X} be the category of p-adic formal schemes with an adic map to X, with the étale topology. The functor μ : (X/A)_Δ → fSch_{/X}, (B,g,f) ↦ (Spf(B/IB) → X), is cocontinuous. It therefore induces a morphism of topoi μ_X : Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv(fSch_{/X}); composing with the restriction Shv(fSch_{/X}) → Shv(X_ét) gives ν_X : Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv(X_ét). For an étale map U → X the site (U/A)_Δ is the slice of (X/A)_Δ over U, restriction to it preserves sheaves, and for every sheaf F on (X/A)_Δ one has (ν_* F)(U → X) = H^0((U/A)_Δ, F|_{(U/A)_Δ}); for a sheaf of abelian groups, R^iν_*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^i((U/A)_Δ, F).

X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I (the construction only uses that X is a p-adic formal scheme; smoothness is the standing hypothesis of BS22 §4.1). The étale site of a p-adic formal scheme is that of its reduction modulo p; it is required from SF.2. μ is cocontinuous, not continuous: only the pushforward ν_* and its derived functors are used.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.4; p. 37; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.4; p. 37.)

*Needs:* [§1.2](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-site), [§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness), [PerfectoidQuotients §0.0](#pq-delta-etale), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCocontinuous`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous`, Mathlib `Algebra.Etale`.

**Proof route.** Lift each étale quotient cover uniquely to a completely étale delta algebra by PerfectoidQuotients §0.0; bounded-prism complete flatness makes these covering prism objects. Thus the functor is cocontinuous and its right Kan extension is the indicated pushforward (Stacks 00XO). Over étale U→X the site is the slice h_U, so evaluation and sheafification give the stated R^iν_* formula.

**Checks.**

- X = Spf(R) and a p-completely étale R → S, (ν_*O_Δ)(Spf S) = H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ). For U = X the formula gives ν_*F(X) = H^0((X/A)_Δ, F), the global sections. The lift of a Zariski cover Spf(R_f) of Spf(B/IB) is the (p,I)-completed localisation of B at a lift of f, with its unique δ-structure.

<a id="layer-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology"></a>

### 1.4 Relative prismatic cohomology Δ_{X/A}

For a bounded prism (A,I) and a smooth p-adic formal scheme X over A/I put Δ_{X/A} := Rν_*O_Δ ∈ D(X_ét, A) and RΓ_Δ(X/A) := RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) = RΓ(X_ét, Δ_{X/A}) ∈ D(A). For a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R put Δ_{R/A} := RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) = RΓ(Spf(R), Δ_{Spf(R)/A}) ∈ D(A). These are commutative algebra objects (E_∞-A-algebras), derived (p,I)-complete, concentrated in cohomological degrees ≥ 0, and equipped with a φ_A-semilinear endomorphism ([§1.9](#layer-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology)). Functoriality: a map X → Y over A/I gives Δ_{Y/A} → Rf_*Δ_{X/A}; a map of bounded prisms (A,I) → (B,IB) with a compatible map of formal schemes gives a map from Δ_{X/A} to the restriction of scalars of Δ_{X'/B}; every object (B,g,f) of (R/A)_Δ gives an evaluation map Δ_{R/A} → B of E_∞-A-algebras, and Δ_{R/A} is the limit of O_Δ over a Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object ([§1.8](#layer-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology)).

(A,I) is a bounded prism. X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I; R is a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra: R is derived p-complete and R ⊗^L_{A/I} (A/I)/p is a smooth (A/I)/p-algebra in degree 0. For other X the same formula defines site cohomology, which this layer uses only for p-completely syntomic algebras ([§1.15](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison-syntomic), [§1.23](#layer-1-p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic)). The commutative algebra structure is in the derived ∞-category; in a 1-categorical derived category only the commutative ring structure on cohomology and the cosimplicial ring models are visible. Derived (p,I)-completeness follows because Δ_{R/A} is a limit of the (p,I)-complete rings B.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.9, first paragraph, and Notation 4.16; pp. 39, 41; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8, opening; p. 4; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Definition 3.1.5; p. 16.)

*Needs:* [§1.2](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-site), [§1.3](#layer-1-prismatic-to-etale-morphism), [§1.1](#layer-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, Mathlib `DerivedCategory`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Site.cohomologyEval`: For an object (B,g,f) of (R/A)_Δ, the evaluation map Δ_{R/A} → B in D(A) (B viewed as an A-module through g); it is natural in the object.
- `Prismatic.Site.cohomologyUnit`: The unit A → Δ_{R/A} of the algebra structure, as a map A[0] → Δ_{R/A} in D(A).
- `Prismatic.Site.cohomologyMap`: For a map R → S of A/I-algebras, the map Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A} in D(A); cohomologyMap_id and cohomologyMap_comp express functoriality.
- `Prismatic.Site.cohomologyMap_id`: The map induced by the identity of R is the identity of Δ_{R/A}.
- `Prismatic.Site.cohomologyMap_comp`: The map induced by a composite R → S → T is the composite of the induced maps.
- `Prismatic.Site.cohomologyBaseChangeMap`: For a map of bounded prisms f : (A,I) → (B,IB), a B/IB-algebra R′ and a compatible ring map R → R′, the map Δ_{R/A} → f_*Δ_{R′/B} in D(A).
- `Prismatic.Site.cohomology_isZero_of_neg`: H^i(Δ_{R/A}) = 0 for i < 0 when R is p-completely smooth over A/I.
- `Prismatic.Site.cohomologyCup`: The derived tensor product Δ_(R/A)⊗^L_AΔ_(R/A)→Δ_(R/A), with the unit A→Δ_(R/A), gives a commutative algebra object; evaluation and maps in R respect multiplication and the unit. Hodge–Tate reduction carries this to its cup product.

**Proof route.** Apply enhanced derived pushforward/global sections to the structure sheaf; Leray gives the displayed equality and sheaf cohomology is coconnective. Acyclicity on prism objects and RHom(A[1/f],B)=0 for f∈(p,I) prove derived completeness. Slice functoriality gives pullbacks/evaluations; the sheaf Frobenius supplies the semilinear endomorphism.

**Checks.**

- `pr1_cohomology_base`: For R = A/I the unit A → Δ_{(A/I)/A} is an isomorphism.
- `pr1_cohomology_unit_natural`: For a map R → S of A/I-algebras, the composite of the unit A → Δ_{R/A} with Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A} is the unit of Δ_{S/A}.
- `pr1_cohomology_base_degrees`: For R = A/I, H^i(Δ_{(A/I)/A}) = 0 for every i ≠ 0.
- `pr1_cohomology_not_discrete`: If the p-completed module Ω̂^1_{R/(A/I)} ≠ 0 for a p-completely smooth R (for instance R = A/I⟨X⟩), then Δ_{R/A} is not concentrated in degree 0: H^1(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) ≠ 0. So Δ_{R/A} is not the value of O_Δ on any single object.

- Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A, with the identity Frobenius-semilinear structure φ_A. For R = A/I⟨X⟩ the complex Δ_{R/A} is not concentrated in degree 0: H^1(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) ≅ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}{−1} ≠ 0. For a crystalline prism (A,(p)) and R smooth over A/p, φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A) ([§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison)).

<a id="layer-1-hodge-tate-cohomology"></a>

### 1.5 Hodge–Tate cohomology Δ̄_{X/A} and Breuil–Kisin twists of A/I-modules

For (A,I) bounded and X smooth over A/I put Δ̄_{X/A} := Rν_*Ō_Δ ∈ D(X_ét, O_X), a commutative algebra object with structure map O_X → Δ̄_{X/A}, and for a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R put Δ̄_{R/A} := RΓ((R/A)_Δ, Ō_Δ) ∈ D(R). Then Δ̄_{X/A} ≃ Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I and Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I. For an A/I-module M and i ∈ Z put M{i} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗i}, where I/I² is an invertible A/I-module and negative powers are powers of the dual; for i ≥ 0, M{i} = M ⊗_{A/I} I^i/I^{i+1}. A generator d of I identifies M{i} with M through d^i. For every i ≥ 0 there is a distinguished triangle Δ̄_{X/A}{i+1} → Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+2} → Δ̄_{X/A}{i}.

(A,I) is a bounded prism, X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. The twist M{i} of this layer is the twist of A/I-modules of Bhatt–Scholze Construction 4.9. The Breuil–Kisin twists A{n} of the prism itself, with A{1}/I = I/I², belong to [Breuil–Kisin twists A{n} of a prism](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist) and are not used here. The Hodge–Tate comparison carries the twist {−i} on Ω^i and no Frobenius twist.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.9, first paragraph; p. 39; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Definition 3.1.5; p. 16.)

*Needs:* [§1.4](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology), [§1.2](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-site), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), Mathlib `Ideal.Cotangent`, Mathlib `TensorPower`, Mathlib `DerivedCategory`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.Twist`: For i ≥ 0 the invertible R-module R{i} = R ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗i}; M{i} = M ⊗_R R{i} and M{−i} = M ⊗_R Hom_R(R{i}, R).
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistZero`: R{0} ≅ R.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistAdd`: R{i+j} ≅ R{i} ⊗_R R{j}.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistOfOrientation`: A generator d of I gives an isomorphism R{i} ≅ R, the class of d^{⊗i} going to 1.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.reduction`: The reduction map Δ_{R/A} → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(A) (Δ̄ viewed as an A-complex through A → A/I → R).
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.structureMap`: The structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}, as a map R[0] → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(R).
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.cohomologyMap`: For a map R → S of A/I-algebras, the map Δ̄_{R/A} → Δ̄_{S/A} over R (the target restricted to R).

**Proof route.** Rigidity and Cartier regularity give B/IB=B⊗^L_AA/I on every object; A/I is perfect, so this base change commutes with derived sections. Apply Δ⊗^L_A− to the successive invertible-ideal quotient sequences for the triangle. Tensor powers of I/I², including negative ones, give the intrinsic twists.

**Checks.**

- `pr1_twist_zero`: R{0} = R.
- `pr1_twist_oriented`: If I = (d) then R{i} is free of rank one over R for every i ≥ 0, with basis the class of d^{⊗i}.
- `pr1_hodge_tate_base`: For R = A/I the structure map A/I → Δ̄_{(A/I)/A} is an isomorphism.
- `pr1_hodge_tate_not_discrete`: If the p-completed module Ω̂^1_{R/(A/I)} ≠ 0 for a p-completely smooth R then H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}) ≠ 0; so Δ̄_{R/A} is not R[0], the reduction of the structure sheaf of a lift.

- Δ̄_{(A/I)/A} = A/I. For an oriented prism (A,(d)) every twist M{i} is identified with M by d^i, and the triangle for i = 0 is the reduction of Δ →d Δ modulo d². For the q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)), I/I² is free on the class of [p]_q.

<a id="layer-1-change-of-topology"></a>

### 1.6 Flat, étale, Nisnevich and Zariski topologies compute the same cohomology

On the category underlying (X/A)_Δ consider the topologies whose covers are the maps of prisms (B,IB) → (C,IC) that are (p,I)-completely étale covers, Nisnevich covers or Zariski covers. There are morphisms of topoi Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,ét}) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,Nis}) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,Zar}), and the derived pushforward along each of them carries O_Δ to O_Δ and Ō_Δ to Ō_Δ. Hence RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) and RΓ((X/A)_Δ, Ō_Δ) may be computed in any of the four topologies. The same holds for coefficients in a crystal in (p,I)-complete complexes, that is an assignment (B,g,f) ↦ M(B) ∈ D_{(p,I)-comp}(B) compatible with completed base change.

(A,I) is bounded and X is a p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Zariski, Nisnevich and étale covers of Spf(B) lift uniquely to (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebras, so each of these topologies is coarser than the flat topology. Only the two structure sheaves and crystals are compared; arbitrary sheaves on the four sites have different cohomology.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 4.5; p. 37.)

*Needs:* [§1.1](#layer-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf), [§1.2](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-site), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Proof route.** Flat acyclicity on every prism makes the higher direct images to each coarser topology vanish, giving the same structure-sheaf cohomology. For crystals replace ring acyclicity by DD.1 descent of complete module categories. All comparison maps are induced by the continuous identity site functors.

**Checks.**

- R = A/I the cohomology of O_Δ in the Zariski topology of ((A/I)/A)_Δ is A in degree 0. The étale-topology version is the one used when a statement is checked on an étale chart of X.

<a id="layer-1-cech-alexander-complex"></a>

### 1.7 Weakly initial objects and Čech–Alexander complexes

Extend the supplied smooth affine oriented Čech construction to arbitrary bounded base prisms, with coherent changes of presentation, and to the stated syntomic presentations. Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. A presentation is a surjection B_0 → R of A-algebras with B_0 the (p,I)-completion of a polynomial A-algebra A[x_s : s ∈ S]. Put B := Free_{δ,A}(B_0)^∧, the (p,I)-completed free δ-A-algebra on B_0; J_0 := ker(B_0 → R); R′ := (B/J_0B)^∧ (p-adic completion), a p-completely ind-smooth A/I-algebra; and C := B{J/I}^∧, the prismatic envelope over (A,I) of the δ-pair (B, J), J = ker(B → R′). Then (C → C/IC ← R) is an object of (R/A)_Δ, C is (p,I)-completely flat over A, and the object is weakly initial: it admits a map to every object of (R/A)_Δ (in the algebraic language). The construction is functorial in the presentation and carries completed tensor products of presentations over A to coproducts in (R/A)_Δ (algebraic language; products in the site). The Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object of the presentation is (C^• → C^•/IC^• ← R), obtained by applying the construction to the (p,I)-completed Čech nerve B_0^• of A → B_0 with its surjections B_0^n → R; it is the Čech nerve of (C^0 → C^0/IC^0 ← R), and C^n is the envelope of the completed (n+1)-fold tensor power of B over A along the kernel of the map to R′-type quotients. Taking B_0 = A[x_r : r ∈ R]^∧ with x_r ↦ r gives a strictly functorial cosimplicial δ-A-algebra C^•_R and cochain complex C^•((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ); this functorial choice does not commute with base change in the prism. For R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ the choice B_0 = A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ gives a cosimplicial δ-A-algebra that commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms.

(A,I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. The same construction applies verbatim to a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra, because the hypothesis of the envelope theorem still holds (Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.8). Proposition 3.13 is stated for an ideal that is Zariski-locally (I, x_1,…,x_r) with a finite sequence completely regular relative to A. For a presentation with finitely many variables this is Example 3.14. For infinitely many variables (in particular the functorial choice S = R) the ideal J is a filtered union of such ideals, and the envelope exists and is completely flat as the completed filtered colimit of the envelopes; this step is not in the printed text and is required in the infinite-variable construction. Derived and classical (p,I)-completions of B_0, B and of the tensor powers agree because A is bounded (Lemma 3.7).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.17; p. 41; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.18 and Remark 4.19; pp. 42, 43; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Remark 3.1.8 (2); p. 17.)

*Needs:* [§1.2](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-site), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.8](#layer-0-free-delta-ring), [§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness), [§0.9](#layer-0-delta-ring-category), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, Mathlib `MvPolynomial`, Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Site.weaklyInitial`: For a family g : S → R whose associated map A[x_s]^∧ → R is surjective, the object (C → C/IC ← R) of (R/A)_Δ with C the prismatic envelope described above.
- `Prismatic.Site.weaklyInitial_hom_nonempty`: Every object of (R/A)_Δ receives a map from the weakly initial object in the algebraic language: for every object X there is a morphism X → weaklyInitial in the site.
- `Prismatic.Site.weaklyInitial_flat`: The ring C is (p,I)-completely flat over A; in particular C/(p,I) is flat over A/(p,I).
- `Prismatic.Site.cechAlexander`: The cosimplicial commutative ring C^• of a presentation; C^0 is the ring of the weakly initial object and C^n the ring of its (n+1)-fold self-coproduct.
- `Prismatic.Site.cechAlexander_obj_zero`: C^0 is the ring underlying weaklyInitial.
- `Prismatic.Site.cechAlexanderComplex`: The cochain complex of A-modules associated with C^• (alternating sums of cofaces), concentrated in degrees ≥ 0.
- `Prismatic.Site.cechAlexander_baseChange`: For a map of bounded prisms (A,I) → (A′,IA′) and the base-changed presentation of R′ = R ⊗̂_A A′, the comparison map of cosimplicial rings C^• → C′^•; its termwise (p,I)-completed linearisation C^• ⊗̂_A A′ → C′^• is an isomorphism.

For an oriented affine chart use the supplied Čech–Alexander construction, and for a syntomic chart choose a regular presentation and its envelope. Coproduct presentations give common refinements and coherent transition maps; descent along orientation covers gives the nonorientable case. For an infinite presentation take completed filtered unions of finite subsets containing a finite set of generators on each finitely presented smooth chart, retaining the relations and then using the regular-envelope base-change interface.

**Checks.**

- `pr1_cech_alexander_base`: For R = A/I and the empty family of variables the weakly initial object is the final object (A, id, id) of the site, and C^• is constant with value A.
- `pr1_cech_alexander_affine_line`: For R = A/I⟨X⟩ with the presentation A⟨X⟩ → R: C^0 = A{X}^∧ is the completed free δ-A-algebra on one generator, so maps of prisms over (A,I) from (C^0,IC^0) to a bounded prism (B,IB) over (A,I) correspond bijectively to elements of B; and C^1 = A{X,Y}{(X−Y)/I}^∧.
- `pr1_weakly_initial_not_initial`: If Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} ≠ 0 the two coface maps C^0 ⇉ C^1 are different; so the weakly initial object is not initial and Δ_{R/A} ≠ C^0.

- R = A/I and the empty set of variables, C^• is the constant cosimplicial ring A. For R = A/I⟨X⟩ and B_0 = A⟨X⟩: C^0 = A{X}^∧ and C^1 = A{X,Y}{(X−Y)/I}^∧. For a crystalline prism the same recipe with PD envelopes in place of prismatic envelopes computes crystalline cohomology, and the two are related by [§0.16](#layer-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope).

<a id="layer-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology"></a>

### 1.8 Čech–Alexander complexes compute prismatic cohomology; independence of the presentation

For the preceding nonoriented and syntomic extension, prove the following presentation independence and computation; its smooth affine oriented restriction is supplied. Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and C^• the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of a presentation B_0 → R. Then the natural maps Δ_{R/A} → lim_Δ C^• and Δ̄_{R/A} → lim_Δ C^•/IC^• are isomorphisms in D(A) (of E_∞-A-algebras), so Δ_{R/A} is computed by the cochain complex of C^• and Δ̄_{R/A} by that of C^•/IC^•. For two presentations B_0 → R and B_0′ → R the presentation B_0 ⊗̂_A B_0′ → R receives maps from both, and the induced maps of cosimplicial rings are compatible with the identifications with Δ_{R/A}; hence the isomorphism class and the comparison isomorphisms do not depend on the presentation (the category of presentations is sifted). In particular the strictly functorial complex C^•((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) represents the functor R ↦ Δ_{R/A}.

(A,I) bounded; R p-completely smooth over A/I (or p-completely syntomic, with the same proof). The statement uses the general fact: for a topos 𝒳, an abelian sheaf F and a weakly final object X_0 with Čech nerve X_0^•, RΓ(𝒳,F) ≃ R lim RΓ(X_0^•,F); if F is acyclic on each X_0^n this is the complex F(X_0^•) (Bhatt–Scholze, footnote to Construction 4.18).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.18 and its footnote; p. 42; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 5.2, proof (the same argument on the crystalline side); p. 45.)

*Needs:* [§1.7](#layer-1-cech-alexander-complex), [§1.1](#layer-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf), [§1.4](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

The supplied oriented affine computation identifies each chart complex with site sections. The category of common coproduct refinements gives comparison maps with their higher coherence, and complete faithfully flat descent glues these equivalences independently of the orientation or syntomic presentation. Reduction by the invertible ideal is perfect base change, so the same argument applies to the Hodge–Tate reduction.

**Checks.**

- R = A/I the theorem gives Δ_{R/A} = A. Two presentations of A/I⟨X⟩, by A⟨X⟩ and by A⟨X,Y⟩ with Y ↦ 0, give quasi-isomorphic complexes through the presentation A⟨X,Y,X′⟩. H^0(Δ_{R/A}) is the equaliser of the two coface maps C^0 ⇉ C^1.

<a id="layer-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology"></a>

### 1.9 The Frobenius of prismatic cohomology

The structure sheaf O_Δ of (X/A)_Δ is a sheaf of δ-A-algebras: on each object (B,g,f) the ring B carries its δ-structure, with Frobenius lift φ_B(x) = x^p + pδ(x), and maps of prisms commute with δ. Hence φ : O_Δ → O_Δ is an endomorphism of sheaves of rings which is φ_A-semilinear, that is A-linear as a map O_Δ → φ_{A,*}O_Δ. It induces φ_X : Δ_{X/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) and φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A} in D(A), maps of commutative algebra objects, natural in X (or R) and compatible with base change of the prism. By adjunction φ_R is the same as its linearisation φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, where φ_A^* = − ⊗^L_{A,φ_A} A (derived (p,I)-completed where stated). On a Čech–Alexander model, φ_R is induced by the termwise Frobenius lifts of the cosimplicial δ-ring C^•.

(A,I) bounded prism, X a p-adic formal scheme over A/I (smooth where comparison theorems are used). φ_A need not be flat or an isomorphism; φ_A^* is a derived functor and is not assumed to commute with totalisations unless proved (Theorem 5.2, proof). φ carries I into φ(I)A, which is contained in I only for crystalline prisms; so in general Ō_Δ has no induced endomorphism (for I = (p) it has the Frobenius); reduction modulo I after φ gives the maps used in the de Rham comparison.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8, opening; p. 4; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Definition 3.1.5; p. 16.)

*Needs:* [§1.4](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology), [§1.2](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-site), [§1.8](#layer-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [§0.1](#layer-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary), [§0.1](#layer-0-associated-frobenius), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.sheafFrobenius`: The endomorphism φ of the presheaf of rings O_Δ, with component φ_B on the object (B,g,f).
- `Prismatic.Site.RelativePrism.sheafFrobenius_structureMap`: φ_B(g(a)) = g(φ_A(a)) for a ∈ A: the Frobenius of O_Δ is φ_A-semilinear.
- `Prismatic.Site.frobenius_naturality`: For a map R → S of A/I-algebras the square formed by φ_R, φ_S and the induced maps Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A} commutes.
- `Prismatic.Site.frobeniusLinearization`: The linearisation φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, the adjoint of φ_R under φ_A^* ⊣ φ_{A,*}.

**Proof route.** Naturality of each prism Frobenius gives a φ_A-semilinear structure-sheaf map, hence a map after derived sections. Adjunction for completed scalar extension gives its linearization. On a Čech model it is the termwise delta Frobenius and commutes with all cosimplicial maps.

**Checks.**

- `pr1_frobenius_sheaf_component`: On an object (B,g,f) the Frobenius of O_Δ is x ↦ x^p + pδ(x).
- `pr1_frobenius_trivial_base`: If φ_A is the identity (for instance A = Z_p) then φ_{A,*} is isomorphic to the identity functor of D(A), so φ_R is an A-linear endomorphism of Δ_{R/A}.
- `pr1_frobenius_not_linear`: If φ_A(a) ≠ a and g : A → B is injective then φ_B(g(a)) ≠ g(a): the Frobenius is not A-linear, so it is not an endomorphism of Δ_{R/A} in D(A).

- On Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A the Frobenius is φ_A. For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) the Frobenius of Δ_{R/Z_p} is Z_p-linear. For a crystalline prism, φ corresponds under the crystalline comparison to the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology ([§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison)).

<a id="layer-1-base-change-finite-tor-amplitude"></a>

### 1.10 Base change along maps of finite complete Tor amplitude

Extend the supplied affine oriented base-change map to the nonoriented formal-site construction, before using the unrestricted comparison theorem. Let (A,I) → (A′,IA′) be a map of bounded prisms such that A → A′ has finite (p,I)-complete Tor amplitude, let R be a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and R′ := R ⊗̂_A A′ its p-completed base change (a p-completely smooth A′/IA′-algebra). Then the natural maps Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ → Δ_{R′/A′} and Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A/I} A′/IA′ → Δ̄_{R′/A′} are isomorphisms, the completions being derived (p,I)-adic and p-adic. More precisely, for every map of bounded prisms the termwise completed base change C^• ⊗̂_A A′ of the functorial Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of R computes Δ_{R′/A′}, and the Tor amplitude hypothesis is used only to commute the completed base change with the totalisation.

Both prisms are bounded; A → A′ has finite (p,I)-complete Tor amplitude: A′ ⊗^L_A A/(p,I) has finite Tor amplitude over A/(p,I). R is p-completely smooth over A/I. The Tor amplitude hypothesis is removed by [§1.20](#layer-1-prismatic-base-change), which uses the Hodge–Tate comparison; the present statement is an input of that comparison and cannot be replaced by it.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 4.20, Lemma 4.22 and their proofs; pp. 43, 44.)

*Needs:* [§1.7](#layer-1-cech-alexander-complex), [§1.8](#layer-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

Use the supplied base-change map on oriented affine Čech terms. DD.1 finite-complete-Tor-amplitude base change commutes with the bounded-below totalizations here, and the coherent orientation descent gives the map on the formal site. Its compatibility with Frobenius and with reduction is checked on these charts.

**Checks.**

- A completely flat map of bounded prisms satisfies the hypothesis with amplitude 0. The map α of [§1.16](#layer-1-crystallization-of-oriented-prism) satisfies the hypothesis. For A → A′ with infinite complete Tor dimension the statement is not available at this point of the theory.

<a id="layer-1-etale-localization"></a>

### 1.11 Étale localisation of Hodge–Tate cohomology

Extend the supplied affine calculation to the restriction and localization maps on the formal étale site. Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R → S a p-completely étale map of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras. Then the natural map Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R S → Δ̄_{S/A} is an isomorphism (derived p-completed tensor product). The restriction functor (S/A)_Δ → (R/A)_Δ has, in the algebraic language, a left adjoint F : (R/A)_Δ → (S/A)_Δ sending (B → B/IB ← R) to (B_S → B_S/IB_S ← S), where B_S is the unique (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra with B_S/IB_S = B/IB ⊗̂^L_R S; F preserves coproducts and weakly initial objects.

(A,I) is bounded; R and S are p-completely smooth over A/I and R → S is p-completely étale: S is derived p-complete and S ⊗^L_R R/p is étale over R/p. The statement is for Δ̄; the corresponding statement for Δ follows only after completion along I and is not an S-linear statement, since Δ_{R/A} is not an R-module.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 4.21 and its proof; p. 43.)

*Needs:* [§1.7](#layer-1-cech-alexander-complex), [§1.8](#layer-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), [§1.5](#layer-1-hodge-tate-cohomology), [§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness), [PerfectoidQuotients §0.0](#pq-delta-etale), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, Mathlib `Algebra.Etale`.

Apply PerfectoidQuotients §0.0’s unique delta extension to completely étale lifts of each affine chart. The site base-change functor and its adjunction identify restricted Čech terms with the new terms, and complete descent glues the resulting equivalence. This is locality of the reduced complex on its R-module site; the unreduced Δ is not silently made an R-module.

**Checks.**

- A p-completed localisation S = R⟨1/f⟩: Δ̄_{S/A} = Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R⟨1/f⟩. Étale chart: for a p-completely étale map A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ → S, Δ̄_{S/A} = Δ̄_{A/I⟨X⟩/A} ⊗̂^L S; with the Hodge–Tate comparison for the polynomial ring this gives H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}) = Ω^i_{S/(A/I)}{−i}. For R = S the functor F is the identity.

<a id="layer-1-bockstein-differential"></a>

### 1.12 The Bockstein differential on twisted Hodge–Tate cohomology

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra (or X smooth over A/I, with sheaves on X_ét). For i ≥ 0 the connecting map of the triangle Δ̄_{R/A}{i+1} → Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+2} → Δ̄_{R/A}{i} is the Bockstein differential β_I : H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} → H^{i+1}(Δ̄_{R/A}){i+1}. With the cup product of the commutative algebra object Δ̄_{R/A}, the graded group H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}){∗} = ⊕_i H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} is a graded-commutative differential graded A/I-algebra: β_I is A/I-linear, β_I ∘ β_I = 0 and β_I(xy) = β_I(x)y + (−1)^{deg x} x β_I(y). Its degree-0 part is an R-algebra through η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}), and β_I ∘ η^0_R : R → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} is an A/I-linear derivation into a derived p-complete R-module. It therefore induces the R-linear map η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1}, f dg ↦ f·β_I(η^0_R(g)), where Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} is the p-completed module of differentials, finite projective over R.

(A,I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. β_I is A/I-linear but not R-linear. Graded commutativity is xy = (−1)^{deg x · deg y} yx. The vanishing of squares of odd elements is not part of this target; for elements β_I(f), f ∈ R, it is Lemma 4.10 and is proved in [§1.17](#layer-1-hodge-tate-affine-line). When I = (d) the twists are trivialised by d and β_I is the Bockstein of the triangle Δ → Δ → Δ̄ given by multiplication by d (the convention of the source for d = p).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.9; p. 39.)

*Needs:* [§1.5](#layer-1-hodge-tate-cohomology), [§1.4](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`, Mathlib `KaehlerDifferential`, Mathlib `KaehlerDifferential.D`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.twistedCohomology`: The R-module H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} = H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) ⊗_R R{i}, for i ≥ 0.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein`: The additive map β_I : H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} → H^{i+1}(Δ̄_{R/A}){i+1}; it is A/I-linear.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein_comp_bockstein`: β_I ∘ β_I = 0.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.cup`: The cup product H^i{i} × H^j{j} → H^{i+j}{i+j}, R-bilinear, associative, unital and graded-commutative.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.bockstein_cup`: β_I(x ∪ y) = β_I(x) ∪ y + (−1)^i x ∪ β_I(y) for x of degree i.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.eta0`: The R-linear map η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}){0}, a ring map for the cup product.
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.eta1`: The R-linear map η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} with η^1_R(dg) = β_I(η^0_R(g)).

**Proof route.** The successive I-adic triangles give the connecting map, and the three-step filtration makes its consecutive composite zero on cohomology. Multiplicativity of the filtration gives the graded Leibniz rule. Complete differentials corepresent the induced derivation on H⁰, giving η¹.

**Checks.**

- `pr1_bockstein_eta1_d`: η^1_R(dg) = β_I(η^0_R(g)) for every g ∈ R; hence η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(η^0_R(g)).
- `pr1_bockstein_base_zero`: For R = A/I, β_I vanishes on H^0(Δ̄_{(A/I)/A}) = A/I.
- `pr1_bockstein_not_linear`: If dg ≠ 0 in Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} for a p-completely smooth R, then β_I(η^0_R(g)) ≠ 0 although β_I(η^0_R(1)) = 0: β_I is not R-linear.

- R = A/I the cohomology is A/I in degree 0 and β_I = 0. For R = A/I⟨X⟩, β_I(X) is a generator of H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} ≅ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} (PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3). For a crystalline prism and I = (p), β_p is the Bockstein of crystalline cohomology modulo p², which on the de Rham complex of a lift sends the class of x^p to the class of x^{p−1}dx.

<a id="layer-1-relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma"></a>

### 1.13 Laurent relative Frobenius on a Čech nerve

Extend the supplied polynomial Čech lemma to a Laurent algebra. Let k have characteristic p, S be any set, G=⊕_(s∈S)Z and B=k[G]. For the Čech nerve B^n=B^(⊗_k(n+1)) and its relative Frobenius twist B^(•,(1))=B^•⊗_(k,Frob_k)k, prove `Prismatic.laurentRelativeFrobenius`: for every cosimplicial B^(•,(1))-module N, the map N→N⊗_(B^(•,(1)))B^• is a quasi-isomorphism on unnormalized cochain complexes of k-modules. Tensor is ordinary and degreewise; the relative Frobenius maps are free, and N need not be k-flat. No finite-rank assumption on G is used; an arbitrary nonfree group or monoid with p-torsion is outside this statement. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 5.4 and proof, pp.48–49, for the polynomial argument; [K1](#ref-k1), Appendix B, Lemma B.4, pp.61–62, for the Laurent consumer.)

Choose the pointed representatives T of G/pG with finitely supported coordinates in {0,…,p−1}; the unique decompositions g=ph+a identify the relative-Frobenius extension in each degree with the free factor k[ET], compatibly with cofaces. This factor is the underlying semicosimplicial module of the split Čech nerve of k→k[G/pG], so its split homotopy makes the augmented comparison a homotopy equivalence after degreewise tensoring with any cosimplicial N. Every group element has finite support, which proves the assertion directly for infinite S without descending an arbitrary N to finitely many variables; codegeneracies need not respect the chosen basis.

**Checks.**

- For S empty, B=k and the comparison is the identity on N.
- For G=Z and p=2, −1=2(−1)+1, so X^(−1)=X^(−2)X; the coefficient exponents must include negative integers.
- At p=2, a codegeneracy sends the residue pair (1,1) to 2, outside {0,1}; the proof requires only cofaces.
- Take k=F_p[ε]/(ε²) and constant N=k/(ε), with all group variables acting as 1. The same split homotopy works despite failure of k-flatness.

*Needs:* [the polynomial relative-Frobenius input](#ps-affine), Mathlib `AlgebraicTopology.alternatingCofaceMapComplex`, E0 cosimplicial homotopies and tensor products.

<a id="layer-1-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### 1.14 The crystalline comparison

Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism (A is a p-torsion-free, p-complete δ-ring) and let I ⊂ A be an ideal with divided powers and p ∈ I. The Frobenius of A/p kills I/pA, so it induces ψ : A/I → A/p. Let R be a smooth A/I-algebra and R^{(1)} := R ⊗_{A/I,ψ} A/p, a smooth A/p-algebra. Let RΓ_crys(R/A) be the crystalline cohomology of Spec(R) relative to the PD thickening Spec(A/I) ⊂ Spf(A) (p-adically: the derived limit over n of the crystalline cohomology over A/p^n). Then there is a canonical isomorphism Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A) of E_∞-A-algebras, compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms (the Frobenius of prismatic cohomology on the left, the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology induced by the Frobenius of Spec(R) and φ_A on the right). In the case I = (p), with C^• the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of a presentation B_0 → R and D^• the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope of the same presentation, the isomorphism is induced by a map of cosimplicial δ-A-algebras φ_A^*C^• → D^•, where φ_A^*C^• (termwise base change along φ_A) computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A}.

(A,(p)) is a crystalline prism, hence bounded; I is a PD ideal containing p (its divided powers are unique since A is p-torsion-free, and they are compatible with the canonical ones on (p)). R is a smooth A/I-algebra in the usual sense (A/I has characteristic p). The Frobenius twist is on the prismatic side: it is R^{(1)}, not R, whose prismatic cohomology is the crystalline cohomology of R. For I = (p) and with base change ([§1.20](#layer-1-prismatic-base-change)) this reads φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A); the untwisted statement Δ_{R/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A) is false in general. The statement φ_A^*C^• computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} is termwise; it is not claimed here that φ_A^* commutes with the totalisation of C^•.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Notation 5.1, Theorem 5.2 and its proof; p. 45; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8 (1) and Example 1.9 (1); pp. 4, 5; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Theorem 3.1.7 and the paragraph before it; p. 17.)

*Needs:* [§1.7](#layer-1-cech-alexander-complex), [§1.8](#layer-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§1.10](#layer-1-base-change-finite-tor-amplitude), [§1.9](#layer-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology), [§0.20](#layer-0-crystalline-prism), [§0.16](#layer-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.1`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.3`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, Mathlib `DividedPowers`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

**Proof route.** For I=(p), use the crystalline PD and prismatic delta-envelope Čech models; their comparison is relative Frobenius and is an equivalence mod p by the polynomial Čech theorem of PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3, hence by derived Nakayama. Their termwise delta maps give Frobenius compatibility. For general PD I, lift the smooth algebra through the locally nilpotent A/p→A/I kernel and enlarge the PD ideal; the canonical site map through the Frobenius of the PD envelope identifies the resulting comparison independently of the lift.

**Checks.**

- A = Z_p, I = (p), R = F_p[x]: Δ_{F_p[x]/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(F_p[x]/Z_p), the de Rham complex of Z_p⟨x⟩; here R^{(1)} = R. A = W(k) with k perfect and R̃ smooth over k: Δ_{R̃^{(1)}/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)); the twist is by the Frobenius of k. A = A_crys(O_C/p) and I = ker(A_crys → O_C/p), a PD ideal strictly containing (p): for R smooth over O_C/p, Δ_{R^{(1)}/A_crys} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A_crys), with ψ : O_C/p → A_crys/p induced by the Frobenius.

### 1.15 The crystalline comparison for syntomic algebras

Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism, J ⊂ A a PD ideal with p ∈ J, and R a syntomic A/J-algebra (flat, of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres). Put R^{(1)} := R ⊗_{A/J,ψ} A/p. Then there is a canonical Frobenius-compatible isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras RΓ((R^{(1)}/A)_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), where the left side is the cohomology of the prismatic site of R^{(1)} and the right side is crystalline cohomology relative to the PD thickening Spec(A/J) ⊂ Spf(A). For R smooth this is [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison).

(A,(p)) crystalline; J a PD ideal containing p; R syntomic over A/J. The left side is site cohomology. Its identification with derived prismatic cohomology of R^{(1)}, and the extension of the comparison from quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras to all quasisyntomic F_p-algebras by descent, belong to Layer 2 ([§2.11](#layer-2-derived-agrees-with-site), The prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring and Quasisyntomic descent and unfolding) and consume this target; they are not asserted here. For J ≠ (p) the reduction to J = (p) uses a syntomic lift of R to A/p, which exists Zariski-locally (a relative global complete intersection lifts by lifting its equations, and flatness is checked on the unchanged fibres); the canonical map of the smooth case glues the local isomorphisms.

([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Remark 3.1.8 (2); p. 17; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Remark 3.1.8 (2), last sentence; p. 17.)

**Proof route.** A syntomic lift has ind-completely-regular polynomial kernels, so the supplied regular envelopes form the weakly initial Čech model. Compare with the crystalline PD model using relative Frobenius and the polynomial Čech theorem as in [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison). Derived Nakayama and the same canonical site map prove the Frobenius-compatible comparison without assuming smoothness.

**Checks.**

- R = F_p[x]/(x^n) over (Z_p,(p)): the prismatic site cohomology of R^{(1)} = R is RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), computed by the PD envelope of (x^n) in Z_p⟨x⟩ with its de Rham complex. R = k[x,y]/(xy) over W(k): a syntomic, non-smooth example. For R smooth the statement and the map coincide with [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison).

### 1.16 Mapping an oriented prism to a crystalline one

Let (A,(d)) be an oriented prism such that A/(d) is p-torsion-free and the Frobenius A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p), x ↦ x^p, is flat (for example the universal oriented prism, the (p,d)-completion of Z_(p){d, δ(d)^{−1}}). Let B := A{φ(d)/p}^∧ be the p-complete animated δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining φ(d)/p. Then: (a) B is discrete and p-torsion-free, it is the p-completed PD envelope of (d) ⊂ A, and φ(d) = p·u in B with u a unit; B is (p,d)-complete. (b) The composite α : A → B of φ_A : A → A with the canonical map A → B satisfies α(d) ∈ pB, so α is a map of prisms (A,(d)) → (B,(p)) and (B,(p)) is a bounded crystalline prism. (c) Modulo p, α factors as A/p → A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p) → B/p = D_{(d)}(A/p), where the first map has finite Tor amplitude, the second is the Frobenius and is faithfully flat, and the third is free. (d) The completed base change functor α̂^* : D_{comp}(A) → D_{comp}(B) on derived (p,d)-complete objects is conservative and has finite (p,d)-complete Tor amplitude. (e) For every p-completely smooth A/(d)-algebra R with p-completed base change R_B, α̂^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R_B/B} and α̂^*Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Δ̄_{R_B/B}.

(A,(d)) is an oriented prism with A/(d) p-torsion-free; then p is a nonzerodivisor on A and (p,d) is a regular sequence. The Frobenius hypothesis is: only the flatness of A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p) is used, and this is what Example 3.4 provides for the universal oriented prism; the printed hypothesis 'the Frobenius on A/p is flat' is stronger than what is proved there. α is the Frobenius-twisted canonical map; the canonical map A → B itself is not a map of prisms to (B,(p)), since the image of d is not divisible by p.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 6.1; p. 51.)

- `Prismatic.Crystalline.crystallizationMap`: The map of prisms α : (A,(d)) → (B,(p)).

For the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]],(E(u))) the construction gives the p-completed PD envelope of (E(u)), a ring of Breuil type, with α induced by φ. α(d) = φ(d) is p times a unit; the canonical image of d is not in pB.

### 1.17 The square of the Hodge–Tate Bockstein class

For a smooth p-adic formal X over A/I and a local function f, prove β_I(f)²=0, including at p=2. Import the affine-line Hodge–Tate calculation from PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3; this target adds the canonical twisted, nonoriented formal-scheme consequence. Locally orient I and pull back the affine-line class, whose square lies in the vanishing second Hodge–Tate group; compatibility on rescaling and étale restriction descends the result. Graded commutativity alone only proves twice the square is zero at p=2. (BS22 Lemma 4.10, p.39, and Proposition 6.2, p.51.)

The API is `Prismatic.bockstein_square_zero`, natural under pullback, local orientation change and étale restriction.

**Checks.** At f=0 the class vanishes; at f=X on the affine line its square vanishes because H²=0; at p=2 the conclusion is square-zero, not just 2β²=0. Pullback of X along X↦f gives the prescribed local class rather than an unrelated degree-one element.

### 1.18 The Hodge–Tate comparison map η^*

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. There is a unique map η^*_X : (Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{X/A}){∗}, β_I) of sheaves of commutative differential graded A/I-algebras on X_ét which in degree 0 is the structure map η^0_X : O_X → H^0(Δ̄_{X/A}); in degree 1 it is η^1_X, f dg ↦ f β_I(g), and η^i(f_0 df_1 ∧ … ∧ df_i) = f_0 β_I(f_1) ⋯ β_I(f_i). It is O_X-linear in each degree, compatible with the O_X-module structures, functorial in X and compatible with maps of bounded prisms. Its construction depends functorially only on the commutative algebra object Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, A) together with the O_X-algebra structure on Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I. For X = Spf(R) one writes η^i_R : Ω^i_{R/(A/I)} → H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i}. Here Ω^i is the p-completed module of differential forms.

(A,I) is a bounded prism and X is smooth over A/I. The existence of η^* uses Lemma 4.10: β_I(f)² = 0 for every local section f of O_X. For p odd this follows from graded commutativity; for p = 2 it is deduced from the affine line ([§1.17](#layer-1-hodge-tate-affine-line)), by functoriality along A/I⟨T⟩ → O_X(U), T ↦ f. The universal property used is that of the de Rham complex: Ω^*_{R/k} is initial among graded-commutative differential graded k-algebras E with a k-algebra map R → E^0 such that squares of the elements d(r) vanish (completed form for p-completely smooth R).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 4.9 and Lemma 4.10; p. 39; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 4.10 and the sentence after it; p. 39; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Theorem 3.1.6 and the paragraph before it; p. 17.)

- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap_wedge`: η^{i+j}_R(ω ∧ τ) = η^i_R(ω) ∪ η^j_R(τ).
- `Prismatic.HodgeTate.comparisonMap_d`: η^{i+1}_R(dω) = β_I(η^i_R(ω)), for d the de Rham differential.

DD.2's de Rham universal property therefore extends η⁰⊕η¹ uniquely to η*. Uniqueness gives prism/base functoriality and compatibility with étale gluing. (BS22 Construction 4.9 and Lemma 4.10, p.39.)

- `pr1_comparison_map_square_zero`: η^2_R(dg ∧ dg) = 0 = β_I(g) ∪ β_I(g), also for p = 2.

- Η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(g). For R = A/I the map is the identity of A/I in degree 0. For an étale map R → S the maps η^*_R and η^*_S are compatible with Ω^i_R ⊗_R S ≅ Ω^i_S and with [§1.11](#layer-1-etale-localization).

### 1.19 The Hodge–Tate comparison theorem

Globalize the supplied affine oriented Hodge–Tate comparison to smooth p-adic formal schemes over every bounded prism, retaining the conormal twists and étale descent. Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The Hodge–Tate comparison map η^*_X : (Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{X/A}){∗}, β_I) is an isomorphism of sheaves of differential graded A/I-algebras on X_ét. In particular Δ̄_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, O_X) is a perfect complex with H^i(Δ̄_{X/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}{−i}, zero for i larger than the relative dimension. For X = Spf(R) affine: Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) as R-modules, for every i.

(A,I) is a bounded prism; X is smooth over A/I (R p-completely smooth over A/I). Without smoothness the statement fails for site cohomology. The twist is {−i} = ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ −i}; there is no Frobenius twist in this comparison. Ω^i denotes p-completed differential forms, a finite locally free O_X-module.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 4.11; p. 40; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 6.3 and its proof; p. 52; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8 (2); p. 4.)

Extend supplied affine oriented base change to smooth formal schemes over arbitrary bounded prisms. Let (A,I) → (B,IB) be a map of bounded prisms, X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, X_B := X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Spf(B/IB) and g : X_B → X the projection. Then (g^*Δ_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ_{X_B/B} in D(X_{B,ét}, B), the completion being derived (p,I)-adic, and (g^*Δ̄_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ̄_{X_B/B} with p-adic completion. For X = Spf(R): Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A B ≃ Δ_{R ⊗̂_A B/B}. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated then RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_A B ≃ RΓ_Δ(X_B/B). Consequence (the φ_A-twisted crystalline comparison): for a crystalline prism (A,(p)) and R smooth over A/p, base change along the map of prisms φ_A : (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) gives φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} := Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), compatibly with Frobenius; for X smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over A/p, RΓ_crys(X/A) ≃ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A.

Both prisms are bounded; no flatness or Tor amplitude hypothesis on A → B. X is smooth over A/I. The statement for global sections requires X quasi-compact and quasi-separated: completed base change does not commute with infinite products. Theorem 1.8 (5) of the source omits this hypothesis; the sheaf statement, Corollary 4.12, needs no such hypothesis. φ_A : A → A is a map of prisms (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) only for crystalline prisms; for a general prism the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{X/A} is not the prismatic cohomology of a base change over (A,I).

### 1.21 The de Rham comparison (W(A/I) p-torsion-free)

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism such that the ring of p-typical Witt vectors W(A/I) is p-torsion-free, and let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Then there is a natural isomorphism Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I ≃ Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} of commutative algebra objects of D(X_ét, A/I), where A/I is an A-algebra through A → A → A/I, the first map being φ_A, the completion is p-adic, and the right side is the p-completed de Rham complex. More precisely, for a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R there is a functorial isomorphism Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,ψ} W(A/I) ≃ RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)) of commutative algebra objects of D(W(A/I)), where ψ : A → W(A/I) is the composite of the δ-map A → W(A/I) lifting A → A/I with the Witt vector Frobenius, and the crystalline cohomology is relative to the PD ideal ker(W(A/I) → A/(I,p)); reducing along W(A/I) → A/I gives the first isomorphism. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, RΓ_dR(X/(A/I)) ≃ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I.

(A,I) is a bounded prism and W(A/I) is p-torsion-free. This holds if A/I is p-torsion-free, or if I = (p) and A/p is reduced. This is the hypothesis of Theorem 6.4. The statement for every bounded prism, without the hypothesis on W(A/I), is Corollary 15.4 of the source; it is deduced from the Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius and is the target [De Rham comparison for every bounded prism (BS22 Corollary 15.4)](#layer-3-de-rham-comparison-general). It is not asserted here. The reduction is along the Frobenius-twisted map A → A/I. The untwisted reduction Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is Hodge–Tate cohomology, whose cohomology sheaves are Ω^i{−i} with the Bockstein as differential; the two are different objects. In the proof of Theorem 6.4, ψ carries I into FV W(A/I) = pW(A/I).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 6.4, the paragraph before it, and its proof; p. 53; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 6.4, proof; p. 53; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8 (3); p. 4.)

The W(A/I) p-torsion-free hypothesis makes this a crystalline prism, so apply crystalline comparison and the smooth crystalline/de-Rham computation. The composite W(A/I)→A/I after the Witt map is φ modulo I, retaining the displayed twist.

- A = Z_p[[u]], I = (E(u)), A/I = O_K p-torsion-free: Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_{A,φ} O_K ≃ Ω^*_{X/O_K}. A = W(k), I = (p), k perfect: Δ_{R/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k),φ} k ≃ Ω^*_{R/k}; with the Cartier isomorphism this is consistent with Δ̄_{R/W(k)} having cohomology Ω^i_{R/k}. ### 1.22 Perfectness of prismatic cohomology of proper smooth formal schemes

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme over Spf(A/I). Then RΓ_Δ(X/A) is a perfect complex of A-modules, and RΓ(X_ét, Δ̄_{X/A}) = RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗^L_A A/I is a perfect complex of A/I-modules with a finite filtration whose graded pieces are RΓ(X, Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}){−i}[−i], 0 ≤ i ≤ dim(X/(A/I)). In particular RΓ_Δ(X/A) has Tor amplitude in [0, 2 dim], and its formation commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms.

(A,I) is a bounded prism; A/I need not be noetherian. X is proper and smooth over Spf(A/I): quasi-compact, separated, of finite relative dimension, with X ⊗ Z/p^n proper and smooth over A/(I,p^n) for all n. Perfectness is asserted for the complex of global sections, not for the individual cohomology modules H^i_Δ(X/A), which need not be finitely presented or flat.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8, final sentence; p. 4; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8, final sentence; p. 4.)

*Needs:* [§1.19](#layer-1-hodge-tate-comparison), [§1.20](#layer-1-prismatic-base-change), [§1.5](#layer-1-hodge-tate-cohomology), [§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Proof route.** The Hodge–Tate filtration has vector-bundle graded pieces, whose proper smooth formal cohomology is perfect and obeys base change by DD.5. Completeness and DD.1 perfectness detection lift this from A/I to A. Apply prismatic base change; tensor of perfect complexes already agrees with completed tensor.

**Checks.**

- X = P^1 over A/I: RΓ_Δ(X/A) ≃ A ⊕ A{−1}[−2] as a complex, of rank 2. X an abelian formal scheme of dimension g: RΓ_Δ(X/A) is perfect of amplitude [0,2g] with H^1 of rank 2g after base change to a field. For X affine of positive dimension (not proper), RΓ_Δ(X/A) is not perfect: H^0(Δ̄) = O(X) is not finitely generated over A/I.

<a id="layer-1-p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic"></a>

### 1.23 p-torsion-freeness for syntomic algebras and its completion hypothesis

Let (A,I) be a bounded prism with A p-torsion-free. Assume in addition that the I-power torsion of A/p is bounded, locally after trivialising the invertible ideal I. Equivalently, the transition system ((A/I^n)[p])_n is pro-zero. For a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra S, prove `SyntomicPrismatic.p_torsion_free`: H⁰((S/A)_Δ,O_Δ) is p-torsion-free. Here p-completely syntomic means that S is p-complete with bounded p-power torsion, S⊗ᴸ_{A/I}(A/I)/p is the ordinary quotient S/p, and (A/I)/p→S/p is syntomic. Layer 2 identifies this site cohomology with H⁰(Δ_{S/A}). The extra completion hypothesis holds for crystalline, transversal, perfect and noetherian prisms, including the perfect A_inf bases used in prismatic Dieudonné theory. It cannot be omitted for arbitrary bounded prisms.

The source is [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Lemma 5.1.6, p.76. Its statement has no extra completion hypothesis; the completed-flatness step in its proof has the larger generality ruled out below. The valid argument uses [BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 3.13, pp.33–35, together with the one-element bounded-torsion argument of [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Lemmas 4.6–4.7, pp.18–19. Replacing the element p in that module argument by a generator d of I uses the same Koszul-tower proof and no primality property of d.

*Needs:* [§1.7](#layer-1-cech-alexander-complex), [§1.8](#layer-1-cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

The local module assertion is `CompleteFlat.p_torsion_free`: a derived (p,d)-complete, (p,d)-completely flat A-complex B has no p-torsion when A is p-torsion-free and A/p has bounded d-power torsion. Indeed, B is discrete by BS22 Lemma 3.7. The complex B⊗ᴸ_A A/p is derived d-complete and d-completely flat over A/p. The one-element bounded-torsion argument makes this complex discrete. Since p is a nonzerodivisor on A, its degree −1 cohomology is precisely B[p], which therefore vanishes. Trivialisations of I and their completed localisations preserve this argument; complete faithfully flat descent detects the vanishing. Apply it to the first Čech–Alexander term for S. The equaliser H⁰⊂C⁰ is then p-torsion-free. This proof does not replace (p,I)-complete flatness by p-complete flatness without checking the completion ideal.

Define the following explicit square-zero prism to distinguish the two flatness notions. Fix a prime p, put T₀=Z_p[[d]], J_n=(p,d^n)⊂T₀ for n≥1, and M=∏_{n≥1}J_n. Let T be the (p,d)-completion of Z_p[d,t]. Give M its T₀-module structure and the continuous t-action

```text
(t m)_1 = 0,                 (t m)_{n+1} = d m_n.
```

This action is defined because dJ_n⊂J_{n+1}; it commutes with p and d and extends to T by completeness. Form A=T⊕M with M²=0, φ_T(d)=d^p+p, φ_T(t)=t^p, and φ_A(a,m)=(φ_T(a),0). Both p and d are nonzerodivisors on A, so its delta operation is

```text
δ_A(a,m) = (δ_T(a), −a^(p−1)m),             δ_A(d)=1.
```

The quotient J_n/dJ_n is Z_p·y_n⊕F_p·x_n, with y_n represented by p and x_n by d^n. Thus (A/d)[p^∞]=(A/d)[p]. Products commute with the quotients by (p,d)^r because these ideals have finitely many generators. Consequently M, and then A, is classically (p,d)-complete. This is also derived completeness: d is regular, and each A/d^n has bounded p-power torsion by its finite filtration with subquotients A/d. The iterated Koszul inverse limit therefore equals lim_n lim_r A/(d^n,p^r), which is A by classical completeness and cofinality. The regularity of d, distinguishedness δ_A(d)=1, and the displayed uniform torsion bound make (A,(d)) a p-torsion-free bounded prism.

Now let e_n∈M be p in component n and zero elsewhere. In M/pM one has

```text
d^n e_n = 0,                 t e_n = d e_{n+1}.
```

For every r≥0, t^r e_n is represented by p d^r in component n+r. It is nonzero modulo pJ_{n+r}, since d^r∉(p,d^{n+r}). Hence e_n remains nonzero after inverting t. Put R=A[1/t] and, in R/p, z_n=t^(1−n)e_n. Then d^n z_n=0 and d z_{n+1}=z_n, with z₁≠0. This is an actual nonzero inverse-limit element, stronger than the mere failure of a pro-zero condition.

Let B=LΛ_(p,d)R. Since R is flat over A, BS22 Lemma 3.7 makes B a discrete bounded prism over A. The perfect complex A/p commutes with derived completion, so

```text
B⊗ᴸ_A A/p ≃ LΛ_d(R/p),
B[p] ≅ H^(−1)(LΛ_d(R/p)) ≅ lim_n (R/p)[d^n].
```

The last equality is the degree −1 Milnor sequence for the two-term Koszul complexes; there is no degree −2 term. Its transition maps multiply by d. The compatible sequence (z_n) proves B[p]≠0. Moreover B/d is the p-completion S of (A/d)[1/t]. Bounded p-power torsion and BMS2 Lemma 4.7 make A/d→S p-completely étale, hence p-completely syntomic. The prism (B,(d)) is initial in (S/A)_Δ: on every PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2 D, the image of t is invertible modulo d, hence invertible in D because d lies in its Jacobson radical. The map A[1/t]→D therefore extends uniquely through B. It follows that H⁰((S/A)_Δ,O_Δ)=B, which has the exhibited p-torsion. Thus the unqualified bounded-prism version of the syntomic assertion is false even for a p-completely étale algebra. This construction is an elementary consequence of BS22 Lemma 3.7 and the completion definitions, rather than an assertion attributed to ALB23.

**Checks.**

- `SyntomicPrismatic.crystalline`: For (A,I)=(Z_p,(p)) and S=F_p, the structure cohomology is Z_p, whereas the Hodge–Tate structure cohomology is F_p. The theorem concerns O_Δ.
- `SyntomicPrismatic.perfect_base`: For A=A_inf(R), A/p is reduced. If d^n x=0 then (dx)^n=0, hence dx=0; the d-torsion bound is one. This covers the perfect-prism applications, including p=2.
- `CompleteFlat.shift_two_terms`: At p=2, t e₁=d e₂ is nonzero modulo 2M and d²e₂=0. Dividing by the now invertible t gives d(t⁻¹e₂)=e₁, rather than a zero transition.
- `CompleteFlat.localization_counterexample`: The sequence (t^(1−n)e_n)_n is nonzero in lim_n(R/p)[d^n], so the completed localisation B has nonzero p-torsion although A is p-torsion-free.
- `CompleteFlat.boundedness_not_enough`: A/d has all its p-power torsion killed by p, while A/p has d-torsion of every order. Boundedness modulo I is distinct from the extra hypothesis modulo p.
- `SyntomicPrismatic.zero_base`: For A=0 and S=0, both structure cohomology and its p-torsion are zero. No faithfulness or nonzero-ring assertion is used.

For a perfect A_inf base, this applies to the coordinate rings of finite locally free group schemes and to p-completely syntomic algebras of the form O_C⟨x⟩/(x^n−p). If p-torsion-freeness of A itself is dropped, S=A/I already gives H⁰=A and disproves the conclusion whenever A[p]≠0.

<a id="layer-1-acceptance-computations"></a>

### 1.24 polynomial algebra, étale chart, crystalline base, Frobenius twist

(1) Smooth polynomial algebra. For a bounded prism (A,I) and R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, Δ_{R/A} is computed by the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, and H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} is the free R-module on the products β_I(X_{j_1}) ⋯ β_I(X_{j_i}), j_1 < … < j_i; so H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}){∗} is the exterior algebra over R on β_I(X_1),…,β_I(X_n) with differential determined by β_I(X_j^m) = m X_j^{m−1} β_I(X_j). (2) Étale chart. For a p-completely étale map A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ → S, H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}){i} ≅ Ω^i_{S/(A/I)} is free over S on the same classes, and Δ̄_{S/A} ≃ Δ̄_{A/I⟨X⟩/A} ⊗̂^L S. (3) Crystalline base. For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) and R = F_p[X], Δ_{R/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(F_p[X]/Z_p) is the de Rham complex Z_p⟨X⟩ → Z_p⟨X⟩dX: H^0 = Z_p and H^1 is the cokernel of d, X^m ↦ mX^{m−1}dX; its reduction modulo p, which is Δ̄_{R/Z_p}, has cohomology F_p[X^p] in degree 0 and F_p[X^p]·X^{p−1}dX in degree 1, with β_p(X) the class of X^{p−1}dX. (4) Nontrivial Frobenius-twisted coefficient map. For A = W(k) with k = F_{p²} and R̃ = k[X,Y]/(Y² − X³ − aX − b) an affine elliptic curve whose j-invariant is not in F_p (p ≥ 5), the algebras R̃ and R̃^{(1)} = R̃ ⊗_{k,Frob} k are not isomorphic over k, and Δ_{R̃^{(1)}/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)) while φ_A^*Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)): the comparison holds only after the scalar extension along φ_A, which is not the identity on W(k). Likewise Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k),φ} k ≃ Ω^*_{R̃/k}, whereas the untwisted reduction Δ̄_{R̃/W(k)} = Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k)} k has cohomology modules Ω^i_{R̃/k} and is the de Rham complex of the Frobenius untwist R̃ ⊗_{k,Frob^{−1}} k, a curve not isomorphic to R̃.

(1), (2): any bounded prism. (3): the crystalline prism (Z_p,(p)). (4): k = F_{p²}, p ≥ 5, a, b ∈ k with j-invariant outside F_p. In (3) the twist is invisible because F_p[X]^{(1)} = F_p[X] over F_p; (4) is chosen so that the twist changes the algebra. In (4) the two W(k)-module structures on RΓ_crys differ by φ; the complexes are abstractly isomorphic as complexes of abelian groups since φ is an automorphism of W(k).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 4.19; p. 43; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 1.9 (1); p. 5.)

*Needs:* [§1.19](#layer-1-hodge-tate-comparison), [§1.11](#layer-1-etale-localization), [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison), [§1.20](#layer-1-prismatic-base-change), [§1.21](#layer-1-de-rham-comparison), [§1.7](#layer-1-cech-alexander-complex), [§1.12](#layer-1-bockstein-differential), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§0.20](#layer-0-crystalline-prism), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`.

**Proof route.** Apply [§1.19](#layer-1-hodge-tate-comparison) and the Bockstein Leibniz rule to the polynomial chart, then [§1.11](#layer-1-etale-localization) for its étale charts. For the crystalline computation combine [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison) with CR.2's affine-line de Rham complex and PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3's characteristic-p Bockstein. For the nontrivial coefficient twist use [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison), [§1.20](#layer-1-prismatic-base-change)–[§1.21](#layer-1-de-rham-comparison): Frobenius sends the elliptic coefficients to a^p,b^p and j to j^p≠j. (BS22 Remark 4.19, p.43, and Example 1.9(1), p.5.)

**Checks.**

- Each of the four computations is a test of the corresponding comparison theorem with a wrong twist: (1) fails with the twist {i} in place of {−i} for a non-orientable prism, (3) fails if β is omitted, (4) fails without φ_A. The torus R = A/I⟨X^{±1}⟩ is an étale chart of the affine line and gives H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} = R·η^1(dX/X).

<a id="layer-1-prismatic-hyperdescent"></a>

### 1.25 Prismatic hyperdescent

On the flat site of bounded prisms, the assignments (B,J)↦B and (B,J)↦B/J, valued in the respective derived categories, satisfy hyperdescent. A flat hypercover of an object computes its derived sections by totalisation. The same holds on a relative prismatic site and after derived pushforward to the small étale site.

Bounded prisms; finite jointly completely faithfully flat covering families; a universe cut-off is fixed. The statement uses derived totalisations, not an ordinary equalizer of rings.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Corollary 3.12 and Definition 4.1, §3–4; pp. 33, 36.)

*Needs:* [§1.1](#layer-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf), [§1.2](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-site), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Proof route.** The structure sheaves’ derived sections agree with their degree-zero values on objects by acyclicity. Enhanced hyperdescent identifies these sections with every hypercover totalization, and the same holds on the relative category of elements. Derived pushforward preserves the required limits.

**Checks.**

- The Čech hypercover of a flat cover recovers Corollary 3.12. The zero prism has the empty covering family and zero derived module of sections.

### Examples

For R=A/I the relative site has final object (A,I,id), Δ=A and Δ̄=A/I. For R=(A/I)⟨X⟩, the model begins C⁰=A{X}^∧ and C¹=A{X,Y}{(X−Y)/I}^∧. The Hodge–Tate comparison sends dX to β(X) in H¹(Δ̄){1}; β(1)=0 while β(X)≠0 when A/I≠0. Thus β is not R-linear. At p=2 its square vanishes by the affine-line argument, not solely by graded commutativity. Over the crystalline prism (Z_p,(p)), reduction of the de Rham differential of x^p and division by p gives x^(p−1)dx, fixing the Bockstein sign.
