## Layer 2: Animated inputs and perfectoidization

Extend the polynomial theory by completed left Kan extension, retaining the animated input and its conjugate filtration. Regular quotient and quasiregular semiperfectoid computations distinguish site cohomology from its derived extension. Frobenius perfection is a completed colimit, and perfectoidization is its derived reduction. Base independence and arc descriptions require the additional perfect-site inputs stated above.


<a id="layer-2-local-arc-foundations"></a>

### 2.0 Arc descent for the comparisons

Use valuation rings from ordinary commutative algebra, the schemes and sheaves of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1–SF.2, and the completed formal geometry of SF.4. PerfectoidSpaces P1 and §§P4.15.2–P4.15.5 supply perfectoid rings, André covers and the universal semiperfectoid quotient. This prefix constructs the topologies and descent statements used by the perfect-site, étale and logarithmic comparisons.

Define `Arc.Cover (f : Y → X)` for qcqs schemes by the following lifting condition. Given a rank-at-most-one valuation ring V and Spec V → X, there must be an injective local extension V → W of rank-at-most-one valuation rings and a compatible Spec W → Y. Define `Arc.Site` using finite affine refinements of covering families and Zariski localization. Prove closure under composition and base change and that the resulting covering families generate a Grothendieck topology. (Bhatt–Mathew, [The arc-topology](#ref-arc), Definitions 1.1–1.2, pp.2–3; Proposition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2, p.9.)

Prove the following API:

- `Arc.Cover`, `Arc.Site`: the lifting predicate and its associated site, with the universe of test valuation rings explicit.
- `Arc.Cover.baseChange`, `Arc.Cover.comp`, `Arc.Cover.ofVCover`: stability and the comparison with the v-topology.
- `Arc.Site.affineBasis`: the affine refinement equivalence, compatible with restriction to an open subscheme.

**Checks for the covering predicate.** The identity of Spec Z_p is a cover by choosing W=V. The empty scheme does not cover Spec F_p, as the identity map from F_p has no lift. The reduction Spec F_p → Spec F_p[ε]/(ε²) is a cover, because every map to a valuation ring annihilates ε; requiring faithful flatness of the displayed scheme map would reject it.

**Checks for the site.** A two-open affine Zariski covering is a covering family after the finite affine refinement. The empty family does not cover the nonempty scheme Spec F_p. For a rank-two valuation ring V with a height-one prime q, Spec(V_q) ⊔ Spec(V/q) covers Spec V in the arc-topology although it is not a v-cover; this distinguishes the rank-one testing convention (Example 2.8, p.10).

Define `ArcPCover (R → S)` over Z_p by testing rank-one valuation rings V in which p is a pseudouniformizer, permitting an injective local extension of valuation rings before lifting. Define `ArcP.Equivalence` by bijectivity on maps to p-complete absolutely integrally closed valuation test rings. The topology generated by these covers is the algebraic arc_p topology. This is different from imposing an adic completeness condition on every algebra under consideration. (Bhatt–Mathew, [The arc-topology](#ref-arc), Definition 6.14, p.51; Definition 6.19 and Example 6.20, pp.53–54, with t=p.)

Prove the following API:

- `ArcPCover`, `ArcP.Site`, `ArcP.Equivalence`: the predicates and generated topology, with the pseudouniformizer condition in their signatures.
- `ArcPCover.baseChange`, `ArcPCover.comp`: the structural closure properties.
- `ArcP.Equivalence.complete`, `ArcP.Equivalence.killPowerTorsion`, `ArcP.Equivalence.integralClosure`: the three invariance inputs for generic-fibre cohomology.

**Checks for the topology.** The identity of Z_p is a cover. Z_p → Q_p is not a cover: a map to the test ring Z_p cannot extend across p⁻¹, even after a local extension. Z_p → F_p is not a cover, since the same test map cannot annihilate p. These exclude conventions allowing p to be a unit or zero in the test rings.

**Checks for arc_p equivalences.** Z_p → Z_p is an equivalence. Z_p[ε]/(pε,ε²) → Z_p is an equivalence because the target valuation rings have no p-torsion. Z_p → Z_p⟨T⟩ is not an equivalence: evaluation at T=0 and T=1 give different lifts of the same map from Z_p. In particular an arc_p cover need not be an arc_p equivalence.

Define `FormalArc.Site` on p-adic formal schemes using Zariski covers and qcqs maps with the lifting property for p-complete rank-one valuation rings and faithfully flat, p-complete rank-one extensions. Give the full subcategory of locally perfectoid formal schemes the induced topology, denoted `FormalArc.PerfectoidBasis`. (Bhatt–Scholze [BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 8.7, Lemma 8.8, Remark 8.9, pp.67–68.)

Prove the following API:

- `FormalArc.Site`, `FormalArc.Cover`: the formal site and covering predicate, including continuity of the morphisms.
- `FormalArc.PerfectoidBasis`: the induced site on formal schemes locally of the form Spf S for perfectoid S.
- `FormalArc.coverByPerfectoids`, `FormalArc.coverByValuations`: covers by that basis and by products of p-complete rank-one valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction fields.
- `FormalArc.restrictToBasis`: the sheaf-category equivalence associated with the basis.

**Checks for the formal site.** Spf Z_p → Spf Z_p is a cover. Spf F_p → Spf Z_p is not a cover, as the Z_p valuation test cannot lift. A nilpotent reduction has the same valuation tests, so Spf F_p → Spf F_p[ε]/(ε²) is a cover; ordinary structure sections on all formal schemes consequently do not satisfy this topology's sheaf condition.

**Checks for the basis.** The p-completion of the ring of integers in an algebraic closure of Q_p supplies a perfectoid cover of Spf Z_p. A characteristic-p perfection supplies a cover of Spf F_p[T]. Spf Z_p itself is not a perfectoid basis object: it has no element whose p-th power generates an ideal containing p but smaller than the unit ideal. Thus being p-complete does not suffice for membership in this basis.

Prove the following descent statements before using this prefix in the comparison targets. For a torsion étale sheaf G on a base, X ↦ RΓ(X_ét,G) satisfies arc descent and excision. For a finite coefficient ring Λ, the bounded constructible categories Dᵇ_cons(X_ét,Λ), also with a fixed cohomological range, satisfy hypercomplete arc descent. For a formal-gluing datum (A → B,I), with I finitely generated and A/Iⁿ ≅ B/IⁿB for every n, the square of torsion étale cohomology on Spec A, Spec B and their complements of V(I) is cartesian. If (A,I) is henselian, cohomology on Spec A \ V(I) agrees with that on Spec Â_I \ V(IÂ_I). Finally, R ↦ RΓ_ét(Spec R̂_p[1/p],G) is an arc_p sheaf. Prove these as torsion statements first; the Z_p versions are derived inverse limits of the finite-level assertions. (Bhatt–Mathew [ARC](#ref-arc), Theorem 5.4, p.38; Theorem 5.13, pp.42–43; Proposition 6.4, pp.48–49; Theorem 6.11, p.50; Corollary 6.17, pp.51–52.)

On the perfectoid formal basis prove that the presheaf O is an arc sheaf with RΓ_arc(Spf S,O) ≅ S for perfectoid S. This is the structure-sheaf acyclicity needed by the local perfect-prismatic-site comparison, rather than an assertion about every p-complete ring. (Bhatt–Scholze [BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 8.10, pp.67–68.) For the formal-gluing square check I=A, when both open complements are the whole spectra and its vertical maps are identities, and I=0, when both complements are empty. Do not apply the henselian theorem to I=A unless A=0, since a henselian ideal lies in the Jacobson radical. Check the nilpotent affine reduction above, where O on the entire formal site cannot have the acyclicity just proved on the perfectoid basis.

<a id="layer-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology"></a>

### 2.1 Derived prismatic cohomology

Glue the supplied oriented animated functors across changes of local orientation to obtain the following functor for every bounded prism. Fix a bounded prism (A, I). Let Poly_{A/I} be the category of p-completed polynomial algebras (A/I)⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩, n ≥ 0, and Sm_{A/I} the category of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras. Let CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)) be the ∞-category of commutative algebra objects E of D_comp(A) equipped with a map of commutative algebras φ_E : E → φ_{A,*}E. Layer 1 gives a functor Sm_{A/I} → CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)), R ↦ (Δ_{R/A}, φ_R). Derived prismatic cohomology is its left Kan extension Δ_{−/A} to the ∞-category of derived p-complete simplicial commutative A/I-algebras, with colimits in the target derived (p, I)-completed. Equivalently Δ_{−/A} is the unique functor on derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras that preserves sifted colimits and restricts to Layer 1's functor on Poly_{A/I}; for a simplicial resolution P_• → R by objects of Poly_{A/I} (or by p-completely ind-smooth algebras) one has Δ_{R/A} ≃ (colim_{[n] ∈ Δ^op} Δ_{P_n/A})^∧, independently of the resolution. Derived Hodge–Tate cohomology is Δ̄_{R/A} := Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I, a derived p-complete commutative algebra in D(R). The functor carries: (1) the unit A → Δ_{R/A}, with Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A; (2) the structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}; (3) the φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A}, natural in R. For R in Sm_{A/I} the value is the site cohomology of Layer 1 ([§2.11](#layer-2-derived-agrees-with-site)). Δ_{R/A} is an invariant of the animated ring R and not of π_0(R) alone ([§2.13](#layer-2-derived-input-higher-homotopy)).

D(A) is the derived ∞-category of A-modules with cohomological indexing; D_comp(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects with its completed tensor product; "discrete" means concentrated in degree 0. A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. Layer 1's functor is used as a functor of ∞-categories; its coherence in R is supplied by the functorial Čech–Alexander complexes. The left Kan extension from Sm_{A/I} and the one from Poly_{A/I} agree; this is part of the statement and is proved through the Hodge–Tate comparison (BS22 Construction 7.6 (1)).

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Derived.cohomology`: The object Δ_{R/A} of D(A) attached to a simplicial commutative A/I-algebra R.
- `Prismatic.Derived.map`: A map R → S of simplicial A/I-algebras induces Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{S/A}.
- `Prismatic.Derived.map_id`: The identity of R induces the identity of Δ_{R/A}.
- `Prismatic.Derived.map_comp`: The map induced by a composite is the composite of the induced maps.
- `Prismatic.Derived.frobenius`: The Frobenius φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A}.
- `Prismatic.Derived.frobenius_naturality`: For f : R → S one has φ_S ∘ Δ(f) = φ_{A,*}(Δ(f)) ∘ φ_R.
- `Prismatic.Derived.hodgeTate`: Derived Hodge–Tate cohomology Δ̄_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I, as an object of D(A/I).
- `Prismatic.Derived.unit`: The unit map A → Δ_{R/A} in D(A).
- `Prismatic.Derived.constIso`: For an ordinary p-complete A/I-algebra R, identify its constant simplicial presentation with R as an animated algebra; the values of the derived functor are canonically equivalent. For p-completely smooth R this value is the site cohomology of Layer 1. Agreement with site cohomology for other inputs requires the hypotheses of [§2.11](#layer-2-derived-agrees-with-site).
- `Prismatic.Derived.hodgeTateUnit`: The natural map of derived commutative R-algebras R→Δ̄_(R/A) is the structure map. On a smooth algebra it is the degree-zero Hodge–Tate comparison map.
- `Prismatic.Derived.cohomology_realization`: For a simplicial diagram of animated A/I-algebras, Δ of its geometric realisation is the derived (p,I)-completed geometric realisation of its Δ-values. Values on p-completed polynomial algebras and this property characterize the left Kan extension; ordinary uncompleted colimits are not claimed.
- `Prismatic.Derived.hodgeTate_const`: For an ordinary p-complete A/I-algebra R viewed as a constant simplicial algebra, reduction of the animated construction gives Δ̄_(R/A) as computed by any polynomial resolution, naturally in R and compatibly with R→Δ̄. This is a comparison between presentations of the derived theory, not an identification with singular site cohomology.

The supplied oriented functors and their canonical base-change maps agree on overlaps; orientation changes act trivially on Δ and by the conormal transition on its reduction. Complete descent therefore glues them to the stated nonoriented functor with its unit and semilinear Frobenius. Their polynomial universal property, checked after the same cover and by Hodge–Tate graded pieces, gives resolution independence and agreement with the smooth formal-site construction.

- `pr2_derived_base_ring`: Δ_{(A/I)/A} is A, in degree 0.
- `pr2_derived_const_agrees`: The value of the simplicial functor on a constant simplicial algebra R is isomorphic to Δ_{R/A}.
- `pr2_derived_product`: Δ_{(A/I × A/I)/A} is A × A, in degree 0.
- `pr2_derived_not_pi0_invariant`: When A/I ≠ 0 there is a simplicial A/I-algebra R with H^{−1}(Δ̄_{R/A}) ≠ 0; so Δ̄_{R/A} is not the Hodge–Tate cohomology of the site of π_0(R), which lies in D^{≥0}.

For R = A/I × A/I (p-completely étale over A/I) the value is A × A. For a discrete p-complete R, two polynomial simplicial resolutions give canonically equivalent values. A non-discrete input is computed in [§2.13](#layer-2-derived-input-higher-homotopy).

<a id="layer-2-conjugate-filtration"></a>

### 2.2 Conjugate filtration on derived Hodge–Tate cohomology

Descend the supplied oriented conjugate filtration to the canonical twisted filtration over any bounded prism. For a bounded prism (A, I) and a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra R, the conjugate filtration is the functorial increasing N-indexed filtration Fil_0^conj → Fil_1^conj → ⋯ → Δ̄_{R/A} by derived p-complete objects of D(R), defined as the derived p-completed left Kan extension, from p-completely smooth A/I-algebras, of the canonical filtration Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} := τ^{≤i} Δ̄_{R/A}. It is exhaustive (Δ̄_{R/A} is the derived p-completed colimit of the Fil_i^conj), multiplicative (there are maps Fil_i^conj ⊗^L_R Fil_j^conj → Fil_{i+j}^conj compatible with the product of Δ̄_{R/A}), natural in R (compatibility with base change of prisms is [§2.7](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-base-change)), and Fil_0^conj = R with Fil_0^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} the structure map. Its graded pieces gr_i^conj := cofib(Fil_{i−1}^conj → Fil_i^conj) are computed by [§2.3](#layer-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison). The filtration is not the Postnikov filtration of Δ̄_{R/A} outside the smooth case: for a nonzero regular quotient R = (A/I)/(f) with bounded p^∞-torsion, Δ̄_{R/A} is discrete while no Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is an isomorphism.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. Filtered objects are functors (N, ≤) → D(R); completed filtered tensor products and graded pieces are those of DD.1.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 7.6; p. 56; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Proposition 3.1.10 (published: Proposition 3.10); p. 18.)

- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFil`: The object Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} of D(R), for a discrete A/I-algebra R and i ∈ N.
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFilMap_refl`: The transition map for i ≤ i is the identity.
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFilMap_trans`: Transition maps compose: (i ≤ j) followed by (j ≤ k) is (i ≤ k).
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFilι`: The map Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A}.
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFilMap_ι`: The transition map followed by Fil_j^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A}.
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFilZeroIso`: Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} is R in degree 0.
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjGr`: The graded piece gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A}, an object of D(R) with a map from Fil_i^conj.
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFilMap`: An A/I-algebra map R→S gives a filtered map Fil^conj_•Δ̄_R→Fil^conj_•Δ̄_S, after restriction of scalars to R; identity and composition hold. The graded maps are the corresponding maps on p-completed exterior powers of the cotangent complex.
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFil_cofiber`: For i≥0, Fil^conj_(i−1)→Fil^conj_i→gr^conj_i is a canonical cofibre sequence, with Fil^conj_(−1)=0.
- `Prismatic.Derived.conjFilCup`: Pairings Fil^conj_i⊗^L_RFil^conj_j→Fil^conj_(i+j) respect transition maps, the degree-zero unit, and the cup product on Δ̄. The associated graded pairings are exterior products on the cotangent complex.

The oriented increasing filtrations descend in the category of completed filtered modules, with the twists on their graded pieces. Exhaustiveness and multiplicativity are preserved by this descent, and the degree-zero unit glues to R. For a nonzero regular quotient every divided-power graded piece persists, giving the stated distinction from Postnikov truncation.

- `pr2_conj_fil_zero`: Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ R[0].
- `pr2_conj_fil_base`: For R = A/I the map Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is an isomorphism for every i.
- `pr2_conj_fil_smooth_truncation`: For R smooth over A/I, H^n(Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A}) = 0 for n > i: the filtration is the canonical one.
- `pr2_conj_fil_not_postnikov`: For f a nonzerodivisor of A/I with (A/I)/(f) nonzero and of bounded p^∞-torsion, Fil_i^conj → Δ̄ is not an isomorphism for any i, although Δ̄ is discrete.

- Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} = R for every R. For p-completely smooth R the filtration is τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{R/A}, so Fil_i^conj ∈ D^{≤i}. For R = A/I every Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} = A/I is an isomorphism. For a nonzero regular quotient the filtration is strictly increasing although Δ̄ is discrete.

<a id="layer-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison"></a>

### 2.3 Derived Hodge–Tate comparison

Descend the supplied oriented graded comparison with its conormal transition functions to every bounded prism. Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. For every derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra R and every i ≥ 0 there is an isomorphism in D(R), natural in R and multiplicative in i, gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ (∧^i_R L_{R/(A/I)}){−i}[−i]^∧, where L_{R/(A/I)} is the cotangent complex, ∧^i the derived exterior power (DD.0), {−i} the Breuil–Kisin twist and ^∧ derived p-completion. For i = 0 it is Fil_0^conj = R; for p-completely smooth R it is the Hodge–Tate isomorphism Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) of Layer 1. Consequences. (a) If R is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{R/(A/I)} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0], then gr_i^conj ∈ D^{[0,i]}(R) and Δ̄_{R/A}, Δ_{R/A} ∈ D^{≥0}. (b) If R is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{R/(A/I)}[−1] is p-completely flat over R, then gr_i^conj ≃ Γ^i_R(L_{R/(A/I)}[−1]){−i}^∧ is a p-completely flat R-module in degree 0, Δ̄_{R/A} is discrete, has bounded p^∞-torsion and R → Δ̄_{R/A} is p-completely faithfully flat, and Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free. (c) If the derived p-completion of L_{R/(A/I)} vanishes, then R ≃ Δ̄_{R/A}.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. Derived exterior and divided powers and the décalage isomorphism ∧^i(M[1]) ≃ Γ^i(M)[i] are those of DD.0; p-complete Tor-amplitude and p-complete flatness are those of BMS2 §4.1.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 7.6; p. 56; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Proposition 3.1.10 (published: Proposition 3.10); p. 18; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Lemmas 4.6 and 4.7; p. 19.)

*Needs:* [§2.2](#layer-2-conjugate-filtration), [§2.1](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology), [§1.19](#layer-1-hodge-tate-comparison), [§1.18](#layer-1-hodge-tate-comparison-map), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

On orientation charts use the supplied derived Hodge–Tate comparison and descend with the inverse conormal powers. For the Tor-amplitude consequences use derived exterior-power décalage and the bounded-p-torsion criterion on the completed filtration; in the shifted-flat case its pieces are discrete divided powers and the unit has faithfully flat reduction. Derived Nakayama for the invertible ideal then gives discreteness and I-torsion-freeness of Δ; if the completed cotangent complex vanishes, all positive graded pieces vanish.

**Checks.**

- Polynomial algebra: recovers Ω^i{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ̄). R = A/I: gr_i^conj = 0 for i > 0. R = (A/I)/(f), f a nonzerodivisor, R of bounded p^∞-torsion: gr_i^conj = Γ^i_R(R·f̄){−i}, free of rank 1. S perfectoid over a perfect prism: L^∧_{S/(A/I)} = 0, so Δ̄_{S/A} = S and Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S). R = A/I ⊗^L_{(A/I)⟨x⟩} A/I: gr_i^conj ≃ R{−i} for all i ([§2.13](#layer-2-derived-input-higher-homotopy)).

### 2.4 Étale descent and derived prismatic cohomology of formal schemes

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (1) Étale base change: for a p-completely étale map R → R′ of derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras, Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R′ ≃ Δ̄_{R′/A}, compatibly with conjugate filtrations. (2) Sheaf property: for a p-completely étale cover R → R′ with derived p-completed Čech nerve R′^•, the map Δ_{R/A} → lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{R′^n/A} is an equivalence of commutative algebras with Frobenius in D_comp(A); so R ↦ Δ_{R/A} is a sheaf for the p-completely étale topology on derived p-complete A/I-algebras. (3) Globalisation: for a p-adic formal scheme X over Spf(A/I), locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion, there is a functorially defined derived (p, I)-complete commutative algebra Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) with a φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_X, such that RΓ(U, Δ_{X/A}) ≃ Δ_{R/A} for every affine object U = Spf(R) of X_ét, compatibly with Frobenius; Δ̄_{X/A} := Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is an object of D(X_ét, O_X) with an increasing exhaustive multiplicative filtration Fil_•^conj and gr_i^conj Δ̄_{X/A} ≃ (∧^i L_{X/(A/I)}){−i}[−i]^∧.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. The bounded-torsion hypothesis on X in (3) is the one of the arXiv v4 text of ALB23 Proposition 3.1.11; BS22 state the globalisation for every p-adic formal scheme.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 7.6 (2); p. 56; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Proposition 3.1.11 (published: Proposition 3.11); p. 18.)

*Needs:* [§2.1](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology), [§2.2](#layer-2-conjugate-filtration), [§2.3](#layer-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Proof route.** Étale cotangent vanishing identifies completed exterior powers under base change, hence each conjugate stage and the Hodge–Tate complex. Complete faithfully flat descent totalizes these stages, and derived Nakayama lifts the comparison to Δ. Étale sheafification gives the formal-scheme construction with its Frobenius and filtration.

**Checks.**

- X smooth the object Δ_{X/A} is the one of Layer 1. For X = Spf(R) affine, RΓ(X, Δ_{X/A}) = Δ_{R/A}. For a finite disjoint union the value is the product: Δ_{(R_1 × R_2)/A} = Δ_{R_1/A} × Δ_{R_2/A}.

### 2.5 The first conjugate piece is the cotangent complex over the prism

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. There is a canonical isomorphism in D(R), natural in R, α_R : (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ ≃ Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{R/A}, where L_{R/A} is the cotangent complex of R over A (not over A/I). It is an isomorphism of extensions: the transitivity triangle R ≃ (R ⊗^L_{A/I} L_{(A/I)/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ → (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ → (L_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧, formed with L_{(A/I)/A} ≃ I/I²[1], is carried to Fil_0^conj → Fil_1^conj → gr_1^conj with the identifications gr_0^conj = R and gr_1^conj = (L_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧ of the derived Hodge–Tate comparison. For p-completely smooth R it reads L_{R/A}^∧ ≃ (τ^{≤1}Δ̄_{R/A}){1}[1]. For a p-adic formal scheme X over A/I that is locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion the isomorphisms glue to α_X : (L_{X/Spf(A)}{−1}[−1])^∧ ≃ Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} in D(X).

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. All cotangent complexes are derived p-completed; the hypothesis on X is the one added in Proposition 3.1.11 of the arXiv v4 text of ALB23.

([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Proposition 3.2.1 (published: Proposition 3.12) and its proof; p. 18; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 4.15; p. 41.)

**Proof route.** Pull back B/J²→B/J along R→B/J and classify this square-zero extension by L_(R/A)→B/J{1}[1]; take its enhanced site limit and then polynomial extension. On the affine line the conormal summand gives the canonical degree-zero map of the shifted complex, while dx gives the degree-one Bockstein map. Naturality and generation by dr identify both cohomology maps and the transitivity triangles, proving the truncated equivalence.

**Checks.**

- R = A/I: both sides are A/I. R = (A/I)⟨x⟩: Fil_1^conj = τ^{≤1}Δ̄ = Δ̄ and the class of the extension of Ω^1{−1}[−1] by R vanishes, in accordance with the lift A⟨x⟩ over A/I². R = (A/I)/(f) with f a nonzerodivisor: Fil_1^conj is the discrete module (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1]) = J/J²{−1} for J = (I, f), an extension of R·f̄{−1} by R.

<a id="layer-2-conjugate-splitting-and-lifting"></a>

### 2.6 Splitting of the first conjugate piece and liftings modulo I²

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a p-completely flat p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The extension Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{X/A} = O_X → Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} → gr_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} = (L_{X/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧ has a splitting in D(X) exactly when a p-completely flat lift of X across A/I²→A/I exists. More precisely, the class of this extension in Ext^1_{O_X}(gr_1^conj, gr_0^conj) = Ext^2_{O_X}((L_{X/(A/I)})^∧{−1}, O_X) is, up to sign, the obstruction class to lifting X over A/I².

M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module. X is locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion (automatic for p-completely flat X over the bounded A/I). ALB23 phrase the splitting as "isomorphic in D(X) to a complex with zero differentials"; the target uses the precise form from their proof, the vanishing of the extension class.

([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Corollary 3.2.3 (published: Corollary 3.14) and Proposition 3.2.2; p. 20; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Proposition 3.2.2 (published: Proposition 3.13); p. 20; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 4.14; p. 40.)

*Needs:* [§2.5](#layer-2-first-conjugate-piece-cotangent), [§2.2](#layer-2-conjugate-filtration), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`.

**Proof route.** The previous comparison identifies the conjugate extension with the twisted transitivity triangle. Globalize DD.0’s affine square-zero extension groupoids over an affine hypercover: the degree-two cocycle of RHom(L,(I/I²)⊗O) measures incompatibility on triple overlaps, with changes by coboundaries. Its nullhomotopy groupoid is the flat lifting groupoid, with Ext¹ differences and Ext⁰ automorphisms; this proves the scheme obstruction and its boundary sign, rather than merely local vanishing.

For the formal version, perform the same polynomial-resolution construction in derived p-complete algebras, with square-zero coefficient O_X⊗(I/I²) and continuous derivations represented by the completed cotangent complex. The base rings A/I and A/I² and this coefficient are p-complete with bounded p-power torsion. DD.1 identifies the completed derivation complexes with inverse limits of their derived p-power reductions; thus a chosen nullhomotopy gives a compatible system of deformation data, rather than an unrelated lift at each level. Flatness in this argument is p-complete flatness. The square-zero flat deformation criterion and the bounded-torsion discreteness criterion of BMS2 Lemma 4.7 make the resulting completed affine lifts ordinary rings; SF.4 affine descent glues their formal spectra. This proves the formal obstruction theorem. When A/I has p-torsion, use the derived reductions of the square-zero extension, not an assumption that its kernel after ordinary reduction is (I/I²)/p^n.

**Checks.** For X=Spf(A/I), the relative cotangent complex and the obstruction both vanish, and the base lift exists. For an étale X over Spf(A/I), the completed relative cotangent complex vanishes, so the lift is unique up to unique isomorphism. For a smooth affine X the positive Ext groups of its finite projective cotangent module vanish, while global smooth schemes can have nonzero Ext² from sheaf cohomology; the construction must use the global derived Hom rather than a product of affine Ext² groups. If a lift exists, changing its chosen identification is detected by Ext⁰ and changing the lift by Ext¹; replacing the groupoid by a bare existence predicate loses these tests.

- If X lifts to a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-scheme, the Higgs specialisation of BS22 Remark 4.13 splits O_X → Δ̄_{X/A}, in particular Fil_1^conj. For (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)) the statement is the Deligne–Illusie criterion: Fil_1^conj splits exactly when X lifts to Z/p². X = Spf(A/I): the class lies in the zero group.

<a id="layer-2-derived-prismatic-base-change"></a>

### 2.7 Base change for derived prismatic cohomology

Extend the supplied oriented animated base-change equivalence to arbitrary bounded prisms, coherently with their orientation covers and twists. Let (A, I) → (B, J) be a map of bounded prisms (so J = IB) and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. Let R_B := (R ⊗^L_A B)^∧ = (R ⊗^L_{A/I} B/J)^∧ be the derived p-completion. Then the natural map Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A B → Δ_{R_B/B} is an isomorphism of commutative algebras in D_comp(B), the completion on the left being the derived (p, J)-completion. It is compatible with Frobenius, and its reduction modulo J, Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A/I} B/J ≃ Δ̄_{R_B/B}, is compatible with the conjugate filtrations and, through L_{R_B/(B/J)} ≃ L_{R/(A/I)} ⊗^L_R R_B, with the identifications of the graded pieces.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. No flatness of A → B is assumed; R ⊗^L_A B is computed in animated rings, and A/I ⊗^L_A B = B/J because I is invertible and B is I-torsion-free.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 7.6 (4); p. 56.)

Use the supplied oriented animated base-change equivalence on orientation charts of both prisms. Its coherent tensor compatibility descends, including Frobenius and the filtered reduction. The perfectness of A/I over A identifies R⊗^L_A B with R⊗^L_(A/I)B/J, without a flatness assumption on A→B.

**Checks.**

- B = A: the identity. Base change to the perfection (A, I) → (A, I)_perf and to an orientable cover (A, I) → (B, (d)). For a map of perfect prisms A → A′ and S an A/I-algebra: Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ ≃ Δ_{(S ⊗̂^L A′/I)/A′}, the formula used by PerfectoidSpaces §§P4.15.2–P4.15.5 to descend surjectivity of perfectoidization. The universal case of Example 7.9 is reached by base change from Z_p{d, f_1,…,f_r}[δ(d)^{−1}]^∧.

<a id="layer-2-kunneth-formula"></a>

### 2.8 Colimit preservation and the Künneth formula

Descend supplied oriented colimit preservation to the nonoriented functor and its relative tensor-product formula. Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. The functor R ↦ Δ_{R/A} from derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras to commutative algebras in D_comp(A) (derived (p, I)-complete E_∞-A-algebras) commutes with all colimits. In particular it is symmetric monoidal: Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A, and for every diagram R_1 ← R_3 → R_2 the canonical map Δ_{R_1/A} ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{R_3/A}} Δ_{R_2/A} → Δ_{(R_1 ⊗̂^L_{R_3} R_2)/A} is an equivalence of commutative algebras with Frobenius, where the completion on the left is derived (p, I)-adic and on the right derived p-adic.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. D(A) is the derived ∞-category of A-modules with cohomological indexing; D_comp(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects with its completed tensor product; "discrete" means concentrated in degree 0.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 7.6 (5); p. 56; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Proposition 3.5.1 (published: Proposition 3.30) and its proof; p. 25.)

*Needs:* [§2.1](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology), [§2.3](#layer-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison), [§1.19](#layer-1-hodge-tate-comparison), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/symmetric-monoidal-infinity-category`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

The supplied oriented functor preserves completed colimits and the unit. These equivalences are compatible on overlaps, so complete descent gives them for the nonoriented functor. Applying this to the relative bar construction gives the pushout formula, with completion taken in the stated source and target categories.

**Checks.**

- Δ_{(A/I)⟨x,y⟩/A} ≃ Δ_{(A/I)⟨x⟩/A} ⊗̂^L_A Δ_{(A/I)⟨y⟩/A}. R_1 = R_2 = A/I over R_3 = (A/I)⟨x⟩: Δ of the derived self-intersection is A ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{(A/I)⟨x⟩/A}} A ([§2.13](#layer-2-derived-input-higher-homotopy)). Filtered colimits: Δ of a completed filtered colimit is the completed filtered colimit, as used in BS22 Proposition 7.10. ALB23 apply the formula to the product of an abelian scheme with itself.

<a id="layer-2-kunneth-formula-formal-schemes"></a>

### 2.9 Künneth formula for smooth formal schemes

Fix a bounded (A,I). Require the formal schemes X and Y over Spf(A/I) to be quasi-compact, quasi-separated and p-completely smooth. Their prismatic complexes satisfy RΓ(X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Y, Δ_{X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Y/A}) ≃ RΓ(X, Δ_{X/A}) ⊗̂^L_A RΓ(Y, Δ_{Y/A}), an isomorphism of commutative algebras in D_comp(A) compatible with Frobenius, the completed tensor product being derived (p, I)-adic.

The hypothesis quasi-compact quasi-separated is part of the statement in the arXiv v4 text of ALB23.

([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Corollary 3.5.2 (published: Corollary 3.31); p. 26.)

*Needs:* [§2.8](#layer-2-kunneth-formula), [§2.4](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-etale-descent), [§1.19](#layer-1-hodge-tate-comparison), [§1.4](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Proof route.** Define the external product by functoriality and use the affine Künneth equivalence on charts. Reduce modulo I, where qcqs formal cohomology has projection formula/flat base change and the finite conjugate filtration has the usual exterior-product graded pieces. Derived Nakayama proves the complete comparison.

**Checks.**

- X = Y = Spf(A/I)⟨x⟩ recovers the affine formula. For X, Y proper smooth both sides are perfect complexes of A-modules (Layer 1) and the completed tensor product is the ordinary derived tensor product. X = Spf(A/I): the identity.

<a id="layer-2-comparison-to-prisms"></a>

### 2.10 The comparison map from derived prismatic cohomology to prisms and to site cohomology

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. For every prism (B, J) over (A, I), bounded or not, equipped with an A/I-algebra map π_0(R) → B/J, there is a map ev_{(B,J)} : Δ_{R/A} → B of commutative algebras in D_comp(A), natural in (B, J) and in R, commuting with Frobenius (φ_B ∘ ev = ev ∘ φ_R), whose reduction modulo I is a map Δ̄_{R/A} → B/J of R-algebras. Restricting these evaluations to bounded prisms gives the comparison map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → lim_{(B,J) bounded} B = RΓ((π_0(R)/A)_Δ, O_Δ) to the cohomology of the prismatic site of π_0(R). Evaluation on all prisms also gives a map to the all-prism limit; the equality with bounded-site cohomology is not asserted for that limit in general. Construction: the functor R ↦ RΓ((π_0(R)/A)_Δ, O_Δ) restricts on p-completed polynomial algebras to Layer 1's functor, and c is the unique natural transformation out of the left Kan extension extending the identity there; concretely, for a resolution R_• → R by p-completely ind-smooth algebras, Δ_{R/A} = colim_{Δ^op} lim_{C ∈ (R_•/A)_Δ} C and (B, J) defines compatible objects of all (R_n/A)_Δ, which gives Δ_{R/A} → colim_{Δ^op} B = B. The map c_R is an isomorphism for p-completely smooth R ([§2.11](#layer-2-derived-agrees-with-site)), for regular quotients ([§2.12](#layer-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope)) and for quasiregular semiperfectoid R over a perfect prism (PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3). It is not an isomorphism in general: the target depends only on π_0(R) and lies in D^{≥0}, whereas Δ_{R/A} does not ([§2.13](#layer-2-derived-input-higher-homotopy)).

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. The cohomology of O_Δ on the site of bounded prisms is the limit over the category, because O_Δ is a sheaf with vanishing higher Čech cohomology (Layer 1, BS22 Corollary 3.12 and Remark 4.5). When Δ_{R/A} is discrete, ev_{(B,J)} is a map of δ-rings ([§2.11](#layer-2-derived-agrees-with-site)).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Proof of Lemma 7.7 (3); p. 57; [BS22](#ref-bs22), §8.1, before Proposition 8.5; p. 64; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), §3.4, before Proposition 3.4.1; p. 24.)

*Needs:* [§2.1](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology), [§1.7](#layer-1-cech-alexander-complex), [§1.1](#layer-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf), [§1.2](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-site), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Derived.toPrism`: For a prism (B, J) over (A, I) and an A/I-algebra map R → B/J, the map ev : Δ_{R/A} → B in D(A).
- `Prismatic.Derived.toPrism_frobenius`: ev commutes with the Frobenius of Δ_{R/A} and of B.
- `Prismatic.Derived.toPrism_naturality`: For a map of prisms (B, J) → (B′, J′) over (A, I) compatible with the maps from R, ev′ is ev followed by B → B′.
- `Prismatic.Derived.siteCohomology`: The object RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) of D(A), the limit of B over all bounded prisms (B, J) over (A, I) with a map R → B/J.
- `Prismatic.Derived.toSite`: The comparison map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ).
- `Prismatic.Derived.toSite_isIso_of_smooth`: For R smooth over A/I the map c_R is an isomorphism.

**Proof route.** The bounded weakly initial envelope and its Čech nerve compute the smooth theory even against all target prisms. Polynomial left Kan extension therefore maps naturally to the site limit under π₀(R), and projection to each prism gives evaluation. These maps preserve products, Frobenius and the reduced R-algebra structure by their construction.

**Checks.**

- `pr2_to_prism_base`: For R = A/I and (B, J) = (A, I), the map Δ_{(A/I)/A} → A is an isomorphism.
- `pr2_to_site_smooth`: For R = A/I × A/I the comparison map c_R is an isomorphism.
- `pr2_to_prism_frobenius_base`: For R = A/I and (B, J) = (A, I) the map ev commutes with φ_A.
- `pr2_evaluation_base_identity`: For R=A/I and the base-prism object (A,I,id), evaluation ev:Δ_(R/A)→A is the identity under Δ_(R/A)=A; the site and all-prism limit comparison maps have this same base value.

- R = A/I: Δ_{R/A} = A and ev_{(A,I)} is the identity. For p-completely smooth R the map c_R is an isomorphism. For R = A/I ⊗^L_{(A/I)⟨x⟩} A/I the map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → A is not an isomorphism. For a perfect prism and (B, J) perfect, ev_{(B,J)} factors through the perfection Δ_{R/A,perf}.

<a id="layer-2-derived-agrees-with-site"></a>

### 2.11 Agreement with site cohomology: smooth algebras and the discrete case

Extend the supplied discrete-case and smooth-site statements by descent over arbitrary bounded prisms; keep their weak-initiality qualification. Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (a) If R is a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra, the derived Δ_{R/A} is the site cohomology RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) of Layer 1, compatibly with Frobenius and with the Hodge–Tate comparison; the conjugate filtration is the canonical filtration. (b) Let R be a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra such that Δ̄_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0. Then: (1) Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free, and the Frobenius φ_R lifts naturally to a δ-A-algebra structure on the ring Δ_{R/A}; (2) (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is a prism over (A, I), equipped with a map R → Δ̄_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A}/IΔ_{R/A}; it is bounded exactly when Δ̄_{R/A} has bounded p^∞-torsion; (3) among prisms over (A,I) with a specified R→B/J there exists an initial prism; (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is weakly initial in it (the maps being those of [§2.10](#layer-2-comparison-to-prisms), which are δ-maps), and the initial object is the image of an idempotent endomorphism of (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}). The statement does not assert that (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is initial; Bhatt and Scholze conjecture this. It is proved in the cases of [§2.12](#layer-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope) and The prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, where consequently Δ_{R/A} computes the cohomology of the prismatic site of R.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed. In (b) the category in (3) consists of all prisms over (A, I), bounded or not. A discrete Δ_{R/A} is not called "the initial object" here: the source proves weak initiality, and that the initial object is a retract.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 7.7 and its proof; p. 57; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 7.6 (1); p. 56.)

Use the supplied oriented smooth and discrete-case constructions, including the natural Witt section and idempotent retract, on orientation charts. Their naturality and complete descent glue the delta structure, prism and comparison maps; the idempotent argument applies in the relative category containing all target prisms. The result remains weak initiality in this range; the stronger quotient theorem is proved separately below.

**Checks.**

- R = A/I: the prism is (A, I), which is initial. R p-completely smooth of positive relative dimension: Δ̄_{R/A} is not discrete and (b) does not apply. R = (A/I)/(f): (b) applies and the idempotent is the identity ([§2.12](#layer-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope)). R perfectoid over a perfect prism: Δ_{R/A} = A_inf(R) with its unique δ-structure.

<a id="layer-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope"></a>

### 2.12 Relative initiality for quasiregular quotients

Extend the supplied regular-quotient and perfect-base QRSP calculations to an arbitrary bounded prism (A,I) and a surjection A/I→S. Assume S is derived p-complete with bounded p-power torsion and (L_(S/(A/I))[−1])^∧_p is p-completely flat over S. Prove that Δ_(S/A) is a discrete delta-A-algebra, its Hodge–Tate reduction is p-completely faithfully flat over S with bounded p-power torsion, and (Δ_(S/A),IΔ_(S/A)) is initial among **all** prisms over A equipped with S→B/IB, including unbounded targets. For I=(d), identify it with the general envelope of (A,ker(A→S)). The original kernel need not be generated by a regular sequence, and the base need not be perfect; initiality here is relative to its fixed A-map. ([KY](#ref-ky), Proposition 4.17 and Lemma 4.18 with proof, pp.39–40; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollary 4.1.17 and Remark 4.1.20, pp.81–82, Remark 4.3.9 and Lemma 4.3.10, p.87.)

The API is `Prismatic.quasiregularQuotient.initial`, the lift equivalence for all target prisms; `Prismatic.quasiregularQuotient.bounded`, including the complete faithful flatness of the reduction; `Prismatic.quasiregularQuotient.envelopeEquiv`, respecting δ, A and the map from S; and `Prismatic.quasiregularQuotient.map`, the unique functorial map for maps of quotient diagrams satisfying these hypotheses. It does not assert that arbitrary changes of A induce equivalences.

The conjugate graded pieces Γ^i_S((L_(S/(A/I))[−1])^∧_p){−i}^∧_p are discrete and p-completely flat, giving discreteness and boundedness of the reduction; the supplied discrete-prism construction gives a natural idempotent e_S whose image is initial, so it remains to show e_S=id. For generators f_j of ker(A/I→S), the auxiliary quotient S′=((A/I)⟨X_j^(1/p^∞)⟩/(X_j−f_j))^∧_p maps to S; its relation classes surject onto the shifted completed cotangent complex modulo p, so divided powers and the conjugate filtration give a surjection Δ_(S′/A)→Δ_(S/A), and naturality reduces the idempotent identity to S′. Completed filtered passage reduces S′ to finitely many variables; extend A to A′=(A[X_1^(1/p^∞),…,X_r^(1/p^∞)])^∧_(p,I), with δ of each root zero, whose relatively p-completely formally étale reduction leaves Δ unchanged, and use that X_i−f_i is a successive monic regular sequence at every finite root level, with free quotients over A/I. Thus the supplied regular-quotient calculation over A′ gives e=id, hence initiality for S; only this auxiliary presentation is regular. The general-envelope comparison then follows from the same mapping problem, with boundedness already proved separately by Hodge–Tate theory. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 7.7, pp.57–58, Example 7.9 and Proposition 7.10, pp.59–60.)

**Checks.**

- `quasiregularQuotient_identity`: S=A/I gives the relative prism A, including bounded nonperfect A.
- `quasiregularQuotient_fatPoint`: for A=Z_p⟨x⟩, δ(x)=0, I=(p), and S=F_p[x]/(x²), the shifted cotangent complex over F_p[x] has rank one. The result adjoins x²/p and its delta relations although S need not be semiperfectoid.
- `quasiregularQuotient_unboundedTargets`: the lift equivalence must hold for unbounded targets as well as the bounded site.
- `quasiregularQuotient_nonsurjective`: F_p→F_p[x] is not a surjection and has the degree-zero cotangent generator dx; its positive-dimensional Hodge–Tate complex does not satisfy this discrete initiality assertion.
- In the regular case with r relations, gr_i is free of rank binom(r+i−1,i), interpreted as rank one for i=0 and zero for i>0 when r=0. At (A,I)=(Z_p⟨x⟩,(p)) with f=x^p, the envelope is the p-completed PD envelope of (x); over A_inf(O_C) with f=p it is A_inf{p/ξ}^∧.

*Needs:* [the supplied affine derived, discrete-prism and regular-quotient inputs](#ps-affine), [general envelopes](#layer-0-general-prismatic-envelope), derived Hodge–Tate comparison and conjugate filtration, DD.0 cotangent complexes, DD.1 complete flatness and completion, animated delta algebras. The log application first identifies its complex with this ordinary relative complex after exactification and verifies the stated cotangent and torsion hypotheses.

<a id="layer-2-derived-input-higher-homotopy"></a>

### 2.13 A derived input with nonzero higher homotopy

Let B=A/I≠0 for a bounded prism (A,I), and put R=B⊗̂ᴸ_{B⟨x⟩}B, with x↦0 on both sides. This is the free p-complete animated B-algebra on B[1]; its underlying B-complex is B⊕B[1]. Prove the following statements.

1. L_{R/B}≃R[1], and gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A}≃R{−i} for every i≥0.
2. Δ̄_{R/A} lies in D^{[−1,0]}. The inclusion Fil_0^conj=R has an R-linear retraction after forgetting the filtration, so H^{−1}(Δ̄_{R/A}) contains B as a direct summand. The retraction is not asserted canonical.
3. Δ_{R/A}≃A⊗̂ᴸ_{Δ_{B⟨x⟩/A}}A. The comparison c_R:Δ_{R/A}→Δ_{π₀R/A}=A is not an equivalence: its reduction has nonzero negative cohomology, whereas A⊗ᴸ_A B=B.
4. Nondiscreteness of R does not imply nondiscreteness of Δ_{R/A}. For (A,I)=(Z_p,(p)), let P=Γ_{Z_p}(Z_p·u) be the divided power polynomial algebra, with basis u^{[n]}, and let P̂ be its derived p-completion. Then Δ_{R/Z_p} is represented by the two-term complex [P̂ ε → P̂] in degrees [−1,0], with differential εu^{[n]}↦(n+1)u^{[n+1]}. This differential is injective. Consequently Δ_{R/Z_p} is the discrete ring coker(u:P̂→P̂), with nonzero p-torsion. In particular the stronger assertion that this example always has nondiscrete unreduced cohomology is false.

Twists are tensor powers of the invertible B-module I/I². Tensor products and the displayed completions are derived. No conclusion about discreteness before reduction is drawn from (2). In (4), P̂ consists of coefficient sequences tending to zero p-adically in the divided power basis; the quotient is the actual cokernel of the completed multiplication map. It is not replaced by a coefficientwise quotient or an unqualified ordinary completion of its uncompleted cokernel.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 7.6, p.56, and Theorem 5.2, pp.44–45; [Bha12](#ref-bha12), Lemma 8.3(3)–(4), Theorem 8.4 and the proof of Proposition 8.5, pp.31–32; Warning 8.9, p.33. The two-term model is the derived base-change calculation in that proof with the parameter specialized to zero; the regular-quotient conclusion of Proposition 8.5 is not applied to a zero relation.)

*Needs:* [§2.1](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology), [§2.3](#layer-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison), [§2.8](#layer-2-kunneth-formula), [§2.10](#layer-2-comparison-to-prisms), [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/animated-commutative-rings`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`.

For (1), cotangent base change gives L_{R/B}=R[1], and exterior/divided-power décalage gives ∧^i_R(R[1])[−i]=R. For (2), write F_i=Fil_i^conj. Inductively F_i∈D^{[−1,0]}; the extension F_{i−1}→F_i→R{−i} splits in D(R), since Hom_R(R{−i},F_{i−1}[1])=H¹(F_{i−1}{i})=0. Choose each splitting to retain the preceding inclusion. Thus the uncompleted filtered colimit is a direct sum of twists of R, and its first summand R has a compatible retraction. Its two homology modules are sums of invertible B-modules and have the same uniform bound on p-power torsion as B. Derived p-completion therefore has no extra cohomology outside [−1,0]; completing the retraction preserves the complete summand R. This proves survival through completion, rather than presuming it from the finite stages. Part (3) is completed Künneth, followed by reduction.

For (4), use the free animated Z_p-lift R̃=Z_p⊗ᴸ_{Z_p[x]}Z_p of R. The smooth crystalline comparison, extended along its polynomial simplicial resolution, identifies Δ_{R/Z_p} with the p-completed derived de Rham complex of R̃/Z_p. Derived de Rham base change along Z_p[x]→Z_p, x↦0, applied to Z_p[x]→Z_p, x↦0, gives P̂⊗̂ᴸ_{Z_p[x]}Z_p, where x acts on P̂ by u. Resolve Z_p over Z_p[x] by [Z_p[x]→Z_p[x]], multiplication by x; the resulting differential is multiplication by u. As u·u^{[n]}=(n+1)u^{[n+1]}, it has zero kernel even on restricted coefficient sequences. The class of u^{[p]} in the cokernel is nonzero (reduce its coefficient modulo p), while p·u^{[p]}=u·u^{[p−1]} vanishes. All steps use p-completion, with no Hodge completion.

**Checks.**

- `DerivedPrismatic.derivedInput_survives_completion`: R is a retract of Δ̄ after completion; its nonzero H^{−1}=B cannot disappear at the completed colimit.
- `DerivedPrismatic.derivedInput_not_piZero`: The reduced comparison to B kills that negative direct summand, so c_R is not an equivalence.
- `DerivedPrismatic.crystalline_derivedInput_discrete`: In the crystalline example multiplication by u on P̂ is injective, although its reduction modulo p has kernel containing u^{[p−1]}. The unreduced complex is discrete and the reduced complex is not.
- `DerivedPrismatic.crystalline_derivedInput_torsion`: The nonzero class u^{[p]} is killed by p; at p=2 this is u^{[2]}, with u·u=2u^{[2]}.
- `DerivedPrismatic.reduction_not_discreteness_test`: The discrete A-module A/I has H^{−1}((A/I)⊗ᴸ_A A/I)=I/I². This independently rejects the same invalid inference without a prismatic calculation.

- The crystalline calculation gives negative reduced classes εu^{[kp−1]} for k≥1 and degree-zero reduced classes u^{[kp]} for k≥0. These are direct sums over F_p after reduction, since restricted p-adic coefficients reduce to finite support. They agree with the conjugate-filtration calculation. Base change between bounded prisms carries the self-intersection and the Künneth formula to the corresponding example; no assertion of unreduced nondiscreteness accompanies that base change.

<a id="layer-2-quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms"></a>

### 2.14 Lifting quasisyntomic covers to the prismatic site

Glue the supplied ring-level root covers into covers of formal prismatic sites over arbitrary bounded, possibly nonorientable, bases. Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a quasisyntomic A/I-algebra: R is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and A/I → R is a quasisyntomic map (p-completely flat, with L_{R/(A/I)} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; BMS2 Definition 4.10). Then there is an object (B → B/IB ← R) of (R/A)_Δ such that R → B/IB is p-completely faithfully flat. One may take B = Δ_{S/A}, where S := (A/I)⟨x_j^{1/p^∞} : j ∈ J⟩ ⊗̂^L_{(A/I)⟨x_j : j ∈ J⟩} R for a surjection (A/I)⟨x_j : j ∈ J⟩ → R; then R → S is a quasisyntomic cover, S/p is relatively semiperfect over A/(I, p), (L_{S/(A/I)})^∧[−1] is a p-completely flat S-module, and S → Δ̄_{S/A} is p-completely faithfully flat. Consequently: (1) the map A→B is completely flat for (p,I), and is completely faithfully flat whenever A/I→R is so for p; (2) if A is perfect, (A, I) → (B, IB)_perf is flat, and faithfully flat if A/I → R is p-completely faithfully flat.

### 2.15 Quasisyntomic descent and unfolding

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. Let C_{A/I} be the category of p-complete A/I-algebras B with bounded p^∞-torsion such that L_{B/(A/I)} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0], and call B → C in C_{A/I} a cover if it is a quasisyntomic cover (p-completely faithfully flat with L_{C/B} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]). (1) For every cover B → C with p-completed Čech nerve C^• (each C^n is discrete, of bounded p^∞-torsion and in C_{A/I}), the maps Δ_{B/A} → lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{C^n/A}, Δ̄_{B/A} → lim Δ̄_{C^n/A} and Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{B/A} → lim Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{C^n/A}, for every i, are equivalences. So B ↦ Δ_{B/A} is a sheaf on C_{A/I}^op with values in commutative algebras with Frobenius in D_comp(A). (2) If (A, I) is perfect, C_{A/I} contains the category QSyn_{A/I} of all maps A/I → B with B a quasisyntomic ring (BMS2 Variant 4.33 and Lemma 4.34), so B ↦ Δ_{B/A} is a sheaf for the quasisyntomic topology on QSyn_{A/I}. (3) Unfolding: for perfect (A, I) and B in QSyn_{A/I}, choose a quasisyntomic cover B → S with S quasiregular semiperfectoid. All terms S^n of its Čech nerve are quasiregular semiperfectoid and Δ_{B/A} ≃ lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S^n}, a limit of discrete δ-rings; thus Δ_{−/A} on QSyn_{A/I} is the unfolding (BMS2 Proposition 4.31) of S ↦ Δ_S on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. In particular Δ_{B/A} ∈ D^{≥0}, and Δ_{B/A} with its Frobenius does not depend on the perfect prism (A, I) under B.

### 2.16 a singular quasiregular semiperfectoid algebra

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)), B := R⟨x, y⟩/(xy) the p-completed construction, and S := R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩/(xy). Then: (1) B is quasisyntomic and not p-completely smooth over R; B → S is a quasisyntomic cover; S is quasiregular semiperfectoid and not perfectoid, since x^{1/p}y^{1/p} is a nonzero nilpotent when R ≠ 0. (2) Δ_S ≃ A′{[x^♭][y^♭]/d}^∧ with A′ = A_inf(R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩); Δ̄_S is p-completely faithfully flat over S, with gr_i^conj ≃ S{−i} generated by the i-th divided power of the class of xy. (3) Δ_{B/A} ≃ lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S^n}, where S^n is the (n+1)-fold completed tensor power of S over B; each S^n is quasiregular semiperfectoid, for instance S^1 = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}, x′^{1/p^∞}, y′^{1/p^∞}⟩/(xy, x − x′, y − y′). (4) gr_i^conj Δ̄_{B/A} ≃ (∧^i L_{B/R}){−i}[−i] with L_{B/R} ≃ [B → B dx ⊕ B dy], 1 ↦ y dx + x dy, in degrees −1, 0; for i ≥ 2 the complex ∧^i L_{B/R}[−i] is the Koszul complex of (y, x) on B placed in degrees 0, 1, 2, with H^0 = 0, H^2 = B/(x, y) = R and H^1 ≠ 0. So the conjugate filtration of the singular B has infinitely many nonzero graded pieces, in contrast with a p-completely smooth algebra of relative dimension 1. (5) For an infinite family (f_j), put S′ = R⟨X_j^{1/p^∞} : j ∈ J⟩/(X_j − f_j : j ∈ J)^∧. Its prism is the completed filtered colimit of the envelopes of the finite subfamilies. A concrete example requiring infinitely many relations is R=F_p, J infinite and every f_j=0: the ring S′≠0 is quasiregular semiperfectoid and cannot be presented as a quotient of a perfectoid ring by a finite regular sequence.

### 2.17 Derived crystalline comparison

Let k be a perfect F_p-algebra and (A, I) = (W(k), (p)) the corresponding crystalline perfect prism. For a derived p-complete simplicial k-algebra S put S^{(1)} := S ⊗^L_{k,φ} k, and let RΓ_crys(S/A) be the derived crystalline cohomology of S over A: the p-completed left Kan extension of P ↦ RΓ_crys(P/A) from finitely generated polynomial k-algebras (for k = F_p the derived de Rham–Witt complex LWΩ_S of BMS2 §8.2); its reduction modulo p is the derived de Rham complex dR_{S/k} relative to k. It is not the p-completed derived de Rham cohomology of S over A: dR^∧_{k/W(k)} = (W(k)⟨x⟩/(x − p))^∧ ≠ W(k). Then there are natural isomorphisms of commutative algebras in D_comp(A), compatible with Frobenius, Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A ≃ Δ_{S^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(S/A), extending the crystalline comparison Δ_{P^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(P/A) of Layer 1 for smooth k-algebras P. The Frobenius twist is part of the statement: Δ_{S/A} itself is not A-linearly isomorphic to RΓ_crys(S/A) in general.

### 2.18 In characteristic p the prism of a quasiregular semiperfect ring is A_crys

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with pS = 0 (a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra), k := S^♭ the inverse-limit perfection of S, so that k → S is surjective, and A := W(k) with the crystalline perfect prism (A, (p)). (3) If S = k/(x) for a nonzerodivisor x ∈ k, then Δ_{S/W(k)} = W(k){[x]/p}^∧ and A_crys(S) = W(k){[x]^p/p}^∧. ### 2.20 Perfection of derived prismatic cohomology and perfectoidization

Fix a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, I) = (A_inf(R), ker θ), I = (d), and a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S. It is a derived (p, I)-complete commutative algebra in D(A) with a φ_A-semilinear automorphism φ induced by φ_S and a canonical map can : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A,perf} of commutative algebras commuting with Frobenius. (2) The perfectoidization of S is S_perfd := Δ_{S/A,perf} ⊗^L_A A/I in D(R), a derived p-complete commutative algebra with a map S → Δ̄_{S/A} → S_perfd. Both constructions are functorial in S. They are objects distinct from Δ_{S/A} and Δ̄_{S/A}: can is an equivalence exactly when φ_S is one ([§2.21](#layer-2-perfection-comparison)). The definition is made relative to the base (A, I); see the hypotheses.

### 2.21 Comparison of the perfected and the unperfected theory

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism, R = A/I, and S a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra. (2) If S is a perfectoid R-algebra then L_{S/R} vanishes after derived p-completion, Δ̄_{S/A} = S, Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), can is an equivalence and S_perfd = S. (3) For every perfect prism (B, J) over (A, I) with a map π_0(S) → B/J, the map ev_{(B,J)} of [§2.10](#layer-2-comparison-to-prisms) factors uniquely through can; these factorisations assemble to Δ_{S/A,perf} → RΓ((S/A)_Δ^perf, O_Δ) = lim_{S → R′} A_inf(R′), the limit over all maps from S to perfectoid rings R′. (4) Characteristic p (BS22 Example 8.3): for a crystalline perfect prism (A, I) = (W(k), (p)), k a perfect F_p-algebra (in the source k = F_p), and a k-algebra S, the Frobenius of Δ_{S/A}/p preserves the conjugate filtration and acts on gr_i^conj = ∧^i L_{S/k}[−i] through the map induced by the Frobenius of S, which is zero for i ≠ 0; hence S_perf := colim_φ S ≃ S_perfd through the Frobenius-equivariant map S → Δ̄_{S/A}. (5) The two theories differ: for S = F_p[x] over (Z_p, (p)), H^0(Δ̄_{S/A}) = F_p[x] and H^1(Δ̄_{S/A}) = Ω^1_{F_p[x]/F_p} ≠ 0, while S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}] is discrete. Neither theory is obtained from the other by a formal substitution: Δ_{S/A,perf} forgets the conjugate filtration in positive degrees, and Δ_{S/A} is not recovered from Δ_{S/A,perf}.

(A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (Layer 0). S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed. That the map in (3) is an equivalence is BS22 Proposition 8.5; (3) only constructs it. In (4) the base is crystalline; for a perfect base of mixed characteristic and pS = 0 the source reduces to the base (Z_p, (p)) by independence of the base, which requires the same comparison.

### 2.22 Coconnectivity of perfectoidizations

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with R = A/I and d a generator of I. For every derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S, both Δ_{S/A,perf} and S_perfd lie in D^{≥0}. S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed. ### 2.26 Finite projective modules over derived p-complete rings and their descent

Let R be a derived p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion. Then the natural functor from finite projective R-modules to the 2-limit over n of the categories of finite projective R/p^n-modules is an equivalence. Finite projective modules therefore have effective descent for p-completely faithfully flat covers between derived p-complete rings of bounded p-power torsion: for a p-completely faithfully flat map R → R′ of such rings, finite projective R-modules are equivalent to finite projective R′-modules with a descent datum over the p-completed tensor products R′ ⊗̂_R R′ and R′ ⊗̂_R R′ ⊗̂_R R′.

a derived p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion is classically p-adically complete (DD.1). The completed tensor products are discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion (BMS2 Lemma 4.7 and Corollary 4.8).

([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Appendix A, Lemma A.1 (published: Lemma A.1) and its proof; p. 94; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Corollary 4.8; p. 20.)

*Needs:* `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, Mathlib `Module.Projective`, Mathlib `Module.Finite`, Mathlib `Module.FaithfullyFlat`, Mathlib `IsAdicComplete`.

**Proof route.** For a compatible finite-projective tower choose a fixed finite set of generators modulo J and lift generators and splittings successively; the compatible idempotent matrices converge in the complete matrix ring and realize the tower. Hom between finite projectives is a complete direct summand of a matrix module, giving full faithfulness and composition, while Nakayama detects rank one. Reuse Tau Ceti’s single-idempotent lifting step under its completeness hypothesis; the compatible-system equivalence and rank control are the additional assertions (Stacks 0D4B).

Apply this to J=(p). For a p-completely faithfully flat map R → R′ of p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion, R/p^n → R′/p^n is faithfully flat for all n (BMS2 Corollary 4.8 (3); flatness from Lemma 4.7, surjectivity on spectra from n = 1). Faithfully flat descent for finite projective modules along R/p^n → R′/p^n (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1), and a 2-limit of stacks is a stack.

**Checks for complete-projective effectivity.** A compatible system (Z/p^n)^r, including r=0, has limit Z_p^r and its endomorphism ring is M_r(Z_p), with all entries recovered from the tower. Compatible idempotents diag(1,0) over (Z/p^n)^2 give Z_p⊕0, so taking the inverse limit of the ambient free modules alone gives the wrong rank. For the rank-one system, multiplication by compatible units u_n has limit multiplication by the unit lim u_n; a merely compatible sequence of objects without transition identifications is not descent data. Replacing the complete ring Z_p by Z makes full faithfulness fail already on End(Z), since lim Z/p^n=Z_p.

- R = Z_p: finite free Z_p-modules are compatible systems of finite free Z/p^n-modules. R → R′ = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩: a finite projective R′-module with descent datum descends to R. The hypothesis of bounded p^∞-torsion is used to pass between derived and classical completeness and to make R/p^n → R′/p^n flat.

### 2.27 Descent of finite projective modules along faithfully flat maps of prisms

For bounded prisms, assigning to (A,I) the category of finite projective A-modules satisfies effective completely faithfully flat descent. Explicitly: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, IB) with A → B (p, I)-completely faithfully flat, with Čech nerve B^• (B^n the (n+1)-fold derived (p, I)-completed tensor power of B over A, again a bounded prism), the category of finite projective A-modules is equivalent to the category of finite projective B-modules M equipped with an isomorphism of the two base changes of M to B^1 satisfying the cocycle condition over B^2.

A map of prisms is faithfully flat when A → B is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat (Layer 0); the appendix of ALB23 recalls this with the word "faithfully" omitted.

([ALB23](#ref-alb23), Appendix A, Proposition A.3 (published: Proposition A.3) and its proof; p. 94.)

*Needs:* [§2.26](#layer-2-finite-projective-modules-p-complete), [§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§1.1](#layer-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, Mathlib `Module.Projective`, Mathlib `Module.Finite`.

For the proof, a bounded prism is classically (p, I)-complete (Layer 0), hence classically I-adically complete because I is finitely generated; so finite projective A-modules are compatible systems of finite projective A/I^n-modules (Stacks Project, Tag 0D4B). A 2-limit of stacks is a stack, so it suffices that (A, I) ↦ {finite projective A/I^n-modules} is a stack for every n. For a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms, A/I^n → B/I^nB = B ⊗^L_A A/I^n is a p-completely faithfully flat map of rings with bounded p^∞-torsion (A/I^n is a successive extension of the modules I^k/I^{k+1}, invertible over A/I); apply [§2.26](#layer-2-finite-projective-modules-p-complete).

**Checks.**

- Finite projective modules over A_inf descend along the faithfully flat cover of prisms produced by [§2.14](#layer-2-quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms). Rank one: invertible modules, in particular Breuil–Kisin twists, satisfy descent on the site of bounded prisms. Prismatic crystals in vector bundles on the absolute prismatic site form a stack (used by Layer 7 and by ALB23 for prismatic Dieudonné crystals).

<a id="layer-2-perfect-site-arc-comparison"></a>

### 2.28 Perfect-site comparison, base independence and arc excision

Extend the supplied semiperfectoid perfect-site calculation to general animated inputs, base independence and arc excision. Prove `Prismatic.Perfection.perfectSite_equiv`: for a perfect prism (A,I), R=A/I and a derived p-complete animated R-algebra S, the canonical map Δ_(S/A),perf→RΓ((S/A)_Δ^perf,O_Δ) is an equivalence for every topology between the flat and chaotic topologies. Consequently S_perfd=lim_(S→T perfectoid) T in derived p-complete E_∞ rings, depends only on π₀S, and is independent of the perfect base. Prove `Prismatic.Perfectoidization.arc_sections` and `arc_excision`: this limit is RΓ_arc(Spf S,O); if S→S′ is an isomorphism on rank-one p-complete valuation points outside a derived p-complete ideal J, then the square with vertices S_perfd, S′_perfd, (S/J)_perfd and (S′/J)_perfd is cartesian. Here S′/J is the completed quotient by the image ideal, and the outside-J condition means existence and uniqueness of the extension of every valuation point not killing J. These are local prerequisites, not inputs from a later roadmap. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 8.5, pp.64–66; Corollaries 8.11–8.12, pp.68–69.)

*Needs:* [§2.24](#layer-2-perfection-descendable), [§2.22](#layer-2-perfectoidization-coconnective), [§2.25](#layer-2-connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§2.0](#layer-2-local-arc-foundations), `PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2`, `PerfectoidSpaces §§P4.15.2–P4.15.3`, `PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.5`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/module-descent-and-functoriality`.

**Proof route.** Adjoin solutions to x=X^p+pY successively through a filtered ordinal, preserving extension of maps to perfectoid targets; the completed semiperfectoid result has a universal perfectoid quotient. This yields a weakly final perfectoid point whose Čech resolution computes the structure sheaf by effective perfectoid descent. Check completed filtered-colimit compatibility on these functorial root covers and finite Čech degrees, rather than interchanging arbitrary limits and colimits.

Now reduce π₀S to a topologically finitely generated algebra, choose R⟨X₁,…,X_r⟩→S surjective on π₀, and extract all roots of the X_i. The completed *derived* Čech nerve has semiperfectoid π₀ in every degree. The descendability theorem computes both sides on this nerve. For semiperfectoid π₀S the completed exterior powers of L_(S/Z_p)[−1] are connective. Hodge–Tate then makes Δ connective, while the P⁰ theorem makes its perfection coconnective. Thus the perfection is a discrete perfect δ-ring and S_perfd is perfectoid. It maps split-surjectively to the universal perfectoid quotient of π₀S. To show that this split surjection is an isomorphism, enlarge the perfectoid base so that it surjects onto π₀S, and use André's flat cover to give compatible roots to generators f_j of its kernel. The map from R⟨X_j^(1/p^∞)⟩/(X_j), sending X_j^(1/p^n) to f_j^(1/p^n), is surjective on π₀ and on π₁ of the cotangent complex modulo p. The conjugate filtration therefore gives a surjection on perfectoidizations. Finite sets of j reduce to the explicit QRSP prism and radical root-quotient calculation. Passing to completed filtered colimits proves surjectivity of S→S_perfd. The universal quotient and S_perfd now have mutually inverse unit-preserving maps. All constructions commute with the Čech augmentation, so the resulting comparison is canonical for general animated S and proves both asserted independences.

On affine perfectoids, the arc structure sheaf has no higher cohomology by the local arc prefix. Passing from the arc to the chaotic perfectoid site therefore gives the same derived limit and proves arc_sections. For excision, the valuation condition makes Spf S′⊔Spf(S/J)→Spf S an arc cover. Its twofold fibre product is covered by the diagonal S′ and the two copies of S′/J over S/J. Descent identifies the represented arc sheaf of S with the pushout of the represented sheaves of S′ and S/J along S′/J. Applying derived sections of O turns this pushout into the displayed pullback, with its E_∞ structure. This proof includes integral universal homeomorphisms and does not assume a flat map S→S′.

**Checks.** For S perfectoid, the limit is S and the unit is the identity. For S=F_p[x], it is F_p[x^(1/p^∞)]; for S=F_p[x^(1/p^∞)]/(x), it is F_p, so the unit need not be injective. An animated S and π₀S have identical perfectoidizations even when their unperfected Δ differ, as in [§2.13](#layer-2-derived-input-higher-homotopy). For J=0 the excision square has identical vertical maps; for J=S the outside condition forces an equivalence on arc points and the lower row is zero. Neither control justifies arbitrary base change before perfection.

### 2.29 Integral perfectoidization and arbitrary-ideal almost purity

Prove `Prismatic.Perfectoidization.integral_discrete`: if R is perfectoid with perfect prism (A,I) and S is the p-completion of an integral R-algebra, then Δ_(S/A),perf is a discrete perfect p-complete δ-A-algebra and S_perfd is perfectoid. Prove `Prismatic.Perfectoidization.almostPurity`: for a finitely presented finite R-algebra S that is finite étale away from a finitely generated ideal J, S→S_perfd is an isomorphism there and R/p^n→S_perfd/p^n is almost finite projective and almost unramified for the ideal J_perfd=ker(R→(R/J)_perfd), for every n>0. If a finite group G acts on S and Spec S→Spec R is a G-torsor outside V(J), then R→S_perfd is a J-almost G-Galois cover. These targets extend the universal *semiperfectoid* quotient without using a later integral-perfectoidization roadmap as a prerequisite. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Propositions 10.2–10.4, Lemma 10.5, pp.78–79; Proposition 10.8, Theorems 10.9, 10.11, Lemma 10.12, pp.80–83.)

*Needs:* [§2.28](#layer-2-perfect-site-arc-comparison), [§2.23](#layer-2-perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal), [§2.25](#layer-2-connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid), [PerfectoidQuotients §0.0](#pq-tor), `PerfectoidSpaces P0`, `PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2`, `PerfectoidSpaces §§P4.15.2–P4.15.3`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract`.

**Proof route.** For Q=(R/J)_perfd and K=ker(R→Q), perfectoid Tor-independence gives Q⊗̂_RQ=Q, K⊗̂_RK=K and K⊗̂_RQ=0; the resulting fully faithful complete Q-module subcategory and truncation triangle give the stated connectivity criterion. Compatible roots express the principal K/p^n as a filtered root-difference colimit of R/p^n, giving the needed flatness; test general J on its generators. The finite torsor identity S⊗̂_RS≃∏_GS proves almost finite projectivity/unramifiedness and subgroup descent without division by |G|.

Prove the almost version of almostPurity *before* integral_discrete. Arc excision permits an integral change of model that is unchanged outside J. André's cover permits absolutely integrally closed R; every finite étale cover is then Zariski locally split. Reduce to a principal generator on each of finitely many opens, change the integral model to the split torsor, and check the Galois identities there. For a non-Galois constant degree r cover take its Σ_r closure and Σ_(r−1) invariants. The varying-degree case decomposes into finitely many clopen pieces outside J; the perfectoidizations of their integral images, together with arc excision, reduce to constant degree. This proves J-almost connectivity and the almost-module conclusions without presupposing discreteness.

To prove integral_discrete, completed filtered colimits reduce to a finitely presented finite map. Establish `Prismatic.Integral.finiteStratification`: there are g₁,…,g_m generating the unit ideal such that each reduced locally closed stratum R_i=R/(g₁,…,g_(i−1))_red[1/g_i] maps to the analogous S_i through a finite étale algebra followed by a universal homeomorphism, and p is either zero or invertible on the stratum. Prove this by descending the finite presentation to a noetherian Z_(p)-algebra, separating the separable and purely inseparable factors over its finitely many generic fields, spreading over an open, and noetherian induction on the complement. Replace each g_i in the ordered sequence by p g_i followed by g_i: on the first open p is invertible, while on the second reduced stratum p g_i=0 and g_i is invertible, so p=0. This auxiliary lemma concerns arbitrary finite presentations, rather than assuming the original perfectoid ring noetherian.

Induct on m. For m=1 the reduced algebra is finite étale over R and thus perfectoid; nilpotent invariance of arc sections gives S_perfd. In the inductive step, (S/g₁)_perfd is connective by induction and symmetric monoidality. Over R[1/g₁] the finite étale factor equals S_red[1/g₁]: if p is invertible this is part of the stratification; if p=0, the source is perfect and a universal homeomorphism from a perfect ring to a reduced ring is an isomorphism. Replace S by the integral closure of R in that finite étale algebra. Excision changes its perfectoidization only g₁-almost, and the almost theorem gives g₁-almost connectivity. The connectivity criterion now gives actual connectivity. Coconnectivity and [§2.25](#layer-2-connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid) finish integral_discrete. Finally combine discreteness with the already proved almost version to obtain almostPurity. This order avoids using the full almost-purity theorem to prove its own discreteness hypothesis.

**Checks.** An integral perfectoid S remains S. A finite étale product R^r remains R^r with its product idempotents. For perfect R of characteristic p and S=R[z]/(z^p−a), perfectoidization kills the purely inseparable defect and is the reduced perfect quotient; it cannot retain its nilpotents. For J=(1) the almost statement is ordinary finite étale descent; for J=0 it is vacuous and cannot prove connectivity by itself. For R=O_C and S=R⟨x⟩ the integrality hypothesis fails, consistently with the nonconnective example of [§2.25](#layer-2-connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid).

### Examples

The derived self-intersection R=(A/I)⊗^L_((A/I)⟨x⟩)(A/I), x↦0, has π₀=A/I and π₁=A/I. Its cotangent complex is R[1], so the conjugate graded pieces are R{−i} in degree pattern prescribed below; replacing R by π₀ loses its nonzero negative cohomology. For the crystalline perfect base and S=F_p[x], S_perfd=F_p[x^(1/p^∞)] is discrete, whereas Δ̄ has H¹=F_p[x]dx. The completed Frobenius perfection is therefore a genuine loss of positive conjugate pieces, rather than a substitution of notation.
