## Layer 3: Nygaard filtration and Breuil–Kisin twists

First calculate the Frobenius-divisibility ideals of discrete quasiregular semiperfectoid prisms. Construct their twists and extend to filtered derived objects. Relative Nygaard theory on φ_A^*Δ supplies the Lη factorization and general de Rham comparison. Nygaard completion is a separate object: it is neither an implicit replacement of Δ nor automatically an isomorphism.


<a id="layer-3-filtered-multiplicative-enhancement"></a>

### 3.0 Multiplicative Beilinson cover and décalage

Prove `Prismatic.Filtered.connectiveCover_laxMonoidal` and `Prismatic.Decalage.eInfinity`: for a commutative ring T and an invertible Cartier ideal J, the Beilinson connective cover on DF(T) is lax symmetric monoidal, and Lη_J on D(T) has a natural lax symmetric monoidal refinement, hence carries E_∞ algebras and their coherent maps to E_∞ algebras. For a J-torsion-free cochain model K the underlying object is the ordinary η_J model; reduction modulo J is the Bockstein complex with its multiplicative enhancement. These statements include naturality in the ideal and the coefficient algebra. ([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Definition 5.3, Theorem 5.4(1),(3), pp.28–29; Proposition 5.8, Corollary 5.10, pp.31–32.)

*Needs:* `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1/filtered-modules`, `DD.1/completed-filtered-tensor`, `DD.1/beilinson-t-structure`, `DD.1/beilinson-heart`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`. The filtered category, Day tensor and Beilinson t-structure are imported, rather than constructed again here.

**Proof route.** Day convolution makes Beilinson-connective filtered objects monoidal because their graded bounds add, and the right adjoint τ_B is therefore lax monoidal; the invertible lines J^i supply all integer twists. Cofinality of the underlying colimit toward −∞ makes it monoidal, while BMS2 Proposition 5.8 identifies the connective cover with Lη_J. Its Beilinson heart is the Bockstein complex; apply completion only after these constructions.

**Checks.** For K=T in degree zero, Lη_JK=T and its unit remains 1. For a nonzerodivisor d generating J and K=[T --d→ T] in degrees 0,1, η_JK=[T --d→ dT] is acyclic; retaining its T/d cohomology is incorrect. For K=T[1] in degree −1, η_JK=J^(−1)[1], which detects omission of negative filtration indices. For two homogeneous classes the Bockstein obeys β(xy)=β(x)y+(−1)^deg(x)xβ(y); two degree-one generators over Z at p=2 still have the integral minus sign before reduction.

<a id="layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp"></a>

### 3.1 Nygaard filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring

Let (B, J) be a prism with Frobenius φ_B. For i ≥ 0 put Fil^i_N B = φ_B^{-1}(J^i) = {x ∈ B : φ_B(x) ∈ J^i}, an ideal of B, and Fil^i_N B = B for i ≤ 0; gr^i_N B = Fil^i_N B / Fil^{i+1}_N B. For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring S the Nygaard filtration of S is this filtration on its initial prism (Δ_S, IΔ_S) (PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3): Fil^i_N Δ_S = {x ∈ Δ_S : φ(x) ∈ I^i Δ_S} = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^i Δ_S}, where d is the image of a generator of ker(θ : A_inf(R) → R) for any perfectoid ring R mapping to S (the ideal IΔ_S is principal and does not depend on R). It is an N-indexed decreasing filtration by ideals, multiplicative (Fil^i_N · Fil^j_N ⊂ Fil^{i+j}_N), and functorial: a map of prisms (B, J) → (B', J') carries Fil^i_N B into Fil^i_N B', so a map S → S' of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings carries Fil^i_N Δ_S into Fil^i_N Δ_{S'}. The filtration is by the Frobenius-divisibility condition itself; it is not the IΔ_S-adic filtration, not the powers of Fil^1_N, and not a divided-power filtration. It is not separated in general, and Δ_S need not be complete for it ([§3.23](#layer-3-nygaard-incomplete-example)).

prisms are those of PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2 (δ-ring, invertible ideal, derived (p, I)-complete, p ∈ I + φ(I)). S is quasiregular semiperfectoid in the sense used by PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3 (BMS2 Definition 4.20); Δ_S is its initial prism, a discrete ring. No orientation is chosen in the definition: the condition φ(x) ∈ J^i uses only the ideal J. When J = (d) it reads φ(x) ∈ d^i B. The index set is N; negative indices give the whole ring.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 12.1; p. 86; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.14 (4) and the warning after Definition 12.1; pp. 7, 86; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), the paragraph before Theorem 3.4.4; p. 25.)

*Needs:* [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), Mathlib `Ideal.comap`, Mathlib `Ideal.mem_comap`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Nygaard.fil`: For a prism (B, J) and i ∈ N, the ideal Fil^i_N B = φ_B^{-1}(J^i) of B.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.mem_fil_iff`: x ∈ Fil^i_N B if and only if φ_B(x) ∈ J^i.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_zero`: Fil^0_N B = B.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_antitone`: If i ≤ j then Fil^j_N B ⊂ Fil^i_N B.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_mul_le`: Fil^i_N B · Fil^j_N B ⊂ Fil^{i+j}_N B.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_map_le`: For a map of prisms f : (B, J) → (B′, J′), f(Fil^i_N B) ⊂ Fil^i_N B′.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.fil_eq_span_pow_of_perfect`: If (B, (d)) is a perfect prism and φ(e) = d then Fil^i_N B = (e^i).
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.gr`: The graded piece gr^i_N B = Fil^i_N B / Fil^{i+1}_N B as a B-module.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.intersection_fil`: For quasiregular semiperfectoid S, ⋂_(i≥0)Fil^i_NΔ_S=ker(φ:Δ_S→Δ_S), since Fil^i_N=φ^(-1)(I^iΔ_S) and Δ_S is I-adically separated. This is the kernel of the map to its Nygaard completion.

**Proof route.** Take the inverse images of J^i under φ, which are functorial multiplicative ideals; the supplied QRSP prism makes this an ordinary ideal filtration. Its intersection is ker φ because Δ is J-adically separated. Completeness is a separate assertion, as the counterexample in [§3.23](#layer-3-nygaard-incomplete-example) shows.

**Checks.**

- `pr3_nygaard_fil_zero`: Fil^0_N B = B for every prism (B, J).
- `pr3_nygaard_fil_frobenius_id`: If φ_B is the identity (for example (Z_p, (p))) then Fil^i_N B = J^i.
- `pr3_nygaard_fil_perfect`: For a perfect prism (B, (d)) with e = φ^{-1}(d): Fil^i_N B = (e^i); for B the (p, [p]_q)-completion of Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}] and d = [p]_q this is ([p]_{q^{1/p}})^i.
- `pr3_nygaard_fil_one_perfect`: For a perfect prism (B, (d)): x ∈ Fil^1_N B if and only if x maps to 0 under B → B/dB composed with φ, that is, Fil^1_N B is the kernel of θ ∘ φ.
- `pr3_nygaard_fil_not_powers`: It is false that Fil^i_N B = (Fil^1_N B)^i for all prisms and all i: in the key case Y^p/[p]_q! lies in Fil^p_N Δ_S and not in (Fil^1_N Δ_S)^p.

- S perfectoid, Δ_S = A_inf(S) and Fil^i_N = (φ^{-1}(d))^i A_inf(S); for S = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ this is ([p]_{q^{1/p}})^i. For the key case S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧ the filtration is the one of [§3.2](#layer-3-nygaard-key-case). The definition is intrinsic to S: it does not use a perfectoid ring mapping to S, while the conjugate filtration it is compared with does (BS22 Example 12.3).

### 3.2 The key case: q-divided powers and the Nygaard filtration of Z_p^cycl⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/X

Let A be the (p, [p]_q)-adic completion of Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}] with δ(q^{1/p^n}) = 0, I = ([p]_q), [p]_q = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1}; (A, I) is the perfect prism of R = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧, with q^{1/p^n} ↦ ζ_{p^{n+1}}. Let S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧. Write [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1), [n]_q! = ∏_{i=1}^n [i]_q. (a) Δ_S = A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/[p]_q}^∧ (prismatic envelope), with δ(Y^{1/p^n}) = 0 and S → Δ̄_S sending X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}}; Δ_S is flat over Z_p[[q−1]]. (b) (q-divided powers, BS22 Lemma 12.5) If D is a derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, (p, [p]_q)-completely flat Z_p[[q−1]]-algebra with a ring endomorphism φ, φ(q) = q^p, and x ∈ D satisfies φ(x) = x^p ∈ [p]_q D, then x^n ∈ [n]_q! D for all n ≥ 0. (c) (BS22 Lemma 12.6) In Z_p[[q−1]]: [mp]_q! = u · φ([m]_q!) · [p]_q^m with u a unit, for m ∈ N; and [⌊i⌋p]_q! = v · [⌊ip⌋]_q! with v a unit, for i ∈ N[1/p]. (d) (BS22 Lemma 12.4) Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ Δ_S for all n, and Δ_S is the (p, [p]_q)-adic completion of the free A-module ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} A · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!. On this basis φ(Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!) = u_i · [p]_q^{⌊i⌋} · Y^{ip}/[⌊ip⌋]_q! with u_i a unit. (e) (BS22 Lemma 12.7) Fil^n_N Δ_S is the completion of ⊕_i [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{max(n−⌊i⌋, 0)} · A · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!. The image of φ/[p]_q^n : Fil^n_N Δ_S → Δ̄_S = (⊕_i R · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!)^∧ is the span of the summands with i < p(n+1), and the conjugate filtration Fil_n Δ̄_S relative to R is the same span. In particular Theorem 12.2 holds for S, and Δ_S/Fil^1_N Δ_S = ⊕_{i<1} (A/[p]_{q^{1/p}}) · Y^i, which φ maps isomorphically onto the image ⊕_{j<p} R · Y^j of S in Δ̄_S (Y^i ↦ Y^{pi}, the image of X^i).

R, A, S, Y as in the statement; N[1/p] is the monoid of non-negative elements of Z[1/p]. The normalisation X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}} is that of BS22 §12.2 (so X ↦ Y^p). In (e) the exponent of [p]_{q^{1/p}} is max(n − ⌊i⌋, 0): the factor is 1 as soon as i ≥ n. In the proof of BS22 Lemma 12.6 the display reads ∏[ip]_q! where ∏[ip]_q is meant; the target states the corrected identity.

Its base change along A → Z_p, q^{1/p^n} ↦ 1, is the p-completion of ⊕ Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋! ([§3.23](#layer-3-nygaard-incomplete-example)). ### 3.3 Good filtrations and the Nygaard filtration of regular semiperfectoid quotients

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)). For a quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebra S, a multiplicative filtration Fil^•_M of Δ_S by ideals (i ≥ 0) is good if Fil^0_M = Δ_S, φ(Fil^i_M) ⊂ d^i Δ_S for all i and φ/d^i induces an isomorphism of gr^i_M Δ_S onto Fil_i Δ̄_S ⊂ Δ̄_S (conjugate filtration relative to R). (1) A good filtration equals the Nygaard filtration. (2) If Δ_S carries a good filtration then Theorem 12.2 holds for S. (3) Let S → S′ be relatively perfect (the base change of a map of perfectoid R-algebras). If Fil^•_M is good on Δ_S then Fil^i_M Δ_S ⊗̂^L_{Δ_S} Δ_{S′} is concentrated in degree 0 and is a good filtration of Δ_{S′}; hence Fil^i_N Δ_{S′} = Fil^i_N Δ_S ⊗̂_{Δ_S} Δ_{S′}. (4) Let S → T be relatively perfect and p-completely faithfully flat. If Δ_T carries a good filtration then so does Δ_S. (5) Consequently Theorem 12.2 holds for S = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) with f_1, …, f_m a p-completely regular sequence relative to R, and the Nygaard filtration of S(m) = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_m^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_1, …, X_m) is the completed tensor product over A of the Nygaard filtrations of the factors R⟨X_j^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_j).

R is perfectoid, (A, (d)) its perfect prism, S, S′, T quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras. The regular sequence in (5) is p-completely regular relative to R (BS22 Definition 2.42 with I = (p)); this is the reading used when the same class of rings is quoted in the proof of BS22 Theorem 13.1. Completed tensor products are derived (p, d)-completed (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1). In the proof of BS22 Proposition 12.8 'p-power roots in f_i' reads 'in R′'.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 12.8 and its proof; p. 90; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 12.8; p. 90.)

### 3.4 Nygaard filtration on prismatic cohomology over a perfectoid base

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, I), I = (d). (a) For a p-completely smooth R-algebra B choose a surjection R⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩ → B and put B̃ = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_{R⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩} B, with Čech nerve B̃^• of B → B̃; all B̃^k are semiperfectoid and Zariski locally of the form of [§3.3](#layer-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid) (5), and Δ_{B/A} ≅ Tot(Δ_{B̃^•}). Define Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} = Tot(Fil^i_N Δ_{B̃^•}) → Δ_{B/A}. It is independent of the surjection and functorial in B, a decreasing N-indexed multiplicative filtration of Δ_{B/A} in D(A) with gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤ i} Δ̄_{B/A}{i}, the isomorphism induced by φ/d^i (it is φ_A-semilinear). (b) For a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S define Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} as the derived (p, I)-completed left Kan extension of B ↦ Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} from p-completed polynomial R-algebras. Then Fil^0_N = Δ_{S/A}, the filtration is multiplicative and functorial, and φ/d^i induces a φ_A-semilinear isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i} (conjugate filtration relative to R), that is, an A-linear isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ (φ_A)_* Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i}. (c) Each functor S ↦ Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} on quasisyntomic R-algebras is a sheaf for the quasisyntomic topology with values in D(A).

R is perfectoid and (A, I) is its perfect prism; B is p-completely smooth over R; S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra. Filtered objects are objects of the filtered derived category DF(A) of functors (Z, ≥) → D(A) (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1); the filtration is N-indexed in the sense that Fil^i = Fil^0 for i ≤ 0. BS22 Proposition 12.10 prints gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤i} Δ_{B/A}; the correct target is τ^{≤i} Δ̄_{B/A}{i}, which is what the target states. The identification of this filtration, on quasiregular semiperfectoid S, with the ideals of [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp) is part of [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces) (BS22 Proposition 12.11).

### 3.5 Graded pieces of the Nygaard filtration (BS22 Theorem 12.2)

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, R a perfectoid ring mapping to S with perfect prism (A, (d)), and Fil_i Δ̄_S ⊂ Δ̄_S the conjugate filtration relative to R (increasing, exhaustive, multiplicative, gr_i Δ̄_S ≅ (∧^i L_{S/R}[−i])^∧{−i}). For every i ≥ 0: (1) the image of Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ̄_S, x ↦ (φ(x)/d^i mod d), is Fil_i Δ̄_S, and its kernel is Fil^{i+1}_N Δ_S; (2) hence x ↦ φ(x) mod I^{i+1}Δ_S induces a natural isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i}, where Δ̄_S{i} = I^iΔ_S/I^{i+1}Δ_S; it is φ-semilinear (Δ_S acts on the target through φ), and the left side does not depend on R; (3) in particular Δ_S / Fil^1_N Δ_S ≅ S, the isomorphism being induced by φ : Δ_S → Δ̄_S, whose image is S = Fil_0 Δ̄_S; (4) (BS22 Proposition 12.11) the derived Nygaard filtration Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} of [§3.4](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration) (b) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the ideal Fil^i_N Δ_S ⊂ Δ_S of [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp); consequently on quasisyntomic R-algebras the filtration of [§3.4](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration) is the quasisyntomic unfolding of S′ ↦ Fil^•_N Δ_{S′} from quasiregular semiperfectoid S′, and it does not depend on R. Each gr^i_N Δ_S is a derived p-complete, p-completely flat S-module.

S is quasiregular semiperfectoid; R → S is any map from a perfectoid ring; d is the image of a generator of ker θ. The conjugate filtration depends on R in general (BS22 Example 12.3, S = O_{C_p} ⊗̂_{Z_p} O_{C_p}); the Nygaard filtration and its graded pieces do not. BS22 §12.5 prints that the derived filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring is concentrated in degrees 0 and −1; the correct degrees are 0 and 1. The argument below uses the corrected range. The twist {i} is ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ i}; it is trivialised by d^i, which is how the printed statement, with φ/d^i, reads.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 12.2, with Proposition 12.11 and its proof; pp. 86, 92; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 12.11; p. 92; [ALB23](#ref-alb23), Theorem 3.4.4 (published: Theorem 3.29); p. 25.)

**Proof route.** Induct on i to identify the derived Nygaard stages with the ordinary ideals and to show that their graded pieces are discrete. Choose a root presentation surjective on cotangent complexes, so that the induced map on each finite conjugate stage is surjective; its image under φ/d^i is precisely that stage, with kernel Fil_N^(i+1). Finite extensions of its p-completely flat conjugate pieces prove the asserted flatness.

**Checks.**

- S perfectoid with A = A_inf(S): gr^i_N = (e^i)/(e^{i+1}) ≅ S and A_inf(S)/Fil^1_N ≅ S via θ ∘ φ. Key case: the summands with i < p(n+1) ([§3.2](#layer-3-nygaard-key-case) (e)). Anschütz–Le Bras Theorem 3.4.4 is this statement; they use Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R ≅ R to present the structure sheaf of the quasisyntomic site as a quotient of the prismatic sheaf.

### 3.6 Transversal prisms and the ideals I_r

A prism (A, I) is transversal if A/I is p-torsion-free; more generally a preprism (a δ-ring A with an ideal I that is an invertible A-module) is transversal under the same condition. For a transversal prism: (1) A is p-torsion-free and (A, I) is bounded; (A, I) is transversal if and only if A is p-torsion-free and I/pI → A/pA is injective, and then the image is an invertible ideal of A/pA. (2) For every r ≥ 0 the map (φ_A^r)^*(I) → A induced by I ⊂ A is injective with p-torsion-free cokernel; its image is the ideal φ_A^r(I)A, again written (φ_A^r)^*(I). Put I_r = I · φ_A^*(I) ⋯ (φ_A^{r−1})^*(I), an invertible ideal (I_0 = A, I_1 = I). (3) I_r and I^{(p^r−1)/(p−1)} have the same image in A/pA; A/I_r is p-torsion-free; A = lim_r A/I_r = lim_r A/φ_A^*(I_r). (4) For r > 0 the natural map (φ_A^r)^*(I)/I_{r+1} → A/I_r is injective with image the principal ideal (p); and I_r = ∩_{0 ≤ s < r} (φ_A^s)^*(I). (5) I_r/I_r² is p-torsion-free; the canonical map I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² is p times a unique surjection c_r, and c_r induces an isomorphism I_{r+1}/I_rI_{r+1} ≅ I_r/I_r² of invertible A/I_r-modules. (6) For a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J), J_r = I_r B; a flat map of prisms out of a transversal prism has transversal target, and the converse holds for faithfully flat maps.

(A, I) is a prism in the sense of [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms). Bhatt–Lurie's Definition 2.1.3 (ρ : φ^*(I) → A/I surjective, A derived p- and I-complete) defines the same class of objects. For an oriented prism (A, (d)) transversality says that (d, p) is a regular sequence, the hypothesis of [§0.29](#layer-0-joyal-delta-operations) (Anschütz–Le Bras). Flat and faithfully flat maps of prisms are those for which A/I → B/J is p-completely (faithfully) flat. In the proof of BL22 Corollary 2.2.9 the last line reads 'x belongs to I_r' where 'I_{r+1}' is meant.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Definitions 2.1.1 and 2.1.3, Remarks 2.1.7 and 2.1.8; pp. 19, 20; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Lemmas 2.2.1, 2.2.5 and 2.2.8; Corollaries 2.2.9–2.2.10; §2.2; pp. 21, 22, 23; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remarks 2.2.4 and 2.4.4; pp. 21, 27.)

- `Prismatic.BKTwist.frobeniusIdeal`: The ideal (φ_A^r)^*(I) = φ_A^r(I)A of A.
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.Ir`: The ideal I_r = ∏_{0 ≤ s < r} (φ_A^s)^*(I).

- `Prismatic.BKTwist.Ir_one`: I_1 = I.

- `pr3_transversal_not_crystalline`: A crystalline prism (A, (p)) with A/p ≠ 0 is not transversal.

- The q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) is transversal, with I_r = ([p^r]_q). A nonzero crystalline prism (A, (p)) is not transversal: A/I = A/p is killed by p. The Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) is transversal: the quotient O_K is p-torsion-free. A perfect prism (A_inf(R), ker θ) is transversal exactly when R is p-torsion-free.

### 3.7 Approximation of prisms by transversal prisms

(1) (BL22 Proposition 2.1.10) For a transversal preprism (A, I) there is a preprism map f : (A, I) → (B, J) to a prism (B, J) such that every preprism map from (A, I) to a prism factors uniquely through f; (B, J) is transversal and Spec(B/(J + (p))) → Spec(A/(I + (p))) is an open immersion. (2) (Proposition 2.4.1) For every prism (A, I) there is a map of prisms (B, J) → (A, I) with (B, J) transversal. (3) (Proposition 2.4.5, Corollary 2.4.7, Proposition 2.4.9) If (A, I) is transversal and (B, J) is bounded, the coproduct (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) exists in the category of prisms and (B, J) → (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) is flat; it is faithfully flat when A ≠ 0; if (B, J) is also transversal then so is the coproduct. (4) (Corollary 2.4.8) For every prism (A, I), the category of transversal prisms (A_0, I_0) with a map of prisms to (A, I) is non-empty and has pairwise coproducts; hence it is sifted and its nerve is weakly contractible. (5) (Corollary 2.4.10) A bounded prism (A, I) is transversal if and only if for every bounded prism (B, J) the coproduct (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) exists and is flat over (B, J), if and only if this holds for one nonzero transversal (B, J).

prism are those of PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2; (2) and (4) hold for every prism, bounded or not. In (3) the coproduct is the prismatic envelope of PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2 applied to the (J, p)-completion of A ⊗_Z B and the image of a generator of I, after localising so that I is principal. The free p-complete δ-ring on a ring R is the p-completion of the free δ-ring ([§0.8](#layer-0-free-delta-ring)). In the proof of BL22 Lemma 2.4.2 the scheme of idempotent n × n matrices is a closed subscheme of the affine space of dimension n², printed as A^{2n}.

**Proof route.** Lift the map ρ:φ*I→A/I and complete its nonvanishing locus to obtain the transversal approximation and its W₂ mapping property. Spread I over a smooth Z-algebra B₀, form its symmetric algebra and free completed delta algebra, and use formal smoothness of the Witt vectors to get the needed flat retraction; apply the regular-envelope construction to the resulting preprism. Coproducts are completely regular envelopes, and lifting residue-field points through W(k) detects faithful flatness before completing and choosing orientations.

For a perfect prism of a perfectoid ring with p-torsion (for example (Z_p, (p)), R = F_p) a transversal approximation exists although the prism is not transversal. The coproduct of the q-de Rham prism with itself is transversal; it is the prism on which the two generators e_A of [§3.11](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-examples) are compared.

### 3.8 Breuil–Kisin twist of a transversal prism

Let (A, I) be a transversal prism with the ideals I_r and the surjections c_r : I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² (the canonical map divided by p) of [§3.6](#layer-3-transversal-prism). Define A{1} = lim (⋯ → I_3/I_3² → I_2/I_2² → I/I²), the inverse limit along the maps c_r, with projections π_r : A{1} → I_r/I_r². Then: (1) A{1} is an invertible A-module, and π_r induces an isomorphism A{1}/I_rA{1} ≅ I_r/I_r² for every r ≥ 0; in particular A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I². (2) For a map f of transversal prisms (A, I) → (B, J) there is a unique A-linear f{1} : A{1} → B{1} compatible with the maps I_r/I_r² → J_r/J_r², and it induces B ⊗_A A{1} ≅ B{1}. (3) The canonical isomorphisms φ_A^*(I_r) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗ I_{r+1} induce, modulo φ_A^*(I_r) and in the limit over r, an isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1}) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}, that is, a φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_{A{1}} : A{1} → I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}. On compatible systems it sends (x_r mod I_r²)_r, x_r ∈ I_r, to the system of the classes of φ_A(x_r) ∈ φ_A^*(I_r) = I^{−1} I_{r+1}.

(A, I) is a transversal prism; all the statements of [§3.6](#layer-3-transversal-prism) are available. The transition maps are the canonical maps divided by p; the canonical maps themselves are divisible by p and their inverse limit is not the twist. I^{−1} denotes the dual invertible module Hom_A(I, A); I^{−1} ⊗ M is written I^{−1}M.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 2.2.11 and Proposition 2.2.12; p. 23; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remark 2.2.13 and Construction 2.2.14; pp. 23, 24.)

- `Prismatic.BKTwist.ker_transversalProj`: The kernel of π_r is I_r · A{1}.
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalProj_transition`: If y ∈ I_{r+1} represents π_{r+1}(x), then the class of y in I_r/I_r² is p · π_r(x).
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.transversal_ext`: Two elements of A{1} with the same image under every π_r are equal.
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.transversal_lift`: A family x_r ∈ I_r/I_r² with (class of a representative of x_{r+1}) = p · x_r for all r comes from a unique element of A{1}.
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalFrobenius_projection`: For r≥1, the identity φ_A^*I_r ≃ I^(-1)I_(r+1) induces, after reduction modulo φ_A^*I_r, an isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1})⊗A/(φ_A^*I_r) ≃ I^(-1)A{1}⊗A/(φ_A^*I_r). The Frobenius on A{1} is characterized by these projected maps for all r. Thus its projections are obtained from φ applied to π_r and the specified ideal identification, not by an arbitrary identification of invertible modules (BL Construction 2.2.14).
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.transversalTwist_projection`: For r≥1, π_r:A{1}→I_r/I_r² identifies A{1}/I_r A{1} with I_r/I_r². The maps satisfy π_r=c_r∘π_(r+1), where c_r is the divided transition of cotangentTransition.

Under a prism map J_r=I_rB, yielding functorial base change. The identity φ*I_r=I^−1I_(r+1) passes to the limit and gives the Frobenius formula.

- `pr3_bk_transversal_undivided`: The canonical maps I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² are not the transition maps: each has image in p · (I_r/I_r²).
- `pr3_bk_transversal_proj_zero`: π_0 is the zero map to I_0/I_0² = 0.

- The q-de Rham prism the classes of [p^r]_q form a compatible system, since [p^{r+1}]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q modulo I_r², and define a generator ([§3.11](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-examples)). Reduction: A{1} ⊗_A A/I ≅ I/I², the twist of BS22 used in the Hodge–Tate comparison. Frobenius has a simple pole along I: φ_{A{1}} takes values in I^{−1} ⊗ A{1}, not in A{1}.

### 3.9 Breuil–Kisin twists A{n} of a prism

Let (A, I) be a prism and C the category of transversal prisms (A_0, I_0) with a map of prisms to (A, I) ([§3.7](#layer-3-transversal-approximation) (4)). The diagram C → Mod_A, (A_0, I_0) ↦ A ⊗_{A_0} A_0{1} ([§3.8](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal)) has invertible transition maps and a colimit A{1}, the Breuil–Kisin twist of A; for every object of C the map A ⊗_{A_0} A_0{1} → A{1} is an isomorphism. (1) A{1} is an invertible A-module. For n ∈ Z put A{n} = A{1}^{⊗ n} (negative powers are duals) and, for an A-module or an object M of D(A), M{n} = M ⊗_A A{n}. (2) Functoriality: a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) induces an isomorphism B ⊗_A A{1} ≅ B{1}, compatibly with composition and identities. Hence for a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, IB), A{1} is the equaliser of B{1} ⇉ (B ⊗̂_A B){1}: when I is not principal the twist is obtained by descent from a cover on which I is oriented. (3) There is a canonical isomorphism β : A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I² of invertible A/I-modules, functorial in the prism and equal to that of [§3.8](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal) (1) for transversal prisms. Consequently, for an A/I-module N, N{n} ≅ N ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ n}, the twist of Bhatt–Scholze. (4) A{1} is a free A-module if and only if I is principal. (5) Frobenius: there is a canonical φ_A-semilinear map φ_{A{1}} : A{1} → I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1} inducing an A-linear isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1}) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}, functorial in the prism and equal to that of [§3.8](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal) (3) for transversal prisms; its tensor powers are φ_{A{n}} : A{n} → I^{−n} ⊗_A A{n}, n ∈ Z.

(A, I) is any prism; boundedness is needed only for the descent statement in (2). For a transversal prism the definition returns the inverse limit of [§3.8](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal), because the identity is then an object of C. A{1} has no canonical generator even when I is principal; a generator is extra structure ([§3.11](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-examples)). The prismatic logarithm log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1} of Bhatt–Lurie §§2.3, 2.5, 2.7 is not part of this target; no target of the layer uses it.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 2.5.1, Definition 2.5.2, Notation 2.5.4; p. 28; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remarks 2.5.5, 2.5.7, 2.5.8; pp. 28, 29; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remark 2.5.9; p. 29; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8 (2), the sentence after the display; p. 4.)

- `Prismatic.BKTwist.twist`: The A-module A{1} of a prism (A, I).
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.twist_invertible`: A{1} is an invertible A-module.
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.twistPow`: The A-module A{n} = A{1}^{⊗ n} for n ∈ Z.
- `Prismatic.BKTwist.twistModule`: For an A-module M and n ∈ Z, the A-module M{n} = A{n} ⊗_A M.

Positive powers use tensor products, negative powers use the inverse dual of the linearized map; n=0 gives φ_A. It is compatible with tensor addition and with base change along prism maps.

**Proof route.** The transversal approximation nerve has weakly contractible choices, and its transition lines are invertible, giving the canonical line by descent. Faithfully flat descent proves its base-change maps and the Frobenius identities. Its reduction is I/I², so an orientation is equivalent to trivializing that line.

- A{0} = A and (M{m}){n} ≅ M{m+n}. For A/I-modules the twist agrees with M ⊗ (I/I²)^{⊗ n} of BS22 Theorem 1.8 (2): H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} in the Hodge–Tate comparison is unchanged. Over the q-de Rham prism A{1} = A · e_A with φ(e_A) = e_A/[p]_q; over a crystalline prism φ(e_A) = e_A/p ([§3.11](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-examples)). Consumers: Layer 6 (Z_p(n) uses Δ̂{n}), Layer 4 (absolute prismatic cohomology with twists, the line bundle O_WCart{1}).

### 3.10 Divided Frobenius

(a) Let (B, J) be a prism with J = (d). For i ≥ 0 the divided Frobenius φ_i = φ/d^i : Fil^i_N B → B is the unique map with d^i φ_i(x) = φ(x) (d is a nonzerodivisor). It is additive and φ-semilinear, φ_0 = φ, φ_{i+j}(xy) = φ_i(x)φ_j(y) for x ∈ Fil^i_N, y ∈ Fil^j_N, φ_i(x) = d · φ_{i+1}(x) for x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N, and φ_i(x) ∈ dB if and only if x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N. Replacing d by ud (u a unit) replaces φ_i by u^{−i}φ_i. (b) Without an orientation the invariant object is the filtered Frobenius Fil^i(φ) : Fil^i_N B → J^i, x ↦ φ(x). With the Breuil–Kisin twists of [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist) it becomes the twisted divided Frobenius φ_i : Fil^i_N B ⊗_B B{i} → B{i}, x ⊗ e ↦ φ(x) · φ_{B{i}}(e), where φ_{B{i}} : B{i} → J^{−i} ⊗ B{i}; it is φ-semilinear and independent of all choices. For J = (d) and a generator e of B{1} with φ_{B{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e it is φ/d^i ⊗ 1. (c) For S quasiregular semiperfectoid these are the maps φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ_S and φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_S{i} → Δ_S{i}, and φ_i induces the isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} of [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces). (d) Over a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, (d)), the maps φ/d^i on the terms of the Čech nerve of [§3.4](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration) (a) totalise to a natural φ_A-semilinear map φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} → Δ_{B/A} for B p-completely smooth over R, projecting to the isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i}; left Kan extension gives φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} for all derived p-complete simplicial R-algebras S, with φ_i ∘ (Fil^{i+1} → Fil^i) = d · φ_{i+1}.

(B, J) is a prism; in (a) J is principal with chosen generator d. The twist B{i} is the i-th tensor power of the Breuil–Kisin twist B{1} ([§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist)); Fil^i_N B{i} means Fil^i_N B ⊗_B B{i}, a submodule of B{i} because B{i} is invertible. Semilinearity is over the Frobenius of B (and of A in (d)). BS22 Proposition 12.10 is quoted with the corrected target τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i}.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Proposition 12.10; p. 92; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 12.2; p. 86; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remark 2.5.9; p. 29.)

Key case: φ_n([p]_{q^{1/p}}^{n−⌊i⌋} Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!) is a unit multiple of Y^{ip}/[⌊ip⌋]_q! for i < n+1. BMS2 Theorem 7.2 (4): on π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p) the cyclotomic Frobenius restricted to the i-th Nygaard level is ξ̃^i times a divided Frobenius; under the identification of BS22 Theorem 13.1, whose Layer 7 trace comparison uses [§3.26](#layer-3-bms2-comparison), it is the completion of φ_i.

### 3.11 Breuil–Kisin twists over the q-de Rham prism and over crystalline prisms

(1) Let (A, I) = (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) be the q-de Rham prism. It is transversal with I_r = ([p^r]_q), [p^r]_q = (q^{p^r} − 1)/(q − 1), and [p^{r+1}]_q = [p]_{q^{p^r}} [p^r]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q modulo I_r². There is a unique e_A ∈ A{1} whose image in I_r/I_r² is the class of [p^r]_q for every r; A{1} is the free A-module on e_A, and φ_{A{1}}(e_A) = [p]_q^{−1} e_A. (2) For a map of prisms f : (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) → (B, J), the image e_B of e_A generates B{1} and φ_{B{1}}(λ e_B) = φ_B(λ) f([p]_q)^{−1} e_B; e_B depends on f and not only on (B, J). (3) For a crystalline prism (B, (p)) the map q ↦ 1 gives a canonical generator e_B of B{1} with φ_{B{1}}(e_B) = e_B/p; hence (B{n}, φ_{B{n}}) ≅ (B, p^{−n} φ_B) for all n ∈ Z, and the twisted divided Frobenius of [§3.10](#layer-3-divided-frobenius) is φ/p^i. (4) For an oriented prism (B, (d)) and a generator e of B{1}, φ_{B{1}}(e) = u d^{−1} e for a unit u; replacing e by v e replaces u by φ(v) v^{−1} u.

The q-de Rham prism is [§0.23](#layer-0-q-de-rham-prism): φ(q) = q^p, δ(q) = 0. Bhatt–Lurie characterise e_A by (q − 1) e_A = log_Δ(q^p); the target uses the equivalent description by the classes of [p^r]_q, which is the one their proof establishes, so that no logarithm is needed. BL22 Remark 2.6.2 and Notation 2.6.3 write the target of the Frobenius as I^{−1}{1}; by Notation 2.5.4 this is A{1} ⊗_A I^{−1}, the module written I^{−1}A{1} in Remark 2.5.9.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 2.6.1 and its proof, Remark 2.6.2; p. 31; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Notation 2.6.3 and Example 2.6.4; p. 31.)

*Needs:* [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist), [§3.8](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal), [§3.6](#layer-3-transversal-prism), [§0.23](#layer-0-q-de-rham-prism), [§0.20](#layer-0-crystalline-prism).

**Proof route.** In the cyclotomic prism the product of φ^s([p]_q) is [p^r]_q and q^(p^r)=1 modulo that ideal. The resulting classes divided by p give the stated bases, and Frobenius multiplies the compatible basis by [p]_q^−1. At q=1 this is the crystalline factor p^−1.

**Checks.**

- Crystalline prism example: for (Z_p, (p)), Z_p{n} = Z_p · e^n with φ(e^n) = p^{−n} e^n. Under reduction modulo I the generator e_A maps to the class of [p]_q in I/I². The two generators of the twist of the coproduct of the q-de Rham prism with itself differ by a unit that is not 1, which is why e_B depends on f.

<a id="layer-3-large-quasisyntomic-algebra"></a>

### 3.12 Large quasisyntomic algebras over A/I

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and Ā = A/I. A quasisyntomic Ā-algebra is a derived p-complete Ā-algebra S that is p-completely flat over Ā and whose cotangent complex L_{S/Ā} has p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]; such an S is classically p-complete. A quasisyntomic Ā-algebra S is large if there is a surjection Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞} | t ∈ T⟩ → S for some set T; equivalently, S/pS is generated as an Ā-algebra by the images of elements of S that admit compatible systems of p-power roots in S. For a large quasisyntomic S: Ω^1_{S/Ā} vanishes after p-completion, so L_{S/Ā}[−1] is a p-completely flat S-module, and every (∧^i L_{S/Ā})[−i]^∧ is a p-completely flat S-module. Large quasisyntomic algebras form a basis of the quasisyntomic site of Ā: every quasisyntomic Ā-algebra has a quasisyntomic cover by a large one, and the terms of the Čech nerve of such a cover are large. The standard examples are Ā⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) with (f_1, …, f_m) p-completely regular relative to Ā.

(A, I) is a bounded prism; Ā has bounded p^∞-torsion. Quasisyntomic algebras, covers and the site are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5 (BMS2 §4) over the base Ā. Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ is the p-adic completion of the perfected polynomial ring Ā[X_t^{1/p^∞}]. The second formulation is the one of Bhatt–Lurie (S/pS generated by the images of Ā and of (S/pS)^♭); for p-complete S the two agree because compatible systems of p-power roots lift uniquely from S/pS to S.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Definition 15.1 and the paragraph after it; p. 102; [BL22](#ref-bl22), proof of Proposition 5.1.1, first paragraph; p. 115.)

*Needs:* `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms).

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge`: The predicate on an Ā-algebra S: S/pS is generated over Ā by images of elements with compatible p-power roots in S.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.HasCompatibleRoots`: x ∈ S admits a sequence x = x_0, x_1, x_2, … with x_{n+1}^p = x_n.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.isLarge_iff_exists_family`: S is large iff there is a family (x_t) of elements with compatible p-power roots such that every s ∈ S is congruent modulo p to an element of the Ā-subalgebra generated by the x_t.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge.of_surjective`: If S is large and S → S′ is a surjective map of Ā-algebras then S′ is large.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.IsLarge.kaehler_eq_smul`: For large S: Ω^1_{S/Ā} = p · Ω^1_{S/Ā}.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.isLarge_bar`: Ā is a large Ā-algebra.

**Proof route.** Adjoining compatible roots makes Frobenius surjective modulo p, including after completion. The vanishing of differentials modulo p and the cotangent-amplitude criterion then put the cotangent complex in degree −1 with p-completely flat module. Such root adjunctions form qsyn covers, giving the claimed basis.

**Checks.**

- `pr3_large_base`: Ā is large over itself.
- `pr3_large_generated_by_roots`: If S is generated as an Ā-algebra by elements with compatible p-power roots, then S is large; this covers the p-completion of Ā[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X).
- `pr3_large_kaehler`: For large S every Kähler differential of S over Ā is p times another one.
- `pr3_large_not_polynomial`: If Ā/p≠0, the p-completed polynomial algebra Ā⟨X⟩ is quasisyntomic but not large: its reduction has the nonzero differential dX.

- Ā itself is large (T empty). For a perfect prism, a quasiregular semiperfectoid Ā-algebra that is quasisyntomic over Ā is large; large algebras replace quasiregular semiperfectoid rings when the base prism is not perfect. Ā⟨X⟩ is not large: dX is not divisible by p in Ω^1.

<a id="layer-3-relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic"></a>

### 3.13 Relative Nygaard filtration of a large quasisyntomic algebra (BS22 Theorem 15.2)

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and S a large quasisyntomic A/I-algebra. (1) The derived prismatic cohomology Δ_{S/A} is concentrated in degree 0 and is a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebra; (Δ_{S/A}, IΔ_{S/A}) is the initial object of the relative prismatic site (S/A)_Δ. Let Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A (the Frobenius twist, a discrete (p, I)-completely flat A-algebra) and φ_{S/A} : Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} the relative Frobenius, an A-algebra map. Put Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = {x ∈ Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} : φ_{S/A}(x) ∈ I^i Δ_{S/A}}. (2) φ_{S/A} induces an injection gr^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} → Δ̄_{S/A}{i} = I^iΔ_{S/A}/I^{i+1}Δ_{S/A} whose image is Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i}, for every i ≥ 0. (3) The formation of Fil^i_N commutes with base change in A: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) and S_B the p-completion of S ⊗_A B, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} ⊗̂_A B ≅ Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S_B/B}.

(A, I) is a bounded prism; S is large and quasisyntomic over A/I ([§3.12](#layer-3-large-quasisyntomic-algebra)). The filtration lives on the Frobenius twist Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{S/A}, not on Δ_{S/A}: the relative Frobenius is A-linear only as a map out of the twist. For a perfect prism φ_A is an isomorphism and Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = φ_A^* Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A}. The conjugate filtration is the one of [§2.3](#layer-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison) relative to A/I; on large S its pieces are discrete, p-completely flat S-modules. Completed tensor products are derived (p, I)-completed; on completely flat modules over a bounded prism they are classical completions ([§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness)).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 15.2 and its proof; p. 102; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 15.2 (1); p. 102; [BL22](#ref-bl22), proof of Proposition 5.1.1; p. 115.)

Uniqueness of the good filtration gives base change; André’s cover and Künneth reduce the calculation to one root relation. To reduce an arbitrary oriented prism to a perfect one, use the faithfully flat perfected universal orientation cover and descend the comparison.

- S = A/I: Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = A, φ_{S/A} = id, Fil^i_N = I^i and gr^i = I^i/I^{i+1} = (A/I){i} = Fil_i^conj Δ̄{i} (BL22 Example 5.1.4). S = (A/I)⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X) over the q-de Rham prism: the base change to the perfection is the key case of [§3.2](#layer-3-nygaard-key-case). i = 0: gr^0_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} ≅ S.

<a id="layer-3-relative-nygaard-filtration"></a>

### 3.14 Relative Nygaard filtration on the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I. For an animated commutative Ā-algebra R write φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = Δ^{(1)}_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A for the Frobenius twist of derived prismatic cohomology and φ_{R/A} : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} for the relative Frobenius, a map of commutative algebra objects of the (p, I)-complete derived category of A. The relative Nygaard filtration is a decreasing filtration Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}, an object of the I-complete filtered derived category DF(A), with a refinement Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^• ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} of φ_{R/A} to a map of filtered objects, constructed in three steps. (a) For R large quasisyntomic, Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is the ideal {x : φ_{R/A}(x) ∈ I^iΔ_{R/A}} of [§3.13](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic). (b) For R quasisyntomic over Ā it is the right Kan extension of (a) along the inclusion of large algebras, equivalently the quasisyntomic unfolding: each R ↦ Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf and Fil^0_N = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. For X = Spf R affine and smooth over Ā this reads RΓ_Δ(X/A) ≅ RΓ(X_qsyn, Δ_{−/A}) and Fil^i_N RΓ_Δ(X/A)^{(1)} = RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{−/A}); for a smooth formal Ā-scheme X the filtrations on affine opens glue to a filtered object Fil^•_N Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} of D(X_ét, A). (c) For all animated R it is the (p, I)-completed left Kan extension of its restriction to finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebras; on quasisyntomic algebras this agrees with (b). Characterisation (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.1.1): the pair (Fil^•_N, Fil^•(φ)), functorial in R, is determined up to essentially unique isomorphism by: (1) each R ↦ Fil^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} commutes with sifted colimits; (2) for R a finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebra, gr^n(φ) : gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ̄_{R/A}{n} is an isomorphism on H^m for m ≤ n and H^m(gr^n_N) = 0 for m > n. Properties: gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0, so the filtration is N-indexed; it is multiplicative (a commutative algebra object of DF(A) refining φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}), giving in particular v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^•_N → Fil^{•+1}_N whose composite with Fil^{•+1}_N → Fil^•_N is induced by I ⊂ A; for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) there is a canonical isomorphism B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil^•_N φ_B^*Δ_{(B ⊗^L_A R)/B}; for R = Ā, Fil^n_N = I^n ⊂ A; for a perfect prism, Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = φ_A^*(Fil^•_N Δ_{R/A}) with the filtration of [§3.4](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration).

(A, I) is a bounded prism; R is an animated commutative Ā-algebra (derived prismatic cohomology depends only on the derived p-completion of R). The filtration is on the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. It is not a filtration of Δ_{R/A} unless φ_A is an isomorphism. DF(A) is the filtered derived category of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; the I-adic filtration I^• ⊗ Δ_{R/A} is Z-indexed, with i-th term I^{⊗ i} ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} for all i ∈ Z (negative powers are powers of the dual), as in BMS2 Proposition 5.8 and Bhatt–Lurie. Since gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0 the filtered Frobenius factors through its truncation to i ≥ 0, and for p-completely smooth R (Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}) the Beilinson connective covers of the two filtrations agree. BL22 Proposition 5.1.1 (1) prints the target of R ↦ Fil^n_N as the complete derived category of Ā; the objects are A-complexes (for R = Ā they are the ideals I^n), so the target is the (p, I)-complete derived category of A. Bhatt–Lurie's and Bhatt–Scholze's constructions agree wherever both apply: BL22 defines the filtration on large algebras by the formula of BS22 Theorem 15.2 and extends it by the same Kan extensions.

- `Prismatic.Nygaard.frobeniusTwist`: The object φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} of D(A) for a prism (A, I) and an A/I-algebra R.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.relativeFrobenius`: The A-linear relative Frobenius φ_{R/A} : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}.

- `Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilZeroIso`: Fil^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.relGr`: The graded piece gr^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.

- `Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilMap`: A map R → R′ of A/I-algebras induces a natural transformation Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R′/A}.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil_bar`: For R = A/I: Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is the ideal I^i of A placed in degree 0.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.relFil_large`: For R large quasisyntomic, Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0 (it is the ideal of Frobenius-divisible elements).
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.relFilBaseChange`: For a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) with completed base change functor B ⊗̂^L_A −: B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil^i_N φ_B^*Δ_{R_B/B}.
- `Prismatic.Nygaard.relativeFilteredFrobenius`: The filtered linearized Frobenius Fil^•_N(φ_A^*Δ)→I^•Δ has in degree i the map to I^i⊗Δ, with I^• indexed by all integers using inverse powers for negative i. Transition maps and multiplication commute with Frobenius.

Multiplication and base change hold on the large-basis ideals and therefore extend through the same descent and extension functors.

### 3.15 Graded pieces of the relative Nygaard filtration

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I, and R an animated commutative Ā-algebra. (1) For every n ≥ 0 the map gr^n(φ) : gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^n/I^{n+1} ⊗^L_A Δ_{R/A} = Δ̄_{R/A}{n} factors through an isomorphism gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n}, functorial in R; gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0. (2) gr^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ R̂, the derived p-completion of R. (3) If the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth over Ā (for example X = Spf R affine smooth), then gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ τ^{≤ n} Δ̄_{R/A}{n}: H^m(gr^n_N) ≅ Ω̂^m_{R/Ā}{n − m} for 0 ≤ m ≤ n and H^m(gr^n_N) = 0 otherwise. (4) gr^1_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ L_{R/A}[−1]^∧, the shifted p-completed cotangent complex of R over A. (5) For every R the filtered object Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is connective for the Beilinson t-structure of DF(A): gr^n_N lies in D^{≤ n} for all n.

(A, I) bounded prism; R animated Ā-algebra; the conjugate filtration and the twist {n} = ⊗ (I/I²)^{⊗ n} are those of [§2.3](#layer-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison). The isomorphism in (1) is A-linear: the semilinearity of the perfectoid statement [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces) has been absorbed into the Frobenius twist. (4) is BS22 Remark 15.6, which prints L_{X/A} ≃ gr^1_N Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} without the shift and cites Theorem 1.16 (2) for (3); the target states the corrected form. The Beilinson t-structure is required from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 (BMS2 Definition 5.3).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 15.3 (= Theorem 1.16 (3)) and Theorem 15.2 (2); pp. 8, 102, 103; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remarks 5.1.2, 5.1.3, 5.1.5; p. 115; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 15.6; p. 105.)

**Proof route.** Compute the associated graded by right Kan extension on the large basis and then polynomial left Kan extension, obtaining Fil_n^conj with its twist. Fil₀ is R, and smooth algebras identify conjugate stages with canonical truncations. The first nontrivial piece is the cotangent complex, and the finite filtration gives the asserted amplitude.

**Checks.**

- R = Ā: gr^n = I^n/I^{n+1} = Ā{n}. R = Ā⟨T⟩: gr^n_N has H^0 = R{n} and, for n ≥ 1, H^1 = Ω̂^1_{R/Ā}{n−1}. R large quasisyntomic: gr^n_N is the discrete module Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n}. Comparison with the Hodge–Tate side: the associated graded of the Nygaard filtration is the conjugate (Hodge–Tate) filtration, twisted; comparison with the de Rham side is [§3.19](#layer-3-nygaard-hodge-comparison).

### 3.16 The Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius (BS22 Theorem 15.3)

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra, X = Spf R, Δ = Δ_{R/A} = RΓ_Δ(X/A). (1) The filtered Frobenius Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ → I^• ⊗ Δ factors uniquely through the connective cover τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ Δ) for the Beilinson t-structure, whose underlying complex is Lη_I Δ. On underlying complexes this gives a canonical map φ̃ : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Lη_I Δ_{R/A} such that the relative Frobenius factors as φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Lη_I Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, the second map being the canonical one (it exists because Δ lies in D^{≥0} and H^0(Δ) is I-torsion-free). (2) φ̃ is an isomorphism. (3) The filtered map Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ Δ_{R/A}) is an isomorphism of filtered objects: Fil^•(φ) exhibits the Nygaard filtration as the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration. For an I-torsion-free complex K^• representing Δ, Fil^i_N corresponds under φ̃ to the subcomplex I^iK^• ∩ η_I K^• of η_I K^•. In particular lim_i Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = 0. (4) φ̃ is a map of commutative algebra objects, compatible with base change in (A, I) and with étale localisation on R; for a smooth formal A/I-scheme X it globalises to an isomorphism φ̃ : Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ≅ Lη_I Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A).

(A, I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. No orientation of I and no hypothesis on W(A/I) is made. Lη_I is the derived décalage functor of AInfCohomology:AI.1 for the invertible ideal I ⊂ A (on the ringed topos (X_ét, A) in the global statement); it is not exact, and the statement is one about objects and maps in D(A). The Beilinson t-structure, τ^{≤0}_B, and the identification of Lη_I K with the underlying complex of τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ K) (BMS2 Theorem 5.4 and Proposition 5.8) are required from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 and AInfCohomology:AI.1.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 15.3 (= Theorem 1.16 (4)) and its proof; pp. 8, 103; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollaries 5.2.11 and 5.2.14; p.123; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Proposition 5.8 and its proof; p. 32; [BMS1](#ref-bms1), Lemma 6.10 and Proposition 6.12; pp. 51, 52.)

**Proof route.** The filtered Frobenius factors through the Beilinson connective cover, whose underlying object is Lη_I and whose reduction is the Bockstein de-Rham complex. Étale descent reduces to polynomial charts, where the universal oriented crystalline calculation and Cartier identify the graded maps; filtration completeness and derived Nakayama give the equivalence. Monoidality follows from τ_B, and base change is proved through the smooth differential-form description rather than arbitrary base change for Lη.

- R = A/I: φ_A^*Δ = A = Lη_I A and φ̃ is the identity. Crystalline prism (W(k), (p)): the statement is the Berthelot–Ogus isomorphism φ : RΓ_crys ≅ Lη_p RΓ_crys, with the Nygaard filtration on the source and the décalage filtration on the target (BMS2 Proposition 8.5 and its corollary). Cohomology: H^i(φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) ≅ (H^i(Δ_{R/A})/H^i(Δ_{R/A})[I]) ⊗ I^{⊗ i} (AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-cohomology). ### 3.17 De Rham comparison for every bounded prism (BS22 Corollary 15.4)

(1) Fix a bounded (A,I), and let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I (locally p-completely smooth, with the usual finite presentation condition). On X_ét, the following canonical equivalence respects its E_∞-algebra structure: Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A/I ≅ Ω^•_{X/(A/I)}, the p-completed de Rham complex. No hypothesis on W(A/I) is needed. (2) For R p-completely smooth over A/I the isomorphism φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I ≅ Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)} is the composite of φ̃ ⊗ A/I ([§3.16](#layer-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation)), the Bockstein reduction Lη_IΔ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I ≃ (H^•(Δ̄_{R/A}){•}, β_I), and the Hodge–Tate comparison (H^•(Δ̄_{R/A}){•}, β_I) ≅ (Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)}, d). (3) (Derived form, Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.2.5) For every animated commutative A/I-algebra R there is a natural isomorphism A/I ⊗^L_A φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ dR^∧_{R/(A/I)} with the p-completed derived de Rham complex, the left Kan extension of (2) from polynomial algebras.

(A, I) is a bounded prism; X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, not necessarily affine or proper. The scalar extension is along φ_A followed by A → A/I and is derived (p, I)-completed; it is not the untwisted reduction Δ̄_{X/A}, whose cohomology is the Hodge–Tate cohomology. BS22 Corollary 15.4 prints the right-hand side as Ω^*_{R/(A/I)}; it is Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}. [§1.21](#layer-1-de-rham-comparison) is the same statement under the hypothesis that W(A/I) is p-torsion-free (BS22 Theorem 6.4), proved without Lη. The sources do not compare the two isomorphisms when both are defined, and the target does not assert that they coincide. Bhatt–Lurie prove (3) through the Hodge–Tate divisor of the Cartier–Witt stack; use the Bhatt–Scholze route, which needs nothing from Layer 4.

### 3.18 The image of Frobenius on prismatic cohomology (BS22 Corollary 15.5)

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth formal A/I-scheme. For every i ≥ 0 there is a natural map V_i : τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) such that φ ∘ V_i is the natural map τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} induced by I^{⊗ i} → A, and V_i ∘ (φ ⊗ 1) : τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} is the natural map. In particular V_i induces V_i : H^i_Δ(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}), an inverse of φ up to I^{⊗ i}; when I = (d), V_i φ = φ V_i = d^i on H^i. For X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) = H^i(φ_A^* RΓ_Δ(X/A)) and the linearised Frobenius φ_A^* RΓ_Δ(X/A) → RΓ_Δ(X/A) becomes an isomorphism after inverting I.

BS22 Corollary 15.5 prints the induced map as H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) ⊗ I^{⊗ i} → H^i_Δ(X/A); source and target are interchanged. The target states the corrected direction, which is that of BS22 Theorem 1.8 (6). The identification H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) = H^i(φ_A^*RΓ_Δ(X/A)) uses the completed quasi-coherent projection formula on a quasi-compact quasi-separated X, established through finite affine descent as in [§1.20](#layer-1-prismatic-base-change); the sheaf-level statement needs no such hypothesis.

### 3.19 Comparison of the Nygaard filtration with the Hodge filtration of derived de Rham cohomology

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I, and R an animated commutative Ā-algebra. (1) (Bockstein and de Rham complex) Let β : H^n(gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) → H^{n+1}(gr^{n+1}_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) be the boundary map of gr^{n+1}_N → Fil^n_N/Fil^{n+2}_N → gr^n_N. Then (⊕_n H^n(gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}), β) is a commutative differential graded algebra and there is a unique isomorphism of commutative differential graded algebras θ onto the p-completed de Rham complex (Ω̂^•_{R/Ā}, d) that in degree 0 is the isomorphism H^0(gr^0_N) ≅ H^0(R̂). (2) There is a canonical map of commutative algebra objects of DF(A), Fil^•(γ_R) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}, to the p-completed derived de Rham complex with its Hodge filtration, determined by functoriality in R and by gr^0(γ_R) being the isomorphism gr^0_N ≅ R̂ ≅ gr^0_Hodge. (3) There is a functorial fibre sequence in DF(A): I ⊗^L_A Fil^{•−1}_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}, the first map being the multiplication v of [§3.14](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-filtration) and the second Fil^•(γ_R). In filtration degree 0 it is the de Rham comparison [§3.17](#layer-3-de-rham-comparison-general) (3). (4) Consequently Ā ⊗^L_A lim_m Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ lim_m Fil^m_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}; and if the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d over Ā then v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^n_N → Fil^{n+1}_N is an isomorphism for n ≥ d, so Fil^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ I^{⊗(n−d)} ⊗_A Fil^d_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} for n ≥ d.

(A, I) bounded prism; R animated Ā-algebra; dR^∧_{R/Ā} and its Hodge filtration are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2, p-completed; for p-completely smooth R they are the p-completed de Rham complex with its stupid filtration. In (1) the de Rham complex is that of π_0(R) relative to Ā, and Ω̂^n is H^0 of the derived p-completion of Ω^n_{π_0(R)/Ā} (Bhatt–Lurie's convention; it need not be p-adically separated and agrees with the classical completion when Ω^n has bounded p^∞-torsion). In the proof of BL22 Corollary 5.2.8 the Hodge–Tate comparison is printed gr_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n} ≃ LΩ̂^n_{R/Ā}[n]; the shift is [−n]. The fibre sequence compares three filtrations at once: on graded pieces it reads Fil_{n−1}^conj Δ̄{n} → Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n} → gr_n^conj Δ̄{n} ≅ LΩ̂^n_{R/Ā}[−n].

### 3.20 Nygaard completion

(a) For a prism (B, J) the Nygaard completion is the ring B̂ = lim_i B/Fil^i_N B (inverse limit along the surjections B/Fil^{i+1}_N → B/Fil^i_N), with the canonical map c : B → B̂ and the filtration Fil^i_N B̂ = ker(B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B). Then ker(c) = ∩_i Fil^i_N B; B̂/Fil^i_N B̂ = B/Fil^i_N B; gr^i_N B̂ = gr^i_N B; and B̂ is complete for its filtration. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Δ̂_S denotes the Nygaard completion of Δ_S; Δ̂_S/Fil^1_N Δ̂_S ≅ S and gr^i_N Δ̂_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} ([§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces)). (b) Frobenius. Assume J = (d) (then B is d-adically complete). Since φ(Fil^n_N B) ⊂ d^n B, φ induces a ring map φ̂ : B̂ → lim_n B/d^n B = B with φ̂ ∘ c = φ; the Frobenius of B̂ is c ∘ φ̂, so it factors through B. Likewise the divided Frobenius extends to φ_i : Fil^i_N B̂ → B with d^i φ_i = φ̂ on Fil^i_N B̂, and with twists to φ_i : Fil^i_N B̂ ⊗_B B{i} → B̂{i}. (c) Filtered objects. For a filtered object Fil^• of DF(A) with underlying object M = Fil^0 (N-indexed), the completion is M̂ = lim_i M/Fil^i with Fil^i M̂ = lim_{j ≥ i} Fil^i/Fil^j; M → M̂ is an isomorphism if and only if lim_i Fil^i = 0, and then M is called Nygaard-complete. This defines the Nygaard completions of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ([§3.14](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-filtration)) and of Δ_{S/A} over a perfectoid base ([§3.4](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration)); for a tower of surjections of discrete modules the derived limit is the limit, so (a) is a special case. (d) On quasisyntomic algebras over a perfectoid ring R, S ↦ Fil^•_N Δ̂_{S/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf of complete filtered objects, the unfolding of (a) from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. The map Δ → Δ̂ is not an isomorphism in general; [§3.21](#layer-3-nygaard-completeness) states when it is, and [§3.23](#layer-3-nygaard-incomplete-example) gives a ring S for which Δ_S → Δ̂_S is injective and not surjective.

(B, J) is a prism; in (b) J is principal, which holds for the initial prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring. Completion means completion with respect to the Nygaard filtration only; no (p, J)-adic completion is applied, and by BS22 Lemma 13.2 (2) none is needed for Δ_S ([§3.26](#layer-3-bms2-comparison)). Statement (b) is not printed in the sources in this form; it is immediate from the definition of the filtration and is needed because the syntomic complexes of Layer 6 need φ_i on the completion without passing through topological Hochschild homology. Δ and Δ̂ are distinct objects: no statement of the layer identifies them outside the cases listed in [§3.21](#layer-3-nygaard-completeness).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 13.1 and the proof of Lemma 13.2; p. 94; [BL22](#ref-bl22), §5 introduction and Definition 5.8.5; p. 148; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Definition 5.1 and Lemma 5.2 (2); p. 28.)

- `Prismatic.Nygaard.mem_completion_iff`: A family (x_i) lies in B̂ iff x_j maps to x_i under B/Fil^j_N → B/Fil^i_N for all i ≤ j.

### 3.21 Completeness of the Nygaard filtration: exact statements

(1) (Criterion) For a prism (B, J): c : B → B̂ is injective iff ∩_i Fil^i_N B = 0, and bijective iff moreover lim^1_i Fil^i_N B = 0; for a filtered object, M → M̂ is an isomorphism iff lim_i Fil^i = 0. (2) (Perfectoid rings) If S is perfectoid then Δ_S = A_inf(S) is Nygaard-complete: Fil^i_N = (e^i) with e = φ^{-1}(d), and A_inf(S) is e-adically complete. (3) (Relative criterion, Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.2.10) For a bounded prism (A, I) and an animated A/I-algebra R: φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is Nygaard-complete if and only if the p-completed derived de Rham complex dR^∧_{R/(A/I)} is Hodge-complete (lim_m Fil^m_Hodge = 0). (4) (Smooth case, Corollary 5.2.11) If R is p-completely flat over A/I and R/pR is a filtered colimit of smooth (A/I)/p-algebras, in particular if R is p-completely smooth, then φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is Nygaard-complete; if R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d then moreover Fil^n_N = I^{⊗(n−d)} ⊗ Fil^d_N for n ≥ d. (5) (Perfect base) For a perfect prism (A, I) and a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra S: Δ_{S/A} is Nygaard-complete for the filtration of [§3.4](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration) iff dR^∧_{S/(A/I)} is Hodge-complete. In particular Δ_S ≠ Δ̂_S for S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X) ([§3.23](#layer-3-nygaard-incomplete-example)). (6) (Exhaustiveness) The Nygaard filtration is exhaustive in the trivial sense Fil^0_N = Δ; the non-trivial exhaustiveness statement is [§3.22](#layer-3-nygaard-frobenius-colimit).

Completeness always refers to the Nygaard filtration; all objects are already derived (p, I)-complete. In (3), (4) the filtration is the relative one on the Frobenius twist; in (2), (5) the base prism is perfect and the filtration is on Δ itself. Hodge-completeness of derived de Rham cohomology is a property owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2; for p-completely smooth R the Hodge filtration is the finite stupid filtration. BL22 Remark 5.8.4 prints Fil^n ≃ I^{n−d} Fil^{n−d}; the correct right-hand side is I^{n−d} ⊗ Fil^d; (4) states the relative form.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollaries 5.2.9, 5.2.10, 5.2.11; pp.122–123; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Example 5.8.1 and Proposition 5.8.2; p. 147; [BS22](#ref-bs22), the warning after Definition 12.1; p. 86.)

**Proof route.** Use the Milnor lim/lim¹ criterion for the completion map. For a perfect prism, invertibility of φ identifies the Nygaard ideals with powers of e=φ^−1(d), cofinal with the stated topology; after reduction modulo I, Nygaard completeness is equivalently completeness of the Hodge tower. The smooth-form filtration is complete, and perfect-Frobenius base change gives the remaining comparison.

**Checks.**

- (Z_p, (p)), S = F_p: Δ = Z_p, Fil^i = (p^i), complete. R = A/I⟨T⟩: complete, with Fil^n_N = I^{n−1} ⊗ Fil^1_N for n ≥ 1. S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X): dR^∧_{S/F_p} is the divided power algebra with its divided power filtration, which is not complete; correspondingly Δ_S ≠ Δ̂_S. The statement of BS22 Theorem 13.1 involves Δ̂_S and not Δ_S for exactly this reason.

### 3.22 Prismatic cohomology as the completed colimit of the Nygaard pieces

Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R an animated commutative A/I-algebra. The maps v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^m_N → Fil^{m+1}_N of [§3.14](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-filtration) give a diagram φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{−1} ⊗ Fil^1_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{−2} ⊗ Fil^2_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → ⋯, and the maps I^{−m} ⊗ Fil^m(φ) : I^{−m} ⊗ Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} are compatible with it. (1) The induced map from the (p, I)-completed colimit of this diagram to Δ_{R/A} is an isomorphism: the relative Frobenius exhibits Δ_{R/A} as the completed union of the twisted Nygaard pieces. (2) If the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d, the diagram is constant from m = d on and Fil^m(φ) : Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{⊗ m} ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} is an isomorphism for every m ≥ d. (3) Consequently for X smooth over A/I of dimension ≤ d and i ≥ d, RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{−/A}) ≅ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗ i}.

(A, I) bounded prism; R animated A/I-algebra; I^{−m} is the dual of I^{⊗ m}. The colimit is formed in the (p, I)-complete derived category of A. BS22 states (3) for the Nygaard-completed sheaf; by [§3.21](#layer-3-nygaard-completeness) (4) completion changes nothing for smooth X.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollary 5.2.16 and its proof; p. 123; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollary 5.2.15; p. 123; [BS22](#ref-bs22), §15.2, the paragraph after Proposition 15.7; p. 105.)

**Proof route.** For a polynomial algebra in d variables the conjugate filtration is terminal at d, so Fil_d^conj→Δ̄ is an equivalence. The corresponding graded Nygaard map is therefore an equivalence by derived Nakayama. Polynomial extension and étale gluing give the stated range.

- R = A/I (d = 0): Fil^m_N = I^m and I^{−m} ⊗ I^m = A = Δ for all m. Perfect prism and S perfectoid: e^{−m}(e^m) = A_inf(S). After inverting I the relative Frobenius φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}[1/I] → Δ_{R/A}[1/I] is an isomorphism for smooth R, in agreement with [§3.18](#layer-3-image-of-frobenius).

### 3.23 A quasiregular semiperfectoid ring whose prism is not Nygaard-complete

Let S_0 = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X), a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, with perfect base prism (Z_p, (p)). (1) Δ_{S_0} = Z_p⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/p}^∧, the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) in Z_p[Y^{1/p^∞}], with δ(Y^{1/p^n}) = 0 and X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}}; it is the p-completion of ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋!. (2) Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} is the p-completion of ⊕_i p^{max(n−⌊i⌋, 0)} Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋!; equivalently it is generated by the elements p^a · Y^b/b! · Y^ε with a + b ≥ n, b ∈ N, 0 ≤ ε < 1. (3) ∩_n Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} = 0, and Δ̂_{S_0} is the set of families (a_i)_{i ∈ N[1/p]} of p-adic integers, written Σ a_i Y^i/⌊i⌋!, such that for every n only finitely many i with ⌊i⌋ < n have a_i ∉ p^{n−⌊i⌋}Z_p; Δ_{S_0} is the subset of families with a_i → 0 p-adically. (4) The element exp(Y) = Σ_{m ≥ 0} Y^m/m! lies in Δ̂_{S_0} and not in Δ_{S_0}. Hence c : Δ_{S_0} → Δ̂_{S_0} is injective and not surjective, and lim^1_n Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} ≠ 0. (5) The same holds for the key case S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧ of [§3.2](#layer-3-nygaard-key-case), with Σ_m Y^m/[m]_q! ∈ Δ̂_S ∖ Δ_S. By contrast Δ_S = Δ̂_S for S perfectoid.

S_0 is the reduction of the key case along Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ → F_p; the description (1), (2) is that of [§3.2](#layer-3-nygaard-key-case) at q = 1. ### 3.24 The Nygaard filtration in coordinates (de Rham and q-de Rham models)

Let (A, (d)) be a perfect prism, d′ = φ_A(d), and R a p-completely smooth A/d-algebra. Let M^• be a cochain complex of A-modules in degrees ≥ 0 whose terms are d-torsion-free, d′-torsion-free and d-adically complete, with a φ_A-semilinear endomorphism φ_M of complexes, and an isomorphism M^• ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} in D(A) carrying φ_M to the Frobenius. Assume (a) φ_M(M^n) ⊂ d′^n M^n for all n, and (b) for all n the map M^n/dM^n → H^n(M^•/d′M^•), x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/d′^n, is bijective. Then the subcomplexes N^iM^• = d^{max(i − •, 0)} M^• (in degree n: d^{max(i−n,0)}M^n), with φ_M : N^iM^• → d′^iM^•, represent the relative Nygaard filtration and its filtered Frobenius: there is a unique isomorphism N^•M^• ≅ Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} in DF(A) compatible with the maps to the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A}. If moreover φ_M/d′^n : M^n/d → M^n/d′ is injective for all n, then N^iM^n = {x ∈ M^n : φ_M(x) ∈ d′^i M^n}. Instances. (i) (BMS2 Proposition 8.7) A = W(k) with k a perfect field, d = d′ = p, R smooth over k, Ã a p-completely smooth lift of R with a Frobenius lift, M^• the p-completed de Rham complex of Ã over W(k): the Nygaard filtration of crystalline cohomology is p^{max(i − •, 0)} Ω^•_{Ã/W(k)}. (ii) (BMS2 Remark 9.11) A = A_inf(O_C), d = ξ, d′ = ξ̃ = [p]_q with q = [ε], R with a framing, M^• the framed q-de Rham complex q-Ω^•_{R̃/A_inf} with φ(T_j) = T_j^p: the Nygaard filtration is ξ^{max(i − •, 0)} q-Ω^•_{R̃/A_inf}.

(A, (d)) is a perfect prism; under Δ_{R/A} = (φ_A)_* φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} the ideal I^i Δ corresponds to d′^i M, which is why d′ appears in (a) and d in the conclusion. Hypothesis (b) is the Cartier isomorphism in the model M: in (i) it is the inverse Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3), in (ii) its q-analogue. In instance (ii) the identification of the framed q-de Rham complex with φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf} (through AΩ) and hypothesis (b) are supplied by Layer 5, which applies this target; prove here the criterion and instance (i). BMS2 Remark 9.11 prints q = [ε] − 1; the q-de Rham complex of BMS1 Definition 9.5 is taken with q = [ε], so that q − 1 = μ. BMS2 prove (i) through the de Rham–Witt complex; derive it from the Lη_I factorisation, which needs no de Rham–Witt theory.

### 3.25 δ on the Nygaard completion

For Δ_S of a quasiregular semiperfectoid S over an oriented perfect prism (A,(d)), δ is uniformly continuous for the topology generated by Fil^i_NΔ_S+(p,d)^jΔ_S. It extends uniquely to the Nygaard completion as a δ-structure. It commutes with the extended Frobenius and agrees with δ on Δ_S; this is not an application of δ-adic completion with the Nygaard filtration as an adic ideal.

Δ_S is a δ-ring, derived (p,d)-complete and classically complete by bounded complete flatness. Fil^i_N=φ^(-1)(d^iΔ_S); d is distinguished.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 13.1, Lemma 13.2 and the proof of Theorem 14.1, §§13–14; pp. 94–95, 97.)

*Needs:* [§0.1](#layer-0-delta-frobenius-dictionary), [§0.1](#layer-0-correction-identity), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp), [§3.20](#layer-3-nygaard-completion), [§3.2](#layer-3-nygaard-key-case), [§3.3](#layer-3-nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid), [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces), `PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.4`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Proof route.** Put K=(p,d): choose a root presentation surjective on cotangent complexes and hence on Δ and each Nygaard ideal, then use filtered colimits, Künneth and André’s cover to reduce the estimate δ(Fil_N^i)⊂Fil_N^(pi)+K^(i−1) to the cyclotomic generators e of degree one (unrestricted K⁰ error) and Y^r/[r]_q! (homogeneous delta degree pr). For products, writing δ(x)=x₁+x₂ and δ(y)=y₁+y₂ with x₂∈K^(j−1), y₂∈K^(k−1), group the mixed terms as (φ(x)−px₂)y₂+(φ(y)−py₂)x₂ and px₂y₂ to obtain K^(j+k−1); faithful descent and the integral addition correction finish the estimate, while δ(K^(j+1))⊂K^j proves uniform continuity. Each gr_N^i is semilinearly Fil_i^conj Δ̄{i}, hence classically p-complete, and φ(d) is a unit times p modulo d, so induction makes every finite quotient K-complete and identifies the mixed and Nygaard completions; extend delta and its polynomial identities by continuity, with uniqueness by density (BS22 Lemma 13.2, pp.94–95).


**Checks.** For a perfect prism with e=φ^(-1)(d), the extension is the existing δ on its e-adically complete ring. If S=O_C, then δ(e) is a unit and δ(e²)≡p δ(e)² modulo e; since A_inf(O_C)/e is p-torsion-free, this is nonzero. Thus δ(Fil²_N)⊂Fil¹_N is false even for a perfect prism. In the crystalline prism (Z_p,(p)), δ(p^i)=p^(i−1)−p^(pi−1); the error has exactly the permitted K^(i−1) order for i≥1. The zero ring has the unique zero operation and zero completions. These checks distinguish mixed continuity from an unsupported one-step drop in Nygaard degree.

## Layer 4: Absolute prismatic cohomology and Cartier–Witt geometry

The absolute site and Cartier–Witt stack encode compatible relative complexes over all bounded prisms. The Hodge–Tate divisor, its Sen operator and the absolute Nygaard filtration carry the same twists as the relative comparisons.

<a id="layer-4-formal-qcoh"></a>

### 4.0 Quasi-coherent complexes, descent and formal completion

For a space-valued prestack X on ordinary commutative rings, define `QCohPrestack(X)` as the limit of D(R) over its ∞-category of affine points. A point is a pair (R,x∈X(R)); a transition consists of a ring map R→S and a path from its image of x to the chosen S-point, with all higher path coherences. The transition on complexes is S⊗^L_R−. Thus an object is a family M_(R,x) together with coherent equivalences S⊗^L_R M_(R,x)≃M_(S,y). Construct the limit in symmetric monoidal ∞-categories, using E0 limits and E5:abstract's actual derived module ∞-categories. Its unit evaluates to R; a morphism is an equivalence exactly when every evaluation is. Pullback along f:X→Y is precomposition and preserves colimits and tensor products. Evaluation gives D(Spec R)≃D(R), and D carries colimits of prestacks to limits of categories. Each D(X) is stable with small colimits; presentability is asserted in a fixed larger universe when X lies in the small-colimit closure of affine representables and their fpqc sheafifications. These size conditions apply to the stacks used below. The homotopy category of D(Spec R) agrees with the ordinary derived category, but taking that homotopy category before the pointwise limit loses descent data. (Lurie, [SAG](#ref-sag), Definition 6.2.2.1 and Remarks 6.2.2.5–6.2.2.7, pp.490–491; Proposition 6.2.3.4, pp.492–493.)

Define `QCohPrestack.Perf(X)` by requiring every evaluation to be a perfect R-complex. Prove this is precisely the dualizable subcategory: a dualizable object evaluates to one, and the evaluation duals of a pointwise perfect object, with their evaluation and coevaluation maps, assemble uniquely in the monoidal limit. Tensor-invertibility is likewise pointwise tensor-invertibility. Perfect does not mean concentrated in degree zero; invertible does not mean that a generator has been chosen. ([HA](#ref-ha), Proposition 4.6.1.11, p.620, and Proposition 7.2.4.4, p.1263, applied to the derived module categories; the converse uses that the unit R is compact and that perfect complexes are generated from R by finite colimits and retracts.)

The API is `QCohPrestack.eval`, `QCohPrestack.ofPoints`, `QCohPrestack.pullback`, `QCohPrestack.specEquiv`, `QCohPrestack.limitOfColimit`, `QCohPrestack.isEquiv_iff_eval`, `QCohPrestack.unit_eval`, `QCohPrestack.isDualizable_iff_perfect`, `QCohPrestack.isInvertible_iff` and `QCohPrestack.homotopyCategory_spec`, including the identity, composition and coherent base-change laws for evaluations and pullbacks.

**Checks.**

- `QCohPrestack.empty`, `QCohPrestack.terminal`: D(∅) is the zero stable category; D(Spec Z)=D(Z). Replacing the pointwise limit by a direct sum fails the empty case.
- `QCohPrestack.spec_homotopy`: For Spec R, Hom(O,O[i]) is R for i=0 and zero otherwise. The affine point formula recovers the actual derived category.
- `QCohPrestack.classifying_Z2`: For B(Z/2) over F₂, H¹(B(Z/2),O)=F₂. Pullback to the trivializing affine point forgets that class, so an atlas value alone cannot specify a complex or a map.
- `QCohPrestack.dualizable_spec`: Z⊕Z[3] is perfect and dualizable in D(Z); Q is not dualizable. Restricting perfection to vector bundles, or declaring every flat module perfect, gives wrong answers.
- The unit is invertible; O⊕O over a nonzero field is not. A shift O[1] is invertible although it is not a line bundle in degree zero.

Prove `QCohPrestack.flatDescent`: for a faithfully flat R→S, extension of scalars induces an equivalence D(R)≃Tot D(S^{⊗_R(•+1)}). Flatness makes the ordinary tensor powers agree with the derived ones. Use SAG Corollary D.6.3.3, p.2177, for the full unbounded enhanced module categories; an argument that merely tensors convergent Postnikov towers does not establish this assertion. Combining this affine result with the pointwise limit proves `sheafificationEquiv`: an fpqc sheafification equivalence X→Y induces D(Y)≃D(X). Consequently an effective epimorphism U→X in the fpqc ∞-topos gives `cechDescent`, D(X)≃Tot D(U_•), and the heart on an affine recovers ordinary module descent. D0 supplies ordinary groupoid stacks and SF.1 affine descent; E2 supplies effective epimorphisms and hypercovers in the ∞-topos, rather than treating groupoid stackification as arbitrary space-valued sheafification. ([SAG](#ref-sag), Proposition 6.2.3.1 and Remarks 6.2.3.2–6.2.3.3, p.492.)

**Checks.**

- For R→R the augmented totalization is D(R), with the identity comparison.
- For a faithfully flat finite product of localizations covering Spec R, the degree-zero descent objects are precisely the usual glued modules, and a two-term complex retains its differential.
- Z→F_p is not a descent cover: Q is a nonzero Z-complex whose derived pullback vanishes. Surjectivity of a ring map is not a replacement for faithful flatness.
- The groupoid nerve of B(Z/2) retains the preceding H¹ class; taking invariants of the atlas module without derived totalization loses it.

For a representable **flat affine** f:Y→X, construct `QCohPrestack.affinePushforward` by restriction of scalars on each affine base change: if Y×_X Spec R=Spec B, the value is Res^B_R of the corresponding B-complex. These restrictions form a quasi-coherent family because B is R-flat: for R→R′ and B′=B⊗_R R′, the canonical map R′⊗^L_R Res N→Res(B′⊗^L_B N) is an equivalence. Prove f_* is right adjoint to f^*, preserves colimits, obeys `affineBaseChange` for every ordinary cartesian base-change square, and satisfies `affineProjectionFormula`, f_*(f^*M⊗N)≃M⊗f_*N. All these assertions are identities of derived tensor and restriction on affine points and hence descend. One can instead use derived prestacks and derived fibre products without flatness; that is a different assertion from base change for ordinary prestacks. ([SAG](#ref-sag), Proposition 6.3.4.1, pp.505–506, and Corollary 6.3.4.3, pp.506–507, specialized from spectral affine morphisms to ordinary flat ones.)

**Checks.**

- For f=id, pushforward, its adjunction and projection formula are the identity.
- For R→R[t], restriction of the rank-one B-module gives the actual underlying R-module R[t]; base change to any R′ gives R′[t]. It is not the rank-one R-module.
- In the ordinary square obtained by base-changing Z→F_p along Z→F_p, the fibre product ring is F_p, while F_p⊗^L_Z F_p has nonzero H⁻¹ and H⁰, both F_p. Thus unrestricted ordinary nonflat base change is false.
- For N=B and M=R[1], the projection formula gives B[1] on both sides, fixing the use of derived tensor and the shift.

For a finitely generated ideal J⊂R, let Spf_J R be the ordinary-ring prestack of maps R→S whose image of J is nilpotent. Its pointwise category is lim_n D(R/J^n), with derived transitions. Define the separate complete-module category `FormalQCoh(Spf_J R)=D(R)^∧_J`, with completed tensor and colimits. The target `FormalAffineQCoh.completeEquiv` identifies these categories for every bounded prism with J=(p,I), with no bound on the complexes. The proof below establishes the finite regular-ideal range, including crystalline and transversal prism charts and the Hodge–Tate charts of a transversal Čech nerve. **The nonregular bounded-prism effectivity argument remains a gap.** BL22 states the full comparison before Proposition 3.3.5, p.43, with Warning 3.3.6; SAG Theorem 8.3.4.4 and Remark 8.3.4.5, pp.667–668, only give the restricted connective spectral comparison and do not fill this gap.

For a regular sequence J=(f₁,…,f_r), put B_n=R/(f₁^n,…,f_r^n). These quotients are cofinal with the J-power quotients and perfect of uniform R-Tor amplitude [−r,0]. Given a compatible system M_n∈D(B_n), set M=Rlim M_n. For n≥k the coefficient fibre E_(n,k)=fib(B_n⊗^L_R B_k→B_k) has cohomology in [−r,−1]; its Koszul transition from m to n multiplies degree-one generators by f_i^(m−n), so kills cohomology when m−n≥k. Restrict all terms to D(B_(n+rk)): r such ghost maps have zero composite by the t-structure truncation argument on this interval of length r. Thus E_(n+rk,k)→E_(n,k) is zero **before tensoring** with M_(n+rk). The resulting fibre tower is uniformly pro-zero even for two-sided unbounded M_n, and perfectness of B_k permits tensoring through Rlim, giving B_k⊗^L_R M≃M_k. The unit is the Koszul completion formula of DD.1. This proves `FormalAffineQCoh.regularIdealEquiv` without noetherianity or completeness of R; its unit is Λ_J R. For J=0 use the affine equivalence. Crystalline charts use the regular element p; transversal charts use (d,p), and their Hodge–Tate charts use p on A/d. (BS15 Lemmas 3.5.4–3.5.7, pp.25–26; BS22 §1.2 footnote 7, p.12.)

The API is `FormalAffineQCoh.eval` (M evaluates to S⊗^L_R M), `FormalAffineQCoh.unit`, `FormalAffineQCoh.tensor`, `FormalAffineQCoh.colimit`, `FormalAffineQCoh.pullback`, `FormalAffineQCoh.reductions`, `FormalAffineQCoh.regularReductions`, `regularIdealEquiv` and `completeEquiv`. Tensor and colimits apply Λ_J after the underlying D(R) operation; pullback along an adic map is Λ_(JB)(B⊗^L_R−). All equations include monoidal and composition coherence. The complete-module operations themselves follow from DD.1 independently of that obligation.
