<a id="layer-4-absolute-prismatic-site"></a>

### 4.1 The absolute prismatic site of a p-adic formal scheme

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. The absolute prismatic site X_Δ is the opposite of the category whose objects are triples (A, I, u), with (A, I) a bounded prism and u : Spf(A/I) → X a morphism of p-adic formal schemes (A/I carries the p-adic topology), and whose morphisms (A, I, u) → (B, J, v) are the maps of prisms f : (A, I) → (B, J) with u ∘ Spf(f mod I) = v. The flat topology on X_Δ is generated by the finite families {(A, I, u) → (A_s, I_s, u_s)}_s of maps of prisms over X for which A → ∏_s A_s is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat. The structure sheaf is O_Δ(A, I, u) = A, with its δ-structure and Frobenius φ; the prism-ideal sheaf (the ideal sheaf of the Hodge–Tate divisor) is I_Δ(A, I, u) = I ⊂ A; the reduced structure sheaf is Ō_Δ(A, I, u) = A/I = O_Δ/I_Δ. For all integers m, n the presheaf (A, I, u) ↦ I^m ⊗_A A{n} is a sheaf with values in the p-complete derived ∞-category D̂(Z_p), and RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(X){n} denotes the limit of I^m{n} over the category of triples (A, I, u). Comparison with relative sites: if X lies over Spf(A/I) for a bounded prism (A, I), the relative site (X/A)_Δ is the category of objects (B, J, v) of X_Δ together with a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) such that v lies over Spf(B/J) → Spf(A/I); the forgetful functor (X/A)_Δ → X_Δ carries covers to covers and O_Δ, I_Δ, Ō_Δ to the relative sheaves. If (A, I) is a perfect prism this functor is an equivalence (X/A)_Δ ≃ X_Δ.

X is a p-adic formal scheme; Bhatt–Lurie assume in addition that X is bounded (locally Spf of a p-complete ring with bounded p-power torsion) wherever the site computes cohomology. Every prism in the site is bounded; the convention is that of Bhatt–Scholze (the site is the opposite category), while Bhatt–Lurie write (X)_Δ for the category of triples itself and put the topology on its opposite. For clarity, for a semiperfectoid ring the category having an initial object consists of all prisms, not only bounded ones; the absolute site here always uses bounded prisms. Complete flatness and the complete derived category are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Definition 2.3; p. 5; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Definition 4.4.27 and Remark 4.4.28; pp. 94, 95; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 4.7 and the lemma inside it; p. 38.)

- `Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.Hom`: A morphism (A, I, u) → (B, J, v): a map of prisms whose reduction carries u to v.
- `Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.ofPrism`: The tautological object (A, I, id) of (Spf A/I)_Δ attached to a bounded prism.
- `Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.idealSheaf`: The value I of the prism-ideal sheaf I_Δ on an object; the quotient of the structure sheaf by it is the reduced sheaf.
- `Prismatic.Absolute.RelativeObj`: An object of the relative site (R/A)_Δ is an object of (Spf R)_Δ with a map of prisms from (A, I) compatible with the structure maps.
- `Prismatic.Absolute.SiteObj.existsUnique_hom_of_perfect`: For a perfect prism (A, I), every object of (Spf A/I)_Δ receives a unique morphism from (A, I, id); hence (X/A)_Δ ≃ X_Δ for X over A/I.

Unwinding the relative and absolute definitions gives their comparison; for a perfect base the unique lift of each quotient map gives the equivalence. Repleteness follows from Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals Remark 2.4 and EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2.

For an F_p-algebra R every object (A, I, u) of (Spf R)_Δ is crystalline: I = (p).

<a id="layer-4-generalized-cartier-divisor"></a>

### 4.2 Generalized Cartier divisors and the stack Cart

Let R be a commutative ring. A generalized Cartier divisor of Spec R is a pair (I, α) with I an invertible R-module and α : I → R an R-linear map. Cart(R) is the groupoid whose objects are these pairs and whose morphisms (I, α) → (I′, α′) are the R-linear isomorphisms ρ : I → I′ with α = α′ ∘ ρ. A ring map f : R → S induces the pullback functor Cart(R) → Cart(S), (I, α) ↦ (S ⊗_R I, S ⊗ α). The pair is a Cartier divisor exactly when α is injective; the Cartier divisors form a full subgroupoid with only identity automorphisms. The functor R ↦ Cart(R) is a stack for the fpqc topology, equivalent to the quotient stack [A^1/G_m]: the divisor of an element f ∈ R is (R, f·), and (R, f·) ≅ (R, g·) exactly when g = u f for a unit u.

R is any commutative ring; for a scheme X the definition is the same with an invertible O_X-module. Injectivity of α is not preserved by pullback: this is the reason for the generalized notion.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Definition 3.1.1, Remarks 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 and the paragraph after them; p. 39.)

- `Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.Iso`: A morphism of Cart(R): a linear equivalence ρ : I ≃ I′ with α′ ∘ ρ = α.
- `Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.ofElement`: The principal divisor (R, f·) of an element f ∈ R.
- `Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.ofIdeal`: The Cartier divisor (I, inclusion) of an invertible ideal I ⊂ R.
- `Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.baseChange`: Pullback along a ring map f : R → S: (I, α) ↦ (S ⊗_R I, S ⊗ α).
- `Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.IsCartier`: α is injective; equivalently (I, α) comes from a Cartier divisor of Spec R.
- `Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.ofElement_iso_iff`: (R, f·) and (R, g·) are isomorphic in Cart(R) if and only if g = u f for a unit u of R.
- `Prismatic.WCart.GeneralizedCartierDivisor.isStack`: The fibre groupoid of invertible modules with a map to R defines a pseudofunctor on affine rings; its fpqc descent is expressed using Mathlib CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.IsStack and DescentData. Torsor and quotient-stack constructions remain owned by D0.

**Proof route.** An invertible module with a map to O gives the groupoid, with effective Cartier divisors precisely the injective maps (BL Definition 3.1.1 and Remarks 3.1.2–3.1.3). Effective fpqc descent for modules and their maps gives the stack property. Local trivializations identify its atlas with A¹ and its transition maps with G_m, giving [A¹/G_m].

<a id="layer-4-cartier-witt-divisor"></a>

### 4.3 Cartier–Witt divisors

Let R be a commutative ring in which p is nilpotent and let W(R) be its ring of p-typical Witt vectors, with its δ-structure whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius F. A Cartier–Witt divisor of R is a generalized Cartier divisor (I, α) of Spec W(R) such that (a) the image of I → W(R) → R (α followed by the restriction x ↦ x_0) is a nilpotent ideal of R, and (b) the image of I → W(R) → W(R) (α followed by δ) generates the unit ideal of W(R). WCart(R) is the full subgroupoid of Cart(W(R)) on these objects, and WCart(R) = ∅ when p is not nilpotent in R. In Witt coordinates x = (x_0, x_1, …) one has δ(x)_0 = x_1, and an element of W(R) with invertible x_0 is a unit when p is nilpotent in R; hence (a) and (b) together are equivalent to: every α(y)_0 is nilpotent, and the elements α(y)_1, y ∈ I, generate the unit ideal of R. A divisor is principalized when I = W(R); then α is multiplication by f = α(1), and (W(R), f·) is a Cartier–Witt divisor if and only if f lies in WCart_0(R) = {f ∈ W(R) : f_0 nilpotent, f_1 a unit}, the set of distinguished Witt vectors (equivalently f = Σ V^n[a_n] with a_0 nilpotent and a_1 a unit). For an invertible ideal I ⊂ W(R), the inclusion (I, ι) is a Cartier–Witt divisor if and only if (W(R), I) is a prism and the images of p and I in R are nilpotent.

p is nilpotent in R; by convention there is no Cartier–Witt divisor otherwise. The δ-structure on W(R) is the canonical one (natural in R, with Frobenius F); when W(R) has p-torsion it is not determined by F alone. Condition (a) is stated for the ideal image; since I is finitely generated it is equivalent to the nilpotence of each element α(y)_0.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Definition 3.1.4 and Remark 3.1.5; p. 39; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 3.2.1 and Remark 3.2.2; p. 40.)

- `Prismatic.WCart.IsCartierWitt`: The predicate on a generalized Cartier divisor (I, α) of W(R): p is nilpotent in R, every α(y)_0 is nilpotent, and the α(y)_1 generate the unit ideal of R.
- `Prismatic.WCart.CartierWittDivisor`: A generalized Cartier divisor of W(R) satisfying IsCartierWitt: an object of WCart(R).
- `Prismatic.WCart.IsDistinguishedWitt`: f ∈ WCart_0(R): f_0 is nilpotent and f_1 is a unit.
- `Prismatic.WCart.CartierWittDivisor.ofWitt`: The principalized Cartier–Witt divisor (W(R), f·) of a distinguished Witt vector f over a ring in which p is nilpotent.
- `Prismatic.WCart.isCartierWitt_ofElement_iff`: (W(R), f·) is a Cartier–Witt divisor if and only if p is nilpotent in R and f ∈ WCart_0(R).
- `Prismatic.WCart.coeff_zero_delta`: For the canonical δ-structure on W(R): δ(x)_0 = x_1; this turns condition (b) of the source into the coordinate condition of IsCartierWitt.
- `Prismatic.WCart.CartierWittDivisor.zariski_principal`: Every Cartier–Witt divisor on a p-nilpotent R is generated by a distinguished Witt vector after a Zariski cover of Spec R. First principalize its reduction to R; lift a generator through W(R)→R, using the kernel in the Jacobson radical and finite-projective Nakayama (the kernels of the finite Witt truncations are nilpotent; the infinite Witt kernel need not be). The condition that δ generates the unit ideal makes that generator distinguished.

**Proof route.** The universal torsion-free Witt calculation gives δ(x)₀=x₁, hence the coordinate conditions by naturality; the Witt restriction kernel is Jacobson when p is nilpotent. Reduce the invertible Witt module to R, trivialize it Zariski-locally and lift its generator: finite-projective Nakayama gives a split surjection whose finitely generated kernel vanishes, proving principalization without completeness for powers of the infinite Witt kernel. The Teichmüller expansion gives WCart₀, and the local distinguished-generator criterion identifies divisors coming from prisms (BL §§3.1–3.2).

- `pr5_cw_verschiebung_one`: V(1) ∈ W(R) lies in WCart_0(R): its coordinates are (0, 1, 0, …).

V(1) ∈ W(R) is a distinguished Witt vector for every R; it defines the point η of the Hodge–Tate divisor. A Teichmüller element [a] is never distinguished over a nonzero ring (its coordinate x_1 is 0), and a unit of W(R) is never distinguished when R is nonzero.

<a id="layer-4-cartier-witt-stack"></a>

### 4.4 The Cartier–Witt stack WCart

A ring map f : R → S induces W(f) : W(R) → W(S), and pullback along W(f) carries Cartier–Witt divisors of R to Cartier–Witt divisors of S, giving a functor f^* : WCart(R) → WCart(S), (I, α) ↦ (W(S) ⊗_{W(R)} I, W(S) ⊗ α), with coherent isomorphisms (g f)^* ≅ g^* f^*. The Cartier–Witt stack WCart is the resulting functor from commutative rings to groupoids (empty on rings in which p is not nilpotent, so WCart lives over Spf Z_p). It satisfies descent for the fpqc topology: for a faithfully flat map R → S, WCart(R) is equivalent to the groupoid of descent data in WCart(S) relative to S ⊗_R S and S ⊗_R S ⊗_R S. Restriction along W(R) → R gives a morphism of stacks μ : WCart → Cart = [A^1/G_m], (I, α) ↦ (R ⊗_{W(R)} I, R ⊗ α), which factors through [Â^1/G_m] (the formal completion of A^1 at 0): the image of μ(I, α) is a nil ideal, so μ(I, α) is never a Cartier divisor unless R = 0. WCart is not a formal scheme: its points have nontrivial automorphisms.

Rings are ordinary commutative rings; WCart(R) is empty unless p is nilpotent in R. Corrected direction: the functor induced by f : R → S goes from WCart(R) to WCart(S); Bhatt–Lurie Remark 3.1.7 prints the opposite direction, and Warning 3.1.8 uses the correct one. The fpqc descent is asserted in the source without proof; W(R) → W(S) is in general not flat for a flat map R → S, so the proof below does not use flat descent along it.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Remarks 3.1.6–3.1.7; pp.39–40; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remarks 3.1.6–3.1.7; pp.39–40.)

- `Prismatic.WCart.CartierWittDivisor.groupoid`: WCart(R) is a groupoid: morphisms are the isomorphisms of the underlying generalized Cartier divisors.
- `Prismatic.WCart.pullback`: For f : R → S the functor f^* : WCart(R) → WCart(S) of base change along W(f).
- `Prismatic.WCart.pullbackComp`: The coherence isomorphism g^* ∘ f^* ≅ (g ∘ f)^*.
- `Prismatic.WCart.toCart`: μ : WCart(R) → Cart(R), base change along the restriction W(R) → R.
- `Prismatic.WCart.toCart_not_isCartier`: For a nonzero ring R, μ(I, α) is never a Cartier divisor.
- `Prismatic.WCart.pullback_faithful`: For a faithfully flat map f the functor f^* is faithful: the separatedness half of fpqc descent.

**Proof route.** Witt functoriality preserves the coordinate conditions, and after local principalization the isomorphism sheaves are given by units u with g=uf, hence are fpqc sheaves. Descend objects successively over W_n: the unit-lifting kernels have finite filtrations with quasi-coherent graded pieces, whose Čech H¹ and H² vanish by Amitsur exactness; the compatible invertible-module tower is effective, and its map descends too. BL Remark 3.1.6 gives μ and its formal-line factorization.

**Checks.**

- `pr5_wcart_hom_principal`: Morphisms (W(R), f·) → (W(R), g·) in WCart(R) correspond to the units u of W(R) with g = u f.
- `pr5_wcart_zero_ring`: Over the zero ring any two Cartier–Witt divisors are uniquely isomorphic.
- `pr5_wcart_pullback_principal`: f^*(W(R), x·) ≅ (W(S), W(f)(x)·) for a distinguished Witt vector x.

<a id="layer-4-wcart-quotient-presentation"></a>

### 4.5 Presentation of WCart as the quotient [WCart_0 / W^×]

Let WCart_0 be the functor R ↦ WCart_0(R) of distinguished Witt vectors; it is represented by the affine formal scheme Spf(A^0), A^0 the (p, a_0)-adic completion of Z[a_0, a_1^{±1}, a_2, a_3, …]. Let W^× be the affine group scheme R ↦ W(R)^×; it acts on WCart_0 by multiplication. The morphism WCart_0 → WCart, f ↦ (W(R), f·), exhibits WCart as the quotient stack [WCart_0 / W^×], the quotient being formed in the 2-category of stacks for the Zariski topology on Spec R. Explicitly: (i) every Cartier–Witt divisor of R is, Zariski-locally on Spec R, isomorphic to a principalized one; (ii) for f, g ∈ WCart_0(R) the isomorphisms (W(R), f·) → (W(R), g·) are the units u ∈ W(R)^× with g = u f, so WCart_0 ×_{WCart} WCart_0 ≅ WCart_0 × W^×. Since WCart is an fpqc stack, the same morphism exhibits it as the fpqc quotient, and Spf(A^0) → WCart is a surjection for the Zariski topology whose (n+1)-fold fibre power is Spf(A^0) × (W^×)^n.

The quotient is formed for the Zariski topology, as in the source; its agreement with the fpqc quotient uses the fpqc descent of the previous construction. W^× is a flat affine group scheme over Z that is not of finite type; WCart_0 is a formal scheme, a functor on rings in which p is nilpotent. Carriers imported: groupoid quotient stacks and their universal property from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0, the QCoh/Perf interface from [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh), and effective descent from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1; exact extensions beyond those suppliers are given in the supplier contracts.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 3.2.3 with its proof, and Construction 3.2.1; pp. 40, 41.)

*Needs:* [§4.4](#layer-4-cartier-witt-stack), [§4.3](#layer-4-cartier-witt-divisor), [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

**Proof route.** The description of morphisms between principal divisors makes the quotient map fully faithful. Principalization from [§4.3](#layer-4-cartier-witt-divisor) makes it Zariski-locally essentially surjective, using Jacobson Nakayama rather than completeness along the Witt kernel. The coordinates f₀ nilpotent and f₁ invertible represent WCart₀ by the indicated formal affine chart (BL Proposition 3.2.3).

**Checks.**

- Over a local ring R in which p is nilpotent every Cartier–Witt divisor is principalized, and WCart(R) is the action groupoid of W(R)^× on WCart_0(R). The fibre product WCart_0 ×_{WCart} WCart_0 is the formal scheme WCart_0 × W^×, with the two projections f and u f. For principalized generalized divisors f and g, the isomorphism set is the set of Witt units u satisfying g = u f. It can contain several units: at the Hodge–Tate point over dual numbers, 1 + [ε] is a nonidentity stabilizer. Uniqueness follows when f is a nonzerodivisor, and is not assumed for Cartier–Witt divisors.

<a id="layer-4-transversal-prism-coproducts"></a>

### 4.6 Transversal prisms and coproducts of prisms

For the prism charts used in Cartier–Witt geometry, import the transversal approximations, coproducts and residue-field lifts of [§3.7](#layer-3-transversal-approximation). Their maps to Cartier–Witt divisors are compatible with the canonical cocones and with change of base. The coproduct of two chart points corresponds to the common refinement of their prism charts; this target supplies chart compatibility, rather than a second construction of transversal coproducts.

Prisms are those of PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2 (δ-ring, invertible ideal, derived (p, I)-complete, p ∈ I + φ(I)A). The coproduct construction used here requires (A, I) transversal and (B, J) bounded; existence of coproducts without these hypotheses requires animated prisms and is not claimed. Flat and faithfully flat maps of prisms are defined by p-complete (faithful) flatness of A/I → B/J (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1).

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Definition 2.1.3 with Remark 2.1.4; p. 19; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Propositions 2.4.1, 2.4.5 and 2.4.9, Corollaries 2.4.7, 2.4.8 and 2.4.10; pp. 25, 27.)

*Needs:* [§3.7](#layer-3-transversal-approximation), [§3.6](#layer-3-transversal-prism), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.8](#layer-0-free-delta-ring), [§0.20](#layer-0-crystalline-prism), [§0.23](#layer-0-q-de-rham-prism), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, [§0.9](#layer-0-delta-ring-category).

**Proof route.** Apply [§3.7](#layer-3-transversal-approximation)’s transversal coproduct construction. Its functorial Cartier–Witt divisors give the cocone equalities on Witt modules. The cofree Witt universal property supplies residue-field lifts with the required reduction.

**Checks.**

- The identity chart maps to the identity Cartier–Witt point. Two transversal charts mapping to one prism give isomorphic Cartier–Witt points on their Layer 3-owned common refinement.

<a id="layer-4-prism-point-of-wcart"></a>

### 4.7 The point ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart of a prism

Let (A, I) be a prism and f : A → R a ring map. f lifts uniquely to a δ-map f̃ : A → W(R). Put f̃^*(I) = W(R) ⊗_A I and let α : f̃^*(I) → W(R) be induced by the inclusion I ⊂ A. The pair (f̃^*(I), α) is a generalized Cartier divisor of W(R), and it is a Cartier–Witt divisor of R exactly when the image of I + (p) in R consists of nilpotent elements. This defines a morphism of stacks ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart, where Spf(A) is the formal scheme of the (p, I)-adic topology, functorial in the prism: for a map of prisms h : (A, I) → (B, J) there is a canonical isomorphism ρ_B ≅ ρ_A ∘ Spf(h). Composing with μ gives the Cartier divisor I ⊂ A pulled back along f. Special cases: (i) the de Rham point ρ_dR = ρ_{Z_p} : Spf(Z_p) → WCart of the crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)), which is R ↦ (W(R), p·); more generally ρ_A(f) ≅ (W(R), p·) for a crystalline prism; (ii) the universal oriented prism (A^0, I^0): A^0 = Z[a_0, a_1^{±1}, a_2, …]^∧_{(p, a_0)} with the δ-structure induced by the Witt vector Frobenius on WCart_0 = Spf(A^0) and I^0 = (a_0); it is a transversal prism, maps of prisms (A^0, I^0) → (B, J) correspond bijectively to generators of J via h ↦ h(a_0), and ρ_{A^0} is the atlas WCart_0 → WCart.

(A, I) is any prism; boundedness is needed only where D(Spf A) is identified with complete complexes. The δ-lift f̃ exists because W is right adjoint to the forgetful functor from δ-rings ([§0.9](#layer-0-delta-ring-category)). The condition for a Cartier–Witt divisor is that f is continuous for the (p, I)-adic topology on A and the discrete topology on R.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 3.2.4, Examples 3.2.5 and 3.2.6, Remark 3.2.7; p. 41.)

*Needs:* [§4.4](#layer-4-cartier-witt-stack), [§4.3](#layer-4-cartier-witt-divisor), [Presentation of WCart as the quotient [WCart_0 / W^×]](#layer-4-wcart-quotient-presentation), [§4.6](#layer-4-transversal-prism-coproducts), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.9](#layer-0-delta-ring-category), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.20](#layer-0-crystalline-prism), [§0.13](#layer-0-distinguished-element), [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh), [§0.24](#layer-0-universal-oriented-prism), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.WCart.prismPoint`: For a prism (A, I) and f : A → R with f(I + (p)) nilpotent, the Cartier–Witt divisor ρ_A(f) = (W(R) ⊗_A I → W(R)).
- `Prismatic.WCart.prismPoint_comp`: g^* ρ_A(f) ≅ ρ_A(g ∘ f) for a ring map g : R → S.
- `Prismatic.WCart.prismPoint_map`: ρ_A(f ∘ h) ≅ ρ_B(f) for a map of prisms h : (A, I) → (B, J) and f : B → R.
- `Prismatic.WCart.exists_universalOrientedPrism`: There is a prism (A^0, (a_0)) such that maps of prisms (A^0, (a_0)) → (B, J) correspond bijectively to generators d of J by h ↦ h(a_0).

**Proof route.** The cofree Witt lift of a map A→R has zeroth coordinate the given map, and the prism relation makes its delta-image ideal the unit ideal once p and I become nilpotent. Rigidity identifies the pulled-back ideals under prism maps, giving functoriality. On the universal chart the torsion-free Witt Frobenius has δ(a₀)=a₁ invertible, so a₀ is distinguished and the chart has the claimed universal orientation property (BL Construction 3.2.4 and Remark 3.2.7).

**Checks.**

- `pr5_point_crystalline_is_p`: For a crystalline prism the point ρ_A(f) is isomorphic to the principalized divisor (W(R), p·).
- `pr5_point_orientable_principal`: If I is principal then ρ_A(f) is isomorphic to a principalized divisor.
- `pr5_point_to_cart`: μ(ρ_A(f)) is isomorphic in Cart(R) to the pullback along f of the Cartier divisor (I ⊂ A).

- The crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)) and R = Z/p^n the point is (W(Z/p^n), p·). For an oriented prism (A, (d)) the point ρ_A(f) is the principalized divisor (W(R), f̃(d)·). μ(ρ_A(f)) is the generalized Cartier divisor (R ⊗_A I → R) of Spec R.

### 4.8 Fibre products of prisms over WCart and flatness of ρ_A

(1) Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and (B, J) a transversal prism, with coproduct (C, K) in the category of prisms. Then the square formed by Spf(C) → Spf(A), Spf(C) → Spf(B), ρ_A and ρ_B is a pullback square of stacks: Spf(A) ×_{WCart} Spf(B) ≅ Spf(C). (2) For every prism (B, J) the morphism ρ_B : Spf(B) → WCart is affine: for every ring R and every Cartier–Witt divisor of R, Spf(B) ×_{WCart} Spec(R) is an affine R-scheme. (3) A bounded prism (B, J) is transversal if and only if ρ_B is flat; if (B, J) is transversal and B ≠ 0 then ρ_B is faithfully flat. In particular for the universal oriented prism the (n+1)-fold fibre power of Spf(A^0) over WCart is Spf(A^n), where (A^n, I^n) is the coproduct of n+1 copies of (A^0, I^0); (A^•, I^•) is a cosimplicial transversal prism, the Čech nerve of the atlas.

(1): (A, I) bounded and (B, J) transversal; the roles are not symmetric in the source and the coproduct exists by Transversal prisms and coproducts of prisms. (3): (B, J) bounded. Corrected misprints of the proof: the fibre product computed there is Spf(A^0) ×_{WCart} Spf(B) ≅ Spf(B) × W^×, and the bijection is with the invertible elements of the test prism.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 3.2.8 and Corollary 3.2.9; pp. 41, 42; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollary 3.2.10; p. 42; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Notation 3.3.9; p. 44.)

**Proof route.** Locally orient both ideals and factor through the universal oriented prism; the quotient presentation identifies its fibre product with the completed free delta algebra on a unit, whose universal property is exactly the coproduct. For arbitrary chart points first pass to a transversal prism and principalize the divisor. Flatness and faithful flatness then follow from transversal coproducts and descend along the atlas (BL Proposition 3.2.8 and Corollaries 3.2.9–3.2.10).

**Checks.**

- Spf(Z_p) ×_{WCart} Spf(A) = Spf(A{p/I}^∧) for a transversal prism (A, I): the universal crystalline prism over (A, I). ρ_dR : Spf(Z_p) → WCart is affine and not flat (the crystalline prism is not transversal); the atlas ρ_{A^0} and the q-de Rham point are faithfully flat.

<a id="layer-4-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart"></a>

### 4.9 Quasi-coherent and perfect complexes on WCart

For a commutative ring R let D(R) be the derived ∞-category of R-modules, a symmetric monoidal stable ∞-category, functorial in R by derived base change. D(WCart) is the limit of the categories D(R) over the category of points of WCart, whose objects are pairs (R, (I, α)) with (I, α) a Cartier–Witt divisor of R and whose morphisms are ring maps with an isomorphism of pulled-back divisors. Its objects are the quasi-coherent complexes on WCart: such an E assigns to every Cartier–Witt divisor (I, α) of R a complex E_α ∈ D(R), compatibly with base change. Perf(WCart) ⊂ D(WCart) is the full subcategory of the E with every E_α perfect; these are the dualizable objects. The structure sheaf O_WCart is the unit object, (R, α) ↦ R. The Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf I ∈ D(WCart) is (R, (I, α)) ↦ R ⊗_{W(R)} I, an invertible object with a morphism I → O_WCart induced by α; I^m denotes its m-th tensor power for m ∈ Z. Subject to [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh)’s pointwise effectivity target outside regular charts, for a bounded prism (A, I) pullback along ρ_A is a symmetric monoidal exact functor ρ_A^* : D(WCart) → D(Spf A) ≃ D̂(A), where D̂(A) ⊂ D(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete complexes; ρ_A^* O_WCart = A and ρ_A^* I = I. Presentability gives a right adjoint ρ_{A*} : D̂(A) → D(WCart). For a transversal prism, ρ_A is flat affine, so this adjoint is the affine restriction-of-scalars construction of [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh) and obeys ordinary base change and the projection formula there. For an arbitrary bounded prism, [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh) supplies base change along a flat morphism and the projection formula for dualizable coefficients; further ordinary base-change assertions require Tor-independence. The functor D(Z) → D(WCart), M ↦ M ⊗ O_WCart, has a right adjoint RΓ(WCart, −) : D(WCart) → D(Z), the global sections functor; it takes values in D̂(Z_p).

The limit is a limit of ∞-categories; it is not the limit of the triangulated homotopy categories. For bounded (A,I), the pointwise identification D(Spf A) ≃ D̂(A) is established here on regular-ideal charts by [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh); its use outside that range is conditional on the nonregular effectivity obligation there. WCart is a stack over Spf Z_p, so every R in the index category has p nilpotent.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Definition 3.3.1, Examples 3.3.3 and 3.3.4; p. 43; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollary 3.3.11; p. 44.)

*Needs:* [§4.4](#layer-4-cartier-witt-stack), [§4.7](#layer-4-prism-point-of-wcart), [§4.8](#layer-4-wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms), [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/stable-infinity-category`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0/limits-colimits-and-slices`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

- `Prismatic.WCart.carriers`: The carriers constructed by this target and its successors on the Cartier–Witt stack.

Presentability and colimit preservation give the indicated right adjoints; on transversal charts the flat affine formula supplies base change and projection formula, excluding the nonflat de-Rham point. Global sections are p-complete because p is nilpotent at every point (BL Corollary 3.3.11).

<a id="layer-4-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart"></a>

### 4.10 Quasi-coherent complexes on WCart are prismatic crystals

The pullback functors ρ_A^* induce an equivalence of symmetric monoidal stable ∞-categories D(WCart) → lim_{(A, I)} D̂(A), the limit being indexed by the category of all bounded prisms with transition functors M ↦ B ⊗̂^L_A M (derived (p, J)-completed base change). The limit is unchanged if the index category is enlarged to all prisms or restricted to transversal prisms. Equivalently, with (A^•, I^•) the cosimplicial prism of coproducts of the universal oriented prism, pullback along ρ_{A^•} gives an equivalence D(WCart) ≃ Tot D̂(A^•). Passing to dualizable objects, Perf(WCart) ≃ lim_{(A, I)} Perf(A). Hence D(WCart) is the ∞-category of crystals of (p, I_Δ)-complete complexes on the absolute prismatic site ((Spf Z_p)_Δ, O_Δ), and Perf(WCart) is the category of perfect complexes on it. Consequences: (1) the Breuil–Kisin twists (A, I) ↦ A{n} define invertible objects O_WCart{n} ∈ D(WCart) with ρ_A^* O_WCart{n} = A{n}, and E{n} denotes E ⊗ O_WCart{n}; (2) under D(WCart) ≃ Tot D̂(A^•) the global sections functor is M^• ↦ Tot(M^•) ∈ D̂(Z_p).

The index category is that of bounded prisms. Its complete-module limit has the stated transversal Čech description. Interpreting each D̂(A) as pointwise D(Spf A) for a nonregular prism requires the effectivity target of [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh); boundedness alone is not a proof of that target here (Bhatt–Lurie, Warning 3.3.6). D̂(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects of D(A) (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1). The equivalence is one of ∞-categories; in particular the pullback functors ρ_A^* are jointly conservative.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 3.3.5 with its proof, Warning 3.3.6 and Remark 3.3.7; pp. 43, 44; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Lemma 3.3.10 and Example 3.3.8; p. 44; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Proposition 2.7; p. 6.)

*Needs:* [§4.9](#layer-4-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart), [Presentation of WCart as the quotient [WCart_0 / W^×]](#layer-4-wcart-quotient-presentation), [§4.8](#layer-4-wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms), [§4.6](#layer-4-transversal-prism-coproducts), [§4.7](#layer-4-prism-point-of-wcart), [§4.1](#layer-4-absolute-prismatic-site), [§0.14](#layer-0-local-distinguished-prism-generators), [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2/hypercovers-and-cohomological-descent`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0/limits-colimits-and-slices`, [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

**Proof route.** The universal chart and its transversal Čech nerve compute D(WCart) by descent; complete-flat descent reduces the prism limit to principal ideals without requiring maps to preserve a chosen generator. For each oriented prism C, the simplex category of nonempty tuples of its generators is contractible, giving the required coinitiality, while transversal approximation gives the stated restricted-index variant (BL Proposition 3.3.5 and Warning 3.3.6). Dualizability in the monoidal limit identifies perfect objects, and the functorial Breuil–Kisin lines give the twists.

**Checks.**

- A morphism of D(WCart) is an isomorphism as soon as its pullback to every bounded prism is; it suffices to test on one nonzero transversal prism, for example the q-de Rham prism. The rule (A, I) ↦ Δ_{(A/I ⊗^L R)/A} with its base-change isomorphisms defines an object of D(WCart): the prismatic cohomology sheaf. The rule (A, I) ↦ A/I is ι_* O_{WCart^HT}, and (A, I) ↦ I is the Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf.

<a id="layer-4-divided-power-multiplicative-group"></a>

### 4.11 The group scheme G_m^♯ and the Frobenius kernel of W^×

Let O(G_m) = Z[t^{±1}]. O(G_m^♯) is the subring of Q[t^{±1}] generated by t^{−1} and the divided powers (t−1)^n/n!, n ≥ 0; it is the divided power envelope of the ideal (t−1) ⊂ Z[t^{±1}]. G_m^♯ = Spec O(G_m^♯), with β : G_m^♯ → G_m induced by the inclusion; β is an isomorphism over Q and there is a unique group structure on G_m^♯ making β a homomorphism (the comultiplication t ↦ t ⊗ t preserves O(G_m^♯)). For a torsion-free ring R, β(R) is injective with image the units u such that n! divides (u−1)^n for all n; in particular G_m^♯(Z_p) = 1 + pZ_p. Let W^×[F] be the kernel of the Witt vector Frobenius F : W^× → W^×, an affine group scheme over Z. Then: (1) F : W → W and F : W^× → W^× are faithfully flat, so W^×[F] is flat over Z; (2) the map W^×[F] → G_m, u ↦ u_0, lifts uniquely to an isomorphism of group schemes W^×[F] × Spec Z_(p) ≅ G_m^♯ × Spec Z_(p). Variant: with G_a^♯ = Spec Z[x^n/n! : n ≥ 1] and W[F] = ker(F : W → W), the map W[F] → G_a lifts uniquely to an isomorphism W[F] × Spec Z_(p) ≅ G_a^♯ × Spec Z_(p).

The isomorphism (2) holds after localisation at p, not over Z: W^×[F] becomes G_m over Z[1/p], while G_m^♯ becomes G_m only over Q, having divided powers at every prime ℓ. G_m^♯(R) → R^× is neither injective nor surjective for general R; G_m^♯(F_p) is trivial.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Notation 3.4.9 and Remark 3.4.10; p. 46; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 3.4.7, Corollary 3.4.8 and Lemma 3.4.11; pp. 46, 47.)

- `Prismatic.WCart.GmSharp.group`: The group structure on G_m^♯(R) for which β is a homomorphism.
- `Prismatic.WCart.GmSharp.toUnits`: β(R) : G_m^♯(R) → R^×, the image of t.
- `Prismatic.WCart.GmSharp.toUnits_injective`: For a torsion-free ring R the map β(R) is injective.
- `Prismatic.WCart.gmSharpEquivFrobeniusKernel`: For a ring R in which every integer prime to p is invertible: G_m^♯(R) ≅ {u ∈ W(R)^× : F(u) = 1}, compatibly with u ↦ u_0.

**Proof route.** The PD comultiplication gives G_m^♯, and ghost coordinates after inverting p together with coordinate Frobenius modulo p prove faithful flatness of F on W. On the p-local Frobenius-kernel ring, φ(t)=1 gives divided powers of t−1 and hence the map from the PD algebra. It is an isomorphism rationally and modulo p, where the truncated monomials in successive divided powers match those in successive deltas; flatness gives the integral group comparison and its additive variant (BL Lemma 3.4.11).

**Checks.**

- `pr5_gmsharp_padic_points`: The image of G_m^♯(Z_p) → Z_p^× is 1 + pZ_p.
- `pr5_gmsharp_rational`: For a Q-algebra R the map G_m^♯(R) → R^× is bijective.

<a id="layer-4-hodge-tate-divisor"></a>

### 4.12 The Hodge–Tate divisor WCart^HT and its identification with BG_m^♯

WCart^HT(R) is the full subgroupoid of WCart(R) of the Cartier–Witt divisors (I, α) for which I → W(R) → R is zero, that is, α factors through V W(R). R ↦ WCart^HT(R) is a closed substack of WCart, the Hodge–Tate divisor; it is the fibre of μ : WCart → [Â^1/G_m] over BG_m = [0/G_m], which gives μ^HT : WCart^HT → BG_m, and it is the effective Cartier divisor cut out by I → O_WCart. For a prism (A, I) the morphism ρ_A carries Spf(A/I) into WCart^HT, giving ρ_A^HT : Spf(A/I) → WCart^HT, and Spf(A/I) = Spf(A) ×_{WCart} WCart^HT. The point η : Spf(Z_p) → WCart^HT is R ↦ (W(R), V(1)·). Its automorphism group is Aut(η)(R) = {u ∈ W(R)^× : u V(1) = V(1)} = W^×[F](R), because u V(1) = V(F(u)) and V is injective. Theorem: η is faithfully flat and extends to an isomorphism of stacks Spf(Z_p) × BG_m^♯ ≅ WCart^HT, where BG_m^♯ is the classifying stack of G_m^♯ for the fpqc topology; under it μ^HT is induced by β : G_m^♯ → G_m. Consequence: for every ring R and Cartier–Witt divisor (I, α) of R, the group Aut(I, α) is commutative and annihilated by a power of p.

R ranges over rings with p nilpotent; η is a point over Spf Z_p. The classifying stack is formed for the fpqc topology; the isomorphism uses that WCart^HT is an fpqc stack (The Cartier–Witt stack WCart). η is not an isomorphism onto WCart^HT and the Hodge–Tate divisor is not a formal scheme.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.2 and Construction 3.4.4; p. 45; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 3.4.13 with its proof, Remark 3.4.14 and Corollary 3.4.16; p. 48.)

- `Prismatic.WCart.etaPoint_isHodgeTate`: η(R) lies in WCart^HT(R).

- `Prismatic.WCart.autEtaEquiv`: Aut(η(R)) ≅ G_m^♯(R) as groups.

After principalization the divisor is V(u) with u a unit, and faithful flatness of F on W^× makes it locally V(1), giving BG_m^♯. Filter automorphisms by the nilpotent ideal (p,image I); its kernels are modules and its residual group is Frobenius-killed, giving the asserted p-power bound (BL Theorem 3.4.13 and Corollary 3.4.16).

<a id="layer-4-sen-operator"></a>

### 4.13 Complexes on the Hodge–Tate divisor and the Sen operator

D(WCart^HT) is the limit of D(R) over the points Spec R → WCart^HT; equivalently D(WCart^HT) ≃ lim_{(A, I)} D̂(A/I) over bounded prisms (D̂(A/I) the p-complete derived category), or the totalization of D̂(A^•/I^•). ι^* : D(WCart) → D(WCart^HT) is restriction and ι_* its right adjoint; O_{WCart^HT}{n} = ι^* O_WCart{n} ≅ ι^* I^n. For E ∈ D(WCart^HT) the fibre at η is E_η = η^* E ∈ D̂(Z_p). Sen operator: let R be an algebra over the dual numbers Z[ε]/(ε²). The Teichmüller element [ε] ∈ W(R) satisfies F([ε]) = [ε^p] = 0, so (1 + [ε]) V(y) = V(y) for all y, and multiplication by 1 + [ε] is an automorphism of every Cartier–Witt divisor (I, α) of R lying in WCart^HT. This is functorial and defines an automorphism γ of the projection π : WCart^HT × Spec Z[ε]/(ε²) → WCart^HT. For E ∈ D(WCart^HT), γ acts on π^* E by a map E → Z[ε]/(ε²) ⊗ E which is the identity modulo ε, hence of the form id + ε Θ_E. The endomorphism Θ_E : E → E, natural in E, is the Sen operator; it induces Θ_E on E_η. Properties: (Leibniz) Θ_{E ⊗ E′} = Θ_E ⊗ id + id ⊗ Θ_{E′}; Θ = 0 on O_{WCart^HT}; Θ is the identity on ι^* I; Θ is multiplication by n on O_{WCart^HT}{n}; on η_* O_{Spf Z_p}, whose fibre at η is the p-completed coordinate ring of G_m^♯, Θ is the differential operator t ∂/∂t.

p ≥ 2 is used in ε^p = 0. Θ_E is an endomorphism in the ∞-category D(WCart^HT), natural in E; on the fibre it makes E_η an object of D(Z[Θ]). The sign convention is that of the source: Θ = +n on O{n}; on gr_n of the conjugate filtration of Hodge–Tate cohomology Θ = −n.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 3.5.4, Remark 3.5.5, Example 3.5.6 and Notation 3.5.7; pp. 49, 50; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Definition 3.5.1 and Remark 3.5.3; p. 49.)

*Needs:* [§4.12](#layer-4-hodge-tate-divisor), [§4.9](#layer-4-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart), [§4.10](#layer-4-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart), [§4.11](#layer-4-divided-power-multiplicative-group), [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist), Mathlib `WittVector.teichmuller`, Mathlib `WittVector.verschiebung_mul_frobenius`, [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.WCart.senOperator`: The natural transformation Θ : η^* → η^* on D(WCart^HT), with values in endomorphisms of E_η ∈ D(Z_p).
- `Prismatic.WCart.senOperator_unit`: Θ = 0 on the unit object of D(WCart^HT).
- `Prismatic.WCart.senOperator_twist`: Θ is multiplication by n on the fibre of O_{WCart^HT}{n}.
- `Prismatic.WCart.fibreEta_twist`: The fibre at η of O_{WCart^HT}{n} is Z_p in degree 0.
- `Prismatic.WCart.one_add_teichmuller_eps_mul_verschiebung`: (1 + [ε]) V(y) = V(y) in W(R[ε]/(ε²)): the identity that makes 1 + [ε] an automorphism of every Hodge–Tate point.

**Proof route.** Apply the crystal descent argument modulo the ideal to obtain the categories and functors. The identities for Verschiebung and Teichmüller Frobenius construct γ, whose diagonal tensor action gives the Leibniz rule and zero action on the unit. Restriction sends 1+[ε] to 1+ε, so Θ=1 on I and Θ=n on its twists, while the regular representation gives f((1+ε)t)=f(t)+εΘ(f) (BL §3.5).

- `pr5_sen_ideal_identity`: The Sen operator of the restricted Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf is the identity of its fibre.
- `pr5_sen_ideal_ne_zero`: The Sen operator of the restricted Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf is not zero; hence that sheaf is not isomorphic to the structure sheaf.
- `pr5_sen_teichmuller_frobenius`: F([ε]) = 0 in W of the dual numbers over any ring.

- Θ = 0 on the unit object, Θ = 1 on the restriction of the Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf, Θ = n on O{n}. For a quasi-coherent complex F on WCart, the Sen operator of ι^* F^* F on its fibre at η is canonically trivial (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.6.8). For the p-complete diffracted Hodge complex η^* of the Hodge–Tate cohomology sheaf of R, Θ acts by −n on the n-th graded piece of the conjugate filtration.

<a id="layer-4-sen-operator-classification"></a>

### 4.14 Classification of complexes on WCart^HT by the Sen operator

The functor D(WCart^HT) → D(Z[Θ]), E ↦ (E_η, Θ_E), is fully faithful, and its essential image consists of the objects M ∈ D(Z[Θ]) such that (a) M is p-complete and (b) the action of Θ^p − Θ on the cohomology H^*(F_p ⊗^L M) is locally nilpotent. Moreover: (1) the unit map O_{WCart^HT} → (η_* O_{Spf Z_p})^{Θ=0} is an isomorphism; (2) for every E ∈ D(WCart^HT) there is a canonical fibre sequence RΓ(WCart^HT, E) → E_η → E_η with second map Θ_E; (3) H^n(WCart^HT, O) is Z_p for n = 0, 1 and zero otherwise, and RΓ(WCart^HT, O{n}) ≅ (Z_p/n)[−1] for n ≠ 0; (4) RΓ(WCart^HT, −) : D(WCart^HT) → D̂(Z_p) commutes with colimits; (5) E ≅ O_{WCart^HT}{n} if and only if E_η ≅ Z_p and Θ_E is multiplication by n; (6) D(WCart^HT) is generated under shifts and colimits by the twists O_{WCart^HT}{n}, n ≥ 0, and D(WCart) is generated under shifts and colimits by the invertible sheaves I^n, n ∈ Z.

D(Z[Θ]) is the derived category of modules over the polynomial ring Z[Θ]; no completeness is imposed on the target beyond (a) and (b). Colimits in D(WCart^HT) and D̂(Z_p) are p-completed colimits. The statement holds for every prime p, including p = 2.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 3.5.8 with its proof; p. 50; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Propositions 3.5.10, 3.5.11 and 3.5.15, Example 3.5.12, Corollaries 3.5.13, 3.5.14 and 3.5.16; pp. 51, 52, 53.)

*Needs:* [§4.13](#layer-4-sen-operator), [§4.12](#layer-4-hodge-tate-divisor), [§4.11](#layer-4-divided-power-multiplicative-group), [§4.9](#layer-4-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart), [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

**Proof route.** After faithfully flat pullback the basic exact sequence is the divided-series operator (c_n)↦(c_(n+1)+nc_n), surjective with constant kernel; tensor and projection formula give the fibre and global-section formulas. Filter the regular representation by its finite divided-degree subcomodules, with graded character n, to prove generation and reduce full faithfulness to the weight-zero fibre calculation; the I-adic fibre sequences give generation on WCart. The essential-image condition holds on every generator, and conversely the factorization Θ^p−Θ=∏_(0≤n<p)(Θ−n) modulo p detects a nonzero map from an integer-weight generator to every nonzero object satisfying the stated conditions (BL Theorem 3.5.8).

**Checks.**

- The pair (Z_p, Θ = n) corresponds to O_{WCart^HT}{n}; the pair (Z_p, Θ = 1/2) for odd p satisfies (b) (Θ^p − Θ acts by 2^{−p} − 2^{−1} ≡ 0 mod p) and gives an invertible sheaf that is not a twist. The pair (Z_p[Θ]^∧_p, Θ) does not satisfy (b) and is not in the image. H^1(WCart^HT, O) = Z_p is generated by the class of the logarithm G_m^♯ → G_a.

<a id="layer-4-wcart-frobenius"></a>

### 4.15 The Frobenius endomorphism of WCart

For a ring R, pullback along F:W(R)→W(R) sends generalized Cartier divisors to generalized Cartier divisors and preserves the Cartier–Witt conditions; these functors are natural in R and define the Frobenius morphism F : WCart → WCart. On principalized divisors it is (W(R), f·) ↦ (W(R), F(f)·); on the atlas Spf(A^0) and on its Čech nerve Spf(A^•) it is induced by the Frobenius lifts φ_{A^n}. For an F_p-algebra R, F on WCart(R) is WCart(φ_R): F lifts the absolute Frobenius of WCart × Spec F_p. For a prism (A, I) there is a canonical isomorphism ρ_A ∘ Spf(φ_A) ≅ F ∘ ρ_A. Pullback gives a symmetric monoidal functor F^* : D(WCart) → D(WCart) with F^* O_WCart{n} ≅ I^{−n} ⊗ O_WCart{n}, and a natural map RΓ(WCart, E) → RΓ(WCart, F^* E). F does not preserve the Hodge–Tate divisor: the square with sides WCart^HT ⊂ WCart, F, WCart^HT → Spf(Z_p) and ρ_dR commutes up to a unique isomorphism, so F contracts WCart^HT to the de Rham point; concretely F^*(I, α) ≅ (W(R), p·) for (I, α) ∈ WCart^HT(R). The closed substack F^{−1}WCart^HT meets WCart^HT in WCart^HT × Spec F_p.

F is an endomorphism of the stack over Spf Z_p; it is not an isomorphism and F^* is not an equivalence. The isomorphism F^* O{n} ≅ I^{−n} O{n} is the Frobenius of the twist from [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist): φ^* A{1} ≅ I^{−1} ⊗ A{1}.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 3.6.1, Remarks 3.6.2, 3.6.3 and 3.6.5; p. 55; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 3.6.6 with its proof, and Remark 3.6.14; pp. 56, 57.)

- `Prismatic.WCart.frobenius_hodgeTate`: For (I, α) in the Hodge–Tate divisor, F(I, α) ≅ (W(R), p·).

**Proof route.** The Witt Frobenius preserves the divisor coordinate conditions and equals W(φ_R) in characteristic p; compatibility of cofree lifts gives its action on prism points and twists. For α=Vβ the linearization of β is invertible and F^*α=FVγ=pγ, giving contraction of the Hodge–Tate divisor to the de-Rham point. Its uniqueness uses the absence of automorphisms of that point, and the intersection statement is BL Remark 3.6.14.

- F(V(1)) = p: the image of η under F is the de Rham point. F^* O_WCart ≅ O_WCart and F^* O_WCart{1} ≅ I^{−1} ⊗ O_WCart{1}. Over the dual numbers F(1 + [ε]) = 1: the non-trivial automorphism of η defining the Sen operator dies under F.

<a id="layer-4-frobenius-pullback-square"></a>

### 4.16 The Frobenius pullback square for global sections on WCart

Let E be a quasi-coherent complex on the Cartier–Witt stack WCart. The commutative square of stacks formed by WCart^HT ⊂ WCart, F : WCart → WCart, WCart^HT → Spf(Z_p) and ρ_dR induces a pullback square in D̂(Z_p): RΓ(WCart, E) is the fibre product of RΓ(WCart, F^* E) and RΓ(Spf Z_p, ρ_dR^* E) over RΓ(WCart^HT, (F^* E)|_{WCart^HT}). Moreover (F^* E)_η ≅ ρ_dR^* E with trivial Sen operator, so RΓ(WCart^HT, (F^* E)|_{WCart^HT}) ≅ ρ_dR^* E ⊕ ρ_dR^* E[−1] and there is a fibre sequence RΓ(WCart, E) → RΓ(WCart, F^* E) → ρ_dR^* E[−1]. Consequently the functor (F^*, ρ_dR^*) : D(WCart) → D(WCart) ×_{D(WCart^HT)} D(Spf Z_p) is fully faithful; it is not an equivalence.

E is a quasi-coherent complex on WCart; Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 3.6.7 prints "on the Cartier–Witt stack WCart^HT", a misprint: the square involves RΓ(WCart, E), F^* E and ρ_dR^* E. The square is a pullback in the p-complete derived category D̂(Z_p). No hypothesis on p.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 3.6.7 with its proof, Remark 3.6.8, Corollary 3.6.9 and Warning 3.6.11; pp. 56, 57; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Lemma 3.6.19, Proposition 3.6.18 and Remark 3.6.20; pp. 59, 60, 62.)

*Needs:* [§4.15](#layer-4-wcart-frobenius), [§4.14](#layer-4-sen-operator-classification), [§4.13](#layer-4-sen-operator), [§4.12](#layer-4-hodge-tate-divisor), [§4.9](#layer-4-quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart), [§4.10](#layer-4-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart), [§4.8](#layer-4-wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms), [§4.7](#layer-4-prism-point-of-wcart), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, [§3.6](#layer-3-transversal-prism).

**Proof route.** I-adic completeness reduces the square to objects supported on the Hodge–Tate divisor, and transversality of the chart nerve identifies the requisite derived pullback squares. Colimit preservation and generation by twists reduce to their global sections, where the nontrivial H¹ map is pZ_p⊂Z_p (BL Lemma 3.6.19 and Proposition 3.6.18). Contraction to the de-Rham point splits the fibre sequence, while generation by I^n proves full faithfulness; BL Warning 3.6.11 supplies the failure of essential surjectivity.

**Checks.**

- E = O_WCart: a fibre sequence RΓ(WCart, O) → RΓ(WCart, O) → Z_p[−1] whose first map is the Frobenius. For E the prismatic cohomology sheaf of R twisted by n: the pullback square of Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.4.14 with corner the p-completed derived de Rham complex.

### 4.17 Relative prismatic complexes of animated rings and the relative prismatic site

Fix a bounded prism (A, I) with Ā = A/I. For an animated Ā-algebra R let Δ_{R/A} ∈ D̂(A) be the derived prismatic complex (the sifted-colimit-preserving extension from finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebras, where it is the limit of B over (R/A)_Δ); no p-completeness of R is required and Δ_{R/A} ≅ Δ_{R̂/A}. For a scheme, formal scheme or algebraic stack X over Ā put RΓ_Δ(X/A) = lim_{Spec R → X} Δ_{R/A} in D̂(A). (1) X ↦ RΓ_Δ(X/A) satisfies étale descent; for an Ā-algebra R with bounded p-power torsion Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_Δ(Spf R̂ / A); for every animated Ā-algebra R, Δ_{R/A} ≅ Tot Δ_{(F_p^{⊗•+1} ⊗^L R)/A} and Δ_{R/A} ≅ lim_n Δ_{(Z/p^n ⊗^L R)/A}. (2) For a bounded p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over Ā let RΓ^site_Δ(𝔛/A) be the limit of B over the relative prismatic site (𝔛/A)_Δ. There is a comparison map ξ_𝔛 : RΓ_Δ(𝔛/A) → RΓ^site_Δ(𝔛/A), functorial in 𝔛 and equal to the tautological identification for the formal spectra of p-completed finitely generated polynomial algebras. If every affine open Spf(R) ⊂ 𝔛 satisfies (∗): R has bounded p-power torsion and R/pR ⊗^L_R L_{R/Ā} has Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0] over R/pR, then ξ_𝔛 is an isomorphism in D̂(A). (3) If R satisfies (∗⁺): R has bounded p-power torsion and R/pR ⊗^L_R L_{R/Ā} is a flat R/pR-module placed in cohomological degree −1, then Δ_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0, Δ̄_{R/A} is p-completely flat over R, and (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is an initial object of (R/A)_Δ. (4) If (A, I) is transversal and (B, J) is a perfect prism, then R = Ā ⊗^L B̄ satisfies (∗⁺) and (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is the coproduct (A, I) ⊔ (B, J).

(A, I) is a bounded prism, fixed; 𝔛 is a bounded p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Condition (∗) holds when R̂ is p-completely smooth over Ā; it is the Tor-amplitude condition of p-quasisyntomic algebras, taken relative to Ā. It is not automatic, and ξ_𝔛 is not claimed to be an isomorphism without it. The relative prismatic site is a large category; the limit defining RΓ^site is taken in a larger universe (Bhatt–Lurie, Warning 4.3.2). Use the BS22 bounded relative site of Layer 1. Under condition (∗), its limit agrees with the BL22 relative-site limit allowing unbounded objects: the (∗⁺) initial objects are bounded and descent reduces to these. Ordinary fibre products of Ā-schemes over Spec A and over Spec Ā coincide, so no base-of-fibre-product erratum is asserted.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 4.3.6 with its proof, Proposition 4.3.4; p. 86; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollary 4.3.14 and Example 4.3.15; pp. 89, 90; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Propositions 4.2.5 and 4.2.8, Corollary 4.2.9; pp. 83, 84.)

<a id="layer-4-absolute-prismatic-cohomology"></a>

### 4.18 The prismatic cohomology sheaf on WCart and absolute prismatic cohomology

Let R be an animated commutative ring. For a bounded prism (A, I) with Ā = A/I, the relative prismatic complex Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} ∈ D̂(A) is compatible with base change: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, IB) there is a canonical isomorphism B ⊗̂^L_A Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} ≅ Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B}. By Quasi-coherent complexes on WCart are prismatic crystals this family is an object H_Δ(R) of D(WCart), the prismatic cohomology sheaf of R, with ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B} for every bounded prism (B, J). R ↦ H_Δ(R) is a functor from animated rings to commutative algebra objects of D(WCart) which commutes with sifted colimits and satisfies étale descent. For integers m, n the absolute prismatic complexes are Δ_R^{[m]}{n} = RΓ(WCart, I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R){n}) ∈ D̂(Z_p); Δ_R{n} = Δ_R^{[0]}{n} and Δ_R = Δ_R{0} is the absolute prismatic complex of R, an E_∞-algebra over Z_p. Concretely Δ_R is the totalization of Δ_{(Ā^• ⊗^L R)/A^•} for the cosimplicial prism (A^•, I^•). For a scheme, formal scheme or algebraic stack X, RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} is the limit of Δ_R^{[m]}{n} over the category of points Spec R → X (R an ordinary ring), RΓ_Δ(X) = RΓ_Δ^{[0]}(X){0} is the absolute prismatic complex of X and H^*_Δ(X) its cohomology; RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(Spec R){n} = Δ_R^{[m]}{n}. For a bounded p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 that is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, (A, I) ↦ RΓ_Δ(Spf(A/I) × 𝔛 / A) on transversal prisms defines H_Δ(𝔛) ∈ D(WCart), characterised by étale descent and agreement with H_Δ(R) for 𝔛 = Spf R with R p-complete of bounded p-power torsion, and RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} ≅ RΓ(WCart, I^m ⊗ H_Δ(𝔛){n}). If 𝔛 is smooth and proper over Spf Z_p then H_Δ(𝔛) is a perfect complex on WCart.

R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; no completeness or boundedness is assumed (Δ_R^{[m]}{n} depends only on the p-completion of R). The sheaf H_Δ(𝔛) of a formal scheme is defined for 𝔛 bounded, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the complex RΓ_Δ(X) is defined for every X by the limit over points. Corrected misprint: the limit defining RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} is over the absolute complexes Δ_R^{[m]}{n}; Bhatt–Lurie Construction 4.4.19 prints a relative symbol. The twists {n} are the Breuil–Kisin twists of Layer 3, imported; they are not constructed here.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 4.4.1, Remarks 4.4.2 and 4.4.3, Variant 4.4.6; pp. 90, 91; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Constructions 4.4.10 and 4.4.19, Remark 4.4.11; pp. 92, 93.)

- `Prismatic.Absolute.prismaticSheaf`: H_Δ(R) ∈ D(WCart) for a commutative ring R.

Twist by I^m{n} and take enhanced global sections; right Kan extension over points gives the formal-scheme construction. Completed base change on qcqs charts uses the completed projection formula and finite affine covers of intersections, with [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh)’s effectivity hypotheses, while proper smooth perfectness is [§1.22](#layer-1-proper-smooth-perfectness); a finite cover alone does not shorten an unbounded Čech limit.

- `pr5_abs_sheaf_zero_ring`: H_Δ of the zero ring is a zero object.
- `pr5_abs_fp`: Δ_{F_p} is Z_p placed in degree 0.
- `pr5_abs_sheaf_fp_not_unit`: H_Δ(F_p) is not isomorphic to O_WCart: its pullback to a transversal prism A is A{p/I}^∧, not A.

<a id="layer-4-absolute-relative-comparison"></a>

### 4.19 Absolute versus relative prismatic cohomology

Let (B, J) be a bounded prism with B̄ = B/J and let R be an animated commutative ring. (1) By construction ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B} in D̂(B), compatibly with maps of bounded prisms. If R is an animated B̄-algebra, the multiplication B̄ ⊗^L R → R induces ξ : H_Δ(R) → ρ_{B*} Δ_{R/B} in D(WCart) and, on global sections, comparison maps Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → J^m ⊗ Δ_{R/B}{n} for all integers m, n; for X over B̄ these give RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} → J^m{n} ⊗^L_B RΓ_Δ(X/B). (2) If (B, J) is a perfect prism, ξ is an isomorphism H_Δ(R) ≅ ρ_{B*} Δ_{R/B}; hence Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ J^m Δ_{R/B}{n} for all m, n, RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} ≅ J^m{n} ⊗^L_B RΓ_Δ(X/B) for X over B̄, and H_Δ(𝔛) ≅ ρ_{B*} RΓ_Δ(𝔛/B) for a bounded qcqs p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over B̄. (3) For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring R: Δ_R is concentrated in degree 0, (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}) is a prism, equal to the initial prism of R, and H_Δ(R) is the pushforward of the structure sheaf along Spf(Δ_R) → WCart. For a prism that is not perfect the maps in (1) are not isomorphisms in general: the pullback ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) is the relative complex of B̄ ⊗^L R, not of R.

(1) holds for every bounded prism; the isomorphisms of (2) require the prism to be perfect. R is an animated algebra over B̄ = B/J in (2); no finiteness or completeness hypothesis. The comparison is not an isomorphism for every bounded prism: for a bounded prism only the identity ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B} holds.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Propositions 4.4.8 and 4.4.12 with their proofs; pp. 91, 92; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Example 4.4.13 and Remark 4.4.21; pp. 92, 94.)

Base change and Künneth identify this with scalar extension of Δ_((Ā⊗ᴸB̄)/A)→C, an equivalence for perfect B by BL22 Example 4.3.15 and Proposition 4.4.8, pp.87,91–92. Tensoring by the dualizable twists and applying projection formula gives (2), while Example 4.4.13, p.92, and the supplied QRSP initial prism give (3); the general nonregular formal-effectivity obligation remains the one in [§4.0](#layer-4-formal-qcoh).

For the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E)) and R = O_K the comparison map Δ_{O_K} → Δ_{O_K/W(k)[[u]]} = W(k)[[u]] is not claimed to be an isomorphism.

<a id="layer-4-absolute-prismatic-descent"></a>

### 4.20 Descent and continuity properties of absolute prismatic cohomology

Fix integers m, n. (1) The functor R ↦ Δ_R^{[m]}{n} from animated commutative rings to D̂(Z_p) satisfies descent for the étale topology, and X ↦ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} satisfies étale descent. (2) Derived descent: for every animated ring R, with R^• = R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}, the map Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → Tot Δ_{R^•}^{[m]}{n} is an isomorphism; each R^k is an animated F_p-algebra. (3) Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ lim_k Δ^{[m]}_{(Z/p^k) ⊗^L R}{n}. (4) Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ Δ_{R̂}^{[m]}{n} for the derived p-completion R̂ of R. (5) If X is a scheme whose structure sheaf has bounded p-power torsion and 𝔛 = Spf(Z_p) × X is its p-adic formal scheme, then RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} ≅ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n}; for a ring R with bounded p-power torsion, Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(Spf R̂){n}. (6) On the category of p-quasisyntomic p-adic formal schemes the functor 𝔛 ↦ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} satisfies descent for the p-quasisyntomic topology. The functor R ↦ Δ_R does not commute with filtered colimits as a functor to D̂(Z_p).

(1)–(4) hold for all animated commutative rings. (5) requires bounded p-power torsion; (6) is stated on p-quasisyntomic formal schemes: affine opens Spf R with R p-complete, of bounded p-power torsion, and L_{R/Z_p} ⊗^L R/p of Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]. Descent is for D̂(Z_p)-valued functors: limits are p-completed derived limits.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Propositions 4.4.14 and 4.4.15, Corollaries 4.4.17 and 4.4.18; p. 93; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Propositions 4.4.25 and 4.4.32, Corollary 4.4.26; pp. 94, 96.)

**Proof route.** Relative étale and derived-reduction descent hold at every prism, so twisting by an invertible sheaf and taking global sections preserves their limits. Reduce the continuity comparisons along the derived F_p cover, where the displayed reduction towers are pro-constant or pro-isomorphic, and use étale descent to pass to formal schemes. Qsyn descent similarly follows from the relative comparison on transversal prisms and the same twisting/global-sections functors (BL §4.4).

**Checks.**

- Δ_R = 0 when p is invertible in R; Δ_{Z[1/N]} ≅ Δ_Z for N prime to p. Δ_R ≅ Tot of the derived crystalline cohomology of the animated F_p-algebras R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗k+1}. Quasisyntomic test: for R p-quasisyntomic with a quasiregular semiperfectoid cover R → S, Δ_R is the totalization of the cosimplicial ring Δ_{S^•}.

<a id="layer-4-absolute-site-comparison"></a>

### 4.21 Absolute prismatic cohomology as cohomology of the absolute prismatic site

Let 𝔛 be a bounded p-adic formal scheme. For integers m, n let RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n} be the limit of I^m{n} over the category of triples (A, I, u) of the absolute prismatic site, formed in D̂(Z_p); it is RΓ(𝔛_Δ, I_Δ^m{n}). For every object (A, I, u), restriction along u gives RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(Spf A/I){n} ≅ Δ_Ā^{[m]}{n} → I^m{n} ⊗^L_A Δ_{Ā/A} = I^m{n}, and in the limit a comparison map ξ : RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} → RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n}. Theorem: if for every affine open Spf(R) ⊂ 𝔛 the ring R is p-quasisyntomic, then ξ is an isomorphism in D̂(Z_p) for all m, n. In particular RΓ_Δ(𝔛) ≅ RΓ(𝔛_Δ, O_Δ) compatibly with the E_∞-algebra structures. Supplements: 𝔛 ↦ RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n} satisfies p-quasisyntomic descent on all bounded p-adic formal schemes; for R quasiregular semiperfectoid the category of triples has the initial object (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}) (a final object of the site) and both sides are I^m{n} of it.

𝔛 is bounded and every affine open is the formal spectrum of a p-quasisyntomic ring; quasi-compactness is not needed. Without the quasisyntomic hypothesis ξ is still defined, and it is not claimed to be an isomorphism: the animated theory and the underived site cohomology of a general formal scheme differ. Smooth formal schemes over Spf Z_p, Spf W(k) or Spf O_K satisfy the hypothesis.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 4.4.30 with its proof, Example 4.4.29; p. 95; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 4.4.31; p. 95.)

Equality on the QRSP basis therefore proves the comparison (BL Theorem 4.4.30).

**Checks.**

- 𝔛 = Spf(O_K): RΓ_Δ(Spf O_K) is the cohomology of the structure sheaf of (Spf O_K)_Δ, computed by the Čech nerve of the Breuil–Kisin prism. For R = Z_p[x_1, …, x_d]^∧ the absolute prismatic complex is the limit of A over all bounded prisms (A, I) with a map R → A/I. For 𝔛 = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid both sides are Δ_R.

<a id="layer-4-absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology"></a>

### 4.22 Absolute Hodge–Tate cohomology and the diffracted Hodge complex

Let R be an animated commutative ring. The Hodge–Tate cohomology sheaf H_Δ̄(R) ∈ D(WCart^HT) is the object given on bounded prisms by (A, I) ↦ Δ̄_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} ∈ D̂(Ā); it equals ι^* H_Δ(R). It carries the conjugate filtration Fil_n^conj H_Δ̄(R), given by (A, I) ↦ Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A}: an exhaustive increasing filtration with Fil_0^conj = R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} and graded pieces gr_n^conj H_Δ̄(R) ≅ LΩ^n_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT}{−n}[−n]. The absolute Hodge–Tate complexes are Δ̄_R{n} = RΓ(WCart^HT, H_Δ̄(R){n}) ∈ D̂(R), with Δ̄_R = Δ̄_R{0}, and Fil_m^conj Δ̄_R{n} = RΓ(WCart^HT, Fil_m^conj H_Δ̄(R){n}), whose colimit over m is Δ̄_R{n}. For all m, n there is a fibre sequence I^{m+1} ⊗ H_Δ(R){n} → I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R){n} → ι_*(H_Δ̄(R){m+n}) in D(WCart), and on global sections Δ_R^{[m+1]}{n} → Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → Δ̄_R{m+n}. Thus Δ_R^{[•]}{n} is a filtered object of D̂(Z_p) with gr^m = Δ̄_R{m+n}; it is filtration-complete, and R ↦ Δ_R^{[•]}{n}, as a functor to filtration-complete p-complete filtered complexes, commutes with sifted colimits, as do R ↦ Fil_m^conj Δ̄_R{n} and R ↦ Δ̄_R{n}. The p-complete diffracted Hodge complex is Ω̂^DHod_R = η^* H_Δ̄(R) ∈ D̂(R), with conjugate filtration Fil_n^conj Ω̂^DHod_R = η^* Fil_n^conj H_Δ̄(R), graded pieces LΩ̂^n_R[−n], and Sen operator Θ acting by −n on gr_n^conj; Fil_n^conj Ω̂^DHod_R lies in D^{≤n}. For every n there is a canonical isomorphism Δ̄_R{n} ≅ fib(Θ + n : Ω̂^DHod_R → Ω̂^DHod_R), and likewise for each step of the conjugate filtration. If (A, I) is a perfect prism and R an animated Ā-algebra, then Δ̄_R{n} ≅ Δ̄_{R/A}{n}.

R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; LΩ^n_R is the n-th derived exterior power of the cotangent complex of R over Z, and LΩ̂^n_R its p-completion (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0). Corrected misprint: the graded pieces of the diffracted Hodge complex are LΩ̂^n_R[−n]; the display in Bhatt–Lurie Construction 4.7.1 omits the shift. Δ̄_R is not the reduction of Δ_R modulo an ideal; it is the first graded piece of the filtration Δ_R^{[•]}. The Hodge-completed and derived de Rham theories are owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology and are not constructed here.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Constructions 4.5.1 and 4.5.5, Remark 4.5.7, Propositions 4.5.8 and 4.5.10; pp. 96, 97, 98; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 4.7.1, Notation 4.7.2 and Remark 4.7.5; pp. 102, 103.)

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Absolute.hodgeTateSheaf`: H_Δ̄(R) = ι^* H_Δ(R) ∈ D(WCart^HT).
- `Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteHodgeTate`: Δ̄_R{n} = RΓ(WCart^HT, H_Δ̄(R) ⊗ O{n}).
- `Prismatic.Absolute.diffractedHodge`: Ω̂^DHod_R = η^* H_Δ̄(R), with its Sen operator given by senOperator.

- `Prismatic.Absolute.absoluteHodgeTate_fibre_sequence`: The fibre sequence Δ̄_R{n} → η^*(H_Δ̄(R){n}) → η^*(H_Δ̄(R){n}) whose second map is the Sen operator, that is Θ + n on Ω̂^DHod_R.

Apply the Sen fibre formula to H_Δ̄(R){n}, whose operator is Θ+n, to identify the diffracted Hodge complex; the perfect-prism specialization follows from the relative comparison (BL §§4.5,4.7).

- `pr5_ht_sheaf_integers`: H_Δ̄(Z) is the unit object of D(WCart^HT).
- `pr5_ht_diffracted_integers`: Ω̂^DHod_Z is Z_p in degree 0.

- Δ̄_Z = RΓ(WCart^HT, O) = Z_p ⊕ Z_p[−1], and Δ̄_Z{n} ≅ (Z_p/n)[−1] for n ≠ 0. For a perfectoid ring R the complex Ω̂^DHod_R is the coordinate ring of the G_m^♯-torsor of the Hodge–Tate point of R, concentrated in degree 0. For R p-torsion-free with R/pR regular Noetherian the conjugate filtration of Ω̂^DHod_R is its Postnikov filtration.

<a id="layer-4-absolute-crystalline-comparison"></a>

### 4.23 Absolute prismatic cohomology in characteristic p is crystalline cohomology

Let X be a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme. There is a canonical isomorphism γ : RΓ_Δ(X) ≅ RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) of commutative algebra objects of D̂(Z_p), characterised up to homotopy by functoriality in X and by the commutativity of the square whose top row is RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_Δ(X) (γ^{−1} followed by the Frobenius φ), whose left side is the crystalline augmentation ε_crys : RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ(X, O_X), whose bottom row is RΓ(X, O_X) ≅ Fil_0^conj RΓ_Δ̄(X/Z_p) → RΓ_Δ̄(X), and whose right side is the reduction RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_Δ̄(X). Supplements: (1) for a perfect field k and a quasisyntomic k-scheme X, RΓ_Δ(X) = RΓ_Δ(X/W(k)) and the identification with RΓ_crys(X/W(k)) is Frobenius-semilinear: RΓ_crys(X/W(k)) ≅ F^* RΓ_Δ(X/W(k)) in D(W(k)); for a perfect F_p-algebra R, under Δ_R = W(R) = A_crys(R), γ^{−1} is W(φ_R^{−1}). (2) On animated F_p-algebras R ↦ Δ_R commutes with sifted colimits and agrees with RΓ_crys(−/Z_p) on polynomial algebras: Δ_R is derived crystalline cohomology. (3) For an arbitrary F_p-scheme X there is a natural map RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_crys(X/Z_p), which need not be an isomorphism. (4) X ↦ RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) satisfies p-quasisyntomic descent on quasisyntomic F_p-schemes, and A_crys(R) is p-torsion-free for a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra R. Here φ means the relative Frobenius over (Z_p,(p)) transported through Δ_X≃Δ_(X/Z_p); this construction uses only the relative Frobenius constructed in Layer 1.

X is a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme: Zariski-locally the spectrum of a p-quasisyntomic F_p-algebra; no quasi-compactness or smoothness is assumed. RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) is the crystalline cochain complex relative to (Z_p, (p)) of CrystallineCohomology:CR.2. The isomorphism is not linear over W(k): the Frobenius twist is the φ_A-twist of [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison).

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 4.6.1 with its proof, Lemmas 4.6.8, 4.6.11 and 4.6.13; pp. 98, 99, 100, 101; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Warning 4.6.2, Remarks 4.6.5 and 4.6.6, Corollary 4.6.7; pp. 98, 99.)

*Needs:* [§4.18](#layer-4-absolute-prismatic-cohomology), [§4.19](#layer-4-absolute-relative-comparison), [§4.20](#layer-4-absolute-prismatic-descent), [§4.22](#layer-4-absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology), [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§2.3](#layer-2-derived-hodge-tate-comparison), [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, [§1.9](#layer-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`.

**Proof route.** For quasiregular semiperfect R the Frobenius-preimage of p has divided powers, giving the map from A_crys; modulo p the one-root eigenvalue calculation sends γ_(pn)(x) to a unit times γ_n(x̄) in conjugate degree n. The supplied CR.4 conjugate-PD calculation and the Hodge–Tate comparison make its associated graded an isomorphism. Extend by qsyn descent and then by the perfected polynomial Čech resolution, on which both crystalline and absolute prismatic theories descend (BL Theorem 4.6.1).

**Checks.**

- A smooth F_p-scheme the isomorphism is the case A = Z_p of [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison). For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x): Δ_R ≅ A_crys(R), the p-completed divided power envelope of (x) in W(F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]). For R perfect, Δ_R = W(R) and the comparison is the inverse Witt vector Frobenius.

<a id="layer-4-absolute-de-rham-comparison"></a>

### 4.24 The absolute de Rham comparison and the de Rham point

Let R be an animated commutative ring, R̄ = F_p ⊗^L R, and let dR̂_R be the p-complete derived de Rham complex of R (over Z) with its Hodge filtration. (1) There is a canonical isomorphism α_R : ρ_dR^* H_Δ(R) ≅ dR̂_R in D̂(Z_p), functorial in R and characterised by the requirement that α_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} is the isomorphism (F^* H_Δ(R))|_{WCart^HT} ≅ dR̂_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} obtained from the relative de Rham comparison Ā ⊗^L_A F^* Δ_{R′/A} ≅ dR̂_{R′/Ā} over all bounded prisms and from F ∘ ι ≅ ρ_dR ∘ (WCart^HT → Spf Z_p). (2) Consequently Δ_{R̄} ≅ dR̂_R as commutative algebra objects of D̂(Z_p), functorially in R. (3) The de Rham comparison map γ^dR{n} : Δ_R{n} → dR̂_R is the restriction to the de Rham point composed with α_R, using the trivialisation of ρ_dR^* O_WCart{n} by the generator e^n of Z_p{n}; the prismatic augmentation ε_Δ : Δ_R → R̂ is γ^dR followed by dR̂_R → gr^0_Hodge = R̂. (4) For every n the square with corners Δ_R{n}, dR̂_R, RΓ(WCart, F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) and dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O) is a pullback square, and there is a fibre sequence Δ_R{n} → RΓ(WCart, F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → dR̂_R[−1]. (5) For a p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 flat over Spf Z_p with regular Noetherian special fibre X, RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) ≅ RΓ_dR(𝔛) (Berthelot).

R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; dR̂_R is the p-completed derived de Rham complex, not Hodge-completed, owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2. The source of γ^dR{n} is Δ_R{n} (Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.4.14). (5) needs flatness over Z_p and a regular Noetherian special fibre, for example 𝔛 smooth over Spf W(k).

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 5.4.2, Proposition 5.4.8 with its proof, Constructions 5.4.7, 5.4.9 and 5.4.10; pp. 129, 130, 131; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollary 5.4.14 and Remark 5.4.15; p. 133.)

*Needs:* [§4.18](#layer-4-absolute-prismatic-cohomology), [§4.19](#layer-4-absolute-relative-comparison), [§4.16](#layer-4-frobenius-pullback-square), [§4.15](#layer-4-wcart-frobenius), [§4.14](#layer-4-sen-operator-classification), [§4.10](#layer-4-prismatic-crystals-on-wcart), [§4.23](#layer-4-absolute-crystalline-comparison), [§3.17](#layer-3-de-rham-comparison-general), [§3.14](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-filtration), [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation`.

**Proof route.** Evaluation at the crystalline de-Rham point identifies the first complex, and the animated Lη/de-Rham comparison identifies the Frobenius pullback on WCart^HT. The possible second component in dR̂_R⊕dR̂_R[−1] is naturally null: left Kan extend the source from torsion-free qsyn rings and right Kan extend the target from QRSP rings, where both are in degree zero (BL Proposition 5.4.8). Insert this into the Frobenius pullback square, and use characteristic-p crystalline comparison and DD.2 for the remaining specializations.

**Checks.**

- R = Z_p[x_1, …, x_d]^∧: Δ_{F_p[x_1, …, x_d]} ≅ the p-completed de Rham complex of R. For R = Z: ρ_dR^* O_WCart = Z_p = dR̂_Z and the fibre sequence of (4) is RΓ(WCart, O) → RΓ(WCart, O) → Z_p[−1]. For a perfectoid ring Ā = A/I the prismatic augmentation Δ_Ā = A → Ā is φ followed by the quotient map.

<a id="layer-4-absolute-nygaard-filtration"></a>

### 4.25 The absolute Nygaard filtration

Let R be an animated commutative ring and n an integer. (a) For a bounded prism (A, I) the relative Nygaard filtration Fil^m_N F^* Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} is compatible with completed base change in the prism, so it defines a decreasing filtered object Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) of D(WCart) with Fil^0_N = F^* H_Δ(R). (b) There is a fibre sequence of filtered objects I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N F^* H_Δ(R) → Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) → ι_*(Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT}). (c) Put Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n}) = Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) ⊗ F^* O_WCart{n}; since F^* O_WCart{n} ≅ I^{−n} O_WCart{n} is canonically trivial on WCart^HT, (b) gives a map RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O). (d) The absolute Nygaard filtration Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} is the fibre product, in the filtered derived category of p-complete complexes, of RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) and Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R over Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O). Then Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} = Δ_R{n}, Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} is an isomorphism for m ≤ 0, and the projection Fil^•(γ^dR{n}) : Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R is the filtered de Rham specialisation. (e) There is a fibre sequence of filtered complexes Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R[−1]. (f) ⊕_n Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} is a graded commutative algebra in filtered complexes; Fil^•_N Δ_R is a filtered E_∞-algebra and each Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} a module over it. (g) Graded pieces: gr^m_N Δ_R{n} = cofib(Fil^{m+1}_N → Fil^m_N) sits in a fibre sequence gr^m_N Δ_R{n} → Fil_m^conj Ω̂^DHod_R → Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod_R whose second map is Θ + m; there is a unique class e^n ∈ H^0(gr^0_N Δ_R{n}) with image 1 in H^0(gr^0_Hodge dR̂_R), and multiplication by e^n is an isomorphism gr^m_N Δ_R ≅ gr^m_N Δ_R{n}. (h) For a scheme, formal scheme or stack X, Fil^m_N RΓ_Δ(X){n} is the limit of Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} over the points Spec R → X. (i) The Nygaard-completed complexes are Fil^m_N Δ̂_R{n} = lim_k Fil^m_N Δ_R{n}/Fil^{m+k}_N Δ_R{n}, with Δ̂_R{n} = Fil^0_N Δ̂_R{n}; Δ_R{n} is Nygaard-complete when lim_m Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} = 0.

R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; the filtration is decreasing, indexed by all integers and constant in degrees ≤ 0. The relative Nygaard filtration and its base-change compatibility are imported from [§3.14](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-filtration); the Breuil–Kisin twists from [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist). The Hodge filtration is that of the p-complete derived de Rham complex of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2; no Hodge completion is used in (a)–(h). Corrected misprint: in (h) the limit is over the absolute complexes Fil^m_N Δ_R{n}. Syntomic complexes built from this filtration are owned by Layer 6 and are not defined here.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Notation 5.5.1, Remark 5.5.2, Construction 5.5.3 and Remark 5.5.6; pp. 133, 134; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remarks 5.5.7, 5.5.8 and 5.5.15, Corollary 5.5.14, Notation 5.5.23, Definition 5.8.5; pp. 134, 135, 136, 138, 148.)
