### 5.18 q-Poincaré comparison of the Čech–Koszul bicomplex

For a framed q-PD datum (P,S,J) over D flat over Z_p[[q−1]], the completed Čech–Koszul total complex has equivalences to the framed q-de Rham complex of its q-PD envelope and to q-crystalline cohomology. These equivalences respect the associative products described below. They are natural for coordinate-injective maps of framed data, including the cofaces of the Čech nerve. Codegeneracies need not be maps of differential graded algebras.

Use finite coordinate sets first and then completed filtered colimits. All complexes and cofibres are derived (p,q−1)-complete. The associative product is part of the conclusion; the exterior product with central forms does not satisfy the q-Leibniz rule.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 16.22 and proof, pp.115–116, and Remark 17.3, p.117; [BMS1](#ref-bms1), Lemma 7.5 and Example 7.7, pp.57–58, and Lemma 6.13, p.53. The semicosimplicial argument below supplies the multiplicative compatibility.)

*Needs:* [§5.15](#layer-5-gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope), [§5.16](#layer-5-framed-q-de-rham-complex), [§5.10](#layer-5-q-crystalline-cech-alexander), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0/limits-colimits-and-slices`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/algebra-objects`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1/ideal-decalage-complex`.

Equip K=qΩ^{*,□}_{F/D}, F=D_{J,q}(P), with the skew differential graded product

dX_s·a=γ_s(a)dX_s, (dX_s)²=0, dX_s·dX_t=−dX_t·dX_s, da=Σ_s∇_{q,s}(a)dX_s.

The identity ∇_{q,s}(ab)=∇_{q,s}(a)γ_s(b)+a∇_{q,s}(b) proves the Leibniz rule. Distinct γ_s commute with each other and with the other coordinate derivatives, so the relations are compatible with d, multiplication is associative and d²=0. This defines `QDeRham.skewDGA` on the already constructed complex. On a torus put e_s=X_s^{−1}dX_s; then e_s a=γ_s(a)e_s and da=Σ_s((γ_s−1)/(q−1))(a)e_s. It is the décalage of the usual skew Koszul group-cochain algebra; BMS1's cited results identify its E₁ structure with the cup product after Lη. Coordinate-injective maps preserve the displayed product: target automorphisms outside the image fix the image of F, while those in the image intertwine the source automorphisms.

For the intrinsic product, take the completed Čech nerve P^n with disjoint copies S^n of the coordinates, and its envelopes F^n. Restrict to Δ_inj, the category with only injective order maps. The cofaces then give a semicosimplicial diagram of these skew differential graded algebras K^n. Projection onto degree zero is a differential graded algebra map K^n→F^n, since the positive-degree ideal is preserved by d. It gives a map of E₁ algebras Tot_{Δ_inj}K^•→Tot_{Δ_inj}F^•. Evaluation also gives an E₁ map Tot_{Δ_inj}K^•→K^0.

Here no degeneracy is being asserted multiplicative. Restriction from Δ to Δ_inj preserves homotopy limits: for each [n], the category of maps [k]→[n] with injective maps between their domains is contractible. Appending a last vertex of value n gives natural maps from the identity and from the constant last-vertex object into that append functor. Thus the inclusion is initial, by E0's limit criterion. In particular Tot_{Δ_inj}F^• is the usual site Čech algebra, with its intrinsic product.

The two maps of E₁ algebras are equivalences on underlying complexes. Every coface K^i→K^j is an equivalence modulo q−1 by the crystalline PD Poincaré lemma and embedding independence of CR.2, and hence before reduction by complete Nakayama. Since the nerve of Δ_inj is contractible, evaluation of their homotopy limit is an equivalence. For the projection onto row zero, in each positive form degree reduce the semicosimplicial row F^•⊗̂Ω^r_{P^•/D} modulo q−1. The classical row has its usual cosimplicial degeneracies and contraction (CR.2; Stacks Tag 07JP). Initiality identifies its semicosimplicial totalisation with that acyclic totalisation. Derived reduction commutes with totalisation because D/(q−1) is perfect over D, and totalisations remain derived complete. Complete Nakayama therefore makes each positive row acyclic before reduction too. The first-quadrant double complex now makes projection onto row zero an equivalence. This proves the multiplicative zigzag

qΩ_{R/D} ← Tot_{Δ_inj}K^• → qΩ^{*,□}_{F/D}

in E₁-D-algebras. Applying the same construction to unions of two, three or finitely many framed data makes the zigzags coherent and natural; the maps to the single site Čech algebra identify all their composites. Frobenius preserves the skew product and these comparisons. Infinite coordinate sets are obtained by completed filtered colimits of these finite constructions.

Prove the following API:

- `QDeRham.skewDGA`: the above real associative product on the framed complex, with its differential and unit.
- `QDeRham.skewDGA_injection`: coordinate-injective functoriality as differential graded algebra maps.
- `QDeRham.siteComparison_E1`: the E₁ zigzag with intrinsic q-crystalline cohomology, compatible with refinements and Frobenius.
- `QDeRham.groupCupProduct`: on unit coordinates, agreement with the Lη of the skew Koszul cup product.

**Checks.** On D⟨X⟩ one has dX·X=qX·dX and d(X²)=(1+q)X·dX; making dX central would give 2X·dX and fail. With two coordinates, dX·dY=−dY·dX and d²(XY)=0, including at p=2 where the separate square-zero relation is still required. With no coordinates the product is F's ring product in degree zero. At q=1 the model becomes the usual differential graded PD de Rham algebra. Merging X₀,X₁↦X is not claimed to be a strict algebra map: sending both dlog generators to e would send e₀X₁=X₁e₀ to the false relation eX=Xe. This is why the multiplicative proof uses only cofaces and coordinate injections.

### 5.19 q-de Rham and q-crystalline comparison

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair with D flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]], R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra and (P, S, J) a framed q-PD datum with P/J ≅ R. Then there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism qΩ_{R/D} ≃ qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D}: the q-de Rham complex of the framed q-PD datum computes q-crystalline cohomology. The identification is natural for morphisms of framed q-PD data injective on coordinate sets lying over maps R → R′, and it carries the Frobenius φ_{R/D} to the Frobenius of The q-de Rham complex of a framed q-PD datum (d).

(D, I) is a q-PD pair with D flat over A; (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum for R. The source states the quasi-isomorphism; naturality in the framed datum and the compatibility with Frobenius are visible in its proof (the bicomplex is functorial and carries the Frobenius) and are used in Theorem 17.2. For q = 1 this is the comparison of crystalline cohomology with the de Rham complex of a PD envelope, owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.2.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 16.22; p. 115; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 16.22, the sentence before the proof and the proof; pp. 115–116.)

*Needs:* [§5.16](#layer-5-framed-q-de-rham-complex), [§5.15](#layer-5-gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope), [§5.10](#layer-5-q-crystalline-cech-alexander), [§5.11](#layer-5-q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison), [§5.8](#layer-5-q-pd-envelope-base-change), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, [§5.18](#layer-5-q-poincare-lemma).

**Proof route.** Take the completed Čech nerve with disjoint labelled coordinate copies, whose cofaces are coordinate injections. The semicosimplicial E₁ zigzag of [§5.18](#layer-5-q-poincare-lemma) identifies its bicomplex totalization both with the zero-column q-de-Rham complex and with the degree-zero site Čech algebra. Those maps preserve products and Frobenius and are natural for the permitted injections.

**Checks.**

- One polynomial coordinate: qΩ_{Z_p⟨X⟩/Z_p[[q−1]]} is computed by Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩ → Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩dX, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^{n−1}dX. A torus over A_inf: qΩ_{O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩/A_inf} is computed by A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ → A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ dlog x, x^n ↦ [n]_q x^n dlog x. Modulo q − 1 the quasi-isomorphism reduces to the statement that the de Rham complex of the p-completed PD envelope of P/(q−1) → R computes RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))).

### 5.20 Change of framing and the cocycle identity

Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair with D flat over A and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. Let (P, S, J) and (P′, S′, J′) be two framed q-PD data for R; the case P = P′ with two coordinate systems is included. Put P″ = P ⊗̂_D P′ (derived (p,[p]_q)-completed), S″ = S ⊔ S′ and J″ = ker(P″ → R). Then (P″, S″, J″) is a framed q-PD datum for R, and the two morphisms of framed q-PD data induce quasi-isomorphisms qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} → qΩ^{*,□″}_{D_{J″,q}(P″)/D} ← qΩ^{*,□′}_{D_{J′,q}(P′)/D}. The resulting isomorphism c_{□,□′} in D(D) equals the composite of the identifications of q-de Rham and q-crystalline comparison with qΩ_{R/D}. Consequently c_{□,□} = id and c_{□′,□″}∘c_{□,□′} = c_{□,□″} for three framed data (the cocycle identity); the isomorphisms are compatible with Frobenius and with maps R → R′ covered by morphisms of framed data; the framed q-de Rham complex is independent of the framing up to canonical isomorphism in D(D); and on a smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over D/I the complexes of framed affine charts descend to the Zariski sheaf qΩ_{𝔛/D} of q-crystalline and crystalline cohomology.

Both data are framed q-PD data for the same R over the same q-PD pair, D flat over A. The complexes of two framings are different complexes; only their images in D(D), with Frobenius and multiplication, are identified. The statement is what the source calls independence 'up to canonical quasi-isomorphism' of the framing; it is deduced from Construction 16.20 and the proof of Theorem 16.22, where the same argument is applied to the face maps of the Čech nerve.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Construction 16.20, functoriality; p. 115; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 16.22, proof; pp. 115–116; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 1.9 (4); p. 5.)

*Needs:* [§5.19](#layer-5-q-de-rham-comparison), [§5.16](#layer-5-framed-q-de-rham-complex), [§5.11](#layer-5-q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

**Proof route.** The tensor-product framing gives the comparison span, and the injection functoriality gives its maps of complexes. Modulo q−1 these are the PD de-Rham embedding comparisons of CR.2, so completeness and Nakayama make them equivalences. Naturality of the Čech–Koszul zigzag identifies them with the intrinsic site comparison, proving the cocycle identities and Zariski descent.

**Checks.**

- Two framings: R = Z_p⟨T⟩ over Z_p[[q−1]] with coordinates T and T + 1. The complexes differ, ∇^{T+1}(T²) − ∇^{T}(T²) = q − 1, and are identified through the datum on Z_p[[q−1]]⟨T_0, T_1⟩{φ(T_1 − T_0)/[p]_q}^∧ with coordinates T_0 and T_1 + 1. Three framings T, T + 1, T + 2 of Z_p⟨T⟩: the three isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle identity. Equal framings give the identity.

### 5.21 The framed q-de Rham complex of a smooth Z_p-algebra and prismatic cohomology

Let A = Z_p[[q−1]] with the q-de Rham prism (A, ([p]_q)), and let R be a p-completely smooth Z_p-algebra with a p-completely étale framing □ : Z_p⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩ → R. Let P be the (p, q−1)-completely étale A⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩-algebra lifting R (so P/(q−1) = R), framed by T_1, …, T_d, and let qΩ_R^□ := qΩ^{*,□}_{P/A} be its (p, q−1)-completed framed q-de Rham complex ([§5.0](#layer-5-framing-foundations)). Let R^{(1)} := R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p], the p-completed base change of R along Z_p = A/(q−1) → A/([p]_q) = Z_p[ζ_p]. Then there are canonical isomorphisms in D(A), compatible with Frobenius, qΩ_R^□ ≃ qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = RΓ_Δ(Spf(R^{(1)})/A). Consequently qΩ_R^□ is independent of the framing □ up to canonical quasi-isomorphism, is functorial in R as an object of D(A), and qΩ_R^□ ⊗^L_A A/(q−1) is the p-completed de Rham complex of R over Z_p. Scope: this is a statement for one prime p over the (p, q−1)-complete base Z_p[[q−1]]; it does not produce a theory over Z[[q−1]] or over the Habiro ring. The gluing over all primes is owned by HabiroCohomologyFoundations HQ.1–HQ.2.

R is p-completely smooth over Z_p with a p-completely étale framing; the prism is (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)), not (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)). The base change to Z_p[ζ_p] is part of the statement: prismatic cohomology is taken of R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂ Z_p[ζ_p], not of R. The framed complex qΩ_R^□ itself is [§5.0](#layer-5-framing-foundations)’s object; this target proves its comparison.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Example 1.9 (4); p. 5; [BS22](#ref-bs22), §16, introduction; p.106.)

*Needs:* [§5.19](#layer-5-q-de-rham-comparison), [§5.13](#layer-5-q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison), [§5.20](#layer-5-change-of-framing), [§5.11](#layer-5-q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison), [§5.5](#layer-5-smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals), [§5.16](#layer-5-framed-q-de-rham-complex), [§0.23](#layer-0-q-de-rham-prism), [§5.0](#layer-5-framing-foundations), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.2`.

**Proof route.** For the indicated framed pair the q-PD envelope is P itself, by complete flatness and the smallest q-PD ideal. Apply q-de-Rham/q-crystalline and q-crystalline/prismatic comparison, retaining R^(1)=R⊗̂_ZpZ_p[ζ_p]. The framing cocycle gives independence and functoriality, while reduction modulo q−1 is the smooth crystalline/de-Rham comparison.

- One polynomial coordinate: R = Z_p⟨T⟩: qΩ_R^□ = (A⟨T⟩ → A⟨T⟩dT), T^n ↦ [n]_q T^{n−1}dT. Modulo [p]_q the coefficient [n]_ζ is a unit for p ∤ n and 0 for p | n, so H^0 = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨T^p⟩ and H^1 = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨T^p⟩·T^{p−1}dT, which are R^{(1)} and Ω^1_{R^{(1)}/Z_p[ζ_p]} through T ↦ T^p, as the Hodge–Tate comparison for Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} predicts. A torus: R = Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩: qΩ_R^□ = (A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → A⟨T^{±1}⟩ dlog T), T^n ↦ [n]_q T^n dlog T. Two framings T and T + 1 of Z_p⟨T⟩ give canonically isomorphic objects of D(A).

### 5.22 The all-coordinates comparison map from q-crystalline cohomology to AΩ

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C) with q = [ε] and ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q), and the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)) of The q-PD pair (A_inf, (ξ)). Let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra that is very small: R/p is generated over O_C/p by units, and R is small, that is, there are units x_1, …, x_n of R defining a formally étale map O_C⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_n^{±1}⟩ → R. Put S = R^×. A coordinate family is a finite labelled set Σ with a map Σ→S; repeated values have distinct labels. Let C_R have these families as objects, with label-preserving injections as arrows, subject to the condition that A[x_s^{±1} : s ∈ Σ]^∧ → R, x_s ↦ s, is surjective and the family contains a framing. This category is not asserted filtered. For Σ ∈ C_R let P_Σ = A[x_s^{±1} : s ∈ Σ]^∧ be the formal torus over A, with δ(x_s) = 0 and the automorphisms γ_s scaling x_s by q, and J_Σ = ker(P_Σ → R); (P_Σ, Σ, J_Σ) is a framed q-PD datum. (1) The q-side. qΩ_{R/A} is computed by the complex hocolim_{Σ ∈ C_R} Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {∇_{q,s}}_{s∈Σ}), with transition maps for injections of labelled families. (2) The AΩ-side. For every Σ in C_R let Δ_Σ = ∏_{s∈Σ} Z_p(1) and let R_{Σ,∞} be the p-completed integral closure of R in the pro-étale Δ_Σ-torsor over R[1/p] obtained by extracting all p-power roots of the x_s; R_{Σ,∞} is perfectoid, and σ_s denotes the automorphism of A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) induced by the s-th basis vector of Δ_Σ. Then AΩ_R is computed by hocolim_{Σ ∈ C_R} η_{q−1} Kos_c(A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}); {σ_s − 1}_{s∈Σ}), and already by each term whose Σ contains units x_1, …, x_n defining a formally étale map O_C⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_n^{±1}⟩ → R. ### 5.23 Comparison with AΩ

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε], ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q), and let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra. Let AΩ_R be the complex of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (AInfCohomology:AI.3). Then the comparison map μ_R : qΩ_{R/A} → AΩ_R of The all-coordinates comparison map from q-crystalline cohomology to AΩ is an isomorphism, and AΩ_R ≃ qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. Here qΩ_{R/A} is taken relative to the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)); R^{(1)} = R ⊗_{A, φ} A is the Frobenius twist, an algebra over A/([p]_q); Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} is prismatic cohomology relative to the prism (A, ([p]_q)); and Δ_{R/A} is prismatic cohomology relative to the perfect prism (A, (ξ)) = (A_inf, ker θ). All these maps are isomorphisms of E_∞-A-algebras compatible with the Frobenius, natural in R. The Frobenius pullback is essential: φ_A is an automorphism of A, so φ_A^* only twists the A-module structure, but AΩ_R is not isomorphic to Δ_{R/A} in D(A) in general. (Remark 17.3.) The construction gives an isomorphism of E_1-A-algebras, natural in R and compatible with Frobenius; it is upgraded to an isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras by left Kan extension to quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras, where it is an isomorphism of associative rings between discrete commutative rings, and then quasisyntomic descent.

C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, with a fixed compatible system of p-power roots of 1; the introduction of the source states the result for C algebraically closed, §17 and BMS1 §§8–9 in this generality. R is a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra; AΩ_R is the value on Spf(R) of the complex AΩ of AI.3. The check that μ_R intertwines the two Hodge–Tate structure maps is left to the reader in the source; step 3 carries it out by reduction to the torus. The Hodge–Tate specialisation of AΩ used in step 2 carries the Frobenius twist that BMS1 Theorem 9.2 leaves implicit: R is an A_inf-algebra through θ̃ there. The labelled-family construction of [§5.22](#layer-5-ainf-omega-comparison-map) supplies arbitrary naturality without merging labels. The semicosimplicial comparison of [§5.18](#layer-5-q-poincare-lemma) supplies the site-to-skew-Koszul product compatibility needed for the E₁ comparison and the E_∞ upgrade.

### 5.25 Uniqueness of comparison isomorphisms

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with perfectoid ring R = A/I. Let Sm_R be the category of p-completely smooth R-algebras and C_{Sm_R} the ∞-category of pairs (G, η) where G : Sm_R → D_{(p,I)-comp}(A) is a symmetric monoidal functor and η : id → G ⊗^L_A R is a natural transformation of symmetric monoidal functors Sm_R → D_{p-comp}(R). Prismatic cohomology with the Hodge–Tate structure maps η_S : S → Δ̄_{S/A} is an object Δ_{−/A} of C_{Sm_R}. (Theorem 18.2.) Δ_{−/A} has no nontrivial endomorphisms in C_{Sm_R}: End(Δ_{−/A}) = {1}. No compatibility with the Frobenius is imposed. (Lemma 18.3.) Let rsPerfd_R be the category of R-algebras that are quotients of p-completely flat perfectoid R-algebras by sequences that are p-completely regular relative to R. Suppose that for every S in rsPerfd_R an A-algebra endomorphism ε_S of Δ_{S/A} is given such that ε_S is functorial in S and compatible with the identity of S under η_S : S → Δ̄_{S/A}. Then ε_S = id for all S. (Use for comparison maps.) If an object (G, η_G) of C_{Sm_R} is isomorphic to Δ_{−/A}, the isomorphism is unique and every morphism between the two objects is that isomorphism or its inverse. In particular the isomorphisms of q-crystalline and prismatic cohomology over a q-PD pair whose prism (D, ([p]_q)) is perfect, such as (A_inf, (ξ)), the isomorphism AΩ ≃ φ_A^*Δ_{−/A_inf} of Comparison with AΩ, and the comparison of Layer 3 with the Nygaard complexes of topological Hochschild homology (BS22 Theorem 13.1) are the unique ones compatible with the Hodge–Tate structure maps; they do not depend on coordinates or presentations and are compatible with one another.

(A, I) is a perfect prism, R = A/I the corresponding perfectoid ring. The theorem is about endomorphisms in the category of pairs (G, η) with the Hodge–Tate structure map, and it imposes no Frobenius compatibility; it is not a statement about automorphisms of a functor to E_∞-A-algebras with φ. In this proof use the following formulas: the sequence f_1, …, f_r lies in R′, the ring presented is A_inf(R′){g_i/d}^∧, the completeness is (p, d)-adic, and Joyal's identity reads φ^{n+1}(x) = x^{p^{n+1}} + pδ_1(x)^{p^n} + … + p^nδ_n(x)^p + p^{n+1}δ_{n+1}(x). For the AΩ comparison the perfect prism is (A_inf, ([p]_q)) with A_inf/[p]_q ≅ O_C through θ̃, and R ↦ R^{(1)} identifies the two categories of smooth algebras.

### 5.26 The Nygaard filtration in q-de Rham coordinates

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε], ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q) and ξ̃ = [p]_q, as in The q-PD pair (A_inf, (ξ)). Let M^• = qΩ^•_{R̃/A} be the framed q-de Rham complex in toric form: the Koszul complex of the commuting endomorphisms ∂_q/∂_q log T_i = (γ_i − 1)/(q − 1) of R̃, with basis the forms d_q log T_{j_1} ⋯ d_q log T_{j_n} in degree n, and with the φ_A-semilinear endomorphism φ_M given on degree n by f·ω ↦ ξ̃^n·φ(f)·ω for a basis form ω. Then: (1) M^• ≅ qΩ_{R/A} ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ AΩ_R in D(A), compatibly with the Frobenius endomorphisms. (2) φ_M(M^n) ⊂ ξ̃^n M^n for every n, and the map M^n/ξM^n → H^n(M^•/ξ̃M^•), x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/ξ̃^n, is bijective. (3) The relative Nygaard filtration of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} (Layer 3) is represented by the subcomplexes N^{≥i}M^• = ξ^{max(i − •, 0)} M^•, that is ξ^i R̃ → ξ^{i−1} R̃^{⊕d} → ⋯ → ξ M^{i−1} → M^i → M^{i+1} → ⋯, with filtered Frobenius φ_M : N^{≥i}M^• → ξ̃^i M^•; moreover N^{≥i}M^n = {x ∈ M^n : φ_M(x) ∈ ξ̃^i M^n}. The statement depends on the framing only through the model M^•; the filtration on φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} does not depend on it (Change of framing and the cocycle identity).

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Remark 9.11; p. 73; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 17.2; p. 117.)

*Needs:* [§3.24](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates), [§3.14](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-filtration), [§3.16](#layer-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation), [§5.16](#layer-5-framed-q-de-rham-complex), [§5.14](#layer-5-framed-q-pd-datum), [§5.19](#layer-5-q-de-rham-comparison), [§5.13](#layer-5-q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison), [§5.23](#layer-5-ainf-omega-comparison), [§5.6](#layer-5-ainf-q-pd-pair), [§5.20](#layer-5-change-of-framing), [§1.11](#layer-1-etale-localization).

**Proof route.** The framed q-PD envelope is R̃, so the three Frobenius-compatible comparisons identify its q-de-Rham model with AΩ. The relation φ(q−1)=[p]_q(q−1) gives the divided-derivative Frobenius identity; on torus monomials, [a]_q modulo [p]_q is a unit for p∤a and zero for p∣a, giving the divided degree-n bijection, which extends by complete étale base change. Apply the filtered comparison of [§3.24](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates) using regularity of ξ and ξ̃ and injectivity of φ modulo ξ; its Lη factorization is the displayed inclusion of the coordinate Frobenius model.

**Checks.**

- One coordinate, R = O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩: N^{≥1}M^• is ξ·A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → A⟨T^{±1}⟩·d_q log T, and N^{≥i}M^• is ξ^i·A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → ξ^{i−1}·A⟨T^{±1}⟩·d_q log T for i ≥ 1. Graded pieces: gr^i of N^{≥•}M^• is, in degree n ≤ i, (ξ^{i−n}M^n/ξ^{i−n+1}M^n) ≅ Ω^n_{R/O_C}, with zero differential, matching gr^i_N ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{R/A}{i} of [§3.15](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-graded-pieces). After base change along A_inf → W(k), k the residue field of O_C (so q ↦ 1 and ξ ↦ p), the filtration becomes p^{max(i − •, 0)} of the de Rham complex of the lift R̃ ⊗̂ W(k), the de Rham instance of [§3.24](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates). Modulo q − 1 alone this is not so: ξ is not p times a unit in A_inf/(q − 1). The element T^a with p ∤ a is not a cocycle modulo ξ̃ in degree 0: ∂_q/∂_q log T (T^a) = [a]_q T^a with [a]_q a unit modulo ξ̃; so H^0(M^•/ξ̃) is spanned by the T^{pa}.

### Examples

In the one-variable framed model, ∇_q(X²)=(1+q)X specializes to 2X at q=1 and to (1+q)X before specialization. At p=2, [p]_q=1+q. For q=1 and x=p in Z_p, γ(p)=p^(p−1), hence γ(2)=2 at p=2. In Z_p[[q−1]] the scalar p is not in φ⁻¹([p]_qD), so N(D) is not the ideal (p,q−1). For two commuting operators, the two middle entries of d¹d⁰ cancel with the specified minus sign. Coordinate merging requires its own coherent comparison and does not follow from the coordinate-injective framed maps.

## Layer 6: Étale comparisons and syntomic complexes

Étale Frobenius fixed points are derived fibres over the coefficient ring, after Laurent inversion and p-completion in the stated order. Syntomic cohomology retains the Nygaard condition and the twist before taking divided-Frobenius fixed points. The affine, type-(S) nearby-cycle and arbitrary formal assertions have the distinct ranges given above.


<a id="layer-6-flat-cohomology-continuity"></a>

### 6.0 Animated flat cohomology and the multiplicative fracture square

Prove `Prismatic.FlatCohomology.pContinuity`: for a discrete ring B, a finite locally free commutative B-group G of p-power order, and an animated B-algebra T with p-henselian π₀T, RΓ_fppf(T,G)≃lim_n RΓ_fppf(T⊗^L_ZZ/p^n,G). Prove `Prismatic.FlatCohomology.excision`: if T→T′ induces an equivalence modulo a derived principal ideal (a), the square of flat cohomology of T,T′ and their localizations at a is cartesian. Its G_m consequence is a cartesian square after derived p-completion for T, its derived p-completion, and their p-inverted rings. Prove also `Prismatic.Gm.reductionCech`: for derived p-complete animated T, completed G_m cohomology is the totalization of its values on T⊗^L_Z F_p^(⊗(•+1)). ([CS](#ref-cs), Theorem 5.3.5, pp.59–61, Lemma 5.4.2, pp.63–66, arXiv v3; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Remark 7.2.8, p.171, Propositions 7.2.13, 7.2.15, pp.172–175.)

*Needs:* [§2.0](#layer-2-local-arc-foundations), [§2.26](#layer-2-finite-projective-modules-p-complete), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation`.

**Proof route.** Sheafify flat cohomology on animated rings and use a Bégueri smooth resolution to identify a square-zero deformation fibre with RHom_B(e*L_(G/B),M[1]); p-power order makes this invariant under derived p-completion, and Postnikov induction reduces continuity to discrete rings. On ind-fppf hypercovers with p-henselian terms and no nonsplit covers, smooth-resolution descent reduces continuity to G(T)=lim G(T/p^n); if p^c kills e*L, the obstruction to lifting modulo p^n to p^(2n) is detected modulo p^(n+c), making the image tower Mittag–Leffler and eliminating lim¹. Tensor the cartesian arithmetic square to obtain animated Beauville–Laszlo gluing for the finite locally free torsor algebra with its action, and apply Fujiwara–Gabber to its p-inverted henselization and completion.

For excision the same deformation triangle reduces Postnikov and nilpotent changes to the module arithmetic square. Separate the primary factors of G. Invert their residual characteristic for the étale part, where arc excision applies; henselize and use pContinuity for the other part. In characteristic p pass to perfect algebras and apply finite flat Dieudonné descent, then descend the semiperfect root cover. This proves the stated square without requiring ordinary T/(a) to equal its derived quotient. For the G_m consequence reduce modulo p^n by the fppf Kummer sequence; the coefficient μ_(p^n) has the finite-flat hypothesis, so the finite-level squares just proved apply. Taking the derived limit yields the completed G_m square.

For reductionCech, the partial totalization in degree n of the animated Čech ring is T⊗^L_Z Z/p^(n+1). In the normalized degree-n part of its units, positive homotopy is divisible by the product of the n degree-one exterior generators of F_p^(⊗(n+1)); hence that part is in degrees ≤−n. The partial totalization of G_m is consequently connective and agrees with G_m of the partial ring totalization. Étale sheafification commutes with the finite limits here. Apply pContinuity to μ_p, then p-complete, to pass to the full limit. The underlying animated units functor used in this argument is left Kan extended from *Laurent* polynomial algebras: free abelian groups represent units, and their simplicial resolutions give that extension. Polynomial algebras alone do not represent a freely chosen invertible element.

**Checks.** For T=Z_p and G=μ_(p^n), the unit and torsor groups are recovered from the p-adic tower, including the class −1 when p=2. For the zero ring every corner vanishes. For T=F_p⊕F_p[1], the deformation term is retained by the derived reductions; ordinary quotients would lose it. For T→T′ an identity the excision square has identity vertical arrows; for a a unit its horizontal arrows are identities. A Laurent generator may map to any unit, while a polynomial generator may map to a nonunit, distinguishing the two Kan extension domains.

<a id="layer-6-preadic-specialization"></a>

### 6.1 Pre-adic specialization and the perfectoid Spec/Spa comparison

Prove `Prismatic.GenericFiber.specialization`: for a bounded p-complete affine ring B, the generic pre-adic étale site has its specialization morphism to (Spf B)_ét, and for every torsion abelian group Λ the corresponding nearby-cycle sheaf is the étale sheafification of B′↦RΓ_ét(Spec B′[1/p],Λ) over completely étale formal charts B′. This statement uses the pre-adic site even when no sheafy analytic Huber presentation has been chosen. For a perfectoid Tate pair (T,T⁺), prove `Prismatic.GenericFiber.specSpa_lisse`: Spec T and Spa(T,T⁺) have equivalent finite étale categories and equivalent bounded derived lisse Z/p^n-categories, compatibly with cohomology and pullback. The integral model may contain p-torsion: replace it by its localization image before forming the Tate pair. ([Huber96](#ref-huber96), Corollary 3.2.2 and Theorem 3.2.9, pp.174, 180; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 9.1 and its proof, pp.71–73; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Example 3.5, p.10.)

*Needs:* [§1.0](#layer-1-bounded-formal-sites), `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `AdicEtaleGeometry:A1`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`, [PerfectoidSpaces P1.16–P1.18, P1.24–P1.25](#ps-integral).

For the pre-adic construction use the complete affinoid pair associated to B[1/p] and the integral closure of the image of B in its power-bounded elements. Rational charts, finite-presentation étale algebras and their completed rational base changes define the site; take the associated étale sheaves. Pullback of a formal étale chart is the corresponding generic étale chart and preserves finite limits and covering families. This gives the specialization morphism. Huber's Corollary 3.2.2 applies to a complete affinoid ring without a finite-type restriction. Its sheaf version, Theorem 3.2.9, identifies cohomology after restriction; applying it on each formal étale chart gives the asserted nearby-cycle description. Thus the type-(S) hypothesis of the narrower H1 input is not used here. The rational charts and site construction glue along formal open immersions.

For a perfectoid Tate pair the finite étale equivalence is the affinoid finite-étale theorem of P3. Huber's comparison first identifies constant finite-coefficient cohomology. Trivialize a finite local system by a finite étale cover and compare its Čech descent complexes; this gives comparison for finite local systems, and for their internal Hom local systems. Consequently all derived Hom groups between local systems agree. Postnikov induction gives full faithfulness on bounded lisse complexes and lifts their extension classes, hence essential surjectivity. This is the categorical argument needed for Example 3.5, rather than an inference from equality of degree-zero sections.

**Checks.** For B=O_C, both generic constant-coefficient complexes are Z/p^n in degree zero. For pB=0 the generic site is empty and nearby cycles vanish. For a nontrivial finite étale cover of a perfectoid field the equivalence retains the cover and its Galois descent, rather than replacing its local system by a constant one. The internal-Hom comparison retains extension classes in degree one. No noetherian or finite-type assumption is introduced in the pre-adic assertion.

<a id="layer-6-formal-generic-v-descent"></a>

### 6.2 Formal covers and lisse v-descent

For a bounded p-adic formal scheme X, use the generic diamond X_η obtained from the analytic locus of its pre-adic generic fibre. Its construction, local spatiality and compatibility with rational opens are imported from `DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/pre-adic-diamondification`, `D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond`, `D6/gluing-and-the-diamond-functor` and `D6/etale-site-comparison`; in an affine chart it is Spd(B[1/p],B^+), with B^+ the integral closure of the image of B. No sheafiness or finite-type hypothesis on B is added. Prove the following additional bridge.

- `FormalGeneric.qsyn_vCover`: A quasisyntomic formal cover Y→X induces a v-cover Y_η→X_η. Completed affine fibre products are carried to fibre products of generic diamonds.
- `FormalGeneric.lisse_descent`: The category D_lisse^{(b)}(X_η,Z_p) is the limit of the corresponding categories on the Čech nerve of this cover, and also the limit over affinoid perfectoid objects of X_{η,v}. Here objects are derived p-complete and locally bounded, with locally constant finite cohomology modulo p; the finite free heart gives Loc_{Z_p}.
- `FormalGeneric.qrsp_realization`: On the QRSP basis, the affine perfectoid Spec/Spa comparison of [§6.1](#layer-6-preadic-specialization), followed by this descent, gives the generic-fibre category used by the Laurent F-crystal comparison. All transition functors preserve Frobenius fixed points and reduction modulo p^n.

For the cover statement it suffices to consider a p-completely faithfully flat map B→B′ and a geometric point given by B→C^+, where C is an algebraically closed perfectoid field and C^+ an open bounded valuation subring. The completed base change T=B′⊗̂ᴸ_B C^+ is p-completely faithfully flat over C^+. It is discrete and p-torsion-free by complete flatness over the p-torsion-free base C^+; every nonzero a∈C^+ divides some p^m, so T is torsion-free, hence flat over this valuation ring. Its nonzero closed fibre makes it faithfully flat. Valuative lifting of this flat cover gives an extension of the valuation and a map T to the extended valuation ring. Retain the component where p is nonzero and its p-adic rank-one coarsening, complete and take an algebraic closure; the original valuation refines to an open bounded subring C′^+⊂C′. This yields the required lift after the perfectoid extension (C,C^+)→(C′,C′^+). The quasicompact criterion for affinoid v-covers then applies; families and formal charts follow by gluing. This argument only uses complete flatness after passage to a valuation ring, where p-torsion-freeness implies flatness. The counterexample of [§1.23](#layer-1-p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic) shows why this valuation argument cannot be replaced by a general-prism p-torsion assertion.

For lisse descent import `DiamondEtaleCohomology:C2/enhanced-v-derived-category`, `C2/v-hyperdescent` and `C2/etale-test-on-one-cover`, together with effective finite étale descent from `DiamondsAndVStacks:D3`. Finite local systems and their finite internal Hom objects descend by the finite-étale theorem. Their bounded extensions descend in the enhanced derived category. Étaleness is tested on a v-cover, and finite rank and bounded Tor amplitude are tested after a quasicompact strictly totally disconnected cover; thus the lisse subcategories are preserved by this descent. Pass from p^n to p-adically complete objects by the derived inverse limit, retaining the fixed local bound modulo p. Finally apply the affine Spec/Spa equivalence termwise to a QRSP cover and its completed Čech nerve. The limit comparison is independent of the cover by common refinements.

([ECD](#ref-ecd), Proposition 15.4 and Lemma 15.6, pp.90–91, for the imported geometric carrier; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Example 3.5 and Corollaries 3.7–3.8, pp.10–11, for the resulting comparison; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Lemma 4.7, p.19, for the complete-flat discreteness input over C^+.)

*Needs:* [§1.0](#layer-1-bounded-formal-sites), [§6.1](#layer-6-preadic-specialization), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D2`, the exact D6 and C2 targets above, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D3/etale-and-finite-etale-are-v-stacks`.

**Checks.**

- `FormalGeneric.root_cover`: Adjoining all p-power roots to a quasisyntomic affine chart produces a cover after generic diamondification, even though it is not a finite étale formal map.
- `FormalGeneric.special_fibre`: If pB=0, the generic diamond is empty; lisse generic objects and their descent category are zero.
- `FormalGeneric.valuation_lift`: Over C^+, faithful flatness of T is justified by divisibility by powers of p and its nonzero closed fibre. An arbitrary p-torsion-free base ring cannot be substituted for that valuation ring.
- `FormalGeneric.finite_etale_monodromy`: A nonconstant finite local system is descended with its Čech cocycle; comparing only constant sections would lose its monodromy.

<a id="layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points"></a>

### 6.3 Derived Frobenius fixed points of a φ-module

Let Λ be a commutative ring (Λ = F_p, Z/p^n or Z_p in this layer), B a commutative Λ-algebra and σ a Λ-linear ring endomorphism of B (the Frobenius when B is an F_p-algebra; φ_A when B = A/p^n for a prism (A, (d))). The ∞-category D(B[F]) has as objects the pairs (M, φ_M) with M ∈ D(B) and φ_M : M → σ_*M a map in D(B), that is, a σ-semilinear endomorphism of M; it is the lax equaliser of the identity and σ_* on D(B), and a morphism is a map f : M → N with a chosen homotopy φ_N f ≃ σ_*(f) φ_M. The derived Frobenius fixed points are M^{φ=1} := fib(φ_M − 1 : M → M) ∈ D(Λ), the fibre being formed after restriction of scalars to Λ. For t ∈ B such that σ(t) becomes a unit of B[1/t] (for example σ(t) = t^p, or σ(t) ≡ t^p modulo a nilpotent ideal), φ_M extends uniquely to a σ-semilinear endomorphism of M[1/t] = M ⊗^L_B B[1/t], and (M[1/t])^{φ=1} denotes its fixed points. For a Z_p-linear φ-module M one writes (M/p^n)^{φ=1} for the fixed points of M ⊗^L_Z Z/p^n. For every i there is a short exact sequence 0 → coker(φ_M − 1 on H^{i−1}(M)) → H^i(M^{φ=1}) → ker(φ_M − 1 on H^i(M)) → 0; in particular H^0(M^{φ=1}) is in general not the group of φ-fixed vectors of H^0(M), and H^1(M^{φ=1}) can be non-zero for M concentrated in degree 0.

Λ lies in the σ-fixed subring of B, so that φ_M − 1 is Λ-linear; it is not B-linear. The fibre is taken in D(Λ) (or D(Z)); M^{φ=1} carries no B-module structure. For (M[1/t])^{φ=1} the image of σ(t) in B[1/t] is a unit; this holds for B = A/p^n, t = d, since φ(d) ≡ d^p mod p. As a model in the pinned library a φ-module is a cochain complex of Λ-modules with an endomorphism, and the fibre is the shifted mapping cone of φ − 1.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 9.2 (statement: the ∞-category D(B[F]) and the functors M ↦ M^{φ=1}, M ↦ (M[1/t])^{φ=1}); p. 71; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Example 8.1.3; p. 190.)

*Needs:* Mathlib `CochainComplex.mappingCone`, Mathlib `DerivedCategory`, Mathlib `DerivedCategory.Q`, Mathlib `frobenius`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/stable-infinity-category`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Etale.FrobeniusModule`: A φ-module over Λ: a complex of Λ-modules with an endomorphism; the model of an object of D(B[F]) after restriction to Λ.
- `Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints`: M^{φ=1} = fib(φ_M − 1), as the shifted mapping cone of φ − 1, an object of D(Λ).
- `Prismatic.Etale.fixedPointsι`: The canonical map M^{φ=1} → M, whose composite with φ_M − 1 is zero.
- `Prismatic.Etale.fixedPointsMap`: A map of φ-modules induces a map of fixed points; quasi-isomorphisms induce isomorphisms.
- `Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints_isGE`: If M is concentrated in degrees ≥ a then so is M^{φ=1}; if M is in degrees ≤ b then M^{φ=1} is in degrees ≤ b + 1.
- `Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints_isZero_of_isIso`: M^{φ=1} = 0 if and only if φ_M − 1 is an isomorphism in D(Λ).
- `Prismatic.Etale.invert`: The φ-module M[1/t] for t with σ(t) = t^p·u, u a unit after inverting t: the colimit of M along multiplication by t with the induced endomorphism.
- `Prismatic.Etale.reduce`: The φ-module M/p^n = cone(p^n : M → M) and the transition maps M/p^n → M/p^{n−1}; (M/p^n)^{φ=1} ≃ M^{φ=1} ⊗^L Z/p^n.
- `Prismatic.Etale.fixedPointsTriangle`: Derived fixed points are the fibre of φ−1. The canonical sequence M^(φ=1)→M→^(φ−1)M→M^(φ=1)[1] is a distinguished triangle, functorial in Frobenius-equivariant maps.
- `Prismatic.Etale.fixedPoints_cohomology_exact`: For each i, 0→coker(φ−1:H^(i−1)(M)→H^(i−1)(M))→H^i(M^(φ=1))→ker(φ−1:H^i(M)→H^i(M))→0 is canonical. This gives the amplitude increase by at most one.

**Proof route.** Take fib(φ_M−1) in the enhanced category; its triangle gives the displayed kernel/cokernel exact sequences. Extend semilinearity to B[1/t] using invertibility of σ(t), or equivalently the indicated multiplication-by-t telescope when σ(t)=t^p. Fibres commute with limits and, in a stable category, with exact scalar extension and colimits; completed colimits require [§6.4](#layer-6-fixed-points-completed-colimits).

**Checks.**

- `pr4_fixed_points_fp_h1`: For Λ = F_p, M = F_p in degree 0, φ = id: H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≅ F_p (and H^0 ≅ F_p).
- `pr4_fixed_points_zero_map`: If φ_M = 0 then M^{φ=1} = 0.
- `pr4_fixed_points_identity`: If φ_M = id then M^{φ=1} ≅ M ⊕ M[−1]; in particular H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≅ H^1(M) ⊕ H^0(M).
- `pr4_fixed_points_not_fixed_vectors`: For M = F_p[x] in degree 0 with its Frobenius, H^1(M^{φ=1}) ≠ 0 although M is discrete: the class of x is not of the form f^p − f.

- M = F_p in degree 0 with φ = id: H^0(M^{φ=1}) = F_p and H^1(M^{φ=1}) = F_p. For M an algebraic closure of F_p with its Frobenius: M^{φ=1} = F_p in degree 0 (Artin–Schreier equations are solvable). For M = F_p[x] with its Frobenius: H^1(M^{φ=1}) = coker(F − 1) ≠ 0, the group H^1_ét(A^1_{F_p}, F_p). If φ_M is topologically nilpotent for a complete filtration of M then M^{φ=1} = 0.

<a id="layer-6-fixed-points-completed-colimits"></a>

### 6.4 Frobenius fixed points commute with completed colimits

Let B be an F_p-algebra with an element t ∈ B, with its Frobenius σ, and let D_comp(B[F]) ⊂ D(B[F]) be the full subcategory of pairs (M, φ_M) with M derived t-complete. Then the functors D_comp(B[F]) → D(F_p), M ↦ M^{φ=1} and M ↦ (M[1/t])^{φ=1}, commute with colimits. Explicitly, for a diagram (M_i, φ_i) in D_comp(B[F]) with colimit colim M_i in D(B) and derived t-completion (colim M_i)^∧ (the colimit in D_comp(B[F])), the maps colim (M_i)^{φ=1} → ((colim M_i)^∧)^{φ=1} and colim (M_i[1/t])^{φ=1} → ((colim M_i)^∧[1/t])^{φ=1} are isomorphisms. The proof shows N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1} for every N ∈ D_comp(B[F]).

B is an F_p-algebra and φ_M is semilinear over the Frobenius of B, so φ(t) = t^p. t is an arbitrary element; derived t-completeness is required of every M_i and the target colimit is the completed one. The colimits are indexed by arbitrary small diagrams.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 9.2 and its proof; p. 71.)

*Needs:* [§6.3](#layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract/stable-infinity-category`.

**Proof route.** For a derived t-complete N, Frobenius contracts the complete fibre of N→N/t because φ(t)=t^p, so N^(φ=1)≃(N/t)^(φ=1). Reduction modulo t and the finite fixed-point fibre both preserve colimits, proving the first comparison. The fibre of an ordinary colimit→its completion is uniquely t-divisible, so its localization is itself and its vanishing fixed points give the localized comparison as well.

**Checks.**

- B = F_p[t] and the completed direct sum of copies of F_p[[t]] indexed by a set J: the fixed points are the direct sum over J of F_p ⊕ F_p[−1]. For a derived p-complete simplicial algebra S over a perfectoid ring: (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p)^{φ=1} ≃ (Δ_{S/A,perf}[1/d]/p)^{φ=1}, the step used in Theorem 9.1. Without derived t-completeness of the terms the statement N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1} fails: N = B[1/t] has N/t = 0.

<a id="layer-6-perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt"></a>

### 6.5 The étale comparison for perfectoid rings (Artin–Schreier–Witt and tilting)

Let S be a perfectoid ring, (A_inf(S), (d)) its perfect prism and S^♭ its tilt; write d also for the image of d in S^♭ = A_inf(S)/p. For every perfect prism (A, (d)) with a map A/d → S one has Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), so Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n = W_n(S^♭[1/d]). For n ≥ 1: (1) (Artin–Schreier–Witt) RΓ_ét(Spec(S^♭[1/d]), Z/p^n) ≃ fib(F − 1 : W_n(S^♭[1/d]) → W_n(S^♭[1/d])) = (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}; (2) (tilting) there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec(S^♭[1/d]), Z/p^n). Hence RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}, naturally in the perfectoid ring S.

S is a perfectoid ring in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (integral perfectoid; p-torsion and characteristic p are allowed). If p = 0 in S both sides vanish: S[1/p] = 0 and d maps to 0 in S^♭. Étale cohomology is that of the schemes Spec(S[1/p]) and Spec(S^♭[1/d]), not of adic spectra; the adic spectra enter only through Huber's comparison.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Proof of Theorem 9.1, "first approach"; pp. 72–73.)

*Needs:* [§6.3](#layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.21](#layer-0-ainf-prism), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [PerfectoidSpaces P1.16–P1.18, P1.24–P1.25](#ps-integral), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`, Mathlib `WittVector`, Mathlib `TruncatedWittVector`, Mathlib `WittVector.frobenius`.

**Proof route.** The perfectoid initial prism is A_inf(S), whose truncation and localization give W_n(S^♭[1/d]). The Artin–Schreier–Witt sequence is étale-exact, and induction on Witt length gives affine acyclicity from that of quasi-coherent sheaves. This identifies the fixed-point complex with étale cohomology, and tilting gives the indicated analytic comparison.

For (2) use the torsion-removal and decomposition theorem [PerfectoidQuotients §0.4](#pq-consequences), before applying tilting. Choose a compatible-root pseudouniformizer ϖ with (ϖ^p)=(p), allowing ϖ=0 on a characteristic-p component, and put S_tf=S/S[ϖ^∞]. This is the ordinarily complete torsion-free perfectoid quotient; the decomposition in that supplier shows S[1/p]≅S_tf[1/p] and S^♭[1/d]≅S_tf^♭[1/d]. Indeed both characteristic-p pieces of the decomposition disappear upon these localizations, and on the remaining tilt d is a unit multiple of (ϖ^♭)^p. Thus the two localized rings are the ordinary generic rings of a torsion-free perfectoid pair. Apply [§6.1](#layer-6-preadic-specialization) and P3's regular perfectoid tilting theorem to that pair. Every quotient and comparison is canonical after localization, so the result is independent of the auxiliary pseudouniformizer and is natural in S. At pS=0 both localizations are zero. The unrestricted principal-element statements used in [§6.3](#layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points)–[§6.4](#layer-6-fixed-points-completed-colimits) are algebraic fixed-point lemmas and do not require an extension of P3's geometric regular-localization theorem.

**Checks.**

- S = O_C, C complete algebraically closed: both sides are Z/p^n in degree 0 (W_n(C^♭)^{F=1} = Z/p^n and F − 1 is surjective). S a perfect F_p-algebra: both sides are 0. S = Z_p^cycl (the p-completion of Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]): H^1 of the right-hand side is coker(F − 1) on W_n of the tilt of the cyclotomic field, the group Hom_cont(Gal, Z/p^n).

<a id="layer-6-etale-comparison"></a>

### 6.6 The étale comparison theorem for arbitrary p-adic formal schemes

Let R be a perfectoid ring, (A, (d)) the perfect prism with A/d = R, and X an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme over R. Let Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, A) be the derived prismatic cohomology of X relative to A (Layer 2; the étale sheafification of S ↦ Δ_{S/A} on affine opens Spf S), with its Frobenius. For every n ≥ 0 the formal étale sheafification of Spf S↦RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]),Z/p^n) is canonically (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. In particular, for X = Spf S affine, RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. If X is bounded, let X_η be its pre-adic generic fibre and μ : X_{η,ét} → X_ét its specialization map of [§6.1](#layer-6-preadic-specialization). Then the sheafification is Rμ_*Z/p^n, giving the nearby-cycle formulation. The fixed points are the derived ones of [§6.3](#layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points). The identification is natural in X and in (R, A), and for X = Spf S with S perfectoid it is the isomorphism of [§6.5](#layer-6-perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt).

R is perfectoid and (A, (d)) is its perfect prism; a generator d of the prism ideal is fixed (it exists, the prism being perfect). X is any p-adic formal scheme over Spf R: no smoothness, no finite-type, flatness or regularity hypothesis, and no restriction on singularities; this corrects the layer text, which restricted the comparison to smooth formal schemes. Δ_{X/A} is the derived (animated) prismatic cohomology of Layer 2, not the cohomology of the prismatic site of a singular X. (−)[1/d] and /p^n are applied before taking fixed points; no completion is applied after inverting d. The affine Spec comparison and its formal étale sheafification hold for arbitrary X. The geometric Rμ_* formulation here uses the bounded hypothesis of [§6.1](#layer-6-preadic-specialization); no additional extension of its specialization-site theorem is assumed. Smooth formal schemes over R satisfy this boundedness condition. The type-(S) case also follows from H1:formal-adic-comparison.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 9.1 and its proof; p. 71; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Section 9, first sentence; p.71.)

*Needs:* [§6.1](#layer-6-preadic-specialization), [§6.3](#layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points), [§6.4](#layer-6-fixed-points-completed-colimits), [§6.5](#layer-6-perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt), [§2.1](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-cohomology), [§2.20](#layer-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology), [§1.9](#layer-1-frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison`.

**Proof route.** The generic-fibre functor is an arc_p sheaf locally concentrated in degree zero, so its degree-zero comparison gives a map to arc_p cohomology. Completed-colimit fixed-point compatibility identifies the prismatic functor with its perfection, making it an arc sheaf, and its vanishing on characteristic-p factors upgrades it to an arc_p sheaf; the unit then constructs the comparison, an equivalence on perfectoid valuation covers by [§6.5](#layer-6-perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt). Sheafify on the formal étale site and use [§6.1](#layer-6-preadic-specialization)’s bounded Spec/Spa comparison to identify it with Rμ_*.

**Checks.**

- X = Spf O_C: both sides are Z/p^n. X = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ (formal torus): after a choice of ε, H^1 of both sides is the group of units of C⟨T^{±1}⟩ modulo p^n-th powers (Kummer theory; C⟨T^{±1}⟩ is a principal ideal domain); it contains the class of T, of order p^n, and is not finitely generated. For the wild unit classes choose coefficients a_j with distinct valuations 0<v(a_j)<v(p). For a nonempty finite product f=∏(1+a_jT)^{e_j}, with e_j∈{0,…,p−1}, the logarithmic derivative f′/f=∑e_j a_j/(1+a_jT) has Gauss norm |a_j|>|p| for the unique nonzero term of least valuation. If f=g^p for an analytic unit g, then ‖g‖=1 and its reduction satisfies ḡ^p=1, hence ḡ=1. Consequently ‖g′/g‖<1, while f′/f=p g′/g would have norm strictly less than |p|, a contradiction. Thus these Kummer classes are F_p-linearly independent at level p. By comparison, units 1+aT with v(a)>p·v(p)/(p−1) have a convergent binomial p-th root. A singular input, S = O_C⟨x, y⟩/(xy): the statement holds with the derived Δ_{S/A}; no smoothness is used. X of characteristic p: both sides vanish. For S perfectoid the map is the Artin–Schreier–Witt/tilting isomorphism.

<a id="layer-6-etale-comparison-coefficients"></a>

### 6.7 Coefficient compatibility and passage to Z_p in the étale comparison

In the bounded geometric situation of [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison) write c_n : Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. (1) For n ≥ 1 the square formed by c_n, c_{n−1}, the map Rμ_* Z/p^n → Rμ_* Z/p^{n−1} induced by reduction and the map of fixed points induced by Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n → Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^{n−1} commutes; likewise for the maps induced by multiplication p : Z/p^{n−1} → Z/p^n, and c_n ⊗^L_{Z/p^n} Z/p^{n−1} = c_{n−1}. (2) The c_n are maps of commutative algebra objects of D(X_ét, Z/p^n). (3) Passing to derived limits, Rμ_* Z_p := R lim_n Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ ((Δ_{X/A}[1/d])^∧_p)^{φ=1}, where (−)^∧_p is derived p-completion; for X = Spf S, R lim_n RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ ((Δ_{S/A}[1/d])^∧_p)^{φ=1}. The limit is the derived limit of complexes; its cohomology sits in Milnor sequences with lim and lim^1 of the groups H^i(−, Z/p^n).

For the Rμ_* notation, R is perfectoid and X is a bounded p-adic formal scheme over R. The affine Spec assertions and their formal étale sheafifications retain the arbitrary-ring range of [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison). Z_p-coefficients on the generic fibre mean the derived limit of the Z/p^n-cohomology (equivalently pro-étale cohomology of the constant sheaf lim Z/p^n); they are not étale cohomology of a constant sheaf Z_p. The p-completion in (3) is applied after inverting d; (Δ_{X/A}[1/d])^∧_p is in general not Δ_{X/A}[1/d].

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 9.1 (the identification is canonical, for each n ≥ 0) and proof of Theorem 9.4 (the sheaves G_n with Z_p-coefficients); pp. 71, 73; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Section 8.1, first paragraph; pp.189–190.)

*Needs:* [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison), [§6.3](#layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Proof route.** Uniqueness of the unit-preserving arc_p comparison makes it natural in the coefficient ring and multiplicative. Derived reduction is exact and fixed points are a fibre, giving the coefficient squares. Limits commute with that fibre and with Rμ_*, so the p-adic limit is the fixed points of derived p-completion; pro-étale repleteness gives the nearby-cycle identification.

**Checks.**

- X = Spf O_C: Z_p ≃ (W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, and the square for n → n − 1 is reduction Z/p^n → Z/p^{n−1}. Finite level: for the formal torus the Kummer class of T at level n maps to the Kummer class of T at level n − 1 on both sides. For S = Z_p^cycl the lim^1 term vanishes and H^1 = Hom_cont(Gal, Z_p).

<a id="layer-6-etale-comparison-smooth"></a>

### 6.8 The étale comparison for smooth formal schemes (Theorem 1.8(4))

Let (A, I) be a perfect prism and X a quasi-compact quasi-separated smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, with generic fibre X_η over Q_p as a (pre-)adic space and RΓ_Δ(X/A) = RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) the cohomology of the prismatic site (Layer 1). Then for every n ≥ 0 there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_ét(X_η, Z/p^n) ≅ (RΓ_Δ(X/A)/p^n[1/I])^{φ=1} of commutative algebras in D(Z/p^n). It is the corollary of [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison) obtained by taking RΓ(X_ét, −) and using that for smooth X the derived prismatic cohomology agrees with site cohomology.

(A, I) is a perfect prism, so I = (d) is principal and A/I is perfectoid; perfectness is part of the hypothesis of Theorem 1.8(4). X is smooth over A/I; smoothness is needed only to identify the derived Δ_{X/A} with the site-theoretic RΓ_Δ(X/A), not for the comparison itself. X is qcqs for the global statement, so that inverting d and reducing modulo p^n commute with RΓ(X_ét, −).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 1.8 (4); p. 4.)

*Needs:* [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison), [§6.7](#layer-6-etale-comparison-coefficients), [§2.11](#layer-2-derived-agrees-with-site), [§1.4](#layer-1-relative-prismatic-cohomology), `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison`.

**Proof route.** Apply enhanced global sections to the sheaf comparison of [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison). Smooth site comparison identifies its prismatic term, and fibres and finite scalar reduction commute with sections, as does localization under the stated qcqs hypothesis. The algebra comparison of [§6.7](#layer-6-etale-comparison-coefficients) gives multiplicativity.

**Checks.**

- X = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ over (A_inf, ker θ): H^1_ét(X_η, μ_{p^n}) is the group of units of C⟨T^{±1}⟩ modulo p^n-th powers, and the class of T corresponds to a φ-fixed class in H^1 of RΓ_Δ(X/A_inf)/p^n[1/d]. X proper smooth over O_C: with [§1.22](#layer-1-proper-smooth-perfectness), RΓ_ét(X_C, Z/p^n) is the fixed points of φ on a perfect complex over A_inf/p^n[1/d] = W_n(C^♭). The statement for singular X is [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison), not this target.

<a id="layer-6-perfectoid-etale-cohomological-dimension"></a>

### 6.9 Étale cohomological dimension of the generic fibre of a perfectoid ring

Let R be a perfectoid ring corresponding to a perfect prism (A, I). The F_p-étale cohomological dimension of the scheme X = Spec(R[1/p]) is ≤ 1: for every étale sheaf F of F_p-modules on X one has H^i(X, F) = 0 for i > 1.

X is the spectrum, not the adic spectrum, of R[1/p]; the statement is false for general sheaves on the adic spectrum. F is an arbitrary étale F_p-sheaf on the scheme X (a filtered colimit of Zariski-constructible sheaves). The bound concerns F_p-coefficients (hence p-power torsion sheaves by dévissage); nothing is claimed for ℓ ≠ p.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 11.1 and its proof; p. 85.)

*Needs:* [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison), [§6.3](#layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points), [§2.20](#layer-2-perfection-of-prismatic-cohomology), [§2.25](#layer-2-connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid), `PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.5`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Proof route.** Constructible dévissage and the prime-to-p trace reduction reduce to j_!F_p on a finite extension with a finitely generated boundary ideal. By étale comparison its cohomology is the fixed points of the localized mod-p fibre of the two perfected prismatic complexes, so it suffices for that fibre to be connective. Integral perfectoidization is discrete, and the supplied semiperfectoid quotient-surjectivity theorem makes the quotient perfectoidization map surjective, giving the bound after fixed points raise amplitude by at most one.

**Checks.**

- R = O_C: X = Spec C has cohomological dimension 0 ≤ 1. R = Z_p^cycl: X is the spectrum of the completed cyclotomic field, whose absolute Galois group has p-cohomological dimension ≤ 1; H^1_ét(X, F_p) = Hom_cont(Gal, F_p) is non-zero, so the bound 1 is attained. R a perfect F_p-algebra: X is empty and the statement is vacuous.

### 6.10 Syntomic complexes Z_p(n) on quasisyntomic rings

Let S be a quasisyntomic ring (p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{S/Z_p} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]) and n an integer. Let Δ̂_S{n} be the Nygaard-completed prismatic cohomology of S with its n-th Breuil–Kisin twist, with Nygaard filtration N^{≥•}Δ̂_S{n}, obtained by quasisyntomic descent from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings (Layer 3). Let can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} be the canonical map and φ_n : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} the divided Frobenius; when S is an algebra over a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) and the twist is trivialised, for n ≥ 0, φ_n is the restriction of φ/d^n to N^{≥n}Δ̂_S = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^n Δ̂_S}. For n < 0 the filtration term is the entire twisted complex and the Frobenius is multiplied by d^{−n}; no negative ideal power is used. The n-th syntomic complex is Z_p(n)(S) := fib(φ_n − can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n}) ∈ D(Z_p), a derived p-complete complex, and Z/p^r(n)(S) := Z_p(n)(S) ⊗^L_Z Z/p^r. The functor S ↦ Z_p(n)(S) is a sheaf of complexes on the quasisyntomic site. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} and Δ̂_S{n} are discrete, Z_p(n)(S) is the two-term complex N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} in degrees 0 and 1, H^0 = {x ∈ N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} : φ_n(x) = x} and H^1 = coker(φ_n − can). For a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, I), choose a generator e of A{1} and let d be the generator of I with φ_{A{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e (for a Z_p^cycl-algebra: d = [p]_q with e = e_A; in characteristic p: d = p). For n ≥ 0, Z_p(n)(R) ≃ (φ^{−1}(d)^n A → A) with differential φ/d^n − 1. Another choice e' = ve replaces d by d·v/φ(v) and the complexes are identified by multiplication by v^n. For a generator d' = ud not of this form the two-term complex is in general not quasi-isomorphic to Z_p(n)(R) (R = Z_p^cycl, d' = u[p]_q with u ∈ Z_p^×, u^n ≢ 1 mod p: H^0 = 0 instead of Z_p).

S is quasisyntomic; the construction is functorial for all maps of quasisyntomic rings and satisfies quasisyntomic descent. The complex is defined by the formula of BMS2 §7.4 and Theorem 1.12(5) as a fibre of prismatic data; it is not defined as a graded piece of TC (that identification belongs to Layer 7, graded prismatic Beilinson square). In weight i the trace comparison involves gr^iTC. Sign convention: BMS2 writes hofib(φ − can), Bhatt–Scholze write fib(1 − φ_n); the two fibres are canonically isomorphic. The divided Frobenius is a map between different objects (source N^{≥n}, target the whole twisted complex), so Z_p(n) is not an instance of fixed points of an endomorphism for n ≥ 1.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Section 7.4, first display; Theorem 1.12(5) and Remark 1.14; pp. 6, 7; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Section 14, first display, and formula (9.3) in Section 9; p.97; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Example 7.4.3; p. 178.)

*Needs:* [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp), [§3.4](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration), [§3.20](#layer-3-nygaard-completion), [§3.10](#layer-3-divided-frobenius), [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§2.15](#layer-2-quasisyntomic-descent), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, Mathlib `CochainComplex.mappingCone`, Mathlib `DerivedCategory.Q`, Mathlib `PadicInt`.

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Syntomic.NygaardDatum`: The imported data of a ring in weight n: complexes N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} and Δ̂_S{n} of Z_p-modules with the canonical map and the divided Frobenius φ_n (owners Layer 3).
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicComplex`: Z_p(n)(S) = fib(φ_n − can) as an object of D(Z_p).
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicComplexMod`: Z/p^r(n)(S) = Z_p(n)(S) ⊗^L Z/p^r, the cone of p^r.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicToFil`: The canonical map Z_p(n)(S) → N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} of the defining fibre sequence.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicMap`: A map of data compatible with can and φ_n induces a map of syntomic complexes; quasi-isomorphisms of data induce isomorphisms.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicComplex_isGE`: If both complexes of the datum are concentrated in degrees ≥ 0 then Z_p(n)(S) ∈ D^{≥0}.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicComplex_isLE`: If both complexes are discrete (S quasiregular semiperfectoid) then Z_p(n)(S) ∈ D^{≤1}.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.perfectoidDatum`: For n ≥ 0 and a perfect prism (A, (d)): the datum with terms φ^{−1}(d)^n A and A, canonical inclusion and φ/d^n.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.syntomicCup`: Natural pairings Z_p(m)⊗̂^L_ZpZ_p(n)→Z_p(m+n), for all integer weights, and a unit Z_p→Z_p(0) make the direct sum a graded commutative algebra. The pairings are induced by filtered prismatic multiplication and multiplicative divided Frobenius; they respect restriction, base change and the canonical comparison maps.

**Proof route.** On QRSP rings form the fibre of divided Frobenius minus the canonical map using the completed Nygaard filtration and intrinsic twist. Both terms are qsyn sheaves and p-complete, so unfold their fibre to all qsyn rings and reduce derivedly for finite coefficients. For a perfectoid ring the ideal formula gives the explicit two-term complex, and changing a twist basis by v changes d by dv/φ(v), with multiplication by v^n identifying the formulas.

**Checks.**

- `pr4_syntomic_zero_weight_fp`: For the datum Z_p → Z_p with can = φ_0 = id (the ring F_p in weight 0): H^1(Z_p(0)(F_p)) ≅ Z_p.
- `pr4_syntomic_equal_maps`: If φ_n = can then Z_p(n) ≅ fib(0), with H^0 ≅ H^0(N^{≥n}) and H^1 ⊇ H^0(Δ̂{n}).
- `pr4_syntomic_contracting`: If can is an isomorphism and φ_n − can is an isomorphism then Z_p(n) = 0 (the mechanism of the vanishing for n < 0 and of Lemma 7.22).
- `pr4_syntomic_not_fixed_points`: For the perfectoid datum with n = 1 the source φ^{−1}(d)A is a proper submodule of A when d is not a unit: Z_p(1)(R) is not fib(φ/d − 1) on A[1/d], nor fixed points of an endomorphism of A.

- R perfectoid with perfect prism (A, (d)) and n ≥ 0: Z_p(n)(R) is the two-term complex φ^{−1}(d)^n A → A, x ↦ φ(x)/d^n − x. Z_p(0)(F_p) = fib(0 : Z_p → Z_p) has H^0 = Z_p and H^1 = Z_p. Z_p(n)(S) = 0 for n < 0 and Z_p(1) is the Tate module of G_m locally ([§6.26](#layer-6-syntomic-low-weights)). For S a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra: for n ≥ 0, H^0(Z_p(n)(S)) = A_crys(S)^{φ=p^n} ([§6.17](#layer-6-syntomic-complex-char-p)).

<a id="layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes"></a>

### 6.11 Syntomic cohomology of animated rings and bounded p-adic formal schemes

For an animated commutative ring R and an integer n let Δ_R{n} be the absolute prismatic complex with Breuil–Kisin twist and Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} its absolute Nygaard filtration (Layer 4), with ι : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} the canonical map and φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} the Frobenius. Define RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) := fib(φ{n} − ι) in the p-complete derived ∞-category D̂(Z_p). Then: (a) R → R^∧_p induces an isomorphism on RΓ_syn(Spf −, Z_p(n)); (b) the map to the Nygaard-completed version fib(φ̂{n} − ι̂ : Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n} → Δ̂_R{n}) is an isomorphism (Proposition 7.4.6); so for R quasisyntomic RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = Z_p(n)(R) of [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex); (c) R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) satisfies p-complete fpqc descent (7.4.7); (d) it commutes with sifted colimits, hence is left Kan extended from finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras (7.4.8); (e) RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → Tot RΓ_syn(Spf(R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}), Z_p(n)) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 0 (7.4.10) and RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) ≃ lim_m RΓ_syn(Spf(R ⊗^L Z/p^m), Z_p(n)) (7.4.11). For a bounded p-adic formal scheme 𝔛, RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) := lim over maps Spec(A) → 𝔛 of RΓ_syn(Spf A, Z_p(n)); it agrees with the affine definition on Spf R, satisfies étale descent, and sits in the fibre sequence RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) → Fil^n_N RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} with second map φ{n} − ι.

R is any animated commutative ring; p-completeness is not assumed, and is harmless by (a). The construction uses the absolute prismatic cohomology and absolute Nygaard filtration of Layer 4 and the twists of Layer 3; Layer 6 owns only the fibre. 𝔛 is a bounded p-adic formal scheme: locally Spf R with R p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion. n is any integer; the complex vanishes for n < 0 ([§6.26](#layer-6-syntomic-low-weights)).

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Section 7.4, opening sentence; Construction 7.4.1, Warning 7.4.2, Propositions 7.4.6–7.4.8 and 7.4.10, Corollary 7.4.11; pp. 177, 178, 179, 180, 181; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Variant 7.4.12; p. 181.)

<a id="layer-6-prismatic-logarithm"></a>

### 6.12 The prismatic logarithm

Let (A, I) be a prism with Breuil–Kisin twist A{1} (Layer 3) and (1 + I)_{rk=1} := {u ∈ 1 + I : δ(u) = 0} the group of rank-one units congruent to 1 modulo I. If (A, I) is transversal, A{1} = lim_r I_r/I_r^2 with I_r = I φ^*(I) ⋯ (φ^{r−1})^*(I) and transition maps division by p, and for u ∈ (1 + I)_{rk=1} the element log_Δ(u) ∈ A{1} is the unique element with image u^{p^r} − 1 in I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}^2 for all r ≥ 0. For a general prism log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1} is the unique function compatible with every map of prisms (B, J) → (A, I) from a transversal prism. It is a group homomorphism, natural in the prism, satisfies φ_{A{1}}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(u), and log_Δ(u) ≡ (u − 1 mod I^2) under A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I^2. For Ā = A/I the Tate module T_p(Ā^×) = lim (μ_{p^k}(Ā), x ↦ x^p) maps to (1 + I)_{rk=1} by ρ_0 (lift x ∈ Ā^{♭×} uniquely to A^{♭×} and apply ♯), and the composite log_Δ : T_p(Ā^×) → A{1} is also called the prismatic logarithm. For the q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q − 1]], ([p]_q)) there is a unique generator e_A of A{1} with (q − 1) e_A = log_Δ(q^p). For a crystalline prism (A, (p)) and u with φ(u) = u^p, u^p ≡ 1 mod p: log_Δ(u^p) = log(u) e_A with log(u) = Σ_{n>0} (−1)^{n−1}(u − 1)^n/n.

(A, I) is a prism; for the Tate-module form A/I is its reduction. Transversal means A/I is p-torsion-free (so (p, I) is regular locally). Rank one means δ(u) = 0, equivalently φ(u) = u^p when A is p-torsion-free. The construction is algebraic; no K-theory or cyclotomic trace enters (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 9.5 describes the earlier trace-theoretic construction of the comparison for Z_p(1), which this replaces). The twist A{1} is constructed in Layer 3; use the logarithm here to construct the Tate comparison.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 2.3.1, Construction 2.3.2, Proposition 2.3.3 (transversal case); Propositions 2.5.10, 2.5.16, 2.5.18, 2.5.19 and Remark 2.5.17 (general prisms); pp. 24, 25, 29, 30, 31; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Notation 2.7.1, Propositions 2.7.2–2.7.3, Construction 2.7.4; Proposition 2.6.1, Corollary 2.6.12; pp. 31, 33, 34, 35; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 9.5; p. 75.)

*Needs:* [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.19](#layer-0-prism-category), [§0.29](#layer-0-transversal-prism-regular-sequences), [§0.23](#layer-0-q-de-rham-prism), [§0.20](#layer-0-crystalline-prism), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), Mathlib `rootsOfUnity`, Mathlib `Units`, [§3.7](#layer-3-transversal-approximation), [§3.8](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist-transversal), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§0.15](#layer-0-free-delta-pd-envelope).

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.Syntomic.rankOneUnits`: The subgroup (1 + I)_{rk=1} of A^× of units u ≡ 1 mod I with δ(u) = 0.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog`: The group homomorphism log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1}.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_frobenius`: φ_{A{1}}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(u).
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_map`: For a map of prisms f : (B, J) → (A, I): f{1}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(f(u)).
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.prismaticLog_mod`: log_Δ(u) reduces to the class of u − 1 under A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I^2.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.tateModule`: T_p(R^×) = lim (μ_{p^k}(R), x ↦ x^p), the kernel of ♯ : R^{♭×} → R^×.
- `Prismatic.Syntomic.tateLog`: The composite T_p((A/I)^×) → (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1}.

**Proof route.** For transversal prisms the classes of u^(p^r)−1 lie in I_(r+1), division by p makes them compatible modulo squares, and the product error lies in I_(r+1)², giving additivity. Transversal approximation with rank-one lifts descends this construction and its Frobenius/normalization formulas, while p-complete successive ideal quotients identify the inverse-limit unit groups for the Tate-module map. In the crystalline case φ(u−1)∈pA gives (u−1)^p/p!∈A and hence all divided powers, so the logarithm converges in the completed PD ideal and exp(p^m log u)≡1+p^m log u modulo p^(2m), proving log_Δ(u^p)=log(u)e_A (BL Corollary 2.6.12).

**Checks.**

- `pr4_prismatic_log_one`: log_Δ(1) = 0.
- `pr4_prismatic_log_q_de_rham`: In the q-de Rham prism, log_Δ(q^p) = (q − 1) e_A for a generator e_A of A{1}; in particular log_Δ(q^p) ≠ 0.
- `pr4_prismatic_log_mul`: log_Δ(u v) = log_Δ(u) + log_Δ(v) and log_Δ(u^p) = p log_Δ(u).
- `pr4_prismatic_log_not_all_units`: In the q-de Rham prism the unit 1 + [p]_q lies in 1 + I but has δ ≠ 0, so it is not a rank-one unit and lies outside the domain of log_Δ.

- Q-de Rham prism: log_Δ(q^p) = (q − 1) e_A with e_A a generator of A{1}. Perfected q-de Rham prism: for ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) ∈ T_p((A/I)^×), ρ_0(ε) = q^p and log_Δ(ε) = (q − 1) e_A. log_Δ(1) = 0 and log_Δ(uv) = log_Δ(u) + log_Δ(v). log_Δ is not defined on units of rank ≠ 1: for u ∈ 1 + I with δ(u) ≠ 0 the classes u^{p^r} − 1 need not lie in I_{r+1}.

<a id="layer-6-divided-frobenius-contraction"></a>

### 6.13 The divided Frobenius contracts deep Nygaard levels modulo p

Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 and A a p-torsion-free quasisyntomic O_C-algebra; fix i ≥ 0. For every integer m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), both φ_i and the canonical map preserve N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p functorially in A, and φ_i − 1 : N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p → N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p is an equivalence; more precisely φ_i maps N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p into N^{≥m+1}Δ̂_A{i}/p. Consequently Z/p(i)(A) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : (N^{≥i}Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p) → (Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p)), and, for quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebras S, Z_p(i)(S) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ_S) computed without Nygaard completion and without twists.

C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0; over O_C the Breuil–Kisin twists are trivialised. A is p-torsion-free and quasisyntomic over O_C; by left Kan extension and Nygaard completion the endomorphism φ_i of N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p and the equivalence extend to every quasisyntomic O_C-algebra. m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), which is the condition p(m − i) ≥ m + 1.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Lemma 7.22 and its proof; p. 52; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Proof of Theorem 14.1, first paragraph; p. 97.)

*Needs:* [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp), [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces), [§3.20](#layer-3-nygaard-completion), [§3.10](#layer-3-divided-frobenius), [§2.15](#layer-2-quasisyntomic-descent), [PerfectoidQuotients §§0.1–0.6](#pq-consequences).

**Proof route.** On torsion-free QRSP charts, φ_i(N^m)/p lies in ξ^(p(m−i)) and hence in N^(p(m−i))/p, so the stated numerical inequality makes φ_i contract the complete filtration. Its geometric-series inverse makes φ_i−1 invertible there, reducing its fibre to finite Nygaard quotients. For uncompleted complexes, the divided-Frobenius factorization makes the two completion cofibres equal, with Frobenius zero and canonical map the identity, so the fibres agree on every QRSP ring.

**Checks.**

- I = 0: every m ≥ 1 works when p ≥ 2, and φ maps N^{≥m}/p into N^{≥pm}/p. i = 1, p = 2: m ≥ 3; i = 1, p odd: m ≥ 2. A = O_C, i = 1: N^{≥m}A_inf/p = ξ^m O_C^♭ and φ_1(ξ^m x) = ξ^{p(m−1)} x^p, which lies in ξ^{m+1}O_C^♭ exactly when p(m − 1) ≥ m + 1.

<a id="layer-6-syntomic-filtered-colimits"></a>

### 6.14 Z/p^r(i) commutes with filtered colimits

For all i ≥ 0 and r ≥ 1 the sheaf Z/p^r(i) = Z_p(i)/p^r commutes with filtered colimits in the category QSyn of quasisyntomic rings: for a filtered diagram (A_j) of quasisyntomic rings whose p-completed colimit A is quasisyntomic, colim_j Z/p^r(i)(A_j) → Z/p^r(i)(A) is an isomorphism.

Colimits of rings are p-completed colimits; the statement is about the reduction modulo p^r, not about Z_p(i) itself. The proof is the direct proof of BMS2 through Lemma 7.22; the first printed proof, through K-theory and the theorem of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow, is not used (no trace input may enter Layer 6). i ≥ 0; for i < 0 both sides vanish.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Proposition 7.21, direct proof; p. 52; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 7.4.8; p. 179.)

*Needs:* [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§6.13](#layer-6-divided-frobenius-contraction), [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces), [§2.15](#layer-2-quasisyntomic-descent), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Proof route.** Induct on coefficient length to reduce to mod p, and use the functorial cyclotomic qsyn cover to work over O_C. Deep contraction reduces the torsion-free calculation to finite extensions of Nygaard graded pieces, whose cotangent exterior-power formulas preserve filtered colimits. Polynomial extension and completion supply the same contraction for arbitrary qsyn rings, while BL Proposition 7.4.8 gives the animated statement.

**Checks.**

- O_C = colim of the rings of integers of finite extensions, p-completed: Z/p^r(i)(O_C) is the colimit of the complexes of the p-completed finite levels. A filtered colimit of perfectoid rings: Z/p^r(i) of the p-completed colimit is the colimit, as used in the proof of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4. The statement fails for Z_p(i) without reduction: Z_p(0) of a filtered colimit is p-complete, the colimit of Z_p(0) need not be.
