### 6.15 Logarithmic forms as fixed points of the divided Frobenius on the de Rham–Witt complex

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and X a smooth k-scheme, with de Rham–Witt complex WΩ^•_X and Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X ⊂ WΩ^•_X, the subcomplex p^{i−1}VW(O_X) → p^{i−2}VWΩ^1_X → ⋯ → VWΩ^{i−1}_X → WΩ^i_X → WΩ^{i+1}_X → ⋯, on which the Frobenius φ is uniquely divisible by p^i; write φ_i = φ/p^i : N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X. Let W_rΩ^i_{X,log} ⊂ W_rΩ^i_X be the image of dlog[·] : G_m^{⊗i} → W_rΩ^i_X and WΩ^i_{X,log} = lim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}, as pro-étale sheaves. Then for every i ≥ 0 the sequence of complexes of pro-étale sheaves 0 → WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] → N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X → 0, with second map φ_i − 1, is exact in each degree, and WΩ^i_{X,log} = R lim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}.

k is a perfect field of characteristic p and X is smooth over k. Exactness is degreewise and holds for sheaves on the pro-étale site of X; surjectivity of F − 1 in degree i holds only locally. The objects N^{≥i}WΩ and WΩ_log are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.4; this target is the statement about φ_i − 1 that the syntomic comparison needs (link CR.4 → Layer 6). In the printed proof the boundary case reads 'i = n − 1'; it is n = i − 1.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Definition 8.1 and Proposition 8.4 with its proof; pp. 54, 55.)

*Needs:* `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/verschiebung-FV`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/dieudonne-dF`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4/saturated-F-range`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

**Proof route.** Above degree i, p^(n−i)F contracts p-adically and gives an invertible φ_i−1. Below degree i, identify the map through p^(i−1−n)V with 1−p^(i−1−n)V, invertible by p-adic completeness or by V-completeness in the boundary case. In degree i, Illusie Theorem I.5.7.2 gives the finite-level logarithmic kernel sequence, whose inverse limit is exact on the pro-étale site.

**Checks.**

- I = 0: 0 → Z_p → W(O_X) → W(O_X) → 0 with F − 1, the Artin–Schreier–Witt sequence on the pro-étale site. i = 1, X = G_m: dlog[T] ∈ WΩ^1 is fixed by F, since F(dlog[T]) = dlog[T]. X = Spec k, i ≥ 1: N^{≥i}W(k) = p^{i−1}VW(k) = p^iW(k) and (φ_i − 1)(p^i x) = F(x) − p^i x is bijective onto W(k), so WΩ^i_{k,log} = 0 and the cokernel vanishes.

<a id="layer-6-acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective"></a>

### 6.16 Surjectivity of φ_i − 1 on the Nygaard pieces of Â_crys

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, A_crys(S) the p-completed divided power envelope of W(S^♭) → S, with Frobenius φ, Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^i A_crys(S)}, Nygaard completion Â_crys(S) and divided Frobenius φ_i = φ/p^i : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S). (1) For every i > 0 the map φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S) is surjective. (2) For every i ≥ 0 the map φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}Â_crys(−) → Â_crys(−) is surjective as a map of sheaves on the site of quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras with the quasisyntomic topology.

S is quasiregular semiperfect: Frobenius is surjective on S and L_{S/F_p} is a flat S-module placed in degree −1. In (1) i > 0 is necessary: for i = 0 and S = F_p the map φ − 1 on Z_p is zero. The inputs on A_crys(S) are BMS2 Theorem 8.14 (p-torsion-freeness; φ_i mod p identifies N^iA_crys(S) with Fil_i^conj(A_crys(S)/p); the image of N^{≥i} modulo p is the divided power filtration Fil^i_pd, the Hodge filtration of derived de Rham cohomology), required from CrystallineCohomology:CR.4 for the crystalline and Nygaard statements, and DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4 for the derived de Rham reduction.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Lemma 8.19 and its proof; p. 65.)

*Needs:* `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/pd-filtration`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`, [§2.18](#layer-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys), [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp).

**Proof route.** Modulo p the image from N^(i+1) contains Fil_PD^(i+1), while that from pN^(i−1) contains Fil_conj_(i−1). The PD basis gives Fil_conj_(i−1)+Fil_PD^(pi)=A_crys/p, and pi≥i+1 proves surjectivity for i>0, which lifts p-adically. For i=0 the first argument gives Fil_PD^1, and a tower of Artin–Schreier covers gives surjectivity on the remaining quotient S.

**Checks.**

- S perfect, i ≥ 1: A_crys(S) = W(S), N^{≥i} = p^iW(S), φ_i − 1 = (F − p^i)/p^i, surjective because F is bijective and p^iF^{−1} is contracting. S = F_p, i = 0: φ − 1 = 0 on Z_p is not surjective, but becomes surjective on W of an algebraic closure. S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x), i = 1: the class of the divided power γ_p(x) is hit, since it lies in Fil^p_pd.

### 6.17 Syntomic complexes of quasiregular semiperfect rings

Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra. There is a φ-equivariant isomorphism Δ_S ≅ A_crys(S) identifying the Nygaard filtration of Δ_S with N^{≥•}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^• A_crys(S)}, and Z_p(i)(S) is represented by the two-term complex N^{≥i}A_crys(S) → A_crys(S), x ↦ φ(x)/p^i − x (equivalently by its Nygaard-completed version). For i > 0 the complex Z_p(i)(S) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the p-torsion-free group A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i}. For i = 0, H^0(Z_p(0)(S)) = A_crys(S)^{φ=1} is p-torsion-free and H^1(Z_p(0)(S)) = coker(φ − 1) vanishes after sheafification on quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras. In particular Conjecture 7.18 of BMS2 holds in characteristic p. By quasisyntomic descent, for every quasisyntomic F_p-scheme X there is a fibre sequence RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(i)) → Fil^i_N RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) with second map φ/p^i − 1, and after inverting p, RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(i))[1/p] ≃ fib(φ − p^i on RΓ_crys(X/Z_p)[1/p]).

S is a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra; X is a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme. Δ̂_S and its Nygaard filtration are identified with Â_crys(S) through the prismatic crystalline comparison and the Nygaard theory of Layer 1–Layer 3 (Bhatt–Lurie Example 7.4.4; Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 3.4.2), not through BMS2 Theorem 8.17, which is a statement about TC^− owned by Layer 7, graded prismatic Beilinson square. The printed Proposition 8.20 asserts concentration in degree 0 for all i ≥ 0 and every S; for i = 0 this holds only after sheafification (F_p has H^1 = Z_p). The statement above is the corrected one. The exact sequence 0 → π_{2i}TC → π_{2i}TC^− → π_{2i}TP → 0 of the same passage belongs to Layer 7, graded prismatic Beilinson square. The filtration on crystalline cohomology is the Nygaard filtration, not the Hodge filtration; after inverting p it becomes trivial.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Proposition 8.20, its proof and the paragraph before it; p. 66; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Example 7.4.4; p. 178.)

*Needs:* [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§6.11](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes), [§6.16](#layer-6-acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective), [§2.18](#layer-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp), [§3.20](#layer-3-nygaard-completion), [§2.15](#layer-2-quasisyntomic-descent), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`.

**Proof route.** The crystalline comparison identifies the initial prism and its Frobenius-divisibility filtration with A_crys and its Nygaard filtration. Surjectivity is [§6.16](#layer-6-acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective), and the factorization of divided Frobenius through completion gives mutually inverse maps on fixed kernels, identifying the uncompleted kernel with A_crys^(φ=p^i). Qsyn descent globalizes the comparison, including the i=0 cover and the rational assertion because p^i is in Fil_N^i.

**Checks.**

- S perfect: Z_p(i)(S) = W(S)^{F=p^i} = 0 for i > 0, and Z_p(0)(S) = fib(F − 1 on W(S)). S = O_C/p: H^0(Z_p(i)(S)) = A_crys^{φ=p^i} contains t^i for t = log[ε], since φ(t) = pt; after inverting p these are the graded pieces of the ring of the Fargues–Fontaine curve. S = F_p, i = 0: H^1 = Z_p ≠ 0, the counterexample to the uncorrected statement. i = 1: A_crys(S)^{φ=p} ≅ T_p(S^×) via x ↦ log[x] ([§6.26](#layer-6-syntomic-low-weights)).

<a id="layer-6-log-de-rham-witt-comparison"></a>

### 6.18 Syntomic complexes of smooth algebras in characteristic p are logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves

Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, A a smooth k-algebra and X = Spec A. Let λ : qSyn_A^op → X_proét be the natural map from the (opposite of the) quasisyntomic site of A to the pro-étale site of X. Then for all i ≥ 0 there is a natural isomorphism Rλ_* Z_p(i) ≃ WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] of sheaves of complexes on X_proét. Reducing modulo p^r: Rλ_* Z/p^r(i) ≃ W_rΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] on X_ét.

k is a perfect field of characteristic p and A is smooth over k (Theorem 1.15(1) of BMS2 and Corollary 8.21). The statement is on the pro-étale site of X because the coefficients are p-adic; WΩ^i_log is the inverse limit sheaf. The source deduces it from the description of gr^i TC^− and gr^i TP; use instead the identification of Rλ_* of the Nygaard-filtered prismatic sheaves with the Nygaard-filtered de Rham–Witt complex, which needs no trace-theoretic input.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Corollary 8.21 and Remark 8.22; Theorem 1.15(1); pp. 8, 66; [BM23](#ref-bm23), Example 1.3; p. 1.)

*Needs:* [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§6.17](#layer-6-syntomic-complex-char-p), [§6.15](#layer-6-log-forms-divided-frobenius), [§1.14](#layer-1-crystalline-comparison), [§2.15](#layer-2-quasisyntomic-descent), [§4.25](#layer-4-absolute-nygaard-filtration), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, [§2.18](#layer-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys), [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp).

**Proof route.** The crystalline/de-Rham–Witt comparison with its filtered compatibility identifies the étale pushforward of the prismatic filtered complex with (WΩ,N,φ), whose Nygaard filtration is complete in this range. Apply [§6.15](#layer-6-log-forms-divided-frobenius) to compute the fixed-point fibre. For finite coefficients use CR.4’s logarithmic kernel sequence to identify WΩ_log/p^r with W_rΩ_log after étale sheafification; surjectivity of restriction alone would not prove this.

**Checks.**

- I = 0: Rλ_* Z_p(0) = Z_p, the constant pro-étale sheaf lim Z/p^r. i = 1: Rλ_* Z_p(1) = WΩ^1_log[−1], matching the classical fact that the pushforward of μ_{p^n} from the flat site is W_nΩ^1_log[−1]. A = k: Z_p(i)(k) = 0 for i ≥ 1. A = k[T^{±1}], i = 1: dlog[T] is a non-zero section of WΩ^1_log.

### 6.19 Syntomic complexes of smooth formal schemes over O_C vanish above degree i

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = A_inf(O_C) with ξ a generator of ker θ, ξ̃ = φ(ξ), and 𝔛 a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C. On 𝔛_ét the syntomic sheaf Z/p^n(i) = Z_p(i)/p^n is identified with hofib(φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}AΩ_𝔛{i} → AΩ_𝔛{i})/p^n, where AΩ_𝔛 is the A_inf-cohomology sheaf with its Nygaard filtration. Then this complex is concentrated in degrees ≤ i, and the natural map τ^{≤i} hofib(τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ{i}/p^n → τ^{≤i}AΩ{i}/p^n) → hofib(N^{≥i}AΩ{i} → AΩ{i})/p^n (both fibres of φ_i − 1) is an equivalence of sheaves of complexes on 𝔛_ét. In coordinates: for 𝔛 = Spf A with a framing O_C⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ → A (the p-completion of an étale map) and the induced deformation Ã over A_inf, AΩ_A = q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf}, N^{≥i}AΩ_A = ξ^{max(i−•,0)} q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf}, φ(d_q log T_a) = ξ̃ d_q log T_a and φ_i = ξ̃^{−i}φ.

C is algebraically closed and complete (the hypothesis of Theorem 1.15(2); Section 10 itself uses the notation μ, ξ of Section 9 and does not restate it). 𝔛 is smooth over Spf O_C; the framing exists étale-locally. The identification of Z/p^n(i) on 𝔛_ét with the AΩ-fibre uses AΩ ≃ φ^*Δ ([Comparison with AΩ](#layer-5-ainf-omega-comparison)) and the match of the Nygaard filtration with the Lη_ξ filtration ([§3.16](#layer-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation)); the printed text cites BMS2 Theorem 9.6 and Remark 9.11, obtained there through TC, replace that route by the prismatic comparison just stated.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Proposition 10.5 and the computation preceding it; p. 76.)

*Needs:* [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§6.11](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes), [§5.23](#layer-5-ainf-omega-comparison), [§5.19](#layer-5-q-de-rham-comparison), [§3.16](#layer-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation), [§3.14](#layer-3-relative-nygaard-filtration), [§4.19](#layer-4-absolute-relative-comparison), `AInfCohomology:AI.3`, `AInfCohomology:AI.4`, [PerfectoidQuotients §§0.1–0.6](#pq-consequences), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, [§5.26](#layer-5-nygaard-filtration-q-de-rham-coordinates).

In degree j>i, ξ̃^(j−i)φ−1 has inverse the convergent Frobenius geometric series with products ξ̃φ(ξ̃)⋯φ^(r−1)(ξ̃). In degree i, Artin–Schreier covers make φ−1 étale-locally surjective, proving the upper bound and the truncation assertion.

**Checks.**

- I = 0: the complex is fib(φ − 1 on Ã/p^n) étale-locally, namely Z/p^n in degree 0. 𝔛 = Spf O_C: Z/p^n(i) = Z/p^n(i)(C) in degree 0 for all i. 𝔛 the formal torus of dimension 1 and i = 0: the degree-1 term contributes nothing, since ξ̃φ − 1 is invertible on Ã/p. The basis elements d_q log T_{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ d_q log T_{a_i} of degree i are fixed by φ_i.

### 6.20 The condition (As) for Rν_* A_inf,X modulo p^n

Setting: A is a p-power-torsion ring in a topos with an automorphism φ, and μ, ξ ∈ A are non-zero-divisors with μ = ξ φ^{−1}(μ) and ξ − p ∈ φ^{−1}(μ)A; put ξ_r = ξ φ^{−1}(ξ) ⋯ φ^{1−r}(ξ), so μ = ξ_r φ^{−r}(μ). Let C ∈ D^{≥0}(A) with H^0(C) μ-torsion-free and a φ-semilinear quasi-isomorphism φ : C ≃ C. Condition (As): 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} : C/μ^j C → C/μ^j C is a quasi-isomorphism for all i ≥ j ≥ 0. Claim: for a smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over Spf O_C with generic fibre X and ν : X_proét → 𝔛_ét, (As) holds for A = A_inf/p^n and C = Rν_* A_inf,X/p^n. More precisely 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} is an automorphism of the pro-étale sheaf A_inf,X/(p^n, μ^j) for i ≥ j ≥ 0, and 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} : A_inf,X/p^n → A_inf,X/p^n is surjective with kernel Z/p^n · μ^i ≅ Z/p^n(i).

C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, μ = [ε] − 1, ξ = μ/φ^{−1}(μ) (the standing notation of BMS2 Section 9). i ≥ j ≥ 0 in (As); for j = 0 the condition is empty. In the printed remark 'g − μ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g)' reads 'g − ξ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g)'; the target uses the corrected computation.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Section 10, the abstract setting before Remark 10.6, and Remark 10.6; p. 76.)

*Needs:* `AInfCohomology:AI.3`, [PerfectoidQuotients §§0.1–0.6](#pq-consequences), `PerfectoidSpaces:P3`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison`.

**Proof route.** Reduce to mod p, where f−ξ^iφ^−1(f) divisible by μ^j implies h^p−ξ^(i−j)h is integral for h=φ^−1(f/μ^j); integral closedness forces h and then f/μ^j integral. The equation h^p−ξ^ih=f is finite étale after inverting ξ and solvable pro-étale locally by tilting, proving surjectivity. The identity ξφ^−1(μ)=μ and Artin–Schreier–Witt fixed points after inverting μ identify the kernel at every Witt length.

**Checks.**

- I = j = 0: empty; i = j = 1: 1 − ξφ^{−1} is bijective on Ô_X^{♭+}/μ. X = Spa(C, O_C) with C algebraically closed: 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} is surjective on O_C^♭ with kernel F_p · μ^i modulo p. For a non-algebraically-closed C the assertion is about pro-étale sheaves, not surjectivity on global sections; at i=0 the cyclotomic perfectoid field with residue field F_p gives a negative control, since F−1 cannot hit 1 in its valuation ring. The kernel Z/p^n · μ^i is identified with Z/p^n(i) by ε^{⊗i} ↦ μ^i for the chosen ε (over C every Tate twist is trivialised by ε); the identification is canonical only after twisting A_inf by {i}.

<a id="layer-6-leta-frobenius-fixed-points"></a>

### 6.21 Fixed points of ξ^i φ^{−1} are unchanged under Lη_μ in degrees ≤ i

In the abstract setting of [§6.20](#layer-6-ainf-artin-schreier-condition) assume (As). Write T_ℓ=1−ξ^ℓφ^(−1). BMS2 Lemma 10.7, for i≥0 and j≥1, makes three assertions. On the quotient H^i(C)/μ^jH^i(C), the operator T_(ℓ+j) is injective at ℓ=0 and invertible at positive ℓ. On the μ^j-torsion subgroup of H^i(C), T_ℓ is onto at ℓ=0 and invertible at positive ℓ. On the quotient H^i(C)[μ^j]/H^i(C)[μ], T_ℓ is invertible for every ℓ≥0. (Lemma 10.8) Define ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C as the composite τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C ≃ τ^{≤i}Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} C → τ^{≤i}Lη_ξ Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} C = τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C (first map φ^{−1}, second map multiplication by ξ^i). Then the canonical map ι : τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C → C commutes with 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} and induces a quasi-isomorphism τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C) → τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on C).

A is p-power torsion, so p is nilpotent on C and 1 − p·(anything) is an automorphism of C. (As) holds and ξ − p ∈ φ^{−1}(μ)A (the A_inf congruence used in the proof of Lemma 10.7); H^0(C) is μ-torsion-free; φ : C ≃ C is a φ-semilinear quasi-isomorphism. The décalage functor Lη and the identities H^j(Lη_μ C) ≅ H^j(C)/H^j(C)[μ] and Lη_ξ Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} = Lη_μ are owned by AInfCohomology:AI.1.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), The two lemmas after Remark 10.6 (Lemmas 10.7 and 10.8); pp. 76, 77; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Proof of Lemma 10.7; p. 77.)

*Needs:* [§6.20](#layer-6-ainf-artin-schreier-condition), `AInfCohomology:AI.1`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1/derived-decalage`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-cohomology`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-truncations`.

**Proof route.** Use the compatible Bockstein sequence for C/μ^j and (As) to get injectivity on the quotient and surjectivity on torsion; induction on j reduces the remaining torsion injectivity to j=1, where the operator is p-adically contracting. Multiplication by μ identifies the successive torsion quotient and shifts the exponent, proving its operator is invertible. AI.1’s kernel/cokernel formula for the Lη map then makes the kernel operator invertible for j≤i and the cokernel operator invertible for j<i and injective at j=i, so the long exact fibre sequences give precisely the asserted boundary range.

**Checks.**

- J = 0 in Lemma 10.8: H^0(Lη_μ C) = H^0(C) because H^0(C) is μ-torsion-free. i = 0: both truncated fibres are the kernel of 1 − φ^{−1} on H^0(C). For C = Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n the lemma compares fixed points on τ^{≤i}AΩ/p^n and on Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n.

<a id="layer-6-nearby-cycles-comparison"></a>

### 6.22 Syntomic complexes as truncated p-adic nearby cycles

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p and 𝔛 a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C with generic fibre X; let ψ : X_ét → 𝔛_ét be the map of sites. Then for all i ≥ 0 and n ≥ 1 there is a natural equivalence Z/p^n(i) ≃ τ^{≤i} Rψ_* Z/p^n(i) of sheaves of complexes on 𝔛_ét, compatible in n; on the left Z/p^n(i) is the syntomic sheaf Z_p(i)/p^n restricted to 𝔛_ét, on the right the usual Tate twist on X. Passing to the inverse limit over n gives Z_p(i) ≃ τ^{≤i} Rψ_* Z_p(i) on the pro-étale site of 𝔛. Consequently the nearby cycle sheaves R^iψ_* Z/p^n are flat over Z/p^n.

C is algebraically closed and complete over Q_p (BMS2 Theorem 1.15(2)); 𝔛 is smooth over Spf O_C. No properness is assumed. The comparison is with the truncation τ^{≤i}, not with all of Rψ_*: Z/p^n(i) → Rψ_* Z/p^n(i) is an isomorphism exactly when R^jψ_* Z/p^n = 0 for j > i. X is a rigid space, Rψ_* is the nearby-cycles functor of the formal scheme (owner ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology); no theory of nearby cycles beyond the definition is used. The AΩ input is [Comparison with AΩ](#layer-5-ainf-omega-comparison); no TC enters.

([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Theorem 10.1, Remarks 10.2–10.4 and the end of Section 10; p. 75; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Theorem 1.15(2); p. 8; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Remark 10.3; p. 75.)

*Needs:* [§6.19](#layer-6-syntomic-truncation-ainf), [§6.20](#layer-6-ainf-artin-schreier-condition), [§6.21](#layer-6-leta-frobenius-fixed-points), [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§5.23](#layer-5-ainf-omega-comparison), [§3.16](#layer-3-leta-frobenius-factorisation), `AInfCohomology:AI.3`, `AInfCohomology:AI.4`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, [§5.26](#layer-5-nygaard-filtration-q-de-rham-coordinates), `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison`.

**Proof route.** Truncate by [§6.19](#layer-6-syntomic-truncation-ainf) and use divided Frobenius to identify the source with τ≤iAΩ, turning the fibre into fixed points of 1−ξ^iφ^−1. The Lη comparison of [§6.20](#layer-6-ainf-artin-schreier-condition)–[§6.21](#layer-6-leta-frobenius-fixed-points) replaces AΩ by Rν_*A_inf without changing degrees ≤i. Its pro-étale Artin–Schreier–Witt fibre is Z/p^n·μ^i=Z/p^n(i), giving nearby cycles, with coefficient compatibility and flatness from the compatible towers.

**Checks.**

- 𝔛 = Spf O_C: Z/p^n(i)(O_C) ≃ Z/p^n(i)(C) in degree 0, agreeing with [§6.28](#layer-6-tate-twist-perfectoid). 𝔛 = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ and i = 1: H^1 of both sides contains the Kummer class of T, which is non-zero in R^1ψ_*μ_{p^n}. i = 0: Z/p^n ≃ τ^{≤0}Rψ_*Z/p^n = ψ_*Z/p^n. Compatibility in n: the squares with Z/p^n(i) → Z/p^{n−1}(i) commute.

<a id="layer-6-etale-comparison-scalar-extension"></a>

### 6.23 Étale comparison after perfecting the base

Let (A,I) be any bounded prism, let f:(A,I)→(A_∞,I_∞) be its completed perfect prism, and let R be a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. Put R_∞=(R⊗_(A/I)A_∞/I_∞)^∧_p. For n≥1 and a generator d_∞ of I_∞, there is a canonical equivalence RΓ_ét(Spec(R_∞[1/p]),Z/p^n) ≃ ((Δ_(R/A)⊗̂^L_A A_∞)[1/d_∞]/p^n)^(φ=1). This specifies the scalar-extension version for a general base prism. Its étale side is the base-changed algebra R_∞.

The completion of the prism perfection is essential; its raw Frobenius colimit need not be separated. R is p-completely smooth, so ordinary completed base change gives the derived base-changed algebra. The right side has the Frobenius transported through the canonical base-change equivalence; it is not an arbitrary endomorphism.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 3.9; Theorem 1.8(5); Construction 7.6; Theorem 9.1, §§3,7,9,53–55,64–66; pp. 4, 31, 56, 71.)

*Needs:* [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2](#ps-prisms), [§1.20](#layer-1-prismatic-base-change), [§2.7](#layer-2-derived-prismatic-base-change), [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison).

**Proof route.** Perfect the base prism and use prismatic base change, preserving Frobenius. Apply [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison) over that perfect prism and substitute the resulting scalar-extension formula. Independence of the chosen ideal generator and functoriality follow from localization and the universal property of prism perfection.

**Checks.**

- A perfect base prism, A_∞=A and R_∞=R, giving Theorem 9.1. For a crystalline base the base-changed R_∞ has characteristic p, its generic fibre is empty, and localising Δ at d_∞=p before reducing modulo p^n gives zero. Changing d_∞ by a unit has no effect because only localisation at its ideal occurs.

<a id="layer-6-crystalline-logarithm-exact-sequence"></a>

### 6.24 Crystalline logarithmic exact sequence

Let R be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra and J=ker(R^♭→R). There is a natural exact sequence 0→(1+J)^×→^(log[·])Fil^1_NA_crys(R)→^(φ/p−1)A_crys(R)→0. The first map is the crystalline logarithm of the Teichmüller lift, not a logarithm of an arbitrary unit of R.

Use the canonical PD envelope A_crys(R), its Frobenius, and its Nygaard filtration.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 7.1.1 and proof, §7.1; p. 167.)

*Needs:* [§2.18](#layer-2-qrsp-char-p-acrys), [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp), [§6.12](#layer-6-prismatic-logarithm), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`.

**Proof route.** Reduce the three torsion-free complete groups modulo p and isolate the first conjugate step: after removing the degree-zero divided-Frobenius piece, expansion of log[1−x] through degree p gives −[x]^p/p on J/J². The remaining map is the truncated logarithm (1+J²)/(1+φ(J))→J²/φ(J): for injectivity choose a finitely generated K containing x in K² and successively improve its order until K^(pm)⊂φ(K), while for surjectivity invert the truncated series on nilpotent principal ideals generated by products uv. Lift this exactness p-adically.

**Checks.**

- R perfect, J=0 and φ/p−1:pW(R)→W(R) is bijective via multiplication by p followed by 1−pφ^(-1). The nontrivial kernel for a semiperfect quotient consists of lifted units 1+J, not all units of R^♭.

<a id="layer-6-crystalline-first-chern-class"></a>

### 6.25 Crystalline first Chern class as a syntomic fibre

For a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme X there is a natural fibre sequence RΓ_ét(X,G_m)^∧_p[−1]→^(c_1^crys)Fil^1_NRΓ_crys(X)→^(φ/p−1)RΓ_crys(X). The first Chern class gives the canonical weight-one comparison.

The crystalline complex is the canonical derived crystalline complex; the left side is untruncated étale G_m cohomology.

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Construction 7.3.1, Variant 7.3.3, Theorem 7.3.5 and proof, §7.3; pp. 175, 176, 177.)

*Needs:* [§6.24](#layer-6-crystalline-logarithm-exact-sequence), [§2.15](#layer-2-quasisyntomic-descent), [§6.17](#layer-6-syntomic-complex-char-p), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Proof route.** The Frobenius-compatible crystalline Chern class lands in the divided-Frobenius fibre. Both it and the completed G_m complex descend along a simultaneously pro-fppf and qsyn cover. On quasiregular semiperfect rings BL Proposition 7.2.5 identifies the latter with T_p(R^×), and the logarithmic exact sequence identifies this with the former (BL Theorem 7.1.1).

**Checks.**

- A perfect affine ring the chartwise kernel is zero. Using Pic alone in place of untruncated RΓ_ét(G_m) loses the Brauer contribution and fails on fields with p-primary Brauer classes.

<a id="layer-6-syntomic-low-weights"></a>

### 6.26 Syntomic complexes in weights n < 0, n = 0 and n = 1

Let R be an animated commutative ring. (1) For n > 0, RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(−n)) = 0. (2) There is a canonical map of commutative algebra objects α_R : RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p), characterised by functoriality in R, and it is an isomorphism when R is p-complete; here RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) = lim_k RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z/p^k). If moreover R is a p-complete ring with x ↦ x^p − x surjective on R/pR, then RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the ring of continuous Z_p-valued functions on Spec R. (3) There is a canonical map c_1^syn : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)), functorial in R and given, for R quasiregular semiperfectoid, in degree 0 by T_p(R^×) → T_p(Δ̄_R^×) → H^0_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)), the second map being the prismatic logarithm; for R p-complete the induced map RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)) from the p-completion is an isomorphism. (4) Consequently, for a quasisyntomic ring R, Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1], and the natural map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Z_p(1)(R), where Pic(R) = (τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))[1] and (−)^∧ is derived p-completion, is an isomorphism on H^i for i ≤ 1 and injective on H^2; it is an isomorphism if and only if (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧ = 0, which holds for perfectoid R and fails for R = F_p(t) (H^2 of the target is T_p Br(R) ≠ 0). This corrects Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.6, which asserts the isomorphism for every quasisyntomic ring; Z_p(1) is, locally for the quasisyntomic topology, the sheaf R ↦ T_p(R^×) = lim_n μ_{p^n}(R) in degree 0; and for a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra R the sequence 0 → T_p(R^×) → Fil^1_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R) → 0 (maps log[·] and φ/p − 1) is exact.

R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring in (1); p-complete in the isomorphism statements of (2) and (3); quasisyntomic in (4). Étale cohomology with Z_p-coefficients is the derived inverse limit of Z/p^k-cohomology; G_m-cohomology is étale (for (4), flat cohomology gives the same τ^{≤1}). These statements replace BMS2 Propositions 7.16 and 7.17, whose proofs use K-theory and the theorem of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow; the proofs below are Bhatt–Lurie's and use no K-theory, TC or trace (requirement of the BMS2 route). In (2) the comparison is with étale cohomology of Spec R (equivalently of Spec R/p), not of the generic fibre Spec R[1/p].

([BL22](#ref-bl22), Corollary 7.4.9; p. 180; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 8.1.8, Theorem 8.1.9, Corollary 8.1.10; p. 191; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 7.1.1, Proposition 7.5.2, Theorem 7.5.6; pp. 167, 181, 184; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Lemma 9.6; p. 76.)

<a id="layer-6-etale-comparison-without-inverting-d"></a>

### 6.27 The variant of the étale comparison without inverting p or d

Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) and X a p-adic formal scheme over R. Then for all n ≥ 0 there is a canonical identification Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}/p^n)^{φ=1} of objects of D(X_ét, Z/p^n), where Z/p^n is the constant étale sheaf on X. For X = Spf S affine: RΓ_ét(Spf S, Z/p^n) = RΓ_ét(Spec(S/p), Z/p^n) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}/p^n)^{φ=1}, and R lim_n gives RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z_p) ≃ (Δ_{S/A})^{φ=1} = fib(φ − 1 : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A}). The map Δ_{X/A}/p^n → Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n induces on fixed points restriction from special to generic algebraic cohomology; for bounded X it is the adjunction map Z/p^n → Rμ_* Z/p^n of [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison).

Same generality as Theorem 9.1: X arbitrary over a perfectoid ring R. No element is inverted; the right-hand side is in general not concentrated in degree 0 on global sections, since H^1_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) can be non-zero. Work with p-adic formal R-schemes and use the proof below.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 9.3; p. 73; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Theorem 8.1.9 and its proof; p. 191.)

**Proof route.** Perfect-base comparison identifies absolute and relative prismatic complexes, so the weight-zero theorem gives the fixed-point formula. Reduce coefficients and apply affine proper base change for the henselian pair (S,pS), then sheafify on the formal étale site. The square after inverting d commutes by uniqueness of the unit-preserving comparison, checked on perfectoid arc_p covers (BL Proposition 8.3.7).

**Checks.**

- S = O_C: Z/p^n ≃ (A_inf/p^n)^{φ=1} = W_n(O_C^♭)^{F=1}, and F − 1 is surjective on W_n(O_C^♭). S = Z_p^cycl: H^1 of both sides is H^1_ét(Spec F_p, Z/p^n) = Z/p^n, since the residue field of S is F_p. S an F_p-algebra over a perfect ring R: Δ_{S/A}/p is derived de Rham cohomology up to Frobenius twist and the statement is the Artin–Schreier sequence.

<a id="layer-6-tate-twist-perfectoid"></a>

### 6.28 p-adic Tate twists of perfectoid rings and étale cohomology of the generic fibre

Let R be a perfectoid ring. For every integer n ≥ 1 there is a canonical identification Z_p(n)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), Z_p(n)), where the right-hand side is the derived limit over k of RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), μ_{p^k}^{⊗n}). For n = 0 there are canonical identifications Z_p(0)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec((R/p)_perf), Z_p). The identifications are multiplicative in n, natural in R, and for n = 1 the map is the Kummer map T_p-completion of units: on a p-complete, p-torsion-free rank-one valuation ring V with algebraically closed fraction field C it is T_p(V^×) → T_p(C^×) → H^0(Spec C, Z_p(1)). Moreover, as presheaves on perfectoid rings both sides are, p-completely arc-locally, concentrated in degree 0 and p-torsion-free, and the multiplication Z_p(1)^{⊗̂n} → Z_p(n) exhibits the target as the p-complete arc-sheafification of the source.

R is an arbitrary perfectoid ring; for n ≥ 1 both sides vanish on rings of characteristic p. For n ≥ 1 the comparison is with the generic fibre Spec R[1/p]; for n = 0 with Spec R, equivalently with the special fibre. The two cases are different statements. The comparison map for n = 1 is constructed from Z_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n} ([§6.26](#layer-6-syntomic-low-weights)), not from the cyclotomic trace; with this input the proof is purely algebraic (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 9.5). For the proof use (∗_b) concerns (G_1/p)^{⊗n} → G_n/p, and 'stacks' reads 'stalks'.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 9.4 and its proof; p. 73; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Remark 9.5; p. 75.)

Over the cyclotomic base, multiplication by μ^−n identifies the mod-p two-term complexes by a Frobenius telescope of equivalences, compatibly with products. Both sides are p-complete arc sheaves whose tensor-power comparisons can be tested on absolutely integrally closed valuation rings; Kummer theory identifies weight one there because C^×/V^× is uniquely p-divisible and Pic(C)=0, and its tensor powers descend the full multiplicative comparison.

- R = O_C: Z_p(n)(O_C) ≃ Z_p(n) in degree 0, a free Z_p-module of rank one, for every n ≥ 0. R perfect of characteristic p and n ≥ 1: Z_p(n)(R) = 0; for n = 0, Z_p(0)(R) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) = W(R)^{F=1} derived. R = Z_p^cycl: H^1(Z_p(n)(R)) = H^1(Gal of the completed cyclotomic field, Z_p(n)), non-zero. Finite level: Z/p^k(n)(O_C) = μ_{p^k}^{⊗n}(C), and the maps for k → k − 1 are the reduction maps.

<a id="layer-6-picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible"></a>

### 6.29 Picard groups of perfectoid rings are uniquely p-divisible

For a perfectoid ring R the groups Pic(R) and Pic(R[1/p]) are uniquely p-divisible. Moreover the canonical map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Pic(R[1/p])^∧[−2] of p-completed Picard groupoids is an isomorphism, compatible with Pic(R)^∧[−2] ≃ Z_p(1)(R) ([§6.26](#layer-6-syntomic-low-weights)), Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) ([§6.28](#layer-6-tate-twist-perfectoid)) and the Kummer map Pic(R[1/p])^∧[−2] → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)).

R is any perfectoid ring. Pic(R) = (τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))[1] denotes the Picard groupoid as an object of D(Z); Pic(R) with roman type is its H^0, the Picard group. Cohomology of G_m is computed in the flat topology (equivalently étale).

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Corollary 9.7 and its proof; p. 76.)

*Needs:* [§6.26](#layer-6-syntomic-low-weights), [§6.28](#layer-6-tate-twist-perfectoid), [§2.26](#layer-2-finite-projective-modules-p-complete), [PerfectoidSpaces §P1](#ps-integral), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, Mathlib `CommRing.Pic`.

**Proof route.** Apply complete finite-projective effectivity ([§2.26](#layer-2-finite-projective-modules-p-complete)) along d and along p to lift invertible modules uniquely up to isomorphism, obtaining Pic(R)≃Pic(A_inf(R))≃Pic(R^♭); Frobenius on the perfect ring acts both invertibly and as multiplication by p. The completed Picard/Kummer comparison square commutes on O_C and hence by p-complete arc descent, and its truncated G_m map is cohomologically injective, forcing the displayed maps to be equivalences. Mod-p H⁰ and the H⁻¹ Bockstein sequences give Pic(R[1/p])/p=0 and a surjection from Pic(R)[p]=0, proving unique p-divisibility.

**Checks.**

- R = O_C: Pic(O_C) = 0 and Pic(C) = 0. R perfect of characteristic p: R[1/p] = 0 and Pic(R) is uniquely p-divisible because Frobenius acts as an automorphism and as multiplication by p. Consequence used in Theorem 14.1: H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) is H^0 of the derived p-completion of R^×.

<a id="layer-6-tate-twist-discreteness"></a>

### 6.30 Z_p(n) is discrete and p-torsion-free

For each n ≥ 0 the sheaf of complexes Z_p(n) on the quasisyntomic site is discrete and p-torsion-free: for every quasisyntomic ring S, H^0(Z_p(n)(−)) is a sheaf of p-torsion-free abelian groups, and every class in H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) vanishes on some quasisyntomic cover S → S' (so the quasisyntomic sheafification of H^1(Z_p(n)(−)) is 0, and H^i(Z_p(n)(−)) = 0 locally for i ≠ 0). Hence Z_p(n)(S) = RΓ(S_qsyn, H^0(Z_p(n))) is the cohomology of a sheaf of p-torsion-free groups. Two lemmas of the proof: (Lemma 14.4) for a perfectoid Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebra R, R' = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = R'/(X_1, …, X_r), the map Z_p(n)(R') → Z_p(n)(S) is surjective on H^1; (Lemma 14.5) for a perfectoid ring R and a surjection S' → S of quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras such that the p-completion of L_{S'/R} → L_{S/R} is surjective on H^{−1}, the map Δ_{S'} → Δ_S is surjective.

The statement is local: discreteness means vanishing of H^1 after quasisyntomic sheafification; Z_p(n)(S) itself can have H^1 ≠ 0 (already Z_p(0)(F_p)). n ≥ 0; for n < 0 the sheaf is 0. This is Conjecture 7.18 of BMS2. Its K-theoretic consequences, Corollaries 14.2 and 14.3 of Bhatt–Scholze (evenness of K(−; Z_p) locally and for regular quotients), need K(−; Z_p) ≃ τ_{≥0}TC(−; Z_p) on henselian pairs and are outside the scope of these syntomic targets. In the printed proof 'C/Q' reads 'C/Q_p complete and algebraically closed'.

To kill H¹ locally, perfectoid rings reduce to weight one and André’s cover adjoining roots of units; for root-polynomial quotients the q-PD basis makes φ_n−1 contract above total degree n and moves every remaining cokernel class from degree i to i/p until it comes from the perfectoid base. A general QRSP quotient admits such a root presentation surjective on H^−1 of cotangent complexes and hence on Δ and syntomic H¹, and filtered finite subsets finish the reduction (BS22 Lemmas 14.4–14.5).

**Checks.**

- N = 0: Z_p(0) is the constant sheaf lim Z/p^r, and H^1(Z_p(0)(F_p)) = Z_p dies on the cover F_p → algebraic closure. n = 1: Z_p(1) = T_p G_m, and a class in H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) = (R^×)^∧ dies after adjoining p-power roots of units. S = O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X): H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) is a quotient of H^1(Z_p(n)(O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩)) by Lemma 14.4. In characteristic p the statement is [§6.17](#layer-6-syntomic-complex-char-p).

### 6.31 The étale comparison morphism for syntomic cohomology

(1) For every p-complete animated commutative ring R there is a canonical map of graded commutative ring objects of D(Z), ⊕_n γ{n} : ⊕_{n∈Z} RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → ⊕_{n∈Z} RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), Z_p(n)), characterised up to homotopy by functoriality in R and by γ{1} ∘ c_1^syn ≃ c_1^ét, where c_1^ét : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) is the étale first Chern class. (2) γ{0} is the composite of α_R^{−1} : RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) with restriction to Spec R[1/p]. (3) For a perfectoid Z_p^cyc-algebra R with Ext^i_{Z_p^cyc}(F_p, R) = 0 for all i and x ↦ x^p − x surjective on R/pR, the map H^0_ét(Spf R, Z_p)[log_Δ(ε)] → ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is an isomorphism of graded rings; in particular each RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is concentrated in degree 0. This applies to O_C for C algebraically closed and spherically complete of mixed characteristic. (4) For a derived p-complete animated Z[ζ_(p^∞)]-algebra R, the class ε of the compatible roots of unity lies in H^0_syn(Spf R,Z_p(1)); inverting it in the graded syntomic algebra gives the graded generic étale algebra after p-completion. In weight zero this is the p-completed colimit along multiplication by ε of the nonnegative syntomic weights. The statement for arbitrary animated R is in Syntomic cohomology of schemes, after that object is constructed.

R is a p-complete animated ring in (1), (2); a perfectoid algebra over Z_p^cyc, the p-completion of Z[q^{1/p^∞}]/([p]_q), in (3); an animated Z[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebra in (4). γ{n} is in general not an isomorphism, and no range of degrees in which it is one is asserted here: the isomorphism statements are (4) after inverting ε, [§6.28](#layer-6-tate-twist-perfectoid) for perfectoid rings and [§6.22](#layer-6-nearby-cycles-comparison) for smooth formal schemes over O_C. Bhatt–Lurie Section 8 proves no range of degrees in which γ{n} is an isomorphism. (4) is a reformulation of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.1 over the perfectoid base Z_p^cyc and depends on it. In the Bhatt–Lurie text the remark after Theorem 8.1.9 cites the wrong theorem and Remark 8.5.4 misprints a target.

### 6.32 Syntomic cohomology of schemes

For an animated commutative ring R with p-completion R̂ and an integer n, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) is the pullback in D̂(Z_p) of RΓ_syn(Spf R̂, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p], Z_p(n)) ← RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)), the first map being γ{n} of [§6.31](#layer-6-syntomic-etale-comparison); the projection to RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is again called the étale comparison morphism γ{n}. Properties: (a) if R is p-complete then RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)); (b) if p is invertible in R then γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p(n)); (c) with j : Spec R[1/p] → Spec R there is a fibre sequence RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)); (d) R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) satisfies fpqc descent, hence extends to schemes, formal schemes and algebraic stacks X by RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(n)) = lim over Spec R → X; (e) it is left Kan extended from smooth Z-algebras and commutes with filtered colimits; it does not commute with sifted colimits; (f) RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(0)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) canonically; (g) c_1^syn : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(1)) exhibits the target as the p-completion of the source. For a scheme X, Z/p^k(n)_X ∈ D(X_ét, Z/p^k) denotes the restriction of RΓ_syn(−, Z_p(n))/p^k to the small étale site. (h) For every animated Z[ζ_(p^∞)]-algebra R, inverting the compatible-root class ε in ⊕_nRΓ_syn(Spec R,Z_p(n)) and p-completing gives ⊕_nRΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p],Z_p(n)), naturally as graded algebras (BL Theorem 8.5.1).

R is any animated commutative ring; the étale site and étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] depend only on π_0(R). The pullback is formed in the p-complete derived ∞-category; all four corners are p-complete. Étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] with twisted coefficients, j_!, Gabber's affine proper base change and formal glueing for étale cohomology are imported (SF.2 and the arc-descent requirement). In the printed proof of Proposition 8.4.10 the last colimit is indexed by ℰ where ℰ' is meant.

**Proof route.** Define the arithmetic pullback square; when p is invertible or the ring p-complete it reduces to the indicated corner. Formal gluing and affine proper base change identify its localization fibre as RΓ_ét(j_!Z_p(n)); arc descent for that fibre and fpqc descent for the complete term give descent, while its henselian invariance and colimit properties give the stated left Kan extension. The arithmetic fracture squares for Z_p and completed G_m reduce the low-weight identifications to the complete case and the p-invertible case (BL §8.4).

**Checks.**

- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_p_invertible`: For a cospan with zero p-adic corners, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≅ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)).
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_p_complete`: For a cospan whose restriction map is the identity, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≅ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)).
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_zero`: For the zero cospan (the zero ring) RΓ_syn = 0.
- `pr4_syntomic_scheme_not_product`: RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) is not the direct sum of the formal and the étale corner: for the cospan with all three objects M ≠ 0 and both maps the identity the pullback is M, not M ⊕ M.

- RΓ_syn(Spec Q, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_ét(Spec Q, Z_p(n)). RΓ_syn(Spec Z_p, Z_p(1)) = RΓ_syn(Spf Z_p, Z_p(1)) = (Z_p^×)^∧[−1]. RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) for n < 0. For X proper over a p-henselian ring with bounded p-power torsion, RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_syn of its p-adic completion.

<a id="layer-6-syntomic-connectivity"></a>

### 6.33 Connectivity, rigidity and left Kan extension of syntomic complexes

Let i ≥ 0. (1) The functor R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(i)) on animated rings commutes with sifted colimits and is left Kan extended from finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras; on quasisyntomic rings Z_p(i) is left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras. (2) For every quasisyntomic ring R, Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤ i+1}(Z_p). (3) (Rigidity) For a henselian pair (R, I) with R and R/I p-complete, fib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/I)) ∈ D^{≤ i}(Z_p). (4) For a p-complete ring R, H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) ≅ coker(1 − C^{−1} : Ω^i_{R/p} → Ω^i_{R/p}/dΩ^{i−1}_{R/p}); it vanishes when R is w-strictly local, in particular strictly henselian local. (5) Consequently, for every scheme X the étale sheaf of complexes Z/p^n(i)_X obtained by restricting syntomic cohomology ([§6.32](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-schemes)) to the small étale site lies in D^{[0, i]}(X_ét, Z/p^n), and Z/p^n(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤ i} for R strictly henselian local.

Statements (2)–(4) are Theorems 5.1, 5.2 and Corollary 5.43 of Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, as used by Bhatt–Mathew. In (3) both R and R/I are p-complete and (R, I) is henselian. The proofs in the cited sources of (2)–(4) describe Nygaard graded pieces as gr^n THH and use THH of graded rings; the direct prismatic argument requires the Nygaard graded continuity and internal-weight calculation specified above. (5) uses that the generic-fibre part of Z/p^n(i)_X is μ_{p^n}^{⊗i} in degree 0 and that stalks at characteristic-p points are computed on strictly henselian local rings by [§6.14](#layer-6-syntomic-filtered-colimits).

([BM23](#ref-bm23), Section 1.2, before Theorem 1.8; p. 3; [BM23](#ref-bm23), Section 5.3, after Proposition 5.5; p. 24; [AMMN22](#ref-ammn22), Theorem 5.1, Theorem 5.2, Lemma 5.34, Proposition 5.35, Corollary 5.43; pp. 25, 35, 39; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 5.5.19 and Remark 5.5.9; pp. 135, 137.)

*Needs:* [§6.11](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes), [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§6.18](#layer-6-log-de-rham-witt-comparison), [§6.14](#layer-6-syntomic-filtered-colimits), [§6.32](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-schemes), [§4.25](#layer-4-absolute-nygaard-filtration), [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.4`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

First prove the following two local prerequisites. `Prismatic.Nygaard.graded_adicContinuity` says that for a noetherian p-complete ring T with F-finite T/p and a finitely generated ideal J, each gr_N^rΔ_T{i} agrees with lim_m gr_N^rΔ_(T/J^m){i} when T is J-complete. Use the fibre sequence gr_N^rΔ→Fil_r^conjΩ̂_diff --(Θ+r)→Fil_(r−1)^conjΩ̂_diff (BL22 Remark 5.5.8, p.135). These are finite conjugate stages, with graded terms completed exterior powers of the cotangent complex, rather than the whole infinite conjugate colimit. Noetherian F-finiteness makes their fixed truncations pseudocoherent. The transitivity triangle and the pro-zero positive relative cotangent groups of T→T/J^m identify their limits with the corresponding stages over T; prove the pro-zero assertion using a finite presentation, the powers of J in its bar resolution and Artin–Rees in each fixed degree. Pseudocoherent formal functions computes the inverse limits; the bounds on finite conjugate stages justify the passage through this finite filtration. Thus the displayed fibre sequence proves continuity with the Sen operator and the twists. Reconstruct the Nygaard-completed filtered objects by their graded towers, and use the invariance of syntomic fibres under Nygaard completion to obtain the continuity required in (3).

`Prismatic.Nygaard.internalWeight` equips each finite quotient Δ̂_T{i}/N^{≥n} with the internal nonnegative grading of a nonnegatively graded ring T. It also grades N^{≥i}/N^{≥i+r}. Modulo p the map can preserves weights and φ_i multiplies weights by p. The claim concerns these finite quotients: taking the underlying direct sum of a graded inverse limit need not recover the ungraded inverse limit. On homogeneous QRSP root covers first use weights in Z[1/p], the coaction x↦xt^w and relative perfectness after adjoining t^(1/p^∞). The resulting Hodge–Tate and Nygaard graded pieces have the coaction identities. Their finite filtrations are functorial in the completed exterior powers of L_T; when T has integral weights these exterior powers have integral weights, so all nonintegral components vanish. Finite extensions therefore recover the integral grading on the finite Nygaard quotients. The coaction identity F(t^w)=t^{pw} proves the assertion about φ_i modulo p; it is not an assertion that divided Frobenius preserves weights. ([BM23](#ref-bm23), Remark 3.8, Construction 3.9, Remark 3.10, pp.10–11; [AMMN22](#ref-ammn22), Construction 5.40, Proposition 5.41, pp.37–38.)

For T=A⊕N with A a completed finite polynomial algebra and N finite over A, put A in weight zero and N in weight one. In each cohomological degree the completed exterior powers of L_T are finite T-modules, hence have only finitely many weights. The finite Nygaard quotients inherit this property. Choose r sufficiently large for the mod-p finite-quotient formula for F_p(i). Its relative fibre is can−φ_i on the positive-weight parts of N^{≥i}/N^{≥i+r} and Δ̂{i}/N^{≥i+r}. The fibre of can lies in D^{≤i}. A map multiplying positive weights by p is strictly triangular in their increasing order; finite weight support in each cohomological degree identifies direct sums with products, and the product-filtration connectivity lemma gives the same bound for the fibre of can−φ_i (AMMN Lemma 5.42, p.39). This does not require an inverse on the entire completed prismatic complex. General nilpotent ideals reduce to split square-zero extensions by a polynomial simplicial resolution and sifted colimits. Continuity handles the complete noetherian F-finite case. For a finitely generated henselian pair, the map to its completion is a filtered colimit of smooth maps by Néron–Popescu; their sections make the relative fibre a retract of the complete-case fibre. Filtered colimits then give the general henselian assertion (AMMN proof of Theorem 5.2, pp.36–37).

**Checks for the prerequisites.** On a ring concentrated in weight zero every grading is concentrated there. For A⊕N with N≠0 in weight one, Frobenius sends that weight to p rather than preserving it; replacing the weight by a constant grading fails this test. The unit has weight zero and is never killed by the positive-weight pro-nilpotence argument. For T=F_p[[x]], J=(x), gr_N^0 and its finite conjugate constituents are recovered from T/(x^m); using only the individual quotient T/(x) would discard its x-adic coefficients.

**Proof route.** Mod-p sifted-colimit compatibility is [§6.11](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes); the Nygaard graded bound and Frobenius vanishing on the I-adic graded pieces give the fibre connectivity bound first on polynomial rings and then by extension. Continuity, Popescu approximation and square-zero internal gradings, multiplied by p under Frobenius, give pro-nilpotence and rigidity (AMMN Propositions 5.36,5.38,5.41). Reduce via rigidity to ind-smooth F_p-algebras, where the logarithmic Cartier sequence gives the formula, and combine it with connectivity and the arithmetic fibre square for the remaining assertions.

**Checks.**

- I = 0: Z/p^n(0)_X = Z/p^n in degree 0. i = 1: Z/p^n(1)_X = fib(p^n : G_m → G_m) on X_ét, in degrees [0, 1]. R = Z_p, i = 1: Z_p(1)(Z_p) = (Z_p^×)^∧[−1] ∈ D^{≤ 2}; the fibre to Z_p(1)(F_p) = 0 is in D^{≤ 1}. R strictly henselian local: H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) = 0.

<a id="layer-6-syntomic-not-generic-fibre-etale"></a>

### 6.34 Syntomic cohomology is not étale cohomology of the generic fibre in all degrees

The étale comparison morphism γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is not an isomorphism in general, and the φ = 1 statement of [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison) does not extend to the divided-Frobenius fibres Z_p(n). Instances: (1) R = Z_p, n = 1: H^1 of the source is the p-completion of Z_p^× and H^1 of the target the p-completion of Q_p^×; γ{1} is injective on H^1 with cokernel Z_p, generated by the Kummer class of p. (2) R an F_p-algebra: the target is 0 for every n, while RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) ≠ 0 for R ≠ 0, and for R = O_C/p the group H^0(Z_p(n)(R)) = A_crys^{φ=p^n} is non-zero for all n ≥ 0. (3) For 𝔛 smooth over Spf O_C the sheaf Z/p^k(n) on 𝔛_ét is the truncation τ^{≤n}Rψ_*Z/p^k(n), so Z/p^k(n) → Rψ_*Z/p^k(n) is an isomorphism if and only if R^jψ_*Z/p^k = 0 for all j > n. (4) For a p-torsion-free F-smooth scheme X (for example regular and flat over Z) with j : X[1/p] → X, Bhatt–Mathew prove that Z/p^k(n)_X → τ^{≤n}Rj_*μ_{p^k}^{⊗n} is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves in degrees < n and injective in degree n with image generated by symbols from O_X^×; instance (1) is the case X = Spec Z_p, n = 1. For a p-complete Z[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebra R with its specified compatible roots of unity, there is an isomorphism after inverting the resulting class ε and p-completing ([§6.31](#layer-6-syntomic-etale-comparison) (4)) and, for the fixed points of φ itself, [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison).

The warning concerns the syntomic complexes Z_p(n), built from the Nygaard filtration and the divided Frobenius; it does not concern the φ = 1 statement of Theorem 9.1, which holds for every p-adic formal scheme over a perfectoid ring. (4) is quoted from Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 1.8 as the general shape of the discrepancy; its proof (F-smoothness, Bloch–Kato) is outside this layer and is not a prerequisite of any construction. In (1) p is odd for the explicit description 1 + pZ_p of the completed units; the statement about the cokernel holds for all p.

([BM23](#ref-bm23), Theorem 1.8 and the paragraph after it; p. 3; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Section 8, introduction; pp.188–189; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Theorem 10.1; p. 75.)

*Needs:* [§6.31](#layer-6-syntomic-etale-comparison), [§6.26](#layer-6-syntomic-low-weights), [§6.17](#layer-6-syntomic-complex-char-p), [§6.22](#layer-6-nearby-cycles-comparison), [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`.

**Proof route.** In weight one on Z_p, Kummer comparison is the inclusion of units into Q_p^×, whose quotient is Z and whose completed valuation gives the missing class. In characteristic p the generic fibre vanishes while weight zero and the crystalline fixed classes do not, with log[ε] satisfying φ(t)=pt. The positive comparison range is [§6.22](#layer-6-nearby-cycles-comparison), and the final assertion is Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 1.8.

**Checks.**

- The cokernel of γ{1} on H^1 for R = Z_p is Z_p, not 0. For R = F_p: RΓ_syn(Spf F_p, Z_p) has H^0 = H^1 = Z_p while Spec F_p[1/p] is empty. For R = O_C: γ{n} is an isomorphism for every n ≥ 0, so the discrepancy is invisible on the basis of the arc_p-topology. A statement 'Z_p(n)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) for every quasisyntomic R' is false by (1).

<a id="layer-6-tate-twists-acceptance-examples"></a>

### 6.35 O_C, the formal torus, finite levels and the maps n → n − 1

Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε^{1/p}] with ε a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, d = [p]_q a generator of ker(A_inf → O_C) and μ = q − 1, so φ(μ) = dμ. (1) For every n ≥ 0, Z_p(n)(O_C) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals Z_p · μ^n ⊂ φ^{−1}(d)^n A_inf, the kernel of φ/d^n − 1; it is identified with H^0(Spec C, Z_p(n)) = T_p(C^×)^{⊗n}. (2) At finite level Z/p^k(n)(O_C) = Z/p^k · μ^n = μ_{p^k}(C)^{⊗n}, and the maps induced by k → k − 1 are the reduction maps, compatible with those of étale cohomology; likewise in [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison) the isomorphisms Z/p^k ≃ (A_inf[1/d]/p^k)^{φ=1} = W_k(C^♭)^{F=1} commute with reduction. (3) For the formal torus 𝔛 = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ with S = O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩: RΓ_ét(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^k) ≃ (Δ_{S/A_inf}[1/d]/p^k)^{φ=1}, and on 𝔛_ét, Z/p^k(0) = Z/p^k and Z/p^k(1) ≃ τ^{≤1}Rψ_*μ_{p^k}, whose H^1 contains the Kummer class of T, a non-zero section of R^1ψ_*μ_{p^k}. (4) For C spherically complete, ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf O_C, Z_p(n)) = Z_p[log_Δ(ε)].

C is complete and algebraically closed; in (4) also spherically complete. The normalisation q = [ε^{1/p}] makes [p]_q a generator of the kernel of θ, as in the proof of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4. These are instances of earlier targets, collected as the layer’s worked examples; nothing new is proved.

([BS22](#ref-bs22), Proof of Theorem 9.4, first step; p. 73; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 8.3.3 and Example 8.3.4; p. 194.)

*Needs:* [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§6.28](#layer-6-tate-twist-perfectoid), [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison), [§6.7](#layer-6-etale-comparison-coefficients), [§6.22](#layer-6-nearby-cycles-comparison), [§6.31](#layer-6-syntomic-etale-comparison), [PerfectoidQuotients §§0.1–0.6](#pq-consequences).

**Proof route.** On O_C the fixed generator is μ^n, and the perfectoid comparison identifies the fibre with a rank-one degree-zero Tate module; derive all finite levels by compatible reduction. For the formal torus the generic-point Kummer class stays nonzero: a hypothetical root on an étale neighborhood is integral over its normal ring, whose reduction would supply a p-th root of T in a separable closure of the characteristic-p function field. The weight transition is the multiplicative logarithm comparison of [§6.31](#layer-6-syntomic-etale-comparison).

**Checks.**

- Φ(μ) = dμ, hence φ(μ^n)/d^n = μ^n. Z/p^k(n)(O_C) → Z/p^{k−1}(n)(O_C) is surjective with kernel p^{k−1}Z/p^k · μ^n. The Kummer class of T in H^1_ét(Spec C⟨T^{±1}⟩, μ_{p^k}) has order p^k. Z_p(n)(O_C) ≠ 0 for every n ≥ 0, whereas Z_p(n)(O_C/p) = A_crys^{φ=p^n} is much larger: reduction modulo p changes syntomic cohomology.

### Examples

For a perfectoid ring, Artin–Schreier–Witt fixed points recover constant Z/p^n coefficients; localization at t=0 gives the zero ring and zero complex. The syntomic complex in weight zero is Z_p, negative weights vanish, and weight one is completed G_m cohomology shifted by [−1]. For a characteristic-p scheme the p-inverted generic fibre is empty, but weight-zero syntomic cohomology is nonzero on a connected scheme. Thus syntomic cohomology cannot be all-degree generic-fibre étale cohomology. The nearby-cycle assertion uses its degree truncation and the correct twist.

## Layer 7: Prismatic F-crystals and crystalline lattices

Develop descent and realizations for finite locally free prismatic F-crystals and their Laurent analogues. The integral crystalline lattice equivalence uses analytic continuation, almost Galois descent and period-theoretic inputs; its mod-p analogue fails.

<a id="layer-7-beilinson-square-foundations"></a>

### 7.0 Graded prismatic square and filtered Frobenius bundle dictionary

Construct the prismatic Beilinson square by comparing specified filtered trace objects with Layers 3 and 6. The cyclotomic trace proof, trace/prismatic and trace/syntomic identifications, and integral mixed-characteristic derived-de-Rham matching are explicit proof obligations of this target, not conclusions supplied by a graph or by the mod-p DD.4 comparison. The trace constructions, circle actions, finite-group Tate maps, perfectoid coefficients and quasiregular evenness are supplied by AInfCohomology AI.7.2, specifically *Topological Hochschild homology as a cyclotomic spectrum*, *Circle actions, homotopy fixed points and Tate constructions*, *Quasisyntomic unfolding of the trace coefficient sheaf*, *Absolute trace comparison with AΩ* and *Characteristic-p trace and crystalline comparison*. Use their actual cyclotomic Frobenius, not an endomorphism chosen after computing homotopy groups. This target adds the absolute trace–prismatic comparison, the graded rational square and the filtered Frobenius bundle dictionary used below.

**Absolute trace–prismatic comparison.** Write D̂^tr_S for the unfolded trace coefficient complex of AI.7.2; for a quasiregular semiperfectoid S it is π₀TC⁻(S;Z_p)≃π₀TP(S;Z_p). Prove a natural equivalence

```text
D̂^tr_S ≃ Δ̂_S,
```

of Nygaard-filtered E∞-algebras, preserving the coefficient twist, can and cyclotomic/divided Frobenius. On quasiregular semiperfectoid S this gives the functorial δ-structure on D̂^tr_S of BS22 Theorem 13.1, including when S has p-torsion. The comparison is then unfolded to all quasisyntomic rings. A statement only for p-torsion-free S would not suffice: R/p occurs in the square.

Here is the construction before completion. Fix a perfectoid base B→S with A=A_inf(B) and d generating its prism ideal. For p-completed smooth B-algebras, take the trace complex of AI.7.2 and then left Kan extend in derived (p,d)-complete A-complexes, obtaining D^tr_nc(S). Carry its Nygaard filtration through the same extension. Smooth Hodge–Tate comparison follows from the supplied trace–AΩ comparison and AI.4’s Hodge–Tate specialization; extension gives the conjugate filtration with graded pieces (∧^iL_(S/B))^∧_p[−i]. Thus D^tr_nc is a quasisyntomic sheaf, discrete on the quasiregular semiperfectoid basis, with N^{≥i}={x:φ(x)∈d^iD^tr_nc}, and its Nygaard completion is D̂^tr. Modulo the de Rham parameter, smooth derived de Rham cohomology is already Hodge-complete after p-completion; this justifies starting from the completed trace theory before Kan extension, rather than claiming uncompleted and completed theories agree for all S. (BMS2 Construction 7.12, p.48, Proposition 7.13, pp.48–49; BS22 proof of Theorem 13.1, pp.95–96.)

On regular semiperfectoid quotients use André’s root covers and the Künneth formula to reduce to B=Z_p[ζ_(p^∞)]^∧ and S=B⟨X^(1/p^∞)⟩/(X). The q-divided-power recognition map of [§3.26](#layer-3-bms2-comparison) gives Δ_S→D^tr_nc(S), compatible with φ and the Nygaard ideals. It is an equivalence: after A→A_crys(B/p) both sides are the characteristic-p crystalline theory of AI.7.2, with its actual comparison map, and A/(p,d) factors through that coefficient ring. Derived Nakayama applies to the two (p,d)-complete complexes. Descent on the regular root covers and polynomial left Kan extension extend the equivalence to all S. Finally [§3.26](#layer-3-bms2-comparison) extends δ to the Nygaard completion and identifies the filtrations and Frobenius there. This proves the assertion without reconstructing δ by division by p on a ring with p-torsion. ([BS22](#ref-bs22), Theorem 13.1 and its proof, pp.94–96; [BMS2](#ref-bms2), Construction 7.12, p.48, Corollary 9.12, pp.73–74, and Theorem 8.17, pp.62–64.)

Define `Prismatic.Trace.TC(R)` to be fib(can−φ:TC⁻(R;Z_p)→TP(R;Z_p)) in spectra. Give it the multiplicative filtration obtained by unfolding the double-speed Postnikov filtrations on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings and taking the filtered fibre. Construct, with the trace–prismatic equivalence above,

```text
gr^n TC⁻(R;Z_p) ≃ N^{≥n}Δ̂_R{n}[2n],
gr^n TP(R;Z_p)  ≃ Δ̂_R{n}[2n],
gr^n TC(R;Z_p)  ≃ Z_p(n)(R)[2n].
```

The first two are identifications of the AI.7.2 filtrations, not new definitions of the prismatic complexes. Their maps are respectively the canonical inclusion and divided Frobenius. In the last line the order can−φ differs by a minus sign from [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex); multiply the target term by −1 to identify the two fibres. Twists descend as invertible filtered coefficient modules; no orientation of every prism is chosen. These assertions hold for all quasisyntomic R, including characteristic p, and respect multiplication and finite coefficients. [§6.11](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes) identifies the same syntomic fibre before and after Nygaard completion. ([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Theorem 1.12(3)–(5), pp.6–7, Proposition 7.13 and §7.4, pp.48–52; [BL22](#ref-bl22), Proposition 7.4.6, pp.178–179.)

The API is `Prismatic.Trace.noncompletedComparison`, `nygaardCompletedComparison`, `deltaCompatibility`, `gradedTCMinus`, `gradedTP`, `gradedTC` and `gradedTC_can_phi`, with naturality, twist, cup-product and mod-p^r compatibility. The relative sphere-polynomial/Breuil–Kisin version is the separate supplied *Trace and prismatic Breuil–Kisin agreement* of AI.7.3; it is not reconstructed here.

**Checks.**

- On a perfectoid B the completed comparison is A_inf(B) with its coefficient Frobenius; in characteristic p it is W(B). For B=F_p, weight-zero TC has π₀=π_(−1)=Z_p, as does the two-term syntomic complex with zero differential. Losing the fibre shift would remove the second group.
- In weight one over a perfectoid base, the source is φ^(−1)(d)A, and its map is φ/d−can. Replacing this by φ−1 on A gives the wrong twist.
- For the key semiperfectoid quotient the q-divided-power basis maps to its prescribed trace basis; reduction to A/(p,d) is the crystalline comparison. Equality of two unnamed reductions is insufficient.
- For a smooth torus the unfolded coefficient object has differential-form cohomology. It is not obtained by taking the discrete π₀ of its global TC⁻ spectrum.
- The zero ring gives zero throughout. Negative-weight graded TC vanishes by Layer 6’s low-weight syntomic theorem, while the coefficient TP theory still has negative graded pieces.

**Linear cyclic theory and the rational trace square.** For a commutative ring R let HH(R/Z;Z_p) be the derived p-completion of the cyclic bar construction relative to HZ, with its circle action. Define HC=HH_(hT), HC⁻=HH^(hT) and HP=HH^(tT), taking the derived p-completion in each theory; the circle norm triangle is

```text
Σ HC(R;Z_p) → HC⁻(R;Z_p) → HP(R;Z_p).
```

Here the suspension in the circle norm is the real dimension of the circle. The map THH→HH is the relative-bar base change THH(R)⊗_(THH(Z))HZ, not the generally different tensor THH(R)⊗_𝕊HZ. Give HC⁻ and HP their complete multiplicative filtrations from quasisyntomic unfolding. Prove gr^nHC⁻≃(Fil_H^n LΩ̂_R)[2n] and gr^nHP≃LΩ̂_R[2n], where the hat denotes both Hodge and p-adic completion. On a p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, HC⁻, HP and HC have only even homotopy groups and these formulas identify their homotopy groups. Derive this from the HKR filtration of DD.2, the quasiregular cotangent amplitude and the circle fixed-point/Tate spectral sequences of AI.7.2. ([BMS2](#ref-bms2), Theorem 1.17, p.9, Lemma 5.14 and its proof, pp.34–35; §2.2, pp.13–15.)

Prove `Prismatic.Trace.rationalBeilinson`: for every ordinary commutative R the trace maps give a functorial pullback square

```text
TC(R;Q_p)     → TC(R/p;Q_p)
    ↓                  ↓
HC⁻(R;Q_p)   → HP(R;Q_p).
```

All four Q_p theories mean derived p-completion followed by inversion of p. In particular the relative fibre of the top row is ΣHC(R;Q_p), and its relative cofibre is Σ²HC(R;Q_p). Supply the bounded-denominator refinement: in each fixed finite homotopy range the relative comparison is a natural zigzag whose kernels and cokernels are killed by a power of p depending only on that range, uniformly in R. This uniformity is needed for Kan extension below.

Use the internal cyclotomic proof, which introduces no algebraic K-theory dependency. The connective map R⊗_𝕊F_p→R/p is a degreewise quasi-isogeny, with an isomorphism on π₀. The cyclic-bar filtration and finite Postnikov towers show that such a map induces a quasi-isogeny in cyclotomic spectra: a positive graded square-zero layer has Frobenius raising its weight by p, hence eventually zero on every fixed finite weight truncation; the fixed-point tower then reduces to a finite product of bounded-torsion terms in any given degree range. Increasing connectivity of the higher weight pieces permits passage to the limit. Resolve a general connective extension by its split square-zero Čech nerve. This proves the required special case of AMMN Theorem 3.4, including its uniform bounds, using only bar realizations, Tate constructions and Postnikov limits. Compare the relative cyclotomic object with HH(R/Z;Z_p) carrying zero cyclotomic Frobenius. The sphere-to-HZ map and THH(Z)→HZ are quasi-isogenies in bounded ranges, and HH(R/p;Z_p) is killed by p. The Tate-orbit lemma makes the Frobenius zero on the intermediate orbit object. Taking TC of a zero-Frobenius object is its suspended circle homotopy orbits. This gives the relative comparison; the norm triangle gives the displayed square and both suspensions. ([AMMN22](#ref-ammn22), Theorem 2.20 and Lemmas 2.21–2.23, pp.12–14; Theorem 3.4, Propositions 3.3–3.7, pp.15–17; Corollary 3.9 and Theorem 3.10, pp.18–19; Remark 2.25, p.14, for uniformity. The proof uses the cyclotomic argument of §3 in place of the K-theoretic argument for Proposition 2.22.)

The API is `Prismatic.Trace.HH`, `HC`, `HCMinus`, `HP`, `circleNormTriangle`, `linearization`, `cyclicHKRFiltration`, `cyclicGraded`, `rationalBeilinson` and `relativeComparison_boundedDenominators`. Circle constructions are the supplied AI.7.2 operations applied to this relative-bar object; these names do not introduce duplicate spectral constructions.

**Checks.**

- The cyclic bar of the base Z relative to itself is HZ. Its p-completed HC⁻ has one Z_p in every nonpositive even homotopy degree, HP one in every even degree, and HC one in every nonnegative even degree. The norm triangle has ΣHC on its left, so the cofibre of HC⁻→HP is Σ²HC.
- For R=F_p the top map of the rational square is the identity, so HC⁻(F_p;Q_p)→HP(F_p;Q_p) is an equivalence. The rational cyclic homotopy-orbit term vanishes; this does not assert that homotopy fixed points or Tate fixed points vanish. Inverting p before those infinite limits is invalid. TC(F_p;Q_p) itself is nonzero, so rationalizing the input ring before p-completed TC also gives the wrong theory.
- At the zero ring all four corners and the relative comparison vanish. At p=2 the same rational statement holds; no low-degree integral isomorphism range is asserted.
- The coefficient in homotopy degree 2n of Σ²HC is HC_(2n−2), not HC_(2n). For n=0 this is zero on a connective base.

**Prismatic Beilinson square.** Let R be p-torsion-free and quasisyntomic and n≥0. With Q_p(n)=Z_p(n)[1/p] from Layer 6 and LΩ_R the p-completed derived de Rham complex over Z_p with its Hodge filtration, construct χ_n and prove that

```text
Q_p(n)(R)             → Q_p(n)(R/p)
   ↓                         ↓ χ_n
(Fil_H^n LΩ_R)[1/p]   → LΩ_R[1/p]
```

is a natural cartesian square in D(Q_p). Here LΩ is not Hodge-completed. A power of p depending only on n clears denominators in χ_n before inversion. The associated cofibre is (LΩ_R/Fil_H^n LΩ_R)[1/p].

To prove it, restrict to p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid R, where R/p is again quasisyntomic. Apply the preceding rational trace square and its bounded-denominator refinement. Since the bottom cyclic terms are even, the homotopy window [2n−1,2n] preserves this pullback. Shift by −2n and use `gradedTC`, including on R/p, to obtain first the square with Hodge-completed derived de Rham complexes. Unfold on the quasisyntomic basis. The syntomic functors of [§6.11](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes) are left Kan extended from finite p-completed polynomial algebras, including the functor R↦Z_p(n)(R/p). On these polynomials, Hodge and p-adic completion agree in the required de Rham theory. Restrict the map with its single uniform denominator and left Kan extend to get χ_n valued in LΩ, retaining the prescribed comparison to its Hodge completion. The relative comparison with ΣHC identifies the cofibre with the finite Hodge quotient LΩ/Fil_H^n, which agrees with its Hodge-completed quotient. Hence this refined square is cartesian too; cartesianness is not deduced by applying rationalization to an infinite totalization. ([AMMN22](#ref-ammn22), Construction 6.16 and Theorem 6.17 with proof, pp.44–45; the syntomic Kan extension input is [§6.11](#layer-6-syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes).)

For p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid R and n>0, prove that χ_n is injective on H⁰, with image exactly A_crys(R/p)[1/p]^(φ=p^n) inside LΩ_R[1/p]. The identification with the standard inclusion of the eigenspace can differ by a nonzero scalar depending on n; no integral normalization is asserted. The comparison is Frobenius compatible: Frobenius acts on Z_p(n) in characteristic p by p^n, as follows from [§6.16](#layer-6-acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective)’s crystalline syntomic calculation and descent. The natural transformation χ_n descends to the characteristic-p input through the completed de Rham–Witt functor, by the Frobenius-equivariant lifting argument of AMMN Corollary B.4. Its multiplicative endomorphism on the syntomic eigenspaces is scalar in each weight: weight one is corepresented on the semiperfect basis by F_p[x^(1/p^∞)]/(x−1); logarithmic de Rham–Witt classes are locally products of weight-one Kummer classes, so multiplicativity gives λ^n. The scalar in weight one is nonzero: take R=O_C. Its weight-one syntomic complex is Q_p(1) in degree zero by the Kummer calculation of [§6.16](#layer-6-acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective). The square already proved therefore makes Q_p(1)(O_C/p)→(LΩ_R/Fil_H¹)[1/p]=C surjective. Since C≠0, χ₁ cannot vanish. Thus λ≠0. This proves the image assertion, rather than merely its containment. ([AMMN22](#ref-ammn22), Propositions 6.18 and 6.21, Lemma 6.19 and Corollary 6.20, pp.45–46; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Proposition 6.8, p.22.)

Also construct `Prismatic.Beilinson.integralDeRhamMatch`: for p-torsion-free QRSP R, the p-completed integral derived-de-Rham object over Z_p is A_crys(R/p), with Hodge filtration and the characteristic-p reduction maps used above; extend on the qsyn basis and match the trace-defined and prismatic syntomic maps. DD.4 only supplies the mod-p calculation. The proof must identify the comparison maps before derived Nakayama or descent; equality of graded terms alone does not do so. The API is `Prismatic.Beilinson.chi`, `chi_boundedDenominator`, `square`, `cofibre`, `chi_characteristicP_natural`, `chi_frobenius`, `chi_eigenspaceImage` and `chi_scalarNonzero`. The last two require n>0; all square and cofibre maps retain their functorial commutative diagrams.
