### 7.1 Almost sections of the Galois product

In the perfect-residue notation of PadicPeriodRings §§4.2–4.3 and FiniteFlatGroups §R07.3.3 let R=O_C⊗̂_{O_K}O_C and S=R_perfd, taking O_C as base through the first factor. Put A_inf=W(O_C^♭) and I=ker θ̃. Prove the following functorial Frobenius-compatible comparisons.

- `GaloisProduct.perfectoidization_sections`: The pairing x⊗y↦(g↦xg(y)) induces an almost isomorphism S→Cont(G_K,O_C), for the almost ideal m_C⊂O_C.
- `GaloisProduct.witt_sections`: It induces an almost isomorphism Δ_{R,perf}→Cont(G_K,A_inf), for the idempotent ideal generated by [a], a∈m_{C^♭}. The function ring uses the (p,I)-adic topology on A_inf.
- `GaloisProduct.laurent_sections`: After derived I-inversion and p-completion the second comparison is an isomorphism. With the same order of operations, this holds on the iterated tensor-product Čech nerve, where G_K is replaced by G_K^n. Thus descent of a lattice after Laurent realization is continuous Galois descent.

First S is a discrete integral perfectoid ring by [§2.29](#layer-2-integral-perfectoidization): R is the p-completion of the filtered union of the integral O_C-algebras O_C⊗_{O_K}O_L, with L/K finite inside K̄. Use [§2.28](#layer-2-perfect-site-arc-comparison) for its universal property, arc description and independence of the chosen perfectoid base. The unit R→S induces an isomorphism on generic diamonds: a map from R to an integral model of a perfectoid test object factors uniquely through its universal perfectoidization. This is an assertion about generic diamonds, not an equality R[1/p]=S[1/p] of raw rings. The product property in [§6.2](#layer-6-formal-generic-v-descent) and the pro-étale Galois torsor Spa(C)→Spa(K) identify this diamond with G_K×Spa(C).

For an integral perfectoid O_C-algebra U, the map U→U_tf removing pseudouniformizer torsion is an almost isomorphism: the compatible-root annihilator lemma of [PerfectoidQuotients §§0.4–0.5](#pq-consequences) shows that its kernel is killed by every sufficiently small compatible root, hence by m_C. The torsion-free quotient is p-root closed in U_tf[1/p]. Its map to the powerbounded ring U_tf^∘ is almost an isomorphism. Indeed, if z is powerbounded, some p^N z^m lies in U_tf for every m; with m=p^r, root closedness gives p^{N/p^r}z∈U_tf, and these scalars generate the almost ideal. Apply v-almost acyclicity of O^+ to Spa(U_tf[1/p],U_tf^∘). Therefore U→RΓ_v(Spa(U[1/p]),O^+) is an almost isomorphism, including vanishing of the higher cohomology. Applying this to S, and then using the Galois-product identification, gives the first comparison, because the integral functions on that affinoid perfectoid profinite product are Cont(G_K,O_C). The structural map is the displayed pairing, as seen on every finite Galois quotient.

Pass to tilts by reducing modulo p and taking the inverse Frobenius limit; almost-zero kernels, cokernels and derived limits remain almost zero for this compatible-root ideal. Finite Witt vectors have their Verschiebung filtrations with successive Frobenius twists of the tilt; induction gives the Witt-length comparisons, and their inverse limit gives Δ_{R,perf}=A_inf(S)→Cont(G_K,A_inf). The ideal J=([a]:a∈m_{C^♭}) is idempotent, since each generator has compatible p-power roots. Witt vectors commute with the relevant limits of continuous functions, with the specified (p,I)-adic topology. Finally choose d generating I. Modulo p its image is a nonzero element of m_{C^♭}, so d∈J+(p). A J-annihilated module reduced modulo p^n is killed by d^n; its I-localization vanishes. Apply this to the cone of the Witt comparison, then take the derived inverse limit over n. This proves the exact Laurent comparison without treating an almost isomorphism as an integral one. Repeating the argument for n+1 tensor factors gives the Čech compatibility and continuous Galois cocycle law.

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), §6.4, pp.26–27, for the Galois product and its presentation; [BS22](#ref-bs22), Corollary 8.12, pp.68–69, and Theorem 10.11, pp.82–83, for the local perfectoidization inputs; [ECD](#ref-ecd), Proposition 8.8, p.43, for v-almost acyclicity. The generic-diamond product is constructed in [§6.2](#layer-6-formal-generic-v-descent).)

*Needs:* [§2.29](#layer-2-integral-perfectoidization), [§2.28](#layer-2-perfect-site-arc-comparison), [§6.2](#layer-6-formal-generic-v-descent), [PerfectoidQuotients §§0.4–0.5](#pq-consequences), `PerfectoidSpaces:P0`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P5`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/higher-v-acyclicity`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-is-a-spatial-diamond`, Mathlib `WittVector`.

**Checks.**

- `GaloisProduct.degree_zero`: On the identity Galois element the pairing is multiplication x⊗y↦xy; reversing the two projections changes the cocycle convention and must be tracked.
- `GaloisProduct.finite_quotient`: For a finite Galois quotient H, the generic function algebra is ∏_(h∈H)C and its integral function ring is ∏_(h∈H)O_C, with the permutation descent action.
- `GaloisProduct.almost_not_integral`: The map before I-inversion is asserted almost. An element killed by all [a] may be nonzero, so it cannot be discarded in an integral lattice argument.
- `GaloisProduct.inversion_order`: Exactness is obtained on the cone modulo p^n after I-inversion, and then by the derived limit. Omitting either inversion or completion does not follow from this proof.
- `GaloisProduct.nerve`: On three tensor factors the two descriptions of the coface pairing give (g,h)↦xg(y)gh(z), so the comparison retains the descent cocycle.

<a id="layer-7-prismatic-crystal"></a>

### 7.2 Prismatic crystals in vector bundles and in perfect complexes

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. A prismatic crystal in vector bundles on X is an object of Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) := lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A): a rule E giving a finite projective A-module E(A) for every bounded prism (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, and for every map of prisms f: (A, I) → (B, J) over X an isomorphism of B-modules c_f: E(A) ⊗_A B ≅ E(B), with c_id = id and c_{g∘f} = c_g ∘ (c_f ⊗_B C) for (A,I) → (B,J) → (C,K). Equivalently the c_f are given by f-semilinear maps E(A) → E(B), functorial in f, each exhibiting E(B) as the base change of E(A). A morphism E → E′ is a family of A-linear maps E(A) → E′(A) commuting with the transition maps. In the same way D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ) := lim D_perf(A) (a limit of ∞-categories, transition functors B ⊗^L_A −), and for the two sheaves of O_Δ-algebras O′ = O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ} (value A[1/p]^∧_I, the I-adic completion of A[1/p]) and O′ = O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p (value A[1/I]^∧_p, the p-adic completion of the ring A[1/I] of functions on Spec A ∖ V(I)) one puts Vect(X_Δ, O′) := lim Vect(O′(A)) and D_perf(X_Δ, O′) := lim D_perf(O′(A)). Structure: the unit O_Δ (A ↦ A); tensor product (E ⊗ E′)(A) = E(A) ⊗_A E′(A) and duals E^∨(A) = Hom_A(E(A), A), making Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) rigid symmetric monoidal; the evaluation functors ev_{(A,I)}: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(A); the pullback g^*: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(Y_Δ, O_Δ) along g: Y → X, (g^*E)(A, I, Spf(A/I) → Y) = E(A, I, Spf(A/I) → Y → X); and base change Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O′), E ↦ (A ↦ E(A) ⊗_A O′(A)).

a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of Layer 0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of Layer 4: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme; no boundedness or quasi-syntomicity is needed for the definition. In the version read (arXiv v2) the definition is the displayed formula opening §4, the sheaf-theoretic notions are Notation 2.1, and their agreement is Proposition 2.7 ([§7.3](#layer-7-crystal-descent)). Completions: A[1/p]^∧_I is the classical I-adic completion; it agrees with the derived one because I is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor of A[1/p]. A[1/I]^∧_p is the derived p-completion; it is the classical completion whenever A[1/I] has bounded p^∞-torsion (for instance A p-torsion-free: transversal, perfect and Breuil–Kisin prisms), but not for every bounded prism. For Vect the two give the same category lim_n Vect(A[1/I]/p^n); for D_perf the derived completion is meant.

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Section 4, opening display; p.12; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Notation 2.1; p. 5; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Definition 2.3; p. 5.)

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.FCrystal.IsBaseChangeAlong`: An additive map t: M → N that is semilinear over a ring map g: R → S exhibits N as S ⊗_R M: every g-semilinear map from M to an S-module factors uniquely through t by an S-linear map.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal`: A crystal in vector bundles over a diagram of rings O: C → CommRing: finite projective O(c)-modules M(c) with functorial semilinear transition maps that are base changes.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.Hom`: A morphism of crystals: O(c)-linear maps M(c) → M′(c) commuting with the transition maps.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.unit`: The unit crystal c ↦ O(c), with transition maps the ring maps.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.tensor`: The tensor product of two crystals, with (E ⊗ E′)(c) ≅ E(c) ⊗_{O(c)} E′(c).
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.pullback`: Restriction of a crystal along a functor D → C; for D = Y_Δ → C = X_Δ this is g^*.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.baseChange`: Base change of a crystal along a map of diagrams of rings O → O′, with values O′(c) ⊗_{O(c)} E(c).
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.Iso`: An isomorphism of crystals: a pair of mutually inverse morphisms.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.Crystal.dual`: The dual crystal has E^∨(A)=Hom_A(E(A),A); base-change compatibility follows from finite projectivity. Evaluation and coevaluation satisfy the triangle identities, making crystals rigid symmetric monoidal.

**Proof route.** Take compatible semilinear families, whose cocycle condition is their transition compatibility. Finite projective base change preserves tensor products and duals, giving the monoidal category; restriction along the formal-map site functor gives pullback and evaluation. Prism rigidity identifies the ideals under base change and therefore gives the two localized-completed coefficient functors.

**Checks.**

- `pr7_crystal_unit_eval`: The unit crystal has value O(c) at every object c.
- `pr7_crystal_base_change_id`: The identity of a module exhibits it as its own base change along the identity ring map.
- `pr7_crystal_initial_object_eval`: If the diagram C has an initial object c₀ (as the category of prisms over Spf(R) does for R quasiregular semiperfectoid, with c₀ = Δ_R), every O(c₀)-linear map E(c₀) → E′(c₀) extends uniquely to a morphism of crystals.
- `pr7_crystal_hodge_tate_quotient_not_projective`: For a prism (A, I) with I ≠ A the A-module A/I is not projective, so A ↦ A/I, although compatible with base change, is not a crystal in vector bundles.

- The unit crystal evaluates to A on every prism. For X = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid, evaluation at Δ_R is an equivalence Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect(Δ_R) ([§7.12](#layer-7-f-crystals-over-qrsp)). The rule A ↦ A/I is compatible with base change but is not a crystal in vector bundles.

<a id="layer-7-crystal-descent"></a>

### 7.3 Descent for prismatic crystals

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. (1) The assignment (A, I) ↦ Vect(A) on X_Δ is a sheaf of categories for the flat topology, and the natural functor lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) to vector bundles on the ringed topos (Shv(X_Δ), O_Δ) (locally of the form P ⊗ O for P finite projective) is an equivalence; the same holds with D_perf in place of Vect. (2) The same two statements hold for O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ} and O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p. (3) Čech form: if (B, J) ∈ X_Δ covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ) and (B^•, J^•) is its Čech nerve (the cosimplicial prism of iterated coproducts in the category of prisms over X), then Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ lim(Vect(B^0) ⇉ Vect(B^1) ⇶ Vect(B^2)): a crystal is a finite projective B-module M with an isomorphism p_1^*M ≅ p_2^*M over B^1 satisfying the cocycle condition over B^2; likewise for the two completed sheaves and for D_perf (with the full cosimplicial limit).

a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of Layer 0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of Layer 4: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. In (3) the Čech nerve exists whenever the iterated coproducts exist in the category of bounded prisms over X; this is checked for the two covers of Spf(O_K) in [§7.13](#layer-7-breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers). The input for (2) is the Drinfeld–Mathew theorem (the source's Theorem 2.2, Mathew, Faithfully flat descent of almost perfect complexes in rigid geometry, Theorem 5.8): for a connective E_∞-ring R and a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ π_0 R the functors S ↦ D_perf, D^-_coh, Vect of Spec(S^∧_I) ∖ V(IS) are sheaves for the I-completely flat topology. It is required from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1.

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Proposition 2.7 and its proof; p. 6; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Theorem 2.2; p. 5; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Example 2.8; p. 7.)

*Needs:* [§7.2](#layer-7-prismatic-crystal), [§2.27](#layer-2-finite-projective-descent-prisms), [§4.1](#layer-4-absolute-prismatic-site), [§1.1](#layer-1-prismatic-structure-sheaf), [§0.27](#layer-0-bounded-prism-complete-flatness), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`.

**Proof route.** At each (p,I)-adic quotient apply faithfully flat descent, then use finite-projective complete effectivity to pass to the limit; the same argument handles perfect complexes. For localized-completed coefficients reduce along the remaining ideal and apply the Drinfeld–Mathew descent input, detecting vector bundles among perfect objects on that reduction. Čech descent for the resulting sheaf of categories gives the comparison, with its 2-truncation sufficient for vector-bundle descent.

**Checks.**

- X = Spf(O_K) and the Breuil–Kisin prism: a crystal is a finite free 𝔖-module with a descent isomorphism over 𝔖^(1) and the cocycle condition over 𝔖^(2). For a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms A → B the sequence Vect(A) → Vect(B) ⇉ Vect(B ⊗̂_A B) is an equaliser of categories. The statement for O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p does not follow from flat descent of modules alone: A[1/I]^∧_p → B[1/I]^∧_p is not flat in general, and Drinfeld–Mathew is used.

### 7.4 Crystals on the prismatic site and on the quasi-syntomic site

Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme, X_qsyn its quasi-syntomic site and X_qrsp ⊂ X_qsyn the full subcategory of Spf(R) → X with R quasiregular semiperfectoid; Δ_• is the sheaf of rings R ↦ Δ_R on X_qsyn (defined on X_qrsp) and I ⊂ Δ_• its ideal sheaf. (1) lim_{R ∈ X_qrsp} Vect(Δ_R) ≃ Vect(X_qsyn, Δ_•). (2) There is a natural equivalence Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect(X_qsyn, Δ_•), induced by pullback along the map of ringed topoi ν: (Shv(X_Δ), O_Δ) → (Shv(X_qsyn), Δ_•) determined by R ↦ Δ_R. (3) Both statements hold with D_perf in place of Vect, and with (O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ}, Δ_•[1/p]^∧_I) or (O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p, Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p) in place of (O_Δ, Δ_•). (4) Concretely, for X = Spf(R) affine and R → S a quasi-syntomic cover with S quasiregular semiperfectoid, with p-completed Čech nerve S^•, both sides are lim Vect(Δ_{S^•}).

a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of Layer 0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of Layer 4: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is quasi-syntomic (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5). For R in X_qrsp the prism Δ_R is bounded. The topos Shv(X_qsyn) equals Shv(X_qrsp) (BMS2 Proposition 4.31, Variant 4.35; DD.5).

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Proposition 2.14 and its proof; p. 8; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Proposition 2.13; p. 7; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Definition 2.9; p. 7.)

*Needs:* [§7.3](#layer-7-crystal-descent), [§7.2](#layer-7-prismatic-crystal), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§2.15](#layer-2-quasisyntomic-descent), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

**Proof route.** On affine QRSP charts the initial-prism adjunction makes Δ preserve finite nonempty coproducts, and a qsyn cover maps to a covering prism. The qsyn Čech nerve and the prismatic Čech nerve therefore give the same module-category limit. Common refinements or the site pullback give independence, and complete-flat descent gives the coefficient variants.

**Checks.**

- X = Spf(O_K): Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ lim(Vect(A_inf) ⇉ Vect(Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C}) ⇶ Vect(Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C ⊗̂ O_C})), completed tensor products over O_K. For X = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid both sides are Vect(Δ_R).

<a id="layer-7-f-crystal-over-prism"></a>

### 7.5 F-crystals over a single prism

Let (A, I) be a prism with Frobenius φ, and let A[1/I] be the ring of functions on Spec A ∖ V(I): the initial A-algebra L with IL = L (it is A[1/d] when I = (d)). The category Vect^φ(A) of F-crystals over (A, I) has objects the pairs (M, φ_M) with M a finite projective A-module and φ_M: (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I] an isomorphism of A[1/I]-modules, where φ^*M = A ⊗_{φ,A} M and N[1/I] = A[1/I] ⊗_A N; equivalently φ_M is a φ-semilinear map M → M[1/I] whose A[1/I]-linearisation is bijective. Morphisms are A-linear maps f: M → M′ with φ_{M′} ∘ φ^*f = f ∘ φ_M after inverting I. (M, φ_M) is effective when φ_M carries φ^*M into M. Tensor product and duals are those of the underlying modules with φ_M ⊗ φ_{M′} and (φ_M^∨)^{-1}; the unit is (A, φ). A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) induces the base change Vect^φ(A) → Vect^φ(B), M ↦ M ⊗_A B. For an A-algebra A′ with a compatible Frobenius (such as A[1/I]^∧_p, A[1/p], A⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) the category Vect^φ(A′) is defined in the same way.

(A, I) is a prism (PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.2); boundedness is not needed for the definition. Objects of Vect^φ(𝔖) for the Breuil–Kisin prism (𝔖, (E(u))) are Breuil–Kisin modules; the effective ones with finite free M are the modules of finite E-height Mod^φ_{/𝔖} of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/kisin-modules. Objects of Vect^φ(A_inf) are the finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules of AInfCohomology:AI.2 ([§7.14](#layer-7-bkf-modules-comparison)). No bound on the poles or zeros of φ_M along I is part of the data; this is why the notion is adequate only for finite locally free coefficients ([§7.27](#layer-7-mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails)).

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Definition 4.1; p. 12; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Example 4.3; p. 12.)

- `Prismatic.FCrystal.IsAwayIdeal`: An A-algebra L is A[1/I]: IL = L and L is initial among A-algebras with this property.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism`: An F-crystal over a prism: a finite projective module M with a φ-semilinear map M → L ⊗_A M that is a base change along A → A → L.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism.Hom`: A morphism of F-crystals over a prism: an A-linear map commuting with the Frobenius structures.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism.IsEffective`: The Frobenius carries M into the image of M in L ⊗_A M.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism.unit`: The unit F-crystal (A, φ).
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.OverPrism.baseChange`: Base change of an F-crystal along a map of prisms, with underlying module B ⊗_A M. The source and target coefficient algebras are required to satisfy IsAwayIdeal for I and J; their universal properties give the coefficient map.

**Proof route.** Localize by the invertible ideal, intrinsically the filtered colimit of I^−n and locally A[1/d]. A semilinear map with invertible localized linearization gives the stated Frobenius datum. Commutation with base Frobenius and rigidity IB=J give its base-change formula.

- `pr7_over_prism_away_principal`: If I = (d) then Mathlib's Localization.Away d is A[1/I].
- `pr7_over_prism_unit_effective`: The unit F-crystal is effective.
- `pr7_over_prism_rank_one_scaling`: On the free module of rank one, x ↦ u ⊗ φ(x) is a Frobenius structure for every unit u of A[1/I] (over the Breuil–Kisin prism, u = c·E(u)^n); it is effective when u is the image of an element of A.

Over a crystalline prism (A, (p)) an F-crystal is a finite projective A-module with an isomorphism φ^*M[1/p] ≅ M[1/p]. The zero map is not a Frobenius structure on a module with M[1/I] ≠ 0.

<a id="layer-7-prismatic-f-crystal"></a>

### 7.6 Prismatic F-crystals on a p-adic formal scheme

Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. A prismatic F-crystal (of vector bundles) on X is a pair (E, φ_E) with E ∈ Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) and φ_E: (φ^*E)[1/I_Δ] ≅ E[1/I_Δ] an isomorphism of crystals over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]; that is, an F-crystal structure φ_{E(A)} on each E(A) ([§7.5](#layer-7-f-crystal-over-prism)) such that the transition isomorphisms E(A) ⊗_A B ≅ E(B) are isomorphisms in Vect^φ(B). Morphisms are morphisms of crystals commuting with φ_E. The category is Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) = lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect^φ(A). (E, φ_E) is effective when φ_E carries φ^*E into E. Tensor products make Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) rigid symmetric monoidal with unit (O_Δ, φ); g: Y → X induces g^*: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect^φ(Y_Δ, O_Δ). For a sheaf O′ of O_Δ-algebras with a compatible Frobenius, Vect^φ(X_Δ, O′) is defined in the same way, and a prismatic F-crystal of perfect complexes is E ∈ D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ) with φ^*E[1/I_Δ] ≃ E[1/I_Δ]. Example: the Breuil–Kisin twist O_Δ{1} of Layer 3 is an invertible prismatic F-crystal on Spf(Z_p), hence by pullback on every bounded X, with φ^*O_Δ{1} ≅ I_Δ^{-1} ⊗ O_Δ{1}; O_Δ{n} = O_Δ{1}^{⊗n} for n ∈ Z.

a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of Layer 0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of Layer 4: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme for the definition; the twist O_Δ{1} is used on bounded X. Finite locally free F-crystals do not classify torsion or derived Galois representations: the source states that with Z/p^n-coefficients or in the derived category the correct objects should also bound the zeros and poles of φ_E along I_Δ (perfect complexes on Drinfeld's stack Σ″, F-gauges). The classification of F-gauges lies outside this roadmap.

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Definition 4.1; p. 12; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Remark 4.2; p. 12; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Example 4.5; p. 12; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Introduction, footnote to Theorem 1.2; p. 2.)

- `Prismatic.FCrystal.SiteData`: The category of bounded prisms over X with the diagrams of rings O_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ] and O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p and the Frobenius of the last.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.SiteData.restrict`: Restriction of the data along a functor, as for Y_Δ → X_Δ.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal`: A prismatic F-crystal: a crystal over O_Δ with a Frobenius structure on every value, compatible with the transition maps.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.Hom`: A morphism of prismatic F-crystals.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.eval`: Evaluation at an object (A, I): an F-crystal over that prism.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.IsEffective`: Every evaluation is effective.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.PrismaticFCrystal.unit`: The unit F-crystal (O_Δ, φ).

- `pr7_fcrystal_twist_not_effective`: If some prism of the site has I ≠ A, then O_Δ{1} is not effective.
- `pr7_fcrystal_unit_effective`: The unit F-crystal is effective.

<a id="layer-7-laurent-f-crystal"></a>

### 7.7 Laurent F-crystals

Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme. For a prism (A, I) the Frobenius φ of A induces a Frobenius on the p-adic completion A[1/I]^∧_p, because φ(I) ≡ I^p modulo p. A Laurent F-crystal in vector bundles on X is an object of Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} := lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}: a crystal E of vector bundles over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p with an isomorphism φ_E: φ^*E ≅ E. In perfect complexes: D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} := lim D_perf(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, the ∞-category of pairs (E, φ_E: φ^*E ≃ E). Since I_Δ is invertible in O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p this category is Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p) in the sense of [§7.6](#layer-7-prismatic-f-crystal). The Z_p-module of Frobenius-fixed sections of E over (A, I) is E(A)^{φ=1} = {x : φ_E(x) = x}.

a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of Layer 0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of Layer 4: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is bounded: locally Spf(R) with R[p^∞] of bounded exponent (the source's Notation 3.1). The definition itself makes sense for every X; boundedness is used to speak of the generic fibre. If X has characteristic p then every prism of X_Δ has I = (p), A[1/I]^∧_p = 0, and the category is zero (the source's Remark 3.3).

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Definition 3.2; p. 9; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Remark 3.9; p. 11.)

Prove the following API:

- `Prismatic.FCrystal.LaurentRing`: The p-adic completion of A[1/I].
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.laurentFrobenius`: The Frobenius of the p-adic completion of A[1/I] induced by φ.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.LaurentFCrystal`: A crystal over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p with a φ-semilinear endomorphism of each value, bijective after linearisation and compatible with the transition maps.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.LaurentFCrystal.Hom`: A morphism of Laurent F-crystals.
- `Prismatic.FCrystal.LaurentFCrystal.fixedPoints`: The additive group of Frobenius-fixed elements of a value.

**Proof route.** Modulo p^n, φ(d) differs from d^p by a nilpotent multiple of p and is therefore invertible after inverting d. Pass to the p-adic limit to obtain its Frobenius. Localized coefficient descent identifies the crystal category with the limit of the objectwise categories with invertible Frobenius linearization.

**Checks.**

- `pr7_laurent_char_p_zero`: If p ∈ I then the p-adic completion of A[1/I] is the zero ring.
- `pr7_laurent_frobenius_extends`: The Frobenius of the completion restricts to φ on the image of A.
- `pr7_laurent_fixed_points_res`: The transition maps of a Laurent F-crystal carry Frobenius-fixed elements to Frobenius-fixed elements (over Spf(O_C) the fixed elements of the unit object are Z_p ⊂ W(C^♭)).
- `pr7_laurent_p_frobenius_non_example`: If p is not a unit of A[1/I]^∧_p, the semilinear map p·φ on the free module of rank one is not a Frobenius structure: its linearisation is multiplication by p, which is not bijective (over O_C this is the F-isocrystal of slope 1, which has no unit-root lattice).

- X = Spf(O_C), with C complete and algebraically closed of characteristic 0, the category is Vect(W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, equivalent to Vect(Z_p) by taking φ-fixed points. For X of characteristic p the category is zero. A crystal over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p[1/p] with φ^*E ≅ E is in general not a Laurent F-crystal up to isogeny: over O_C these are all F-isocrystals over C^♭, of which only those of slope 0 arise (the source's Remark 3.9).

<a id="layer-7-artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert"></a>

### 7.8 Riemann–Hilbert for F_p-local systems and invariance under completed perfection

(1) Let S be a commutative F_p-algebra. Extension of scalars along F_p → O_{Spec(S),ét} and Frobenius fixed points are mutually inverse equivalences D^b_lisse(Spec(S), F_p) ≃ D_perf(S)^{φ=1}, where D_perf(S)^{φ=1} is the ∞-category of pairs (E, α) with E a perfect complex of S-modules and α: φ^*E ≃ E, and D^b_lisse is the bounded derived category of étale F_p-sheaves with locally constant cohomology sheaves of finite rank; on hearts of vector bundles it is Katz's equivalence between F_p-local systems on Spec(S) and finite projective S-modules M with φ^*M ≅ M. Each cohomology module of such an (E, α) is finite projective. (2) Let R be an F_p-algebra with an element t such that R is derived t-complete, and S = (R_perf)^∧_t the t-completed perfection. Then the base change functors D_perf(R[1/t])^{φ=1} → D_perf(R_perf[1/t])^{φ=1} → D_perf(S[1/t])^{φ=1} are equivalences.

In (1) S is an arbitrary commutative F_p-algebra (no noetherian, normality or reducedness hypothesis). In (2) R is derived t-complete, hence henselian along t; R_perf = colim_φ R. Étale sheaves, lisse complexes, the Artin–Schreier sequence and topological invariance of the étale site are required from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.

### 7.9 Laurent F-crystals are Z_p-local systems on the generic fibre

Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme with generic fibre X_η, regarded as a locally spatial diamond. (1) For every bounded prism (A, I) with perfection (B, J), base change is an equivalence D_perf(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(B[1/J]^∧_p)^{φ=1}; hence extension of scalars is an equivalence D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(X_Δ, O_{Δ,perf}[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, the right side being the limit over perfect prisms. (2) The right side is equivalent to D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p): the full subcategory of D(X_{η,proét}, Z_p) of locally bounded, derived p-complete objects whose reduction modulo p has locally constant cohomology sheaves with finitely generated stalks. (3) On vector bundles: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Loc_{Z_p}(X_η), and after inverting p in the Hom groups, Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ⊗ Q_p ≃ Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) ⊗ Q_p. (4) For X = Spf(R) with R perfectoid, Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p = W(R^♭[1/I]) and the equivalence is M ↦ the local system of φ-fixed points on Spa(R[1/p], R). (5) For X = Spf(O_K) as in [§7.23](#layer-7-crystalline-lattices-theorem): Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_K), finite free Z_p-modules with continuous G_K-action, the representation being the φ-fixed points of the value on A_inf with the action induced by that of G_K on the object (A_inf, ker θ̃).

A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is bounded. In the source this is Corollary 3.7 (derived) and Corollary 3.8 (vector bundles); item 3.9 of the source is the remark on the two enlargements described below. The identification (2) uses that X ↦ D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p) is a sheaf of ∞-categories for the quasi-syntomic topology, by v-descent on the diamond X_η; this is required from DiamondEtaleCohomology:C2). Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) ⊗ Q_p is in general smaller than the category of pro-étale Q_p-local systems, and Vect(…)^{φ=1} ⊗ Q_p smaller than Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p[1/p])^{φ=1}; no equivalence between the enlargements is claimed (the source's Remark 3.9).

### 7.10 The étale realisation functor

For every p-adic formal scheme X the p-completed base change E ↦ E ⊗_{O_Δ} O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p, with the induced Frobenius, is a symmetric monoidal functor T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1}: on a prism (A, I) it sends (M, φ_M) to M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p with φ_M ⊗ φ, which is an isomorphism because I is invertible in the target. For X bounded, composing with the equivalence of [§7.9](#layer-7-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems) gives T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Loc_{Z_p}(X_η), the étale realisation; it preserves ranks, tensor products and duals and commutes with pullback along maps of bounded p-adic formal schemes. For F-crystals of perfect complexes the same formula gives T with values in D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p). For X = Spf(O_K), T(E) is the G_K-representation (E(A_inf) ⊗_{A_inf} W(C^♭))^{φ=1}. On twists, T(O_Δ{i}) = Z_p(i) for all i and all bounded X.

A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. The functor to Laurent F-crystals exists for every p-adic formal scheme X; the identification of its target with Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) requires X bounded. The source's Construction 4.8 says "for any p-adic formal scheme" for both and refers to Corollary 3.7; the hypothesis and the reference (Corollary 3.8 for vector bundles) are corrected here. T(O_Δ{1}) = Z_p(1) is stated in the source's Example 4.9 without proof, with a pointer to the q-logarithm of Anschütz–Le Bras and the prismatic logarithm of Bhatt–Lurie. Use, for perfectoid R, the identification of the φ-fixed elements of Fil^1_N Δ_R{1} with the Tate module T_p(R^×) (BS22 Theorem 9.4 and Remark 9.5, [§6.28](#layer-6-tate-twist-perfectoid)), which is natural in R and therefore Galois-equivariant.

<a id="layer-7-crystalline-realization"></a>

### 7.11 The crystalline and de Rham realisations

Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme, flat over Z_p, with special fibre X_{p=0}. (1) For a quasi-syntomic F_p-scheme Z every prism of Z_Δ is crystalline, I = (p), and crystals of vector bundles on Z_Δ and on the crystalline site Z_crys are identified compatibly with Frobenius; hence Vect^φ(Z_Δ, O_Δ) is the category Vect^φ(Z_crys) of F-crystals on Z_crys (finite locally free crystals E with φ^*E[1/p] ≅ E[1/p]). (2) Pullback along X_{p=0} → X gives the crystalline realisation D_crys: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect^φ(X_{p=0,crys}). (3) Forgetting the Frobenius and using that crystals on X_crys and on X_{p=0,crys} agree gives the de Rham realisation D_dR: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_crys); for X formally smooth over a base Y it gives D_{dR,Y} with values in Vect((X/Y)_crys) ≃ vector bundles on X with a topologically quasi-nilpotent flat connection relative to Y. For X = Spf(O_K): the value of D_crys(E) on the prism (W(k), (p)) of Spec(k) is the φ-module E(W(k)); it determines D_crys(E) up to isogeny only (Dwork's trick, [§7.15](#layer-7-crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal)), and D_crys(T(E)[1/p]) = E(W(k))[1/p].

A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ. X is quasi-syntomic and Z_p-flat (the source assumes flatness for simplicity). ### 7.12 F-crystals over a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring; faithfulness of the étale realisation

Let R be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with prism (Δ_R, I) and X = Spf(R). (1) (Δ_R, I) is the final object of X_Δ (the initial prism over R), so evaluation at Δ_R gives equivalences Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect^φ(Δ_R) and D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, and similarly for every sheaf of [§7.2](#layer-7-prismatic-crystal). (2) If R is p-torsion-free then (Δ_R, I) is transversal ((p, d) is a regular sequence for a generator d of I), the map Δ_R → Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p is injective, and so is M → M ⊗_{Δ_R} Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p for every finite projective Δ_R-module M. (3) Consequently the étale realisation T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} is faithful when R is p-torsion-free.

### 7.13 The Breuil–Kisin and A_inf prisms as covers of Spf(O_K), and their Čech nerves

Notation as in OK. (1) Breuil–Kisin prism: for a uniformizer π ∈ O_K with Eisenstein polynomial E(u) ∈ W[u], the prism (𝔖, (E(u))) = (W[[u]], (E(u))) with φ(u) = u^p and 𝔖/E(u) ≅ O_K, u ↦ π, is an object of X_Δ which covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ). For every (B, J) ∈ X_Δ and every lift v ∈ B of the image of π, the prismatic envelope C = B[u]{(u − v)/J}^∧_{(p,J)} is a (p, J)-completely flat δ-B-algebra, E(u)C = JC, and (C, JC) is the coproduct of (𝔖, (E)) and (B, J) in the category of prisms over X. (2) A_inf-prism: (A_inf, ker θ̃) = Δ_{O_C} with O_K → O_C is an object of X_Δ covering the final object, because O_K → O_C is a quasi-syntomic cover. (3) Čech nerves: 𝔖^{(•)}, with 𝔖^{(0)} = 𝔖 and 𝔖^{(1)} = W[[u, v]]{(u − v)/E(u)}^∧_{(p,E(u))}, in which E(v)/E(u) is a unit; each 𝔖^{(i)} is a transversal prism. The Čech nerve of A_inf is Δ_{Y^{•/X}}: its terms are Δ_R for R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} … ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, which are quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free. (4) A compatible system π̃ = (π, π^{1/p}, …) ∈ O_C^♭ of p-power roots of π (so θ([π̃]) = π and θ̃([π̃]^p) = π) gives the map of prisms over X (𝔖, (E)) → (A_inf, ker θ̃), u ↦ [π̃]^p, which on W(k) is the Frobenius of the Witt-functorial inclusion W(k) ⊂ A_inf (BMS1 §4; this is the W-algebra structure of A_inf compatible with θ̃, as in the source's Notation 5.1). It is the composite of Kisin's embedding u ↦ [π̃] with the Frobenius of A_inf, and G_K acts on the object (A_inf, ker θ̃) of X_Δ. (5) Evaluation: for a crystal E on X_Δ (over any of the sheaves of [§7.2](#layer-7-prismatic-crystal)) one has E(𝔖) ⊗_𝔖 A_inf ≅ E(A_inf), E(A_inf) carries a semilinear G_K-action, and E is equivalent to E(𝔖) with a descent datum over 𝔖^{(1)}, and to E(A_inf) with a descent datum over Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C}, each with the cocycle condition over the third term.

K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). π is a uniformizer; 𝔖 depends on π, A_inf does not. The δ-W-algebra map 𝔖 → A_inf depends on the choice of π^♭. The prisms themselves are [§0.22](#layer-0-breuil-kisin-prism) and [§0.21](#layer-0-ainf-prism); this target adds their structure as objects of X_Δ, the covering property and the Čech nerves.

### 7.16 Full faithfulness of the étale realisation over O_K

Notation as in OK. The étale realisation T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_K) is fully faithful. More precisely: (1) T is faithful over X, over Y = Spf(O_C) and over every term of the Čech nerve Y^{•/X}. (2) For a lattice T_0 in a de Rham representation V of G_K the assignment T_0 ↦ (T_0, D_dR(V) ⊗_K B_dR^+) is compatible, through the functor of Fargues' theorem, with restriction of F-crystals from X to Y and of Laurent F-crystals from X to Y. (3) For M, N ∈ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) and a morphism g: T(M) → T(N) there is a unique f: M → N with T(f) = g.

### 7.17 Period sheaves on the quasi-syntomic site of O_K

Notation as in OK. On X_qrsp (quasiregular semiperfectoid O_K-algebras R, quasi-syntomic over O_K; each Δ_R is a transversal bounded prism with ideal I) define the presheaves of rings: Δ_• (R ↦ Δ_R); A_crys = Δ_•{I/p} (R ↦ Δ_R{I/p} = Δ_{R/p} = A_crys(R)); the rational localisation Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ (R ↦ Δ_R[I/p]^∧_p, equal to Δ_R[x]/(px − d)^∧_p for a generator d of I); Δ_•{φ(I)/p} (R ↦ Δ_R{φ(I)/p}, the φ-pullback of A_crys); Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p; and the de Rham period sheaves B_dR^+ = (Δ_•[1/p])^∧_I, B_dR = B_dR^+[1/I]. They are related by natural maps Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p ← Δ_• → Δ_•{φ(I)/p} → Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ → Δ_•{I/p}. The Frobenius of Δ_• carries I to φ(I) and induces φ̃: Δ_•{I/p} → Δ_•{φ(I)/p}, linear over φ; composing with the maps above gives Frobenius endomorphisms of Δ_•, Δ_•{I/p}, Δ_•⟨I/p⟩, Δ_•{φ(I)/p} and Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p. This assertion concerns the five presheaves of Construction 6.2; it does not extend Frobenius to the I-adic completions B_dR^+ or B_dR of Construction 6.4. More generally Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ is defined for n ≥ 0, with maps Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩ → Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ and φ̃: Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ → Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩. For each of the five Frobenius-equipped rings an F-crystal is a vector bundle M with φ_M: (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I]. Lemma (the source's Lemma 6.7): for every transversal prism (A, I) and n ≥ 0 the natural map A[1/p]^∧_I → A⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p]^∧_I is an isomorphism; so B_dR^+ ≅ Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p]^∧_I for all n ≥ 0.

K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). Every R in X_qrsp is p-torsion-free, so Δ_R is transversal: (p, d) is a regular sequence ([§7.12](#layer-7-f-crystals-over-qrsp) (2)). The endomorphism φ of Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ is not a Frobenius lift: it need not be congruent to the p-th power map modulo p; forcing the congruence gives Δ_•{I/p} (the source's footnote to Construction 6.2). Δ_R{I/p} and Δ_R{φ(I)/p} are δ-envelopes, constructed in Layer 0 ([§0.16](#layer-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope): A{φ(f)/p} is the p-completed PD envelope of (f)); Δ_R{I/p} = Δ_{R/p} is PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3 for R/p. For the complete algebraically closed field C of this target, B_dR^+(O_C) is the usual discrete valuation ring (TauCetiRoadmap.PadicPeriodRings §§1.5 and 4.1, with θ̃ in place of θ). For a general perfectoid R the same completion defines a period algebra, without a discrete valuation ring assertion; for example a product of two copies of O_C gives a product of period rings.

(a) M_1 = D ⊗_{W(k)} Δ_•{I/p}, a unit F-crystal over Δ_•{I/p}[1/p] with φ induced by φ_D. (b) M_2 = M_1 ⊗_{Δ_•{I/p}, φ̃} Δ_•⟨I/p⟩, a unit F-crystal over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]. The compatible system M(D) = {M(D)_{⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩}}_{n ≥ 1} has value M(D)(Y) on Y = Spf(O_C) an F-crystal on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {p = 0}.

**Proof route.** Pull the F-isocrystal over k along W(k)→Δ_•{I/p}, then apply φ̃ and the period-ring maps of [§7.17](#layer-7-period-sheaves-qrsp). Glue its localized module to Fil⁰(D_K⊗B_dR) along B_dR to obtain M₃, with the displayed lattice and open-locus identifications. Contraction sends the n-th chart into the next, giving φ* N=φ̃* M and its Frobenius isomorphism; comparison with the imported effective Kisin functor is checked on the Breuil–Kisin chart and extended by twists.

**Checks.**

- `pr7_filtered_crystal_rank_zero`: If dim D = 0 then every value of M(D) is the zero module.
- `pr7_filtered_crystal_finite_projective`: Every value of M(D) is finite projective.
- `pr7_filtered_crystal_twist`: For D of dimension one every value of M(D) is an invertible module (for φ_D = p^{-1}φ and the filtration jumping at −1 it is the Breuil–Kisin twist).
- `pr7_filtered_crystal_not_integral`: The construction does not produce a module over Δ_•: the system M(D) lives over the rings Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p], in which p is a unit.
- `pr7_filtered_crystal_jump_minus_one`: For (D,φ_D)=(K_0,p^(-1)φ) with filtration jumping at −1, M_3=I·M_2 and φ(d e)=(φ(d)/(pd))·d e. This gives φ^*M_3≃I^(-1)⊗M_3, the twist {1}; a jump at 0 produces a different modification.

- D = K_0 with φ and Fil^0 = D_K, Fil^1 = 0: M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} = Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]. D = K_0 with φ_D = p^{-1}φ and Fil^{-1} = D_K, Fil^0 = 0: M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} = Δ_•⟨I/p⟩{1}[1/p], the Breuil–Kisin twist. The rank of M(D) is dim_{K_0} D, and M(D ⊗ D′) = M(D) ⊗ M(D′).

<a id="layer-7-tate-twist-analytic-continuation"></a>

### 7.19 Analytic continuation for p-adic Tate twists

Let R be a quasiregular semiperfectoid p-torsion-free O_C-algebra, and n ≥ 0. The natural map Δ_R{n}^{φ=1}[1/p] → Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}^{φ=1}[1/p] is an isomorphism. Here (−)^{φ=1} denotes fixed points in the ordinary (non-derived) sense: the elements x of Δ_R{n} (resp. of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}) with φ(x) = x in Δ_R{n}[1/I] (resp. in Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}[1/I]).

R is a p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebra; the O_C-structure trivialises the twists, Δ_{O_C}{1} ≅ (q − 1)^{-1}Δ_{O_C}. The source states the proposition without a range for n; its proof and its use (the source's Lemma 6.9 (1)) concern n ≥ 0, the range of the Beilinson fibre square, and that range is stated here. The source recalls Q_p(n)(R) with the uncompleted Nygaard-filtered Δ_R; by Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 7.4.6 the fibre of φ_n − 1 is unchanged by Nygaard completion, so this is the complex of [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex). Input from Layer 7, graded prismatic Beilinson square (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, Theorem 6.17 and 6.18–6.21): for p-torsion-free quasisyntomic R, a functorial pullback square in D(Q_p) with top row Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) and bottom row (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p} → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}, equivalently a fibre sequence Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H LΩ_R)[1/p]; and for R quasiregular semiperfectoid and n > 0 the right vertical map χ_n is injective (for n = 0 the third term of the fibre sequence vanishes and steps 3-5 are not needed) with image the φ = p^n eigenspace of A_crys(R/p)[1/p] = LΩ_R[1/p], so that up to a nonzero scalar it is the forgetful map. Here LΩ_R is p-completed derived de Rham cohomology over Z_p with its Hodge filtration, and the subscript Q_p means p-completion followed by inversion of p. Suspension dictionary: the square comes from the pullback square TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p), HC^-(R; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p) by applying τ_{[2n−1, 2n]}; in cyclic-homology terms the cofibre of TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p) is Σ^2 HC(R; Q_p), and π_{2n} of it is HC_{2n−2} = (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H)[1/p] for these R. The source's introduction writes the third term as HC(R) with the double suspension suppressed.

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Proposition 6.8; p. 22; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Proposition 6.8, proof; p. 22; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Proposition 6.8, proof; p. 22.)

*Needs:* [§7.17](#layer-7-period-sheaves-qrsp), [§7.12](#layer-7-f-crystals-over-qrsp), [§6.10](#layer-6-syntomic-complex), [§3.1](#layer-3-nygaard-filtration-qrsp), [§3.5](#layer-3-nygaard-graded-pieces), [§3.9](#layer-3-breuil-kisin-twist), [PerfectoidSpaces §P4.15.3](#ps-affine), [§0.16](#layer-0-pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), [§4.25](#layer-4-absolute-nygaard-filtration), Layer 7, graded prismatic Beilinson square, Layer 7, graded prismatic Beilinson square, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4`.

**Proof route.** Frobenius-fixed elements lie in their Nygaard preimage, and the characteristic-p quotient has Δ_(R/p)=Δ_R{I/p}, giving the injective factorization of the two rational fixed-point groups. The Beilinson square reduces surjectivity to vanishing in the truncated Hodge quotient; its filtered de-Rham comparison embeds this quotient into I^−nB_dR^+/B_dR^+. On fixed elements the map comes from (q−1)^−nΔ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] and lands in B_dR^+ because q−1 is a unit there, proving vanishing.

**Checks.**

- R = O_C: both sides are one-dimensional over Q_p, equal to Q_p(n) as G_K-modules. R = O_C: the sequence 0 → Q_p(n) → (B_crys^+)^{φ=p^n} → B_dR^+/Fil^n → 0 is the plus form of the fundamental exact sequence (TauCetiRoadmap.PadicPeriodRings §4.3 states the φ = 1 form), which checks the suspension dictionary. For R = O_C and n ≥ 1 the map c is not surjective: its cokernel is B_dR^+/Fil^n.

### 7.20 Boundedness of descent data at the boundary of the open unit disc

Notation as in OK; R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, and q_1, q_2 ∈ Δ_R are the images of q ∈ A_inf under the two structure maps. (A) (the source's Lemma 6.9) (1) Δ_R[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))]^{φ=1} → Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))]^{φ=1} is an isomorphism on H^0. (2) (q_1−1)(q_2−1) is invertible in Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩[1/p]. (3) 0 → Δ_R → Δ_R⟨(q_1−1)^p/p⟩ ⊕ Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩ → Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p, (q_1−1)^p/p⟩ → 0 is exact. (B) (the source's Proposition 6.10) Let M ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf) and suppose M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) is given a descent datum with respect to Y → X, that is a lift to Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]). Then the descent datum extends uniquely to M[1/p] ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf[1/p]): the isomorphism α_{⟨I/p⟩}: p_1^*M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ≅ p_2^*M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] over Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is the base change of a unique isomorphism α: p_1^*M[1/p] ≅ p_2^*M[1/p] over Δ_R[1/p], and α is φ-equivariant and satisfies the cocycle condition.

K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1). M is an F-crystal over A_inf = Δ_{O_C} (a finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module); the descent datum is given only over the rational localisation with p inverted. The rings Δ_R⟨f/g⟩ are p-completed (resp. (q_1−1)-completed) rational localisations as in the source: Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩ = (Δ_R[z]/(z(q_1−1)^p − p))^∧_{(q_1−1)}.

**Proof route.** The two cyclotomic charts identify twists with (q₁−1)^−n(q₂−1)^−n, so [§7.19](#layer-7-tate-twist-analytic-continuation) gives the fixed-section equality; the prism relation makes q₂−1 invertible on the q₁ boundary chart, and complete-flat base change of the blowup exact sequence gives the displayed Mayer–Vietoris sequence. Frobenius continuation extends the descent datum to the inner chart, while its matrix in an étale φ-fixed basis extends to the boundary chart by that fixed-section equality. The two matrices agree on the overlap, and tensoring Mayer–Vietoris with the finite-projective Hom module glues them and their inverses; injectivity preserves Frobenius and cocycle identities.

**Checks.**

- M = A_inf: the descent datum is multiplication by a φ-fixed unit of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p], which lies in Δ_R[1/p]. M = A_inf{1}: in the bases (q_i − 1)^{-1} the datum of the crystal O_Δ{1} is a unit c of Δ_R with φ(c) = c·[p]_{q_2}/[p]_{q_1}. Without a Frobenius structure the extension fails: a general element of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is not in Δ_R[1/p].

Prove the following API:

Over the double overlap the datum is integral after inverting p; on the completed I-inverted chart, full faithfulness after perfection and [§7.1](#layer-7-almost-galois-functions)’s almost Galois-product sections reduce integrality to G_K-stability of that lattice, and regular-sequence extension glues it globally. The rational crystalline comparison identifies the resulting representation with L[1/p], so repeat the modification with lattice L; full faithfulness then gives functoriality and the quasi-inverse property.

- `pr7_lattice_hom`: Morphisms 𝔐(L) → 𝔐(L′) correspond bijectively to G_K-equivariant maps L → L′.
- `pr7_lattice_not_all_representations`: Not every Z_p-representation of G_K is the étale realisation of a prismatic F-crystal: the lattice of a ramified character of finite order is not.

- 𝔐(Z_p) = O_Δ and 𝔐(Z_p(n)) = O_Δ{n}. rk 𝔐(L) = rk_{Z_p} L, and 𝔐(L ⊗ L′) ≅ 𝔐(L) ⊗ 𝔐(L′). For two G_K-stable lattices L ⊂ L′ in the same crystalline representation, 𝔐(L) → 𝔐(L′) is an isomorphism after inverting p and the two differ by a modification along p = 0.

### 7.27 Failure of full faithfulness with mod p coefficients

Let K = Q_p and X = Spf(Z_p). The invertible F-crystal E = O_Δ{p−1}/p ∈ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ/p) has étale realisation T(E) = Z/p(p−1) ≅ Z/p, the trivial local system, but E is not isomorphic to the unit object O_Δ/p; in fact E ≅ I_Δ^{-1}/p as O_Δ/p-modules, and I_Δ/p is a non-trivial invertible O_Δ/p-module. Hence the étale realisation Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ/p) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]/p)^{φ=1} is not fully faithful, and the analogue of [§7.23](#layer-7-crystalline-lattices-theorem) with mod p coefficients is false. More generally the layer makes no claim that finite locally free prismatic F-crystals with torsion or derived coefficients classify torsion or derived Galois representations.

X = Spf(Z_p); any prime p. The source attributes the failure to the fact that sections of vector bundles on Spec(A_inf/p) change when the closed point is removed, unlike on Spec(A_inf) (Kedlaya), which is what full faithfulness in Fargues' theorem uses. The source refers the Sen-operator computation to Bhatt–Lurie §3.5; use the corresponding calculation from [§4.12](#layer-4-hodge-tate-divisor).

([BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Remark 5.8; p. 18; [BS23-FCRYS](#ref-bs23-fcrys), Introduction, footnote to Theorem 1.2; p. 2.)

**Proof route.** Monoidality identifies the étale realization with Z/p(p−1), trivial modulo p. Frobenius pullback of a line modulo p is its p-th tensor power, so the twist formula identifies the crystal with I^−1/p. On the Hodge–Tate locus the line I/p has Sen weight one and the unit has weight zero, distinct at every prime, proving nontriviality.

**Checks.**

- P = 2: E = O_Δ{1}/2 has trivial realisation Z/2(1) ≅ Z/2 and is not trivial. With Z_p-coefficients the same twist O_Δ{p−1} is distinguished from O_Δ by its realisation Z_p(p−1). The correct torsion and derived objects are expected to be perfect complexes on Drinfeld's stack Σ″ (F-gauges), which also record the Nygaard filtration; their construction lies outside this roadmap.

### Examples

For K=Q_p, the unit prismatic F-crystal realizes the trivial Z_p representation. The twist O_Δ{1} realizes Z_p(1) with HT=+1; the effective Kisin module is obtained after twisting into weights ≤0. On the Breuil–Kisin prism the map u↦[π^♭]^p uses θ̃, whereas u↦[π^♭] uses θ. The two coefficient extensions are identified by φ_M before comparing their fixed points. Modulo p, O_Δ{p−1}/p realizes the trivial character but is not the unit crystal, including p=2. Hence the integral full-faithfulness theorem cannot be transferred to mod-p crystals.

## Layer 8: Logarithmic prismatic cohomology

Begin with logarithmic delta algebra and its logification, Frobenius and exactification. Construct relative, animated, saturated and absolute log prismatic theories, preserving the non-fine and boundedness distinctions. The de Rham, crystalline and Nygaard comparisons lead to Kummer-étale realization on log schemes and diamonds. The final Laurent equivalence uses the corrected p-Kummer essential image and the proper pushforward and BKF consequences in their stated ranges.


<a id="layer-8-algebraic-witt-frobenius"></a>

### 8.0 Algebraic Witt–Frobenius modules and extension by zero

For an F_p-algebra R and n≥1, define `LogRH.AlgebraicFrobeniusModule R n` to be a W_n(R)-module M with an invertible semilinear Frobenius such that each x∈M is annihilated by a monic polynomial in the skew operator F with coefficients in W_n(R). Invertible Frobenius means an automorphism of the additive group; it does not mean that M is finite projective as a ring-module. Define `LogRH.algebraicDerived` as the full subcategory of bounded complexes of W_n(R)[F]-modules with algebraic Frobenius cohomology. Prove `LogRH.solution_equivalence`: derived Frobenius solutions give an equivalence with Dᵇ(Spec R_ét,Z/p^n), including arbitrary sheaves, natural under pullback and compatible with Witt reduction. Prove `LogRH.extensionByZero`: the algebraic left adjoint for an étale open immersion corresponds to j_! and its bounded derived functor. ([BLRH](#ref-blrh), Definition 2.4.1 and Theorem 2.4.3, pp.16–17; Definition 5.2.1, Propositions 5.2.2, 5.2.4, pp.39–42; Definition 9.5.2, Proposition 9.5.6, Theorem 9.6.1, Proposition 9.6.2, pp.83–87.)

*Needs:* [§6.3](#layer-6-frobenius-fixed-points), `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract`, Mathlib `WittVector`, Mathlib `TruncatedWittVector`, [§0.14](#layer-0-perfect-delta-rings).

Prove the following API:

- `LogRH.AlgebraicFrobeniusModule`, `LogRH.algebraic_iff_pFiltration`: the predicate and its equivalent formulation on the successive p-power subquotients, including p-torsion modules.
- `LogRH.perfection`: the Frobenius colimit, with its invertible Frobenius and universal property.
- `LogRH.sol`: the étale sheaf of Frobenius-fixed sections after étale scalar extension; its derived version uses the fibre of F−1.
- `LogRH.solution_equivalence`, `LogRH.Ext_comparison`: the equivalence and all nonnegative Ext comparisons, rather than only Hom on lisse objects.
- `LogRH.extensionByZero`, `LogRH.extensionByZero_baseChange`: the left adjoint, its restriction to the open and its compatibility with the solution functor and with Cartesian open base change.
- `LogRH.wittReduction`: compatibility with Z/p^n→Z/p^(n−1) by derived coefficient change, with the corresponding p-torsion and quotient triangles.

**Proof route.** At length one build the left adjoint from étale free generators: monic skew-Frobenius equations make F−1 locally surjective after perfection, giving exact solutions, the unit/counit, and the holonomic/constructible equivalence; filtered colimits then cover arbitrary algebraic modules and sheaves (BLRH Theorem 2.4.3, pp.16–17). The p-power subquotient criterion and induction on Witt length, together with solutions-acyclic injective perfect Frobenius modules, give all Ext comparisons and hence the bounded derived equivalence by Postnikov induction (Definition 9.5.2 through Proposition 9.6.2, pp.83–87). For an open D(t), clear denominators in a finitely presented Frobenius lattice and multiply by a high power of t so that its perfected closed-fibre quotient vanishes; the resulting left adjoint has original solutions off t and zero on t, and filtered colimits, the p-filtration and Ext comparison extend its j_! compatibility to all algebraic objects and bounded complexes (Propositions 5.2.2 and 5.2.4, pp.39–42).

In the special valuation case R=O_(C^♭), t a nonzero topologically nilpotent element and j:Spec C^♭→Spec R, the constant sheaf on the generic point extended by zero corresponds to W_n(m_(C^♭)), the p-power radical Witt ideal, with its Frobenius. Modulo p the assertion is the union of the principal root ideals t^(1/p^r)R. Its tensor square is itself and its tensor with the residue field vanishes; Witt induction gives the length-n assertion. Tensoring by that ideal therefore realizes the extension-by-zero operation used in KY Lemma 8.5. Its cone from the corresponding generic extension is supported at the closed point and almost zero. This supplies the actual non-lisse input for [§8.40](#layer-8-global-etale-comparison).

**Checks.** For R=F_p, W_n(R) with its identity Frobenius has solutions the constant Z/p^n sheaf. Over algebraically closed R=k, arbitrary direct sums of this object give arbitrary constant sheaves and are usually not perfect ring-modules. For R=O_(C^♭), W_n(m_(C^♭)) has zero geometric stalk at the closed point and a rank-one stalk on Spec C^♭, so it is algebraic and fails the lisse condition on Spec R. At n=1, perfection of a nilpotent Frobenius module is zero, so forgetting the perfection would give the wrong category. For t=0 the open is empty and extension by zero is zero; for t=1 it is the identity. These include the two excluded localization extremes.

<a id="layer-8-formal-log-charts"></a>

### 8.1 Formal integral logarithmic charts

Construct `FormalLog.Chart` over a classically J-complete ring A, with J finitely generated, using the finitely generated adic formal carrier of SF.4. Its formal étale charts are compatible étale charts of the nilpotent reductions; uniqueness of étale lifting identifies their overlaps and coverings. For bounded p-adic objects this agrees with [§1.0](#layer-1-bounded-formal-sites). A log structure is an integral monoid sheaf on that site with its structure map to O_X and the usual identification above O_X^×. A chart P→Γ(X,M_X) induces this sheaf after logification. For a fixed integral base chart M→A, distinguish: relatively coherent means P is finitely generated over M; relatively fine means finitely presented over M in integral monoids; small means P surjects onto Γ(X,M_X)/Γ(X,O_X^×); exact at x means the chart map to the geometric stalk is exact. Log affine means that the identity on Γ(X,M_X) is a chart. These predicates are extra data/properties of charts, not consequences of affine underlying geometry.

Use CR.5's integral monoid pushouts, groupifications and logification. In particular, exactify a surjection h:P→Q of integral monoids by P^ex=(h^gp)⁻¹(Q) inside P^gp, and use the completed monoid-algebra base change on the ring. An exact surjection has P/P^×≃Q/Q^× and gives a strict exact closed immersion after logification. None of these definitions requires a fine base monoid.

([K1](#ref-k1), Appendix A.2, Definitions A.2–A.3, Lemmas A.4–A.5 and Corollaries A.6–A.7, pp.51–53; Definition A.8 and Lemmas A.9–A.10, pp.53–54; Definitions A.22–A.23, pp.59–60; §3, proof of Proposition 3.9, pp.17–18.)

*Needs:* [§1.0](#layer-1-bounded-formal-sites), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra/integral-monoid`, `associated-log`, `log-chart`, `integral-log-fiber-product`, `exact-morphism`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`.

Prove the following API:

- `FormalLog.Chart.logification`: Compatible logifications on the formal étale site and on every X/J^n, with descent of charts and their morphisms.
- `FormalLog.Chart.relativeFinite`: An integral injection M→P with P finitely generated over M is relatively fine. Consequently chart maps out of P and equality of such maps extend from a geometric stalk to an étale neighbourhood.
- `FormalLog.Chart.exact_neighbourhood`: If a group G contains M′^gp, is finitely generated over it and maps onto M_X,x^gp/O_X,x^×, its inverse image of M_X,x/O_X,x^× extends to an exact chart near x provided ker(M′^gp→M_X,x^gp/O_X,x^×) is finitely generated modulo M′^×.
- `FormalLog.Chart.small_neighbourhood`: If |X| is locally noetherian and either Spec M is finite or the images of M∖M^× lie in √J, a relatively coherent chart is small on sufficiently small Zariski neighbourhoods of x and on their smaller neighbourhoods containing x. Affine such neighbourhoods are log affine.
- `FormalLog.Chart.global_integral`: For a small chart exact at x, integrality or exactness of M→P passes to M→Γ(X,M_X).
- `FormalLog.Chart.exactSurjection`: The groupification formula, its universal property, and the exact-closed-immersion conclusion for exact surjections.

For the construction, apply CR.5's associated-log construction on each ordinary étale chart, use the common underlying étale topos of nilpotent reductions, and take the compatible formal structure sheaf. Relative finite presentation is in integral monoids: finite relations are imposed before integralization. It makes the stalk Hom comparison commute with the relevant filtered neighbourhood limit. Extend an inverse stalk map and its two identities to prove local isomorphism detection. To obtain an exact chart take the indicated inverse-image monoid; finite generation of the kernel supplies relative finite presentation. For the small-chart assertion, only finitely many characteristic faces occur under either stated hypothesis. Shrink so their unit loci stabilize. Surjectivity on characteristic global sections then gives smallness, and exactness at x identifies P/P^× with the global characteristic monoid, proving the last assertion.

**Checks.**

- `FormalLog.Chart.rational_base`: The identity over (A,Q_{≥0}→A) is relatively coherent and integral although the base monoid need not be fine.
- `FormalLog.Chart.affine_warning`: Affineness alone is not used to infer that Γ(X,M_X) is a chart; the small-chart hypothesis is retained in `small_neighbourhood`.
- `FormalLog.Chart.exactification`: For 2N⊂Z mapping isomorphically to its image 2N, exactification does not introduce the missing generator 1. For a surjection N²→N adding the exponents, it introduces the kernel units in Z², rather than replacing both labelled generators by one freely.
- `FormalLog.Chart.relative_presentation`: Relative finite presentation is not silently replaced by finite presentation of Z[P] over Z[M]. The smoothness definition below therefore makes no general finite-presentation claim about X/A.

<a id="layer-8-formal-log-smoothness"></a>

### 8.2 Smooth formal logarithmic geometry

Define `FormalLog.IsSmooth` over (A,M) by the following local chart criterion. There is a relatively coherent integral chart M→P which is integral and injective on groupifications; the torsion subgroup of P^gp/M^gp is finite of order invertible on X/J; and X→Spf(A⟨P⟩)×_{Spf(A⟨M⟩)}Spf(A) is étale. For `FormalLog.IsEtale` require the whole group quotient to be finite of invertible order. Dropping integrality of M→P defines the corresponding Kato variants. Smoothness includes integrality; the Kato variant need not give flat underlying geometry. All formal fibre products and monoid algebras here are J-completed.

Prove stability under completed base change between integral prelog bases, using integral log fibre products for the Kato variant. Integral smoothness implies J-complete flatness of the underlying ring. Its completed log differentials are finite locally free. At each finite level, maps from affine integral exact nilpotent thickenings lift to a smooth affine target. If that target is also of finite presentation over A, a log-affine nilideal thickening is allowed; the ideal need not have one uniform nilpotence exponent. An exact closed immersion X→Y of smooth log schemes over A/J is quasi-regular; it is regular if Y is locally of finite presentation over A/J.

([K1](#ref-k1), Definition A.11 and Remarks A.12–A.14, pp.54–55; Proposition A.15, pp.55–56; Remark A.16 and Proposition A.17, pp.57–58; Remarks A.18–A.19 and Proposition A.20, pp.58–59.)

*Needs:* [§8.1](#layer-8-formal-log-charts), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra/log-smooth-chart-criterion`, `integral-morphism`, `qc-log-smooth`, `fine-model-descent`, `log-differentials`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0/regular-quotient-cotangent`, `DD.1/complete-flatness`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

Prove the following API:

- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.base_change`: The completed base-change theorem, retaining integrality of the chart and the invertible torsion condition.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.completeFlat`: J-complete flatness, obtained from the flat integral monoid algebra map and étale localization.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.fine_model`: A Kato-smooth chart is an integral base change of a fine chart whose reductions are formally smooth. If X/A is locally of finite presentation, the fine model is log smooth. A finitely presented original chart permits such a log-smooth fine model after enlarging the fine base monoid. Compare with CR.5's finite-model notion exactly in this range.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.nilpotent_lift`: The affine exact nilpotent lifting property and finite locally free completed Ω^i_log.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.nilideal_lift`: The stronger log-affine lifting theorem with finite presentation of the affine smooth target as an explicit hypothesis.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.exactImmersion_quasiregular`: Flat conormal module and Sym(J/J²)≃gr_J for an exact closed immersion of smooth log schemes, with the stated finite-presentation upgrade to regularity.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.change_chart`: For another integral base chart M′ defining the same log structure, smooth/étale charts exist near x if ker(M′^gp→M_X,x^gp/O_X,x^×) is finitely generated modulo M′^×. They may be chosen exact at x. An exact base chart satisfies this kernel condition for an integral smooth morphism.

**Proof route.** Integral injective chart maps give flat monoid algebras and hence complete flatness after completion; the group quotient computes the finite free log differentials, and affine H¹ of their Hom torsor gives square-zero lifting, then nilpotent induction. Descent to a fine submonoid gives the nilideal statement only with the additional finite-presentation hypothesis; a local conormal basis and smooth splitting identify successive immersion neighborhoods with truncated symmetric algebras, proving quasiregularity. Preserve the free group quotient under chart change, absorb invertible-order torsion by étale roots of units, and apply exact_neighbourhood under the stated kernel hypothesis.

**Checks.**

- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.trivial_log`: With trivial charts the étale polynomial model gives ordinary smooth formal geometry and its completed differentials.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.semistable`: The diagonal N→N^r yields the completed chart A⟨x_1,…,x_r⟩/(x_1⋯x_r−a), finite free log differentials modulo Σ dlog x_i, and complete flatness over A.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.torsion_order`: N→N, 1↦m, meets the étale group condition only when m is invertible on X/J; m=p over a characteristic-p reduction is excluded.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.finite_model_range`: A fine model that is merely formally smooth at each reduction is not called a fine log-smooth finite-presentation model without the additional hypothesis in `fine_model`.
- `FormalLog.IsSmooth.nilideal_range`: The nilpotent theorem and the finite-presentation nilideal theorem have different hypotheses; neither is obtained from formal smoothness by dropping those hypotheses.

<a id="layer-8-formal-log-cotangent"></a>

### 8.3 Completed logarithmic cotangent sheaves

Construct `FormalLog.completedCotangent` for maps of bounded integral log J-adic formal schemes by étale descent of the derived J-completion of DD.6's affine Gabber log cotangent complex. Retain its universal d and dlog. It has the completed transitivity triangle, derived base change and logification invariance in the supplier's ranges. For integral smooth charts of [§8.2](#layer-8-formal-log-smoothness) it is Ω¹_log in degree zero, finite locally free; its derived exterior powers are the completed ordinary Ω^i_log. Integral étale charts give zero. A nonintegral Kato-étale map is not included in this degree-zero/vanishing assertion.

Also prove the following discrete deformation statement without a finite-presentation assumption: if L_log(B/A)=0 for a map of discrete integral log rings, maps from B lift uniquely across strict square-zero extensions of discrete integral log rings over A. Iterate for nilpotent extensions; take limits only for compatible complete rings and log structures. This is the formal lifting statement, with no assertion that the morphism is of finite presentation. Applied levelwise to (A_inf(R),M^♭)^a and then to the complete (p,I)-tower, it supplies the lifting step of KY Lemma 2.40.

([KY](#ref-ky), Definition 2.5, Lemmas 2.9–2.10 and Theorem 2.11 with Remark 2.12, pp.13–15; Remark 2.13, pp.15–16; Lemma 2.40, pp.21–22; [SSV](#ref-ssv), Theorem 4.17 and Remark 4.18, pp.19–21, and the proof of Theorem 5.6, pp.23–24. The formal lifting implication uses that proof; the theorem's additional finiteness hypotheses are needed for its finite-presentation conclusion.)

*Needs:* [§8.2](#layer-8-formal-log-smoothness), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/gabber-log-cotangent`, `log-cotangent-functoriality`, `log-derived-derivations`, `free-prelog-resolutions`, `DD.1/derived-completeness`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/enhanced-derived-category`, `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4`.

Prove the following API:

- `FormalLog.completedCotangent.etale_descent`: The affine-to-formal sheaf and its étale base-change maps, independent of chart and compatible with logification.
- `FormalLog.completedCotangent.transitivity`: The completed triangle and derived base change, replacing ordinary pushouts only in the supplied homologically log-flat range.
- `FormalLog.completedCotangent.smooth_discrete`: The degree-zero smooth calculation and exterior-power identification.
- `FormalLog.completedCotangent.formalEtale_lift`: The unique discrete strict square-zero and nilpotent lifting statements, with the complete-tower version under completeness.

For the construction, strict étale restriction is homologically log flat. DD.6's base change therefore identifies the affine complexes on overlaps; descend them and their derivations in the complete derived category. On an integral smooth chart, the integral injection makes the toric monoid-algebra pushout a homotopy pushout. Its cotangent module is O_X⊗^L_Z(P^gp/M^gp): injectivity removes the kernel term and invertible torsion removes its derived torsion term. The strict étale extension has zero cotangent. Complete and descend to obtain the calculation. For lifting, a strict square-zero log extension is a homotopy pullback classified by a log derivation into J[1] (SSV Theorem 4.17). The fibre of the map on mapping spaces is controlled by RHom_B(L_log, J[1]); its obstruction vanishes and it is contractible when L_log=0. Each finite nilpotent stage is discrete, as required in that result. The complete-tower assertion then follows from compatible uniqueness, rather than assuming a deformation theorem for arbitrary animated log thickenings.

**Checks.**

- `FormalLog.completedCotangent.coordinate`: For the completed free log coordinate (A,0)→(A⟨x⟩,N), the result is R·dlog x in degree zero with dx=x dlog x.
- `FormalLog.completedCotangent.zero_chart`: For (k,0)→(k,N→0), the full complex retains its degree −1 term; formal completion cannot remove the log point's derived cotangent term.
- `FormalLog.completedCotangent.nonintegral`: The nonintegral log-étale chart of KY Remark 2.13 is excluded from `smooth_discrete`; its unbounded Gabber homology is preserved.
- `FormalLog.completedCotangent.lifting_unique`: If the complex vanishes, the space of lifts across a strict square-zero extension has one component and no automorphism ambiguity. Merely requiring H⁰L_log=0 does not suffice.

### 8.4 Completed log PD envelopes and the big formal site

Construct `FormalLog.CompletedPDEnvelope` for an exactified closed embedding Spf(R,P)^a→Spf(B,N)^a over a p-adic log PD base: first use CR.5's integral log exactification and CR.0's ordinary compatible PD envelope, then p-complete its ring and logify the chart. Its universal property is among classically p-complete log PD thickenings with continuous maps and compatible base divided powers. The embedding ideal is p-closed, the quotient is R when R is already classically p-complete, and each divided-power operation is continuous. Require the divided powers on the embedding ideal and on the base ideal to extend jointly; the image of the base ideal is not required to lie in the embedding ideal for a general mixed-characteristic object. No assertion of p-torsion-freeness is made for an arbitrary PD envelope.

Construct `FormalLog.BigCrystallineSite` with objects (B,J,M_B)^a, B and B/J classically p-complete, integral quasi-coherent log structure, a map Spf(B/J)→X and an exact closed immersion into Spf B over the base. Take ordinary étale coverings and the sheaf B. There is no delta structure and no p-torsion-freeness condition on B. For a p-torsion-free base A with a compatible PD ideal I and X smooth over (A/I,M_A), prove the local completed log PD-envelope Čech computation and independence of presentations. If p∈I, comparison with the small characteristic-p sites modulo p^m and their derived inverse limit gives the usual p-adic log crystalline cohomology. For general formal X the corresponding reductions are X_m; one does not identify a mixed-characteristic X with a fixed characteristic-p scheme.

([K1](#ref-k1), Remark 6.6, pp.32–33, Remark 6.7 and Proposition 6.8 with its proof, pp.33–34; Remark 6.9, p.34. The ordinary finite-level PD envelopes and log PD de Rham computation are `CR.5/qc-log-pd-envelope`, `log-pd-de-rham`, `embedding-descent` and `p-adic-log-crystalline`; the completion and big-site adapters are the targets here.)

*Needs:* [§8.2](#layer-8-formal-log-smoothness), [§8.1](#layer-8-formal-log-charts), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0/pd-envelope`, `CR.5/qc-log-pd-envelope`, `log-pd-thickening`, `log-pd-de-rham`, `embedding-descent`, `p-adic-log-crystalline`, [§0.18](#layer-0-pd-envelope-complete-flatness), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, `E3`.

Prove the following API:

- `FormalLog.CompletedPDEnvelope.lift`: The continuous PD/log universal property and its uniqueness, compatible with exactification and étale localization.
- `FormalLog.CompletedPDEnvelope.reduction`: Comparison with the compatible finite-level envelopes, with derived reduction asserted only in the complete-flat setting used below.
- `FormalLog.BigCrystallineSite.structureSheaf`: The site, its ring sheaf and the morphism to X_ét, allowing p-torsion in objects.
- `FormalLog.BigCrystallineSite.cech`: For smooth X over the stated p-torsion-free base, an exactified completed free prelog presentation and its completed PD-envelope nerve compute derived sections; unions of presentations give the comparison coherences.
- `FormalLog.BigCrystallineSite.small_comparison`: The characteristic-p small/big and inverse-limit comparison; derived tensor with A/p^m is used in the reduction statement.
- `FormalLog.BigCrystallineSite.pd_deRham`: If p∈I and a surjection from a p-completely smooth delta-log algebra of topologically finite presentation is chosen as in K1 Remark 6.9, its envelope is PD smooth at every finite level, and its log PD de Rham complex and its Čech nerve compute the same cohomology, functorially for Frobenius maps.

For the universal property, maps from the ordinary envelope to a p-complete target extend uniquely through p-completion. For each fixed r the PD addition and product identities show p-adic continuity of γ_r; the possible loss of p-adic valuation is bounded by v_p(r!), so these operations extend to the closed ideal. This proves the compatible PD structure on the completion and the stated universal property. Use the surjection from the ambient ring to R to identify its quotient by the closed embedding ideal. Finite-level exactification and PD universal properties give the reduction maps; do not assume that a derived tensor is an ordinary quotient when torsion prevents it.

For the Čech calculation, lift a smooth chart locally and choose a completed free prelog ring surjecting onto it. Exactify first. The weak finite-generation condition reduces its monoid of extra units to a filtered union of finite-rank free groups, as in K1 Proposition 3.9, pp.17–18. At each such stage the smooth exact-immersion calculation supplies the relative completely regular presentation, so Layer 0's PD-envelope flatness applies. Pass through completed filtered colimits. The resulting envelope terms are p-completely flat over A, hence p-torsion-free here; this is a conclusion about these terms, not all objects of the site. Their lifting property makes the envelope weakly final locally. The resulting Čech nerve therefore computes cohomology. Additional delta generators are completely free, with the extra-variable contraction, so the same calculation will compare this site with the delta-log site in [§8.20](#layer-8-delta-log-crystalline-site).

For the PD de Rham calculation, use the stronger nilideal lifting theorem of [§8.2](#layer-8-formal-log-smoothness) on the finite-presentation smooth ambient, precisely as in K1 Remark 6.9. This supplies PD smoothness rather than assuming it for every non-fine smooth formal object. CR.5's finite-level log PD Poincaré calculation and embedding descent now apply. The finite-level maps are compatible; take their derived inverse limit. In the characteristic-p range the reduction is the usual small-site comparison; the projection formula is valid since A is p-torsion-free and A/p^m is perfect over A. All comparison maps are induced by the universal PD/log maps, so functorial Frobenius diagrams commute before taking limits.

**Checks.**

- `FormalLog.CompletedPDEnvelope.trivial_log`: Trivial monoids recover the ordinary p-completed compatible PD envelope with its continuous universal property.
- `FormalLog.CompletedPDEnvelope.point`: The envelope of the identity R=B with zero embedding ideal is B, with the prescribed base PD structure; a nonzero base PD ideal is not thereby forced into the zero embedding ideal.
- `FormalLog.CompletedPDEnvelope.torsion_warning`: An arbitrary PD envelope is allowed to have p-torsion. Complete-flatness hypotheses are required before using derived reduction as ordinary reduction.
- `FormalLog.BigCrystallineSite.torsion_object`: A finite-level PD thickening with p-torsion is an object of the ordinary big site but need not be an object of the delta-log crystalline site.
- `FormalLog.BigCrystallineSite.characteristic_p`: When p∈I, reduction modulo p^m and the limit use the same X; otherwise the system is X_m, so the two statements cannot be interchanged.
- `FormalLog.BigCrystallineSite.ambient_finiteness`: The PD de Rham theorem uses a topologically finitely presented smooth ambient and its nilideal lifting property. A weakly finitely generated target chart is not itself declared to have that stronger lifting property.
