- `LogPrismaticSite.crystallineFunctor_untwisted_fails`: Without the Frobenius twist (sending (B, J, M_B) to (B, (p), M_B)) one does not get an object over X: Spf(B/p) need not map to X since only B/J does.


<a id="layer-8-local-crystalline-comparison"></a>

**Local log crystalline comparison.**

In the setting of the comparison map, let (R, P) be a smooth prelog ring over (A/I, M_A) with P integral, M_A → P integral, (weakly) finitely generated and of Cartier type (M_A/M_A^× → P/P^× integral with exact relative Frobenius P^(1) → P), and assume (R, P) admits an exact surjection from a smooth lift (R̃, P̃) over (A/p, M_A). Then there is a canonical isomorphism Δ_{(R^(1),P^(1))/(φ_*A,φ_*M_A)} ≅ φ_*RΓ_crys((R, P)/(A, M_A)) of E_∞-φ_*A-algebras compatible with Frobenius; by base change the left side is the p-completed base change of Δ_{(R̃,P̃)/(A,M_A)} along φ.

As in the comparison map; Cartier type of M_A → P; existence of the exact surjection from a smooth lift.

([K1](#ref-k1), §6, Theorem 6.1 (p. 31); [K1](#ref-k1), §6.2 (p. 36).)

*Needs:* [§8.20](#layer-8-crystalline-comparison-map), [§8.20](#layer-8-delta-log-crystalline-vs-log-crystalline), [§8.20](#layer-8-cartier-type-cosimplicial-frobenius), [§8.18](#layer-8-cech-alexander-log), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra`, Layer 1.

**Proof route.** Compute the two theories by the exactified PD and prismatic envelope nerves. Relative Frobenius extends to their comparison and agrees with the topoi map. Modulo p its monoid component is the Cartier-type theorem just proved and its free polynomial component is PerfectoidSpaces’ Čech Frobenius theorem, so derived Nakayama gives the equivalence.


<a id="layer-8-log-crystalline-comparison"></a>

**The log crystalline comparison.**

Let (A, (p), M_A) be a bounded prelog prism with M_A integral, of rank 1 or with (A, M_A) a log ring, I a PD ideal of A containing p, and (X, M_X) a smooth log scheme over (A/I, M_A) of Cartier type (Kato 4.8). Then the crystalline comparison map is an isomorphism of E_∞-φ_*A-algebras on X_ét: Δ_{(X^(1),M_X^(1))/(φ_*A,φ_*M_A)} ≅ φ_*Ru^crys_*O_crys. Globally, for I = (p) and X qcqs of Cartier type over (A/p, M_A): RΓ_logcrys((X, M_X)/(A, M_A)) ≅ RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(A, M_A)) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A, φ-equivariantly, as E_∞-A-algebras.

The prism ideal is (p); the auxiliary PD ideal I contains p. The smooth log scheme over (A/I, M_A) is of Cartier type. For the displayed global form specialize I = (p) and assume X qcqs.

([K1](#ref-k1), §6, Theorem 6.3 (p. 31); [KY](#ref-ky), §1, Theorem 2(3) (p. 3).)

*Needs:* [§8.20](#layer-8-local-crystalline-comparison), [§8.20](#layer-8-crystalline-comparison-map), [§8.20](#layer-8-delta-log-crystalline-vs-log-crystalline), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-prismatic-base-change), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`.

**Proof route.** Choose smooth Cartier-type charts and smooth lifts étale locally. The local comparison applies and its globally defined map glues the isomorphisms. Identify delta-log crystalline with ordinary log crystalline cohomology and apply base change for the stated reformulation.

- Over (W(k),(p),N→0), the log affine line with chart N⊕N^T has the Frobenius-twisted continuous log de Rham model on both sides. For a qcqs smooth log scheme over this base, the comparison is (φ^*RΓ_Δ)^∧_p≃RΓ_crys of its special fibre, with the same Hyodo–Kato coefficient convention (K1 Example 1.4).

<a id="layer-8-log-q-pd-triple"></a>

### 8.21 Log q-PD triples and log q-PD envelopes

Let A = Z_p[[q − 1]] with δ(q) = 0 and [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1). A q-PD pair is a (p, [p]_q)-complete δ-pair (D, I) over (A, (q − 1)) such that (D, ([p]_q)) is a bounded prism over (A, ([p]_q)), φ(I) ⊂ [p]_q D and γ(I) ⊂ I where γ(x) = φ(x)/[p]_q − δ(x), D/(q − 1) is p-torsion free with finite (p, [p]_q)-complete Tor amplitude over D, and D/I is classically p-complete. A prelog q-PD triple is (D, I, M_D) with (D, I) a q-PD pair and (D, I, M_D) a δ_log-triple; a log q-PD triple is (D, I, M_{Spf(D)}) arising as (D, [p]_q, M_D)^a. Étale maps lift uniquely (Lemma 7.3). For a prelog q-PD triple (D_1, I_1, M_{D_1}) with integral monoid, a p-completely smooth (R, P) over (D_1/I_1, M_{D_1}) with M_{D_1} → P integral and weakly finitely generated admitting a smooth lift, and a surjection (D_2, M_{D_2}) → (R, P) as in Lemma 7.4, there is a universal map to a prelog q-PD triple (D_3, I_3, M_{D_3}) with an exact surjection M_{D_3} → P and D_2/I_2 ≅ D_3/I_3; D_3 is (p, [p]_q)-completely flat over D_1, the construction commutes with completed base change, and D_3 ⊗̂ D_1/(q − 1) is the p-completed log PD envelope. This is the log q-PD envelope.

A = Z_p[[q − 1]]; (D_1, I_1, M_{D_1}) a prelog q-PD triple with integral M_{D_1}. (R, P) p-completely smooth over (D_1/I_1, M_{D_1}); M_{D_1} → P integral and weakly finitely generated; (R, P)^a admits a smooth lift over (D_1, M_{D_1}). A surjection (D_{2,0}, M_{D_2}) → (R, P) over (D_1, M_{D_1}) satisfies one of: (i) (D_{2,0}, M_{D_2}) is a (p, [p]_q)-completely smooth δ_log ring of topologically finite presentation; (ii) M_{D_1} → M_{D_2} is injective integral, M_{D_2}^gp/M_{D_1}^gp is free abelian, and D_{2,0} is (p, [p]_q)-completely free over the completion of D_1 ⊗_{Z_(p)[M_{D_1}]} Z_(p)[M_{D_2}]. In (i), D_2 = D_{2,0}; in (ii), D_2 is the completed universal δ_log ring generated by D_{2,0}. I_{2,0} = ker(D_{2,0} → R), and I_2 is the (p, [p]_q)-completion of I_{2,0}D_2.

([K1](#ref-k1), §7.1, Definition 7.1 (p. 37); [K1](#ref-k1), §7.1, Lemma 7.4 (p. 38); [K1](#ref-k1), §7.1, Example 7.2 (p. 37).)

*Needs:* [§8.4](#layer-8-completed-log-pd), [§8.9](#layer-8-prelog-prism), [§8.8](#layer-8-delta-log-exactification), [§8.5](#layer-8-delta-log-completion-etale), Layer 5, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`.

Prove the following API:

- `LogQPDTriple`: A prelog q-PD triple (D, I, M_D) over Z_p[[q − 1]].
- `LogQPDTriple.gamma_mem`: For x ∈ I, γ(x) = φ(x)/[p]_q − δ(x) ∈ I.
- `LogQPDTriple.etaleLift`: A p-completely étale D/I → Ē lifts uniquely to a prelog q-PD triple (E, J, M_D) over (D, I, M_D) (Lemma 7.3).
- `LogQPDTriple.envelope`: The log q-PD envelope (D_3, I_3, M_{D_3}) of Lemma 7.4.
- `LogQPDTriple.envelope_flat`: D_3 is (p, [p]_q)-completely flat over D_1.
- `LogQPDTriple.envelope_mod_q_sub_one`: D_3 ⊗̂_{D_1} D_1/(q − 1) is the p-completed log PD envelope of I_2/(q − 1) (CR.5).

**Proof route.** Add the quotient completeness condition to the ordinary q-PD data. Unique étale delta-log lifting and the gamma addition/scalar formulas give the lifting lemma. Exactify a smooth lift, whose kernel is locally the base ideal plus a relatively completely regular sequence, and apply the ordinary q-PD-envelope theorem and its universal property.

**Checks.**

- `LogQPDTriple.ainf_example`: (A_inf(O_C), (ξ), O_C♭∖{0}) with q = [ε] is a prelog q-PD triple and ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q).
- `LogQPDTriple.q_eq_one`: At q = 1 a prelog q-PD triple is the same as a pre-δ_log-PD triple (D p-torsion free and p-complete, D/I classically p-complete, I with divided powers).
- `LogQPDTriple.trivial_envelope`: For (R, P) = (D_1/I_1, M_{D_1}) and the identity surjection, the envelope is (D_1, I_1, M_{D_1}).
- `LogQPDTriple.not_q_minus_one_ideal`: (Z_p[[q − 1]], (q − 1)) is a q-PD pair but ([p]_q) cannot be replaced by (q − 1) as the prism ideal: (Z_p[[q − 1]], (q − 1)) is not a prism.

<a id="layer-8-log-q-crystalline-site"></a>

### 8.22 The log q-crystalline site

Fix a prelog q-PD triple (D, I, M_D) with M_D integral and (X, M_X) smooth over (D/I, M_D). The log q-crystalline site ((X, M_X)/(D, M_D))_qCRYS is the opposite of the category of log q-PD triples (E, J, M_{Spf(E)}) from prelog q-PD triples (E, J, M_E) over (D, I, M_D) with M_E integral, with f: Spf(E/J) → X over D/I and an exact closed immersion (Spf(E/J), f^*M_X) ↪ (Spf(E), M_{Spf(E)}) over (D, M_D); étale topology; structure sheaf O_qCRYS: E ↦ E. Write RΓ_qCRYS((X, M_X)/(D, M_D)), a (p, [p]_q)-complete E_∞-D-algebra with φ_D-semilinear endomorphism, and qΩ_{(X,M_X)/(D,M_D)} := Ru^q_{X*}O_qCRYS on X_ét. For affine X with a smooth lift and integral weakly finitely generated chart, the Čech nerve of the log q-PD envelope of a free surjection computes it (Construction 7.8), strictly functorially for (E_0, M_E) = (D⟨N^R, N^P⟩, M_D ⊕ N^P). At q = 1 it is the δ_log-crystalline site.

(D, I, M_D) prelog q-PD triple with M_D integral; (X, M_X) smooth over (D/I, M_D).

([K1](#ref-k1), §7.2, Definition 7.5 (p. 39); [K1](#ref-k1), §7.2, Remark 7.7 (p. 40).)

*Needs:* [§8.21](#layer-8-log-q-pd-triple), [§8.20](#layer-8-delta-log-crystalline-site), Layer 5.

Prove the following API:

- `LogQCrystallineSite`: The site ((X, M_X)/(D, M_D))_qCRYS.
- `LogQCrystallineSite.qOmega`: qΩ_{(X,M_X)/(D,M_D)} = Ru^q_{X*}O_qCRYS, an E_∞-D-algebra on X_ét with φ_D-semilinear Frobenius.
- `LogQCrystallineSite.cech`: For affine X with chart and smooth lift, the Čech nerve of a log q-PD envelope computes qΩ (Construction 7.8, Remark 7.9).
- `LogQCrystallineSite.ofDeltaLogCrystalline`: The functor from ((X, M_X)/(D/(q − 1), M_D))_δCRYS and the induced map qΩ ⊗̂^L D/(q − 1) → Ru^δ_{X*}O_δCRYS.
- `LogQCrystallineSite.strict_change`: For a strict map (D, I, M_D) → (D, I′, M_D), qΩ_{(X,M_X)/(D,M_D)} ≅ qΩ_{(X,M_X)_{D/I′}/(D,M_D)} (Lemma 7.12).

**Proof route.** Étale q-PD lifting defines the site and structure sheaf. The free chart and log q-PD envelope give its Čech construction. At q=1 the definitions recover the delta-log crystalline site.

**Checks.**

- `LogQCrystallineSite.point`: For X = Spf(D/I) with log structure M_D, qΩ = D.
- `LogQCrystallineSite.q_eq_one`: If q = 1 in D the site is the δ_log-crystalline site.
- `LogQCrystallineSite.affineLine_complex`: For (D/I⟨X⟩, M_D ⊕ N) with D flat over A, qΩ is computed by the two-term complex D⟨X⟩ → D⟨X⟩·dlog X, f ↦ (γ(f) − f)/(q − 1)·dlog X with γ(X) = qX (Construction 7.15 with S a point).
- `LogQCrystallineSite.not_prismatic`: The log q-crystalline site is not the log prismatic site over (D, ([p]_q)): its objects carry a q-PD ideal J containing the image of the base q-PD ideal I, with γ(J) ⊂ J and φ(J) ⊂ [p]_qE. J need not contain [p]_q (for example J = (ξ) in A_inf). The comparison of Theorem 7.13 uses a Frobenius twist.

<a id="layer-8-log-q-crystalline-vs-crystalline"></a>

**Log q-crystalline cohomology modulo q − 1.**

The canonical map induces an isomorphism qΩ_{(X,M_X)/(D,M_D)} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q − 1) ≅ Ru^δ_{X*}O_δCRYS, and hence with the ordinary big formal log crystalline complex of [§8.4](#layer-8-completed-log-pd). Its small-site interpretation is the derived inverse limit of the small log crystalline complexes of X_m over D/(q−1,p^m), with the induced compatible PD base. If p lies in the reduced PD ideal, X is already in characteristic p and the same X occurs at every level. For a general p-adic X the reductions X_m must be retained.

As in the log q-crystalline site. The reduced PD ideal is the image of the arbitrary base q-PD ideal I, not necessarily (p); use the arbitrary PD-base version of CR.5.

([K1](#ref-k1), §7.2, Theorem 7.10 (p. 41).)

*Needs:* [§8.22](#layer-8-log-q-crystalline-site), [§8.20](#layer-8-delta-log-crystalline-vs-log-crystalline), Layer 5, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`.

**Proof route.** On an affine smooth chart compute qΩ by its envelope nerve and reduce by D/(q−1). Finite complete Tor-amplitude commutes this base change with totalization, identifying the general delta-log PD envelope. Apply CR.5’s arbitrary PD-base comparison; the crystalline-prism specialization alone would not cover this range.

**Checks.**

- Trivial log: the q = 1 specialisation of q-crystalline cohomology in BS22 §16. Log affine line: the q-de Rham complex reduces to the log de Rham complex.


<a id="layer-8-log-q-crystalline-vs-prismatic"></a>

**Log q-crystalline versus log prismatic cohomology.**

Let (D, I, M_D) be a prelog q-PD triple of rank 1 or with (D, M_D) a log ring, ψ_D: (D/I, M_D) → (φ_*D/[p]_q, φ_*M_D) induced by Frobenius, and (X^(1), M_X^(1)) the base change of (X, M_X) along ψ_D. If the mod p fibre of (X, M_X) is of Cartier type over (D/(p, I), M_D), there is a canonical isomorphism Δ_{(X^(1),M_X^(1))/(φ_*D,φ_*M_D)} ≅ φ_*qΩ_{(X,M_X)/(D,M_D)} of E_∞-φ_*D-algebras on X_ét, relative to the log prism (φ_*D, ([p]_q), φ_*M_D). By base change the left side is the (p, [p]_q)-completed base change along φ_D of Δ_{(X̃,M̃)/(D,M_D)} for a lift.

Cartier type of the mod p fibre; rank 1 or log ring base. M_D is integral, as fixed in K1 §7.2 before Definition 7.5 (p. 39).

([K1](#ref-k1), §7.2, Theorem 7.13 (p. 42).)

**Proof route.** Frobenius twisting gives the map from q-crystalline thickenings to log prisms. Reduce the complete comparison modulo q−1. The reduced map is the log crystalline comparison, giving the equivalence by conservativity.

**Checks.**

- Over (A_inf, (ξ), O_C♭∖{0}) and X semistable: qΩ ≅ the (p, μ)-completed base change of Δ along φ (K1 Remark 8.3). Trivial log structures: BS22 Theorem 16.18 (Layer 5).

<a id="layer-8-log-q-de-rham-complex"></a>

### 8.23 Log q-de Rham complexes

Work over a prelog q-PD base (D,I,M_D) with D flat over Z_p[[q−1]]. Let (R,P) be integral, weakly finitely generated and log smooth over (D/I,M_D), with a log smooth lift over (D,M_D). The q-PD ideal I contains q−1. There are two presentations of the computational model, distinguished by the lattice they use.

For a free chart M_D⊕N^S, put E=D⟨N^S⟩, completed for (p,[p]_q), and write X_s for its generators. The automorphisms γ_s(X_s)=qX_s, γ_s(X_t)=X_t for t≠s, commute. Define D_s=(γ_s−1)/(q−1). Division is integral because γ_s≡1 modulo q−1 and q−1 is regular. Form the completed cochain Koszul complex K_S(E;D_s), with formal exterior basis e_s=dlog X_s. Extend the automorphisms and their divided differences to the exactification and the log q-PD envelope F of a surjection (E,M_D⊕N^S)→(R,P). This gives K_S(F;D_s). Its terms are F⊗̂_E Ω^j_{(E,M_D⊕N^S)/(D,M_D)}; all completions use (p,[p]_q).

For an integral submonoid N⊂M_D^gp⊕Z^S containing M_D, E_N denotes the completed monoid algebra D⊗_{Z_(p)[M_D]}Z_(p)[N]. Ambient γ_s and D_s still act on its monomials: for relative exponent a_s∈Z, γ_s(X^a)=q^{a_s}X^a and D_s(X^a)=[a_s]_qX^a, with [−n]_q=−q^{−n}[n]_q. They do **not** identify Ω¹_log(E_N/D) with E_N⊗Z^S unless the relative group lattice is identified with that lattice. In particular no ambient dlog X_s is declared an integral log form when X_s is absent. For such a chart construct the **resolved log q-de Rham model** by free prelog presentations over M_D, exactification, log q-PD envelopes and the corresponding augmented Čech diagrams of the free complexes just defined. Use their derived totalisation, with completed tensor products. The comparison below makes this model independent of the presentation and supplies its maps. This construction includes every integral N above; it does not assert that an arbitrary lattice presentation has a free differential basis.

Prove a canonical comparison qΩ_{(R,P)/(D,M_D)}≃K_S(F;D_s) for free presentations, and with the resolved model for arbitrary integral charts. These comparisons are natural in (R,P), in presentations, in refinements and in maps identifying coordinates, as morphisms in D_comp(D). Composition and all higher compatibilities are inherited from derived sections on the log q-crystalline site. No ordinary pullback on log forms is used as a q-complex map. Modulo q−1 the comparison identifies the resolved model with the intrinsic log de Rham complex of the p-completed log PD envelope, and a free presentation with its usual free-coordinate model.

On a free model Frobenius sends e_s to [p]_q e_s. If R is topologically finitely presented and its mod p fibre is of Cartier type, the resulting complex has cohomology in [0,r], where r is the rank of Ω¹_log(R/(D/I)), and the linearised Frobenius induces φ_D^*qΩ≃Lη_{[p]_q}qΩ. This statement concerns the intrinsic complex, so auxiliary free presentations with more than r generators do not change its amplitude.

([K1](#ref-k1), Constructions 7.15–7.16, pp.43–44; Theorem 7.17 and its proof, pp.44–45; Remark 7.18, p.45. The unrestricted ambient-basis reading of Construction 7.15 is replaced here by free presentations. The comparison retains arbitrary integral charts and coordinate identifications.)

*Needs:* [§8.21](#layer-8-log-q-pd-triple), [§8.22](#layer-8-log-q-crystalline-site), [§8.5](#layer-8-delta-log-groupification), [§8.22](#layer-8-log-q-crystalline-vs-crystalline), Layer 5, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`, `AInfCohomology:AI.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`.

Prove the following API:

- `LogQDeRham.gamma`: The commuting ambient automorphisms γ_s on E_N and their extensions to free-chart q-PD envelopes, with q acting as a unit. For a chosen intrinsic generator Y the free-chart automorphism is γ_Y(Y)=qY.
- `LogQDeRham.qNabla`: The integral operator D_s=(γ_s−1)/(q−1), giving Σ_sD_s(f)e_s on a free chart. On an arbitrary N its ambient scalar operators are kept separate from intrinsic log forms.
- `LogQDeRham.complex`: K_S(F;D_s) on free charts, and the completed resolved model on integral charts; a natural comparison from each free presentation to the resolved model.
- `LogQDeRham.mergeMap`: For a map of coordinate sets, the q-dependent Koszul map described below; its reduction is ordinary log pullback. It is D-linear and is not asserted F-linear in positive degrees.
- `LogQDeRham.computes`: The presentation-independent equivalence with qΩ, natural for all maps of surjections in the derived category, including coordinate identifications.
- `LogQDeRham.refinement_cocycle`: The derived maps for two successive refinements compose to the map for their composite; the comparison supplies coherent homotopies for changing ordering or presentations.
- `LogQDeRham.mod_q_sub_one`: Reduction gives intrinsic log de Rham cohomology of the p-completed log PD envelope.
- `LogQDeRham.frobenius_dlog`: On free coordinates Frobenius sends dlog X_s to [p]_q dlog X_s.
- `LogQDeRham.frobenius_l_eta`: Under the Cartier-type and finiteness hypotheses, φ_D^*qΩ≃Lη_{[p]_q}qΩ, so Frobenius admits an inverse up to [p]_q^r.

Here is the integral merge map needed for the comparison. Order the finite source coordinates; an infinite set is handled by finite supports before completion. For f:S→T, on a monomial X^a let b_t=Σ_{f(s)=t}a_s. Send its degree-zero coefficient to Y^b and its exterior generator e_s to q^{Σ_{r<s, f(r)=f(s)}a_r}e_{f(s)}. Extend by exterior powers on each monomial, so two generators mapping to the same direction have zero exterior product. The identity Σ_{f(s)=t}q^{Σ_{r<s, f(r)=t}a_r}[a_s]_q=[b_t]_q proves the chain-map equation, including negative exponents. Equivalently, replace each coefficient multiplier by the commuting operator ∏_{r<s,f(r)=f(s)}γ_r before applying the ring map. This operator formula is defined on F even when the envelope is not monomial graded: all γ_r extend as q-PD automorphisms, since they are δ-compatible and induce the identity modulo I; the universal property extends the chart map. The telescoping identity for ∏γ_r−1 proves the same equation without expanding coefficients. Torsionfreeness and continuity extend the divided differences to the envelope as in K1 Construction 7.16.

Orders are auxiliary. For a two-coordinate merge with exponents a,b, swapping the order changes the degree-one coefficients from (1,q^a) to (q^b,1). Their difference is ((1−q)[b]_q,(q−1)[a]_q). A chain homotopy sends the exterior pair to (q−1)e in degree one, with the sign fixed by d(v)=([a]_q e₀+[b]_q e₁)∧v; this accounts for both differences. With the opposite orientation on degree two, reverse that homotopy's sign. For larger diagrams use the augmented Čech comparison, rather than asserting that independently chosen orders make a strictly functorial family of chain maps.

Construct that comparison for the Čech nerve of a free surjection, ordering coordinates first by simplex slot and then by a fixed order within the slot. Use only the cofaces to form a semicosimplicial complex. The cofaces are coordinate injections and hence commute with the differentials. Its degree-zero row is the Čech–Alexander computation of the q-crystalline site and its zero column is K_S(F;D_s). For positive rows reduce modulo q−1. These are then the intrinsic log differential rows on the free presentation and its exactification, with the classical merging codegeneracies; the usual coordinate contraction makes their cosimplicial totalisations zero (Bhatt–de Jong [BdJ11](#ref-bdj11), Lemmas 2.15, 2.17 and Example 2.16, pp.5–6, applied to the free logarithmic basis). The initiality argument for Δ_inj→Δ in [§5.18](#layer-5-q-poincare-lemma) identifies those totalisations with the semicosimplicial ones. Reduction commutes with limits since q−1 is regular on D, and derived completeness and Nakayama make each positive row acyclic before reduction. The first-quadrant double-complex argument gives an equivalence from its totalisation to the zero row. Every coface on columns is an equivalence after reduction modulo q−1 by log crystalline embedding independence, and hence before reduction by complete Nakayama; evaluation therefore identifies the totalisation with the zero column. These are the required comparison zigzags. This proof never needs an ordinary merging pullback to commute with a q-differential.

To identify the displayed q-dependent merge map with the intrinsic derived map, apply it slot by slot to the two Čech diagrams. It commutes with every coface: slot injections preserve the relative order within each merging fibre, and automorphisms of newly inserted slots fix the image of the source envelope. Thus there is a map of the semicosimplicial double complexes. On row zero it is the ring map of envelopes, and on the zero column it is exactly the operator formula above. The two projections commute with it, so the comparison zigzags identify it with the map of site sections. This supplies the compatibility that agreement merely modulo q−1 would not imply. For two free presentations use their union; for several use iterated unions. Their augmentations to site sections identify all composites and supply coherent homotopies. Resolving an arbitrary N by such free prelog presentations applies this same comparison to its free resolutions and identifies its completed model with site sections. No ambient lattice is inverted. Frobenius and the Cartier conclusion follow by reduction to the intrinsic log Cartier isomorphism as in K1 Remark 7.18.

**Checks.**

- `LogQDeRham.affineLine_monomial`: In the free log affine line, D(X^n)=[n]_q X^n, including n=0 and n=2.
- `LogQDeRham.empty`: Empty relative coordinates give the envelope in degree zero.
- `LogQDeRham.q_one_limit`: At q=1 the free operators become X_s∂/∂X_s, the merge coefficients all become 1 and the resolved model gives intrinsic log de Rham cohomology.
- `LogQDeRham.coordinate_merge`: Under X₀,X₁↦X the q-dependent degree-one map sends X₀X₁(e₀+e₁) to (1+q)X²e, exactly the differential of X². Ordinary pullback would give 2X²e and fail by (q−1)X²e.
- `LogQDeRham.merge_order_homotopy`: Swapping the two source coordinates gives coefficients (q,1) instead of (1,q) on X₀X₁. The displayed degree-two homotopy accounts for their difference; strict equality of these chain maps is not a requirement.
- `LogQDeRham.missing_coordinate`: For N=2N⊂Z at p=2, use its intrinsic generator Y=X². The free presentation in Y has differential Y↦Y dlog Y. Its ambient-X operator gives (1+q)Y, but e_X is not an integral log form: converting it to dlog Y would divide by 2. The resolved model makes no such conversion and its q=1 reduction has coefficient 1 in the intrinsic basis.
- `LogQDeRham.intrinsic_lattice`: For N=Z the invertible generator has D(X^{−1})=−q^{−1}X^{−1}; a formula using only nonnegative exponents misses this chart.
- `LogQDeRham.not_nonlog_derivative`: On X^n the log operator gives [n]_qX^n, whereas the ordinary q-derivative gives [n]_qX^{n−1}. Dividing by X changes the theory and is not permitted at a boundary point.

- A semistable chart is computed by a free presentation followed by exactification, retaining dlog x+dlog y=0 for xy=π after intrinsic reduction. A refinement identifying two auxiliary coordinates uses the merge map and the comparison zigzag, not ordinary pullback. A chart with relative lattice 2Z is computed using that lattice's generator even in residue characteristic 2; it is never identified with Z by tensoring with Q.

### 8.24 Comparison with semistable AΩ

Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p, C the completed algebraic closure of W(k)[1/p], and X a p-adic formal scheme over O_C that is étale locally étale over O_C⟨t_0, …, t_r, t_{r+1}^{±1}, …, t_d^{±1}⟩/(t_0⋯t_r − π) for a nonzero non-unit π ∈ O_C, with its canonical log structure M_X (Česnavičius–Koshikawa 1.6). Then there is an isomorphism qΩ_{(X,M_X)/(A_inf,O_C♭∖{0})} ≅ AΩ_X in D(X_ét, A_inf) compatible with Frobenius, where the left side is formed over the prelog q-PD triple (A_inf, (ξ), O_C♭∖{0}) and the right side is ČK's semistable A_inf-cohomology. Since the mod p fibre is of Cartier type, qΩ is the (p, μ)-completed base change of Δ_{(X,M_X)/(A_inf,O_C♭∖{0})} along φ_{A_inf}; hence (φ^*_{A_inf}RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(A_inf, O_C♭∖{0})))^∧_{(p,φ(ξ))} ≅ RΓ_{A_inf}(X).

Semistable formal scheme over O_C in the sense of ČK19, with nonzero non-unit chart parameter π; C algebraically closed; compatible roots fixed as in ČK19 §1.5.

([K1](#ref-k1), §8, Theorem 8.1 (p. 45); [K1](#ref-k1), §8, Remark 8.3 (p. 45); [K1](#ref-k1), §1, Example 1.5 (p. 4).)

*Needs:* [§8.23](#layer-8-log-q-de-rham-complex), [§8.22](#layer-8-log-q-crystalline-vs-prismatic), [§8.11](#layer-8-standard-log-prisms), `AInfCohomology:AI.6`, Layer 5.

**Proof route.** Use the semistable ČK chart embedding into (O_C^♭∖{0})⊕Z^d to form the prescribed log q-de-Rham complexes. AI.6 identifies these with its semistable AΩ models, compatibly with étale maps and Frobenius, so they glue. Combine the q-crystalline/prismatic comparison with base change.

**Checks.**

- X = Spf(O_C⟨t^{±1}⟩) (trivial boundary) this is the torus case of BS22 Theorem 17.2 (Layer 5). For the semistable curve O_C⟨t_0, t_1⟩/(t_0t_1 − p) both sides are computed by the same Koszul complexes.

Let X be as in the semistable AΩ comparison and proper over O_C. The intended commutative comparison diagram has left column RΓ_logcrys((X,M_X)/(A_crys,O_C♭∖{0})) ≅ RΓ_qCRYS((X,M_X)/(A_inf,O_C♭∖{0})) ⊗^L_{A_inf} A_crys ≅ RΓ(X_ét,AΩ_X) ⊗^L_{A_inf} A_crys. The right column starts with RΓ_crys(X_C^ad/B_dR^+) → RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,Z_p) ⊗^L_{Z_p} B_dR^+, the period comparison map of ČK19 Proposition 6.8, followed by the usual isomorphism with RΓ_ét(X_C^ad,A_inf,X_C^ad) ⊗^L_{A_inf} B_dR^+. The first right-column map is not asserted an isomorphism over B_dR^+; it becomes one over B_dR. Horizontals are the ČK19 §6.8 maps transported via Theorem 8.1 and Remark 8.4. K1 Theorem 8.5 contains diagram misprints; this target specifies the corrected intended diagram, not the erroneous isomorphism as printed.

X proper semistable over O_C.

Transport its left column through the A_inf log q-crystalline comparison, then tensor with A_crys and identify each term with log de-Rham, respecting the direction of differential relation (5.15.2). Check ČK19 (6.8.4) before colimits and completions to prove commutativity.

<a id="layer-8-log-quasisyntomic-site"></a>

### 8.26 The log quasisyntomic site

Import DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-quasisyntomic-sites and expose its notions to log prismatic consumers under the API names below; no second site or QRSP definition is constructed in Layer 8. A map of pre-log rings A → B is p-completely homologically log flat (resp. faithfully flat) if B ⊗^L_A A/p ≅ B/p is discrete and (A/p, M_A) → (B/p, M_B) is homologically log flat (resp. homologically log faithfully flat) in the sense supplied by DD.6 (B′ ⊕^L_A B ≅ B′ ⊕_A B for all A → B′, plus faithful flatness of rings). A pre-log ring (A, M_A) is quasisyntomic if A is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and the Gabber log cotangent complex L_{(A,M_A)/Z_p} has p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]. A map A → B of p-complete pre-log rings with bounded p^∞-torsion is quasisyntomic (resp. a quasisyntomic cover) if it is p-completely homologically log flat (resp. faithfully flat) and L_{B/A} ⊗^L_B B/p has Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]. QSyn^prelog is the category of quasisyntomic pre-log rings; its opposite is a site with quasisyntomic covers. For (R, M) p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, qSyn_{(R,M)} is the small site of quasisyntomic maps (R, M) → (S, N); for perfectoid quasisyntomic (R, M), QSyn_{(R,M)} is the slice. On these sites the p-completion of ∧^i L_{(S,N)/(R,M)}[−i] lies in D^{≥0}(S).

Gabber's log cotangent complex and homologically log flat maps as supplied by DD.6. For trivial pre-log structures one recovers BMS2's quasisyntomic site (DD.5).

([KY](#ref-ky), §3.1, Definition 3.2 (p. 27); [KY](#ref-ky), §3.1, Definition 3.3 (p. 27); [KY](#ref-ky), §3.1, Corollary 3.7 (p. 28).)

*Needs:* `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-quasisyntomic-sites`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/homological-log-flatness`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/gabber-log-cotangent`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5/quasisyntomic-site`.

Prove the following API:

- `LogQSyn.IsQuasisyntomic`: The quasisyntomic condition on a pre-log ring.
- `LogQSyn.IsQuasisyntomicMap`: The quasisyntomic condition on a map, with the cover variant.
- `LogQSyn.site`: The site QSyn^{prelog,op} with quasisyntomic covers, and its small variant qSyn_{(R,M)}.
- `LogQSyn.of_cover`: For a quasisyntomic cover A → B, A is quasisyntomic iff B is.
- `LogQSyn.comp`: Quasisyntomic maps compose.
- `LogQSyn.pushout`: The p-completed pushout of a quasisyntomic map along any map is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion and quasisyntomic.
- `LogQSyn.trivialLog`: On pre-log rings with trivial pre-log structure, the notions agree with BMS2's quasisyntomic rings and maps (DD.5).
- `LogQSyn.cotangent_coconnective`: For (S, N) in qSyn_{(R,M)}, (∧^i L_{(S,N)/(R,M)}[−i])^∧_p ∈ D^{≥0}(S).

Use DD.6’s supplied results: KY Lemma 3.5 for a quasisyntomic cover A → B, A ∈ QSyn^prelog iff B ∈ QSyn^prelog (transitivity triangle and faithful flatness of A/p → B/p). Lemma 3.6: quasisyntomic maps compose; their p-completed pushouts are discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion and quasisyntomic over the other factor (using BMS2 Corollary 4.8 and base change of L). Corollary 3.7: QSyn^{prelog,op} is a site; Remarks 3.8–3.9 for the slice and small sites and the D^{≥0} property.

**Checks.**

- `LogQSyn.smoothLog_quasisyntomic`: (Z_p⟨T⟩, T^N) is quasisyntomic: its log cotangent complex is free of rank 1 on dlog T.
- `LogQSyn.trivialLog_eq`: (R, {e}) is in QSyn^prelog iff R is in BMS2's QSyn.
- `LogQSyn.zeroLog_lci`: (Z_p, N → Z_p, 1 ↦ 0) is quasisyntomic: L_{(Z_p,N)/Z_p} is concentrated in degrees [−1, 0] (KY Example 2.30).
- `LogQSyn.not_nonintegral`: For k of characteristic p ≠ 2, (k, P) → (k[x, y]/(x^2, xy, y^2), N^2), with P ⊂ N^2 generated by (2,0), (0,2), (1,1) and P∖{0} ↦ 0, is log étale in Kato's sense but not quasisyntomic: its log cotangent complex is unbounded on the left (KY Remark 2.13).
- `LogQSyn.empty_degenerate`: The identity of a quasisyntomic pre-log ring is a quasisyntomic cover.

- P-completions of smooth Z_p- or O_C-algebras with trivial pre-log structure are quasisyntomic. If (R, M) is a p-completely smooth log algebra over Z_p (in Koshikawa's sense), or the p-completion of a p-torsion free log complete intersection, then R ∈ QSyn^prelog (KY Example 3.4(2)).

<a id="layer-8-log-qrsp"></a>

### 8.27 Quasiregular semiperfectoid pre-log rings

Import DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-quasiregular-semiperfectoid and expose its notions to log prismatic consumers under the API names below; no second site or QRSP definition is constructed in Layer 8. A p-complete pre-log ring S = (S, M) is semiperfectoid if (1) there is a ring map R → S from a perfectoid ring; (2) S/p is semiperfect; (3) the natural map M♭ → M/M^× is surjective. It is quasiregular semiperfectoid if moreover (4) S is quasisyntomic. QRSPerfd^prelog denotes the category of quasiregular semiperfectoid pre-log rings. Conditions (2)–(3) (log-semiperfect) imply L_{(S,M)/R} ⊗^L S/p ∈ D^{≤−1}(S/p) for any R → S; for S quasiregular semiperfectoid, L̂_{(S,M)/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat. Equivalently (when S/p is log-semiperfect, S p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion), S ∈ QRSPerfd^prelog iff for some (equivalently every) perfectoid R → S, L_{(S,M)/R} ⊗^L S/p has Tor amplitude in degree −1.

p-complete pre-log rings; perfectoid in the sense of BMS1.

([KY](#ref-ky), §3.2, Definition 3.11 (p. 29); [KY](#ref-ky), §3.2, Lemma 3.16 (p. 30–31).)

*Needs:* [§8.26](#layer-8-log-quasisyntomic-site), [§8.13](#layer-8-perfectoid-monoid), Layer 2, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-quasiregular-semiperfectoid`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/gabber-log-cotangent`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-cotangent-functoriality`.

Prove the following API:

- `LogQRSP.IsSemiperfectoid`: Conditions (1)–(3).
- `LogQRSP.IsQRSP`: Conditions (1)–(4).
- `LogQRSP.cotangent_flat`: For S ∈ QRSPerfd^prelog, L̂_{(S,M)/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat.
- `LogQRSP.iff_cotangent`: Lemma 3.16: with S/p log-semiperfect and S p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, S is quasiregular semiperfectoid iff the log cotangent complex L_{(S,M)/R} ⊗^L S/p has Tor amplitude in degree −1 for some/any perfectoid R → S (R with trivial prelog structure).
- `LogQRSP.perfectoidCover`: The map (R ⊗̂ W(S♭) ⊗̂ Z_p⟨M♭⟩, M♭) → (S, M) of Remark 3.13.
- `LogQRSP.quotient_monoid`: Condition (3) passes to quotient monoids and pushouts (Remark 3.14).

Use DD.6’s four defining conditions and the variants (5)–(6) of Remark 3.12 and their implications. Remark 3.13: a semiperfectoid (S, M) receives (R ⊗̂ W(S♭) ⊗̂ Z_p⟨M♭⟩, M♭) → (S, M), surjective on rings and modulo units on monoids. Lemma 3.16: purity of π_1 of L_{R/Z_p} ⊗ S/p → L_{S/Z_p} ⊗ S/p, reduced to perfect fields k and Lemma 2.9 (via DD.6).

**Checks.**

- `LogQRSP.perfectoid_divisible`: (O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, N[1/p] → T^{N[1/p]}) is quasiregular semiperfectoid.
- `LogQRSP.trivialLog`: (S, S^×) is in QRSPerfd^prelog iff S is in BMS2's QRSPerfd (Layer 2/DD.5).
- `LogQRSP.log_line_not`: (Z_p⟨T⟩, T^N) is quasisyntomic but not semiperfectoid: N♭ = 0 does not surject onto N.
- `LogQRSP.zero_ring`: The zero pre-log ring is quasiregular semiperfectoid.

- (R, M) with R ∈ QRSPerfd and M uniquely p-divisible is in QRSPerfd^prelog (KY Example 3.15(1)). (O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}, Y^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X − Y), N[1/p] ⊕_N N[1/p]) is log quasiregular semiperfectoid (KY Example 3.15(2)).



<a id="layer-8-log-qrsp-basis"></a>

**Quasiregular semiperfectoid pre-log rings form a basis.**

(1) For maps A → B, A → C in QRSPerfd^prelog with A → B a quasisyntomic cover, the p-completed pushout lies in QRSPerfd^prelog and is a quasisyntomic cover of C; QRSPerfd^{prelog,op} is a site. (2) Every R ∈ QSyn^prelog admits a quasisyntomic cover R → S with S ∈ QRSPerfd^prelog, which can be chosen with p-divisible monoid. (3) For such a cover every term of the Čech nerve lies in QRSPerfd^prelog. (4) Consequently, for every presentable ∞-category C, restriction induces an equivalence Shv_C(QSyn^{prelog,op}) ≅ Shv_C(QRSPerfd^{prelog,op}).

Quasisyntomic topology; presentable target.

([KY](#ref-ky), §3.2, Lemma 3.18 (p. 32); [KY](#ref-ky), §3.2, Corollary 3.20 (p. 32).)

*Needs:* [§8.27](#layer-8-log-qrsp), [§8.26](#layer-8-log-quasisyntomic-site), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5`.

**Proof route.** Choose polynomial ring and free-monoid surjections, then adjoin compatible roots over O_C to obtain the QRSP prelog cover. Log cotangent transitivity gives its qsyn property and that of its Čech terms. The QRSP basis and Yoneda unfolding identify restriction and extension as inverse functors (KY Lemmas 3.17–3.19 and Corollary 3.20).

**Checks.**

- With trivial log structures, this is BMS2 Proposition 4.31 (DD.5). The log affine line (Z_p⟨T⟩, T^N) is covered by (O_C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, T^{N[1/p]}).

<a id="layer-8-derived-log-prismatic"></a>

### 8.28 Derived log prismatic cohomology

Fix a bounded prelog prism (A, I, M_A) with M_A integral. On the log-free pre-log rings Σ_{S,T} := (A/I⟨(X_s)_{s∈S}, N^T⟩, M_A ⊕ N^T) (S, T finite) consider Σ_{S,T} ↦ Δ_{Σ_{S,T}/(A,M_A)} := RΓ_Δ(Spf(Σ_{S,T})^a/(A, M_A)), a (p, I)-complete commutative algebra in D(A) with φ_A-semilinear Frobenius. The derived log prismatic cohomology (R, P) ↦ Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} is its left Kan extension (animation) to all simplicial (animated) pre-log rings over (A/I, M_A), followed by (p, I)-completion; it depends only on the derived p-completion of (R, P); Δ̄^L := Δ^L ⊗^L_A A/I. For a log p-adic formal scheme (X, M_X) over (A/I, M_A), the étale sheaf Δ^L_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} is the (p, I)-complete étale sheafification of U = Spf(R) ↦ Δ^L_{(R,Γ(U,M_X))/(A,M_A)}; similarly Δ̄^L and the conjugate filtration.

Animated pre-log rings as supplied by DD.6 (KY Remark 2.8) built on EDS E5:animation; (A, I, M_A) bounded with integral monoid.

([KY](#ref-ky), §4.1, Definition 4.3 (p. 33); [KY](#ref-ky), §4.2, Definition 4.9 (p. 35).)

*Needs:* [§8.16](#layer-8-log-prismatic-cohomology), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-hodge-tate-comparison), `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation`, Layer 2, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/free-prelog-resolutions`.

Prove the following API:

- `DerivedLogPrismatic`: The functor (R, P) ↦ Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} on animated pre-log (A/I, M_A)-algebras, with Frobenius.
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.reduced`: Δ̄^L := Δ^L ⊗^L_A A/I.
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.onFree`: On Σ_{S,T}, Δ^L agrees with the site-theoretic log prismatic cohomology.
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.leftKanExtension`: Δ^L preserves sifted colimits and is the unique such extension of its values on log-free algebras (after completion).
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.pComplete_invariant`: Δ^L depends only on the derived p-completion of (R, P).
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.sheaf`: The étale sheaf Δ^L_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} on a log p-adic formal scheme.
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.map`: Functoriality in (R, P) and in maps of bounded prelog prisms.

**Proof route.** Construct the theory on log-free compact projective generators and left Kan extend to animated prelog algebras. Globalize by étale sheafification. That step is necessary because global chart sections need not induce the original log structure on every smaller étale open.

**Checks.**

- `DerivedLogPrismatic.free_logLine`: For (A/I⟨N⟩, M_A ⊕ N), Δ̄^L has H^0 = A/I⟨X⟩ and H^1{1} free on dlog X.
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.base`: For (R, P) = (A/I, M_A), Δ^L = A.
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.trivialLog`: For P = M_A pulled back from the base, Δ^L_{(R,M_A)/(A,M_A)} ≅ BS22's Δ_{R/A} (Layer 2).
- `DerivedLogPrismatic.zeroLog_cotangent`: For (R, P) = (A/I, N → 0) over trivial M_A, the log cotangent complex is the two-term complex (A/I → A/I) with zero differential, in degrees −1 and 0 (KY Example 2.30, p.19). Thus the first conjugate graded piece has both degree-zero and degree-one cohomology. This does not infer the cohomology of the whole filtered object from a single graded piece.

- (R, P) = Σ_{S,T} the derived and site-theoretic values agree tautologically. For P = M_A (pulled back) one recovers BS22's derived prismatic cohomology Δ_{R/A} (Basic properties of derived log prismatic cohomology (1)).



<a id="layer-8-derived-log-hodge-tate"></a>

**Derived log Hodge–Tate comparison.**

For a simplicial pre-log ring (R, P) over (A/I, M_A), there is an increasing exhaustive multiplicative filtration Fil_• Δ̄_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} (the conjugate filtration) by derived p-complete objects with gr_i Δ̄_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} ≅ (∧^i L_{(R,P)/(A/I,M_A)}{−i}[−i])^∧_p. Globally, gr_i Δ̄^L_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} ≅ LΩ̂^i_{(X,M_X)/(A/I,M_A)}{−i}[−i] := (∧^i L_{(X,M_X)/(A/I,M_A)})^∧{−i}[−i].

(A, I, M_A) bounded with M_A integral.

([KY](#ref-ky), §4.1, Proposition 4.5 (p. 34); [KY](#ref-ky), §4.2, Remark 4.10 (p. 36).)

*Needs:* [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-prismatic), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-hodge-tate-comparison), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/gabber-log-cotangent`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-cartier`.

**Proof route.** On log-free generators the Hodge–Tate theorem identifies canonical cohomology pieces with completed exterior powers of the log cotangent complex. Left Kan extend the filtration, since its two sides preserve sifted colimits. Sheafification of the affine cotangent complexes is the geometric log cotangent complex by free resolutions and DD.6.

**Checks.**

- Smooth (R, P) with a smooth chart the filtration is the canonical filtration τ_{≤i}. For trivial log structures this is the derived Hodge–Tate comparison of BS22 §7 (Layer 2).


<a id="layer-8-derived-log-properties"></a>

**Basic properties of derived log prismatic cohomology.**

Let (A, I, M_A) be a bounded prelog prism with M_A integral. (1) For every derived p-complete simplicial ring R over A/I, Δ_{R/A} ≅ Δ^L_{(R,M_A)/(A,M_A)} (strict pull-back of the base log structure). (2) Δ^L is invariant under passing to the associated log ring: Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} ≅ Δ^L_{(R,P)^a/(A,M_A)}. (3) Base change: for a map of bounded prelog prisms (A, I, M_A) → (A′, IA′, M_{A′}) and (R′, P′) the homotopy base change, Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} ⊗̂^L_A A′ ≅ Δ^L_{(R′,P′)/(A′,M_{A′})}. (4) Multiplicativity: for the homotopy cofibre product (R_3, P_3) of (R_1, P_1), (R_2, P_2) over (A/I, M_A), Δ_1 ⊗̂^L_A Δ_2 ≅ Δ_3, compatibly with conjugate filtrations (Day convolution); Δ^L_{−/(A,M_A)} commutes with all colimits into the infinity category of derived (p,I)-complete commutative A-algebras. This is an algebra-valued assertion: the coproduct of two unit A-algebras is A, whereas their coproduct as A-modules is A⊕A. (5) For (A/I, M_A) perfectoid or pseudo-perfectoid, Δ^L_{(R,P)/A} ≅ Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)}.

As in Derived log prismatic cohomology.

([KY](#ref-ky), §4.1, Proposition 4.7 (p. 34); [KY](#ref-ky), §4.1, Proposition 4.7(3) (p. 34); [KY](#ref-ky), §6, Remark 6.2 (p. 59).)

*Needs:* [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-hodge-tate), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-prismatic), [§8.13](#layer-8-perfectoid-prelog-cotangent), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6`, Layer 2.

**Proof route.** For equal monoids the cotangent comparison and Hodge–Tate theorem identify the ordinary theory. Associated-log invariance and cotangent base change give the corresponding comparisons by derived Nakayama. Log-free differential-form calculations prove the remaining functor properties, and perfectoid log cotangent vanishing gives the last case.

**Checks.**

- The Breuil–Kisin → A_inf map (3) recovers K1 Example 1.6. (1) shows that strict smooth log schemes have the same prismatic cohomology as their underlying schemes.


<a id="layer-8-derived-vs-site"></a>

**Derived and site-theoretic log prismatic cohomology agree for smooth log formal schemes.**

Let (A, I, M_A) be bounded with M_A integral and (X, M_X) smooth over (A/I, M_A). (1) For every affine U = Spf(R) in X_ét, Δ^L_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)}(U) ≅ RΓ(((U, M_U)/(A, M_A))_Δ, O_Δ). (2) If P → Γ(U, M_X) is a smooth chart, Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} ≅ Δ^L_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)}(U); in particular for X = Spf(R) with smooth chart M_A → P, Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} ≅ RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(A, M_A)) compatibly with Hodge–Tate maps. Hence Δ^L_{(X,M_X)} ≅ Rν_*O_Δ, RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(A, M_A)) ≅ RΓ(X_ét, Δ^L_{(X,M_X)}), Δ̄^L ≅ Rν_*Ō_Δ, and the derived conjugate filtration is the canonical filtration τ_{≤i}Δ̄.

(X, M_X) smooth in Koshikawa's sense over a bounded prelog prism with integral monoid.

([KY](#ref-ky), §4.2, Proposition 4.12 (p. 36); [KY](#ref-ky), §4.1, Corollary 4.6 (p. 34).)

*Needs:* [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-hodge-tate), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-hodge-tate-comparison), [§8.16](#layer-8-log-prismatic-cohomology), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6`.

**Proof route.** Site functoriality constructs the maps of étale sheaves. Hodge–Tate compatibility reduces them to the sheafification comparison for log cotangent complexes. On a smooth chart that complex is the locally free log differentials, so derived Nakayama gives the equivalence.

**Checks.**

- The log affine line, both sides are computed by the Čech–Alexander complex of K1 §5.4. For trivial log structures this is the agreement of BS22 Construction 7.6 with site-theoretic prismatic cohomology for smooth algebras (Layer 2).


<a id="layer-8-log-quasisyntomic-descent"></a>

**Log quasisyntomic descent.**

Let (A, I, M_A) be a bounded prelog prism with M_A integral. On the small log quasisyntomic site qSyn_{(A/I,M_A)} the presheaf (R, P) ↦ Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} is a sheaf (with values in (p, I)-complete objects of D(A)); if (A/I, M_A) is a perfectoid pre-log ring, the same holds on QSyn_{(A/I,M_A)}. The same holds for each step of the conjugate filtration of Δ̄^L.

Bounded prelog prism with M_A integral; for the big site, (A/I, M_A) perfectoid.

([KY](#ref-ky), §4.1, Proposition 4.8 (p. 35).)

*Needs:* [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-hodge-tate), [§8.26](#layer-8-log-quasisyntomic-site), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-power-de-rham-descent`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-quasisyntomic-sites`.

**Proof route.** The qsyn log cotangent amplitude makes the shifted exterior pieces coconnective in the displayed convention. KY Proposition 2.47 proves their descent by the finite transitivity filtration: the top term descends by homological log faithful flatness and the lower terms vanish in the split double Čech direction. Apply the exhaustive conjugate filtration, whose common cohomological bound permits the totalization passage, and derived Nakayama.

**Checks.**

- With trivial log structures, this is BMS2/BS22 quasisyntomic descent of derived prismatic cohomology (Layer 2). The descent is not an ordinary flat descent on underlying rings: homologically log flat covers are required (Remark 2.46).

<a id="layer-8-initial-log-prism-qrsp"></a>

### 8.29 Initial log prisms of semiperfectoid pre-log rings

Let S = (S, N) be a semiperfectoid integral pre-log ring and (R, M) → (S, N) a map from a perfectoid integral pre-log ring, surjective on rings and modulo units on monoids. Exactify M♭ → M → N as M♭ → M̃ → N and put A_inf(R, M̃) := A_inf(R) ⊗̂ Z_p⟨M̃⟩ with the bounded rank-1 prelog prism (A_inf(R, M̃), (ξ), M̃). Applying prismatic envelopes to A_inf(R, M̃) → S gives a prelog prism (Δ^init_{S/R}, (ξ), M^init_{S/R} := M̃) with S → Δ^init/ξ and an exact surjection onto (Δ^init/ξ, N)^a, and its perfection Δ^init_{S/R,perf}. (1) For every integral ''log prism'' (A, I, M_A) with S → A/I and an exact surjection (A, M_A) → (A/I, N → A/I)^a there is a unique compatible map (Δ^init_{S/R}, (ξ), M^init) → (A, I, M_A); similarly for the perfections among perfect A (resp. perfect log prisms). (2) If S is quasiregular semiperfectoid, Δ_{S/A_inf(R)} is discrete with a δ-structure, Δ_{S/A_inf(R)} ≅ Δ^init_{S/R}, the latter is bounded and independent of R, giving an initial ''log prism'' (Δ^init_S, (ξ), M^init_S) for the category of exact-surjection diagrams. (3) If S is semiperfectoid, Δ_{S/R,perf} is discrete, a perfect prism, and Δ_{S/A_inf(R),perf} ≅ Δ^init_{S,perf}. (4) If moreover N is semiperfect (N♭ → N surjective), the p-saturation S^{p-sat} is semiperfectoid and Δ_{S/R,perf} ≅ Δ_{S^{p-sat}/R,perf}.

S semiperfectoid integral; R perfectoid integral; (R, M) → (S, N) surjective on rings and modulo units on monoids.

([KY](#ref-ky), §4.3, Proposition 4.14 (p. 38); [KY](#ref-ky), §4.3, Proposition 4.17 (p. 39); [KY](#ref-ky), §4.3, Corollary 4.21 (p. 41).)

*Needs:* [§8.13](#layer-8-perfect-log-prisms-perfectoid), [§8.27](#layer-8-log-qrsp), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-vs-site), [§8.8](#layer-8-delta-log-exactification), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-properties), Layer 2, Layer 0.

**Proof route.** The A_inf log lifting property and the general prelog-envelope universal property give initiality. In the quasiregular quotient case apply [§2.12](#layer-2-regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope)’s relative initiality, including unbounded targets, and the log Hodge–Tate calculation for discreteness. Perfection and the ordinary coconnectivity calculation give the perfect initial object, whose p-saturated monoid makes the resulting perfectoid log ring universal also after p-saturation.

**Checks.**

- S = O_C/p with trivial monoid: Δ^init = A_crys-type envelope; trivial-log case is BS22 §7. (4) is the key input of the Kummer-étale comparison: the φ-fixed points do not see p-saturation.

<a id="layer-8-log-nygaard-filtration"></a>

### 8.30 The log Nygaard filtration

Let (A, I, M_A) be an integral bounded prelog prism and write Δ^(1)_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} := Δ_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A. For the non-log local setup of KY §5.2 take A_0 = A⟨X_1,…,X_d⟩ with δ(X_i)=0 and R = A_0/(I,f_1,…,f_r), where the f_i form a p-completely regular sequence relative to A/I, and assume ∆^(1)_{R/A_0} is (p,I)-completely flat (Assumption 5.3). In this setup the Nygaard filtration is Fil^i_N Δ^(1)_{R/A_0} = {x : φ_{R/A_0}(x) ∈ I^iΔ_{R/A_0}} (Definition 5.5). For the log-free algebra (R, P) = (A/I⟨N^S⟩, M_A ⊕ N^S), choose a surjection M_A ⊕ N → M_A ⊕ N^S, exactify it (Construction 5.11) to obtain non-log prismatic cohomologies over the non-perfect base prisms Ã^•_∞ obtained by extracting p-power roots (Construction 5.9), and define Fil^i_N Δ^(1)_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} as the totalisation of Fil^i_N Δ_{(A/I)^•/Ã^•_∞} ⊗̂^L_{Ã^•_∞,φ} Ã^•_∞ (Definition 5.13), independent of the choice; extend to Σ_{S,T} by Day convolution with BS22's Nygaard filtration. Left Kan extension gives the derived Nygaard filtration Fil^•_N Δ^{L,(1)}_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} on all simplicial pre-log rings, with a filtered Frobenius φ: Fil^•_N Δ^{L,(1)} → I^•Δ^L and maps I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N → Fil^•_N; étale sheafification gives the global Nygaard filtration on Δ^{L,(1)}_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} (Constructions 5.25–5.26). It is multiplicative.

(A, I, M_A) integral bounded prelog prism; animated pre-log rings (DD.6). The displayed non-log preimage formula is restricted to the §5.2 regular-presentation setup and Assumption 5.3; Proposition 5.7 gives its completed flat base-change compatibility, rather than defining it for arbitrary flat maps.

([KY](#ref-ky), §5.2, Assumption 5.3 and Definition 5.5 (pp. 43–44); [KY](#ref-ky), §5.2, Proposition 5.7 (pp. 45–46); [KY](#ref-ky), §5.4, Definition 5.13 (p. 49); [KY](#ref-ky), §5.5 (p. 50); [KY](#ref-ky), §1 (p. 5).)

Prove the following API:

- `LogNygaard.fil`: The decreasing multiplicative filtration Fil^•_N Δ^{L,(1)}_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} by (p, I)-complete objects.
- `LogNygaard.frobenius`: The filtered Frobenius φ: Fil^i_N Δ^{L,(1)} → I^iΔ^L.
- `LogNygaard.mulI`: The maps I ⊗^L Fil^{i−1}_N → Fil^i_N (Construction 5.21).
- `LogNygaard.mul`: Fil^i_N ⊗ Fil^j_N → Fil^{i+j}_N (Remark 5.20).
- `LogNygaard.free_eq_bs`: For trivial log structures, Fil^•_N is BS22's Nygaard filtration on Δ^(1) (Layer 3).
- `LogNygaard.flatBaseChange`: Formation of Fil^•_N commutes with (p, I)-completely flat base change on A.
- `LogNygaard.sheaf`: The global Nygaard filtration on Δ^{L,(1)}_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} by étale sheafification.

**Proof route.** Flat base change identifies the exact-surjection definition with ordinary derived Nygaard. Adjoin monoid roots and use Frobenius descent and the cosimplicial calculation to prove independence and identify graded pieces. Define on log-free generators, left Kan extend and sheafify; multiplication descends with these maps.

- `LogNygaard.fil0`: Fil^0_N Δ^{L,(1)} = Δ^{L,(1)}.
- `LogNygaard.trivialLog`: For (R, P) = (A/I⟨X⟩, M_A) with trivial M_A, Fil^•_N agrees with BS22's Nygaard filtration on Δ^(1)_{R/A}.
- `LogNygaard.logLine_gr1`: For (R, P) = (A/I⟨N⟩, M_A ⊕ N), gr^1_N Δ^(1) ≅ τ_{≤1}Δ̄{1}, a two-term object with H^0 ≅ R{1} and H^1 ≅ R·dlog X.
- `LogNygaard.naive_fails`: For KY's toy example over (A_inf, (ξ)) the naive filtration {x : φ(x) ∈ ξ^iΔ} on Δ^(1)_{(S,M)/(A,M_A)} differs from Fil^•_N (KY §5.1).
- `LogNygaard.frobenius_fil1`: φ(Fil^1_N) ⊂ IΔ and the induced map gr^0_N → Δ̄ is the inclusion of Fil_0 Δ̄ = (derived) R.

- Trivial M_A and P the construction recovers BS22's Nygaard filtration (Layer 3). The naive condition φ(x) ∈ I^iΔ on Δ^(1)_{(S,M)/(A,M_A)} for log QRSP S does not give the right filtration (KY §5.1 toy example).



<a id="layer-8-log-nygaard-graded"></a>

**Graded pieces of the log Nygaard filtration.**

Let (A, I, M_A) be an integral bounded prelog prism and (R, P) a simplicial pre-log ring over (A/I, M_A). The Frobenius induces an isomorphism gr^i_N Δ^{L,(1)}_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} ≅ Fil_i Δ̄^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)}{i}, where Fil_i is the conjugate filtration. For Σ_{S,T} this reads gr^i_N Δ^(1)_{Σ_{S,T}} ≅ τ_{≤i}Δ̄_{Σ_{S,T}}{i}; globally gr^i_N Δ^{L,(1)}_{(X,M_X)} ≅ Fil_i Δ̄^L_{(X,M_X)}{i}, and for (X, M_X) smooth over (A/I, M_A), gr^•_N Δ^(1)_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} ≅ τ_{≤•}Δ̄_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)}{•}.

As in The log Nygaard filtration; smoothness for the last assertion.

([KY](#ref-ky), §5, Theorem 5.1 (p. 42); [KY](#ref-ky), §5.7, Corollary 5.27 (p. 54).)

*Needs:* [§8.30](#layer-8-log-nygaard-filtration), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-hodge-tate), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-vs-site), Layer 3.

**Proof route.** On log-free generators the divided Frobenius square identifies the graded image with τ≤i. Derive its fibre sequence. Sheafification gives the smooth formula because the conjugate filtration is then the canonical truncation.

**Checks.**

- i = 0: gr^0_N ≅ Fil_0 Δ̄ = R. Trivial log structures: BS22 Theorem 15.2 (Layer 3).


<a id="layer-8-nygaard-hodge-fiber-sequence"></a>

**The Nygaard–Hodge fibre sequence and Nygaard completeness.**

For a simplicial pre-log ring (R, P) over (A/I, M_A) there is a functorial fibre sequence I ⊗^L_A Fil^{•−1}_N Δ^{L,(1)} → Fil^•_N Δ^{L,(1)} → Fil^•_H LΩ̂_{(R,P)/(A/I,M_A)} of filtered objects, the second map being the derived de Rham specialisation γ^• (Construction 5.21, Lemma 5.22). Globally on X_ét it holds with the p-complete étale sheafified Hodge-filtered derived log de Rham complex. If (X, M_X) is smooth over (A/I, M_A) with mod p fibre of Cartier type, the right term becomes Ω^{≥•}_{(X,M_X)/(A/I,M_A)}; if moreover X is qcqs and Ω^1_log has finite rank D, then for i ≥ 0 and j ≥ D the maps RΓ(Fil^j_N Δ^(1)) ⊗^L I^i → RΓ(Fil^{i+j}_N Δ^(1)) are isomorphisms and RΓ(X_ét, Δ^(1)) is complete for the Nygaard filtration.

Derived log de Rham with Hodge filtration from DD.6; Cartier type and finite rank for the last assertions.

([KY](#ref-ky), §5.6, Proposition 5.24 (pp.53–54); [KY](#ref-ky), §5.7, Corollary 5.35 (p. 58).)

*Needs:* [§8.30](#layer-8-log-nygaard-filtration), [§8.30](#layer-8-log-nygaard-graded), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6`, Layer 4.

**Proof route.** Construct γ on log-free generators, compatible with the ordinary comparison, and prove its fibre sequence there. Derive and sheafify the comparison. Under Cartier type DD.6 identifies completed derived log de-Rham with ordinary log de-Rham, so vanishing above dimension makes the deep Nygaard filtration I-adic and proves completeness.


<a id="layer-8-log-l-eta-factorization"></a>

**The Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius.**

Let (A, I, M_A) be bounded with M_A integral. (1) If (R, P) is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and P → R is a smooth chart over (A/I, M_A), then gr^i_N Δ^{L,(1)} ≅ τ_{≤i}Δ̄^L{i} and the Frobenius factors as Δ^L ⊗̂^L_{A,φ} A = Δ^{L,(1)} → Lη_IΔ^L → Δ^L; if M_A → P is of Cartier type, Δ^{L,(1)} → Lη_IΔ^L is an isomorphism identifying the Nygaard filtration with the truncations of the I-adic filtration for the Beilinson t-structure. (2) For (X, M_X) smooth over (A/I, M_A), U ↦ Lη_I(Δ_{(X,M_X)}(U)) is a sheaf on the affine étale site, defining Lη_IΔ_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)}; if the mod p fibre is of Cartier type, Frobenius induces an isomorphism of étale sheaves Δ^(1)_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} ≅ Lη_IΔ_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)}, and RΓ_Δ((U, M_U)/(A, M_A))^(1) ≅ Lη_I RΓ_Δ((U, M_U)/(A, M_A)) for affine U.

Smooth log formal algebras in (1), with the stated chart; Cartier type of the chart (1) or of the mod p fibre (2); Lη_I as supplied by AI.1 through Layer 3.

([KY](#ref-ky), §5.5, Corollary 5.17 (p. 51); [KY](#ref-ky), §5.7, Proposition 5.29 (p. 55).)

*Needs:* [§8.30](#layer-8-log-nygaard-graded), [§8.20](#layer-8-log-crystalline-comparison), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-vs-site), Layer 3, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6`.

**Proof route.** The graded truncation formula factors Frobenius through the Beilinson cover and Lη. Under Cartier type reduce modulo I, identify the Bockstein complex with log de-Rham, and reduce on log-free generators through the universal orientation to the crystalline prism, where log crystalline Cartier compatibility proves the map is an isomorphism. Étale descent globalizes it (KY Proposition 5.29).


<a id="layer-8-log-de-rham-comparison"></a>

**The log de Rham comparison.**

(1) If P → R is a smooth chart of Cartier type over (A/I, M_A), Δ^L_{(R,P)/(A,M_A)} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ} A/I ≅ Ω̂^•_{(R,P)/(A/I,M_A)} as E_∞-algebras in D(A/I). (2) For every simplicial pre-log ring (R, P) over (A/I, M_A), Δ^L ⊗̂^L_{A,φ} A/I ≅ LΩ̂_{(R,P)/(A/I,M_A)} (p-completed derived log de Rham). (3) For (X, M_X) smooth over (A/I, M_A) with mod p fibre of Cartier type, Δ_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I ≅ Ω^•_{(X,M_X)/(A/I,M_A)} as étale sheaves, and for qcqs X, RΓ_logdR((X, M_X)/(A/I, M_A)) ≅ RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(A, M_A)) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I as E_∞-A-algebras.

(A, I, M_A) is bounded with M_A integral. Cartier type is required for the smooth-chart clause (1) and the mod-p fibre in the global smooth clause (3); clause (2) applies to every animated pre-log algebra without a Cartier-type assumption.

([KY](#ref-ky), §5.5, Corollary 5.18 (p. 51); [KY](#ref-ky), §1, Theorem 2(4) (p. 3).)

*Needs:* [§8.30](#layer-8-log-l-eta-factorization), [§8.30](#layer-8-nygaard-hodge-fiber-sequence), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-hodge-tate-comparison), `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-derived-de-rham`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6/log-smooth-cartier-comparison`.

**Proof route.** Reduce the Lη isomorphism modulo I and apply log Hodge–Tate. Derive the log-free calculation via its Fil⁰ fibre sequence for the animated statement. The global comparison follows by the same reduction.

**Checks.**

- (A, I) = (W(k)[[u]], (E)): base change to the PD envelope S and specialisation recovers K1 footnote 7's route. Trivial log: BS22 Theorem 1.8(3) (Layer 1).


<a id="layer-8-log-frobenius-isogeny"></a>

**Frobenius is an isogeny.**

Let (X, M_X) be smooth over (A/I, M_A) with mod p fibre of Cartier type. For each i ≥ 0 there are natural maps V_i: τ_{≤i}Δ_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} ⊗^L_A I^i → τ_{≤i}Δ^(1)_{(X,M_X)/(A,M_A)} with φ∘V_i and V_i∘(φ ⊗ 1) equal to the maps induced by I^i ⊂ A. If X is qcqs, V_i: H^i_Δ((X, M_X)/(A, M_A)) ⊗_A I^i → H^i(RΓ_Δ ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A) inverts Frobenius up to I^i; for I = (d) principal, φ∘V_i = V_i∘φ = d^i. If Ω^1_log has finite rank D, a single V inverts φ up to I^D; in particular the linearised Frobenius RΓ_Δ ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A → RΓ_Δ becomes an isomorphism after inverting I.

Mod p fibre of Cartier type; qcqs for the global maps; finite rank D for the uniform bound.

([KY](#ref-ky), §5.7, Corollary 5.31 (p. 56–57); [KY](#ref-ky), §1, Theorem 2(6) (p. 3).)

*Needs:* [§8.30](#layer-8-log-l-eta-factorization), Layer 3.

**Proof route.** Apply AI.1’s BMS1 Lemma 6.9 to the Lη isomorphism: on τ≤i it has an inverse up to I^i. Take global cohomology to obtain the maps. The finite log-differential rank bounds the uniform exponent.

- At i=0 the specialization map is Δ^(1)→LΩ̂. For the log affine line over (Z_p,(p)) its graded factorization is the log Cartier map. Over the q-prism (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)), the Frobenius isogeny specializes to K1 Remark 7.18’s inverse up to the stated power [p]_q^r; no integral inverse before that multiplication is asserted.

<a id="layer-8-breuil-kisin-log-cohomology"></a>

### 8.31 Breuil–Kisin cohomology of semistable formal schemes

Let K be a totally ramified finite extension of W(k)[1/p] with uniformiser π and X a qcqs semistable formal scheme over O_K with canonical log structure M_X. Define RΓ_BK(X) := RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(W(k)[[u]], N)) over the Breuil–Kisin prelog prism. Then (A_inf ⊗^L_{W(k)[[u]]} RΓ_BK(X))^∧_(p,ξ) ≅ RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)_{O_C}/(A_inf, O_C♭∖{0})), which together with the semistable AΩ comparison is a Breuil–Kisin descent of the A_inf-cohomology of X_{O_C}; if X is proper, RΓ_BK(X) is perfect and the base change holds without completion. Its Frobenius is φ-semilinear over u ↦ u^p, and over (W(k)[[u]], N) the Frobenius is an isogeny when the mod p fibre is of Cartier type.

X qcqs semistable over O_K; canonical log structure M_X = (O_X[1/p])^× ∩ O_X.

([K1](#ref-k1), §1, Example 1.6 (p. 5); [K1](#ref-k1), §1, Example 1.6 (p. 5).)

- `BreuilKisinLogCohomology.toHyodoKato`: Base change along u ↦ 0 and Frobenius twist gives RΓ_crys((X_k, M)/(W(k), N)) (The log crystalline comparison).

**Proof route.** The semistable chart is smooth in Koshikawa’s sense over the Breuil–Kisin quotient. Completed base change to A_inf and the semistable AΩ comparison identify its realization, while log Hodge–Tate gives proper perfectness. The Cartier-type Frobenius isogeny theorem gives the asserted Frobenius bound.

<a id="layer-8-kummer-etale-site-log-scheme"></a>

### 8.32 The Kummer étale site of an fs log scheme

A homomorphism of fs monoids h: P → Q is of Kummer type if it is injective and every a ∈ Q has a power a^n (n ≥ 1) in h(P); a morphism f: X → Y of fs log schemes is of Kummer type if M_{Y,f(x)}/O^× → M_{X,x}/O^× is of Kummer type for every x. For an fs log scheme X, the Kummer étale site X_két is the category (fs/X) (or its small variant of Kummer étale X-schemes) with coverings the families {f_i: U_i → X} of log étale morphisms of Kummer type with X = ∪ f_i(U_i); RΓ_két(X, Λ) is its cohomology. For a pre-log ring (R[1/p], P) with P saturated (not necessarily fine), RΓ_két(Spec(R[1/p], P)^a, Λ) := colim_{P_i ⊂ P} RΓ_két(Spec(R[1/p], P_i)^a, Λ), over fine saturated submonoids P_i (a filtered colimit). Standard covers: for P → Q of Kummer type with Q fs, Spec(R ⊗_{Z[P]} Z[Q], Q)^a → Spec(R, P)^a is a Kummer étale cover when the index is invertible on R.

fs log schemes (CR.5); Kummer-étale coverings are log étale (Kato) and of Kummer type.

([KatoII](#ref-katoii), §2, Definition 2.1 (p. 6); [KatoII](#ref-katoii), §2, Definition 2.3 (p. 7); [KY](#ref-ky), §6, after Theorem 6.1 (p. 59).)

*Needs:* Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra/fine-monoid`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra/saturated-monoid`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra/kummer-morphism`.

Prove the following API:

- `KummerEtale.IsKummerType`: Kummer type for maps of fs monoids and morphisms of fs log schemes.
- `KummerEtale.site`: The Kummer étale site X_két of an fs log scheme.
- `KummerEtale.cohomology`: RΓ_két(X, Λ) for a torsion abelian group Λ, and its colimit extension to saturated charts.
- `KummerEtale.standardCover`: For P → Q of Kummer type with index invertible, Spec(R ⊗_{Z[P]} Z[Q], Q)^a → Spec(R, P)^a is a covering.
- `KummerEtale.trivialLog`: For trivial log structure X_két ≃ X_ét.
- `KummerEtale.baseChange`: Kummer étale covers are stable under fs base change; morphisms of fs log schemes induce morphisms of sites.
- `KummerEtale.toLogEtale`: For constant torsion Λ, Kummer étale and full log étale cohomology agree (Nakayama II Proposition 5.4, KY Remark 6.3).

**Proof route.** Use the chart definition of Kummer maps. Fs base change and composition preserve the coverings, giving the topology. Derived sections and the filtered extension over saturated charts define the indicated cohomology.

**Checks.**

- `KummerEtale.trivialLog_eq`: For X with trivial log structure, RΓ_két(X, Λ) = RΓ_ét(X, Λ).
- `KummerEtale.kummerType_nat`: For n ≥ 1, N → N, 1 ↦ n is of Kummer type; at n = 0 it is not injective. The diagonal N → N^2, 1 ↦ (1,1) is not of Kummer type (not every element has a positive multiple in the image).
- `KummerEtale.empty`: The empty family covers the empty log scheme.
- `KummerEtale.not_etale`: For n > 1 and K algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and the log point X = Spec(K, N → 0)^a, H^1_két(X, Z/n) ≅ Z/n(−1) ≠ 0 = H^1_ét(Spec K, Z/n): Kummer étale cohomology is not étale cohomology of the underlying scheme.

- Trivial log structure X_két is X_ét. For K algebraically closed of characteristic 0, the log point Spec(K, N → 0)^a has H^1_két(−, Z/n) ≅ Z/n(−1) (its Kummer covers adjoin n-th roots of the log generator), while Spec K has no étale H^1.

<a id="layer-8-fs-log-adic-kummer-foundations"></a>

### 8.33 Fs log adic Kummer foundations

On an étale-sheafy adic space X, a log structure is a sheaf of commutative monoids M→O_X on X_ét whose inverse image of O_X^× maps isomorphically to O_X^×. Logification is the sheaf pushout along those units; pullback first pulls back the prelog sheaf and then logifies. An adic chart P→M identifies the associated log sheaf and its map to O_X factors through O_X^+; fs means fs charts exist étale locally. Strictness means the pullback log structure maps isomorphically to the source log structure. For locally noetherian fs X, X_két consists of fs Kummer log-étale spaces over X with jointly surjective coverings, using fs fibre products. A Kummer map is injective on sharp characteristic stalks and every target element has a positive power in the image. Loc_Λ(X_két) consists of finite locally free Λ-sheaves; in the finite-free convention of KYcorr a Z_p-local system is a compatible inverse system of finite free Z/p^n-local systems, n≥1 (DLLZ Definition 6.3.1 also permits finitely generated torsion stalks). For ε:X_két→X_ét and n invertible on X, R^iε_*(Z/n)≅∧^i(M̄_X^gp/nM̄_X^gp)(−i), including i=0. Local log inertia at a geometric point ξ is Hom(M̄_ξ^gp,Ẑ′(1)); its continuous action computes higher direct-image stalks. These noetherian site/cohomology claims do not impose noetherianity on the separate perfectoid log adic construction.

Basic log definitions require an étale-sheafy adic space; both locally noetherian and perfectoid adic spaces have this property. The Kummer site, inertia and higher direct-image statements here require locally noetherian fs spaces; torsion coefficient index n is positive and invertible on the base. The cup-product formula keeps the Tate twist: ∧^i R^1ε_*μ_n maps to R^iε_*(μ_n^{⊗i}). The untwisted μ_n-only formula does not give the degree-i coefficient system.

([DLLZ](#ref-dllz), Definitions 2.2.2 and 2.3.1, pp. 8–9, 13; §4.1, pp. 41–47; Theorem 4.4.15 and Corollaries 4.4.18, 4.4.22, pp. 61–63; Lemma 4.4.27, (4.4.28) and Lemma 4.4.29, pp. 64–65; [KYcorr](#ref-kycorr), Setup before Definition 4 (pp. 2–3).)

*Needs:* AdicEtaleGeometry, Layer A1 (étale site), AdicEtaleGeometry, Layer A1 (étale structure sheaf), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra`, Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tate-twists`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/geometric-stalks-at-field-pairs`, `ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cartan-leray-spectral-sequence`.

Prove the following API:

- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.kummerSite`: The category of fs Kummer log-étale objects over a locally noetherian fs log adic space.
- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.kummerTopology`: The topology of families jointly surjective on underlying spaces, with fs pullbacks.
- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.LocalSystem`: Finite locally free Λ-sheaves on the Kummer-étale site; Z_p coefficients are read as compatible finite-free positive levels.
- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.cohomology`: Derived Kummer-étale cohomology with constant finite torsion coefficients.
- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.trivialLogSite`: For trivial logs the Kummer-étale site is equivalent to the ordinary étale site.
- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.inertiaExterior`: For a geometric point, R^iε_*(Z/n) is the i-th exterior characteristic group modulo n with twist (−i).

**Proof route.** Apply logification and saturation to the étale monoid sheaves, and use DLLZ’s chart-local Kummer maps to define the adic topology and finite Kummer descent. DLLZ Corollary 4.4.22 and Lemma 4.4.27 identify local inertia and higher direct-image stalks by continuous cohomology. The Kummer sequence and local divisibility of units give degree one, and cup products give the exterior formula with its stated Tate twist.

**Checks.**

- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.trivialSite_test`: The Kummer site of a noetherian adic space with trivial log recovers its ordinary étale site.
- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.rankOneH1`: At a geometric rank-one log point over an algebraically closed complete characteristic-zero field, H^1 of constant Z/n is noncanonically Z/n, n>1.
- `NoetherianFsLogAdicSpace.rankZeroH1`: The same underlying geometric point with trivial log has zero H^1 of constant Z/n, n>0.

- Trivial logs give the ordinary étale site and vanish in positive inertia cohomology. At the geometric rank-one log point, degree one is Z/n(−1) and exterior degrees above one vanish. The n-root log disc cover, n>1, is Kummer-étale but its underlying adic map is ramified at the boundary.



<a id="layer-8-log-scheme-vs-log-adic-kummer"></a>

**Kummer étale cohomology of log schemes and of log adic spaces.**

Let n ≥ 1 and Λ = Z/nZ and (R, P) a classically p-complete fs pre-log ring with R topologically finitely generated over a noetherian ring A_0. With X = Spec(R[1/p], P)^a and X^ad = (Spa(R[1/p], R), P)^a the associated fs log adic space (Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu), there is a natural isomorphism RΓ_két(X, Λ) ≅ RΓ_két(X^ad, Λ).

Fs pre-log ring; R topologically of finite type over a noetherian base; Spa(R[1/p], R) is then an adic space. The coefficient modulus n is positive; ZMod 0 = Z is outside this torsion comparison.

([KY](#ref-ky), §6, Lemma 6.5 (p. 60).)
