**Proof route.** Huber comparison and Grothendieck–Serre reduce to the higher direct images of the forgetful maps. The scheme and adic calculations both identify them with ∧^i(M^gp/nM^gp)(−i). Their chart compatibility gives the base-change equivalence.

**Checks.**

- P trivial this is Huber's comparison of étale cohomology of Spec(R[1/p]) and its adic analytification. For (Z_p⟨T⟩, T^N) both sides compute the Kummer étale cohomology of the closed log disc, retaining its boundary T = 0.

<a id="layer-8-affine-kummer-etale-comparison"></a>

### 8.34 The affine Kummer-étale comparison

Let (A, I = (d)) be a perfect prism with I ≠ (p), and (R, P) a p-adically complete pre-log A/I-algebra with P saturated and R of bounded p^∞-torsion. For each n ≥ 1 there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_két(Spec(R[1/p], P)^a, Z/p^n) ≅ (Δ^L_{(R,P)/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}, functorial in (R, P), where (−)^{φ=1} is the derived fibre of φ − 1. The base prism may be replaced by any perfect log prism, or by a pre-log prism with (A/I, M_A) perfectoid or pseudo-perfectoid (Basic properties of derived log prismatic cohomology (5)); the left side may equally be the full log étale cohomology.

Perfect prism, I ≠ (p) (both sides vanish for I = (p)); P saturated; bounded p^∞-torsion.

([KY](#ref-ky), §6, Theorem 6.1 (p. 59); [KY](#ref-ky), §1 (p. 6).)

*Needs:* [§8.32](#layer-8-kummer-etale-site-log-scheme), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-prismatic), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-log-properties), [§8.29](#layer-8-initial-log-prism-qrsp), [§8.28](#layer-8-log-quasisyntomic-descent), [§6.6](#layer-6-etale-comparison), [§6.7](#layer-6-etale-comparison-coefficients).

**Proof route.** The chart-root cover has uniform descendability index at most two: reduce to one log coordinate modulo (p,φ^−1(d)), where the fibre’s tensor square vanishes by the negative-Ext bound, and pass through perfection and localization. Construct the map on its saturated Čech nerve; exactification adjoins root ratios, and p-divisible groupification makes the perfected presentations agree, so p-saturation leaves the fixed-point calculation unchanged (KY Lemmas 6.17–6.18). Saturated perfectoid terms have ordinary étale p-cohomology because the characteristic-group exterior pieces vanish in the root tower; strict log base change and Fujiwara–Gabber compare the henselian puncture with its completion, after which ordinary perfectoid comparison and descent give the result.

**Checks.**

- P trivial this is BS22's étale comparison Theorem 9.1 for perfect prisms (Layer 6). For R=O_C⟨X⟩ with N→R, 1↦X, the comparison applies to the log affine line (KY Proposition 6.16, p.66). In the associated log adic disc, at the geometric boundary point X=0, the logarithmic higher-direct-image stalk R¹ε_*(Z/p^n) is Z/p^n(−1), where ε forgets the log structure; this is the boundary-inertia contribution, not a calculation of all global H¹ (DLLZ Lemmas 4.4.27 and 4.4.29, pp.64–65). As a negative control, y^p=1+pX is an ordinary finite étale cover of Spec(C⟨X⟩): 1+pX is a unit and py^(p−1) is invertible. It has no section, since any root with constant term 1 has formal coefficients binomial(1/p,m)p^m of valuation −v_p(m!), which do not tend to +∞. Its Kummer class restricts trivially to boundary inertia, whereas the class of X has nonzero boundary inertia. Global log H¹ therefore contains ordinary étale classes as well as the boundary class.

<a id="layer-8-untilt-coefficients"></a>

### 8.35 Completed untilt sheaves and profinite coefficients

Let Y be a diamond with a specified map Y→Spd Q_p. On an affinoid perfectoid U=Spa(R,R⁺) in Y_v this map chooses a marked untilt U^♯=Spa(R^♯,R^♯⁺). Define the ring sheaves Ǒ_Y and Ǒ⁺_Y by the sections R^♯ and R^♯⁺ on this basis. Restrict to Y_qproét to obtain Ô_Y and Ô⁺_Y. The marked map is part of the data; the characteristic-p diamond alone does not determine these rings. Pullback of marked untilts gives their restriction maps. With λ:Y_v→Y_qproét, prove λ_*Ǒ^(+)_Y=Ô^(+)_Y, Rλ_*Ǒ_Y≃Ô_Y, and the corresponding almost comparisons for Ǒ⁺ and its pseudouniformizer quotients. The integral higher direct images are not asserted to vanish exactly.

For a condensed ring Λ, represented using Mathlib `Condensed CommRingCat`, use the existing condensed carrier and define Λ_Y as inverse image under Y_qproét→Profinite, with the finite jointly surjective topology, and similarly on Y_v. These geometric morphisms send a profinite set S to the relative constant diamond Y×S. For a T₁ topological coefficient ring Λ, its v-sheaf has sections Cont(|U|,Λ). For Λ=Z_p the topology is its p-adic topology. Define its local systems to be sheaves locally isomorphic to Λ_Y^r for a finite locally constant rank r. Prove Loc_(Z_p)(Y_qproét)≃lim_n Loc_(Z/p^n)(Y_qproét), and the same on the v-site, with quasi-pro-étale/v equivalence for these coefficients. On a locally spatial Y, the finite discrete coefficient local systems also agree with their étale versions. This does not identify p-adic local systems with local systems for the discrete ring Z_p.

([MW20](#ref-mw20), Definition 2.1 and equation (2.1.1), p.9; Lemmas 2.7, 2.9, pp.11–12; Definitions 3.1–3.3, pp.16–17; Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.5, pp.17–19; Propositions 3.7, 3.9, pp.20–21; Corollary 3.15, pp.23–24. [KY](#ref-ky), §7.1, pp.71–72.)

*Needs:* `DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/spd-of-a-tate-pair`, `D6/untilt-descent-along-v-covers`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D2/v-descent-of-functions`, `D2/higher-v-acyclicity`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D1`, `DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0/quasi-pro-etale-site`, `C0/pullback-preserves-limits`, `C0/quasi-pro-etale-pullback-fully-faithful`, `C2/etale-test-on-one-cover`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`, `PerfectoidSpaces:P1`, and Mathlib `CondensedSet` and `Condensed` applied to `CommRingCat` (Mathlib/Condensed/Basic.lean). The latter reuses the generic condensed-object carrier; it does not require a separately named condensed-ring structure.

Prove the following API:

- `DiamondCoefficients.untiltStructure`: The pair (Ǒ_Y,Ǒ⁺_Y) of v-ring sheaves associated to the marked map to Spd Q_p; restrictions along marked morphisms and their composition laws.
- `DiamondCoefficients.qproetStructure`: (Ô_Y,Ô⁺_Y) with sections (R^♯,R^♯⁺) on the quasi-pro-étale affinoid perfectoid basis, and its natural λ_* identification.
- `DiamondCoefficients.almost_vComparison`: The rational exact and integral almost derived λ_* comparisons, including the quotient by a global pseudouniformizer.
- `DiamondCoefficients.adic_completion`: If Y=X^♦ for locally noetherian or perfectoid X over Q_p, then Ô⁺_Y≃lim_n ν⁻¹O⁺_X/p^n and Ô_Y≃Ô⁺_Y[1/p].
- `DiamondCoefficients.constantCondensed`: Λ↦Λ_Y on the quasi-pro-étale and v-sites, compatible with pullback and all limits as well as colimits.
- `DiamondCoefficients.continuous_sections`: For T₁ topological Λ, sections on U of its constant v-sheaf are Cont(|U|,Λ).
- `DiamondCoefficients.localSystem_pTower`: The inverse-limit equivalence for finite-rank Z_p-local systems, compatible with base change, tensor products and internal Hom; require compatibility along Z/p^(n+1)→Z/p^n.
- `DiamondCoefficients.localSystem_v`: Quasi-pro-étale/v equivalence for Z_p and Z/p^n, with the discrete-coefficient étale comparison when Y is locally spatial.

For the construction of the ring sheaves, D6 supplies the chosen untilt functor and its descent; D2's v-descent of functions on perfectoid spaces therefore supplies the sheaf property after untilting. Evaluate λ_* on the quasi-pro-étale basis. Its derived comparison follows by the affinoid perfectoid higher-v-acyclicity theorem, exactly for the rational sheaf and almost for the integral one (MW20 Lemma 2.9). For adic compatibility take a basis of perfectoid pro-étale U→X; if U=lim U_i, the untilted plus ring is the p-completion of colim O⁺(U_i). Quotient sheaves and sections agree here initially only almost. Passing through all p^n and using separatedness of the integral rings gives the exact completed identification of MW20 Lemma 2.7. Thus the exact completed claim does not assume exact quotient sections on every affinoid.

For condensed coefficients, the relative profinite objects and their covers define the morphisms of sites; on a strictly totally disconnected U the inverse image of Λ evaluates as Λ(π₀U). This expression commutes with limits in Λ, and site inverse image commutes with colimits. For topological T₁ coefficients, continuous maps factor through π₀U on that basis. Quotient descent for |V|→|U| along a v-cover extends the formula to all U. For local systems first use the discrete-coefficient étale test on a cover; its finite bases and gluing matrices descend. A compatible p-power tower becomes simultaneously trivial on a quasi-pro-étale weakly contractible cover. Such covers are obtained from a w-strictly local perfectoid cover by an extremally disconnected cover of its profinite component space; the lifting argument in MW20 Lemma 1.2, pp.7–8, shows that each pro-étale cover there splits. On the v-site use a countable tower of trivializing covers and their inverse limit, as in MW20 Proposition 3.5. Their fixed ranks and compatible matrices then give a Z_p-local system. Hom and tensor compatibility follow on those trivializations. Descent of the finite-level objects followed by this inverse-limit construction proves the quasi-pro-étale/v equivalence for Z_p.

**Checks.**

- `DiamondCoefficients.perfectoid_sections`: On U=Spa(C^♭,C^♭⁺) with the marking supplied by Spa(C,C⁺), the two ring sections are C and C⁺, rather than C^♭ and C^♭⁺.
- `DiamondCoefficients.marking_required`: Replacing the marked untilt changes the structure-sheaf construction even though the underlying characteristic-p space and its étale site stay fixed.
- `DiamondCoefficients.integral_almost`: Higher v-cohomology of the integral sheaf is tested in the almost category; exact vanishing is required only after inverting a pseudouniformizer.
- `DiamondCoefficients.profinite_continuity`: For nonempty Y, on Y×Z_p the coefficient section given by the coordinate Z_p→Z_p is continuous and not locally constant. Replacing p-adic Z_p by its discrete topology loses this section.
- `DiamondCoefficients.finite_coefficients`: For Λ=Z/p^n, continuous maps from a profinite component space are locally constant, recovering the usual finite-coefficient constant sheaf.
- `DiamondCoefficients.tower_rank`: The compatible constant rank-r systems (Z/p^n)^r recover Z_p^r; a sequence of objects with no compatible reduction isomorphisms is not an object of the inverse-limit category.

- The log chart P→Γ(Y_qproét,Ô⁺_Y) uses this integral untilt sheaf, and its associated log structure is formed over Ô_Y. Its Z_p-local systems use the continuous constant coefficient sheaf, while every finite level can be computed on the étale site when the log structure is trivial.

<a id="layer-8-log-diamond"></a>

### 8.36 Log diamonds

A log (locally spatial) diamond over Q_p is a (locally spatial) diamond Y with a map Y → Spd Q_p and a log structure M_Y → Ô_Y on the quasi-pro-étale site Y_qproét, where Ô_Y and Ô^+_Y are the completed structure sheaves (for affinoid perfectoid Y′ = Spa(R, R^+) quasi-pro-étale over Y with untilt (R^♯, R^{♯+}), Ô_Y(Y′) = R^♯). A chart is P → Γ(Y_qproét, M_Y) inducing P^a ≅ M_Y and factoring through Ô^+_Y; (Y, M_Y) is quasi-coherent (integral, saturated, fine, fs) if such charts exist quasi-pro-étale locally. Maps are assumed to have compatible charts locally (Convention 7.5). Saturation exists for quasi-coherent log diamonds (via perfectoidisation of R^+ ⊗_{Z[P]} Z[P^sat]) and fibre products exist among saturated quasi-coherent (resp. fs) log diamonds; from now on fibre products are saturated fibre products ×^sat.

Diamonds and their pro-étale presentations are supplied by D4; locally spatial quasi-pro-étale pullbacks and fibre products by D5/quasi-pro-etale-and-fibre-product-permanence; quasi-pro-étale sites by DiamondEtaleCohomology C0.

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.2, Definition 7.3 (p. 72); [KY](#ref-ky), §7.2, Corollary 7.9 (p. 73).)

*Needs:* [§8.35](#layer-8-untilt-coefficients), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D4`, `DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0`, `PerfectoidSpaces §§P4.15.2–P4.15.3`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra`, [§8.33](#layer-8-fs-log-adic-kummer-foundations), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/quasi-pro-etale-and-fibre-product-permanence`.

Prove the following API:

- `LogDiamond`: A diamond Y → Spd Q_p with a log structure M_Y → Ô_Y on Y_qproét.
- `LogDiamond.chart`: Charts P → Γ(Y_qproét, M_Y) factoring through Ô^+_Y, with integral/saturated/fine/fs variants.
- `LogDiamond.IsQuasiCoherent`: Existence of charts quasi-pro-étale locally (with integral, saturated, fine, fs variants).
- `LogDiamond.saturation`: A quasi-coherent log diamond admits a saturation map (Y^sat, M_Y^sat) → (Y, M_Y), terminal among maps from saturated quasi-coherent log diamonds to (Y, M_Y).
- `LogDiamond.satFiberProduct`: Saturated fibre products exist among saturated quasi-coherent (resp. fs) log diamonds.
- `LogDiamond.ofLogAdicSpace`: An fs log adic space (DLLZ, from [§8.33](#layer-8-fs-log-adic-kummer-foundations)), locally noetherian or perfectoid, gives an fs log diamond (X, M_X)^♦.

**Proof route.** Define the completed structural sheaves and log structures on the quasi-pro-étale site. On perfectoid charts saturation is the supplied perfectoidization of the monoid-algebra base change (KY Lemma 7.7). Glue along perfectoid presentations and their pro-étale equivalence relations; saturating ordinary diamond products gives the log fibre products.

**Checks.**

- `LogDiamond.trivial`: Y with M_Y = Ô_Y^× is a saturated quasi-coherent log diamond and its saturation is itself.
- `LogDiamond.disc`: (Spd(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩), T^N)^a is an fs log diamond with chart N → Ô^+, 1 ↦ T.
- `LogDiamond.compat_logAdic`: For an fs log adic space from [§8.33](#layer-8-fs-log-adic-kummer-foundations), the associated log diamond has the log structure induced by ν^{-1} of the étale log structure (KY Example 7.6).
- `LogDiamond.not_naive_product`: For n > 1, take the log n-th-root cover of the disc over an algebraically closed complete C. Its ordinary diamond self-product has branches meeting over T = 0; its saturated log self-product is the disjoint union of n copies of the root disc after choosing μ_n(C). Over Q_p this splitting is asserted only after this geometric base change.

- An fs log adic space (DLLZ) over Spa(Q_p, Z_p), locally noetherian or perfectoid, gives an fs log diamond (X, M_X)^♦ (Example 7.6). A diamond with trivial log structure Ô^× is a saturated quasi-coherent log diamond.

<a id="layer-8-log-diamond-generic-fibre"></a>

### 8.37 The log diamond generic fibre

For a pre-log Huber pair (R, R^+) over (Q_p, Z_p) with a monoid map P → R^+, (Spd(R, R^+), P)^a denotes the associated log diamond (log structure associated with P → Ô^+). For an fs log p-adic formal scheme (X, M_X) over Z_p, its diamond generic fibre X^♦_η → Spd Q_p carries the fs log structure induced by M_X, giving the log diamond (X, M_X)^♦_η, functorial in (X, M_X); for p-complete (R, P) with bounded p^∞-torsion it is (Spd(R[1/p], R^+), P)^a with R^+ the integral closure of R. The underlying pre-adic space Spa(R[1/p], R^+) need not be sheafy; the log diamond always exists.

Fs log p-adic formal schemes; diamonds of Huber pairs via DiamondsAndVStacks D6.

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.2, Example 7.6 (p. 72); [KY](#ref-ky), §1, footnote 5 (p. 3).)

*Needs:* [§8.36](#layer-8-log-diamond), `DiamondsAndVStacks:D6`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra`.

Prove the following API:

- `LogDiamond.genericFibre`: (X, M_X) ↦ (X, M_X)^♦_η for fs log p-adic formal schemes.
- `LogDiamond.ofHuberPair`: (Spd(R, R^+), P)^a for a pre-log Huber pair.
- `LogDiamond.genericFibre_map`: Functoriality in maps of fs log p-adic formal schemes, compatible with composition.
- `LogDiamond.genericFibre_trivial`: For trivial M_X, the underlying diamond is X^♦_η with trivial log structure.
- `LogDiamond.genericFibre_affine`: For X = Spf(R) with fs chart P, (X, M_X)^♦_η ≅ (Spd(R[1/p], R^+), P)^a.

**Proof route.** Apply the supplied Spd construction to the Huber pairs and carry the chart log structure to the quasi-pro-étale site. Maps of charts induce the functorial maps. Glue on affine covers.

**Checks.**

- `LogDiamond.genericFibre_point`: For (Spf Z_p, trivial) the generic fibre is Spd Q_p with trivial log structure.
- `LogDiamond.genericFibre_disc`: For (Spf Z_p⟨T⟩, T^N)^a the generic fibre is (Spd(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩), T^N)^a.
- `LogDiamond.genericFibre_ok_nonsheafy`: For p-complete R with bounded p^∞-torsion whose Spa(R[1/p], R^+) is not sheafy, (Spd(R[1/p], R^+), P)^a still exists as a log diamond.
- `LogDiamond.genericFibre_not_complement`: The log diamond generic fibre of (Spf Z_p⟨T⟩, T^N) is not the punctured disc: its underlying diamond contains T = 0; only its Kummer-étale cohomology sees the puncture.

- Trivial M_X this is the diamond generic fibre X^♦_η. For (Z_p⟨T⟩, T^N) one gets the disc with log structure along T = 0.

<a id="layer-8-stdisc-log-perfectoid"></a>

### 8.38 Strictly totally disconnected log perfectoid spaces

A strictly totally disconnected log perfectoid space is a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space X (qcqs, every étale cover splits) with a saturated quasi-coherent log structure M_X such that M_X/M_X^× is uniquely divisible; then X is affinoid perfectoid and Γ(X, M_X) is saturated and divisible. For such X, H^1(X, Ô_X^×) = 0 for the pro-étale topology, so Γ(X, M_X) → Γ(X, M_X/M_X^×) is surjective for any integral quasi-coherent M_X; it suffices that M_X be divisible, and (X, P)^a is such a space for any divisible saturated P → Γ(X, Ô^+_X).

Strictly totally disconnected perfectoid spaces as in DiamondsAndVStacks D1.

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, Definition 7.12 (p. 74); [KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, Lemma 7.11 (p. 73).)

*Needs:* `DiamondsAndVStacks:D1`, [§8.36](#layer-8-log-diamond).

Prove the following API:

- `LogPerfectoid.IsStrictlyTotallyDisconnected`: The defining condition: X strictly totally disconnected, M_X saturated quasi-coherent, M_X/M_X^× uniquely divisible.
- `LogPerfectoid.h1_units`: H^1_proét(X, Ô_X^×) = 0 for X strictly totally disconnected.
- `LogPerfectoid.sections_surjective`: Γ(X, M_X) → Γ(X, M_X/M_X^×) is surjective.
- `LogPerfectoid.of_divisible`: (X, P)^a for P divisible saturated with P → Γ(X, Ô^+_X).
- `LogPerfectoid.divisible_iff`: It suffices that M_X be divisible (Remark 7.13).

**Proof route.** Pro-étale line bundles descend to étale line bundles and are trivial on strictly totally disconnected perfectoids. Lifts of a characteristic section form a unit torsor, hence trivialize there. A sharp saturated divisible characteristic monoid is uniquely divisible.

**Checks.**

- `LogPerfectoid.trivial`: Any strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space with trivial log structure is a strictly totally disconnected log perfectoid space.
- `LogPerfectoid.rational_monoid`: For C algebraically closed, the chart Q_{≥0} → O_C sending 0 ↦ 1 and every a > 0 to 0 on Spa(C,O_C) gives a strictly totally disconnected log perfectoid space: its characteristic monoid is Q_{≥0}, which is uniquely divisible.
- `LogPerfectoid.not_fs`: On Spa(C,O_C), the chart N → O_C with 0 ↦ 1 and every n > 0 mapping to 0 gives characteristic monoid N, so the log perfectoid space is not strictly totally disconnected as a log space. In contrast, 1 ↦ p gives trivial associated log structure on Ô = C, hence is not this non-example.
- `LogPerfectoid.compat_D1`: The underlying perfectoid space is strictly totally disconnected in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D1.

- (X, Q_{≥0}) for X strictly totally disconnected and P = Q_{≥0} → Ô^+ via T^{Q≥0}. With trivial log structure every strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space qualifies.

<a id="layer-8-quasi-pro-kummer-etale-site"></a>

### 8.39 The quasi-pro-Kummer-étale site

A locally separated map f: (Y′, M_{Y′}) → (Y, M_Y) of saturated quasi-coherent log diamonds is quasi-pro-Kummer-étale (resp. Kummer-étale, finite Kummer-étale) if for every map (X, M_X) → (Y, M_Y) from a strictly totally disconnected log perfectoid space, Y′ ×^sat_Y X is a perfectoid space and (Y′ ×_Y X, M) → (X, M_X) is strict and pro-étale (resp. étale, finite étale); it is surjective if each such pullback is surjective. The quasi-pro-Kummer-étale site (Y, M_Y)_qpkét consists of quasi-pro-Kummer-étale maps to (Y, M_Y) with jointly surjective coverings. Strict maps are quasi-pro-Kummer-étale iff the underlying map is quasi-pro-étale; the classes are stable under pullback and composition and satisfy cancellation in the following direction: if g and g∘f belong to the class, then f belongs to the class (no unrestricted two-out-of-three assertion); maps of log diamonds induce morphisms of sites.

Saturated quasi-coherent log diamonds; locally separated maps (as in Scholze).

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, Definition 7.14 (p. 74); [KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, Definition 7.18 (p. 75); [KY](#ref-ky), §7.1, Definition 7.1 (p. 71); §7.3, Proposition 7.16(1) (p. 74).)

*Needs:* [§8.36](#layer-8-log-diamond), [§8.38](#layer-8-stdisc-log-perfectoid), `DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D4`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D5/quasi-pro-etale-and-fibre-product-permanence`.

Prove the following API:

- `QProKummerEtale.IsQPKet`: The quasi-pro-Kummer-étale condition on a map, with Kummer-étale and finite Kummer-étale variants.
- `QProKummerEtale.site`: The site (Y, M_Y)_qpkét.
- `QProKummerEtale.strict_iff`: A strict map is quasi-pro-Kummer-étale iff its underlying map of diamonds is pro-étale in the quasi sense.
- `QProKummerEtale.comp`: Stability under composition and saturated pullback. Cancellation in KY Proposition 7.16(4): if g and g∘f are quasi-pro-Kummer-étale (respectively Kummer-étale or finite Kummer-étale), then f is too.
- `QProKummerEtale.pullbackSite`: A map of saturated quasi-coherent log diamonds induces a morphism of sites.
- `QProKummerEtale.trivialLog`: For trivial log structures (Y, M_Y)_qpkét ≃ Y_qproét (DiamondEtaleCohomology C0).
- `QProKummerEtale.cohomology`: RΓ_qpkét((Y, M_Y), Λ) for a condensed (discrete or profinite) coefficient ring.

**Proof route.** Define the class by pullback to strictly totally disconnected log perfectoids. The strict criterion retains the quasi-pro-étale prefix, and the usual pullback, composition and cancellation arguments give its stability. Surjective families form the topology and give the stated functorial site.

**Checks.**

- `QProKummerEtale.kummer_root`: (Spd(Q_p⟨T^{1/n}⟩, Z_p⟨T^{1/n}⟩), T^{N/n}) → (Spd(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩), T^N) is surjective finite Kummer-étale; over a strictly totally disconnected log perfectoid space its saturated pullback is n copies indexed by Z/n.
- `QProKummerEtale.trivial`: With trivial log structures quasi-pro-Kummer-étale maps are quasi-pro-étale maps.
- `QProKummerEtale.id`: Identity maps are quasi-pro-Kummer-étale coverings.
- `QProKummerEtale.not_strict_etale`: For n > 1, the Kummer map T ↦ T^n of log discs is Kummer-étale but its underlying map of diamonds is not étale at T = 0.

- Trivial log structures (Y, M_Y)_qpkét is Y_qproét. (Spd(Q_p⟨T^{1/n}⟩), T^{N/n}) → (Spd(Q_p⟨T⟩), T^N) is a surjective finite Kummer-étale map (Lemma 7.21).



<a id="layer-8-kummer-tower-covers"></a>

**Kummer towers and the comparison of sites.**

For the power-tower assertions (1)–(2), let P be an fs monoid with torsion-free group completion (in particular, a sharp fs monoid), P^{1/n} the monoid P with structure map a ↦ a^n, and P_{Q≥0} := colim_n P^{1/n}. (1) For n ≥ 1 and a saturated Q with P ⊂ Q ⊂ P^{1/n}, (Spd(Q_p⟨Q⟩, Z_p⟨Q⟩), Q) → (Spd(Q_p⟨P⟩, Z_p⟨P⟩), P) is surjective finite Kummer-étale. (2) (Spd(Q_p⟨P_{Q≥0}⟩, Z_p⟨P_{Q≥0}⟩), P_{Q≥0}) → (Spd(Q_p⟨P⟩, Z_p⟨P⟩), P) is surjective quasi-pro-Kummer-étale. (3) For any fs chart P and a Huber pair (R, R^+) over (Q_p, Z_p) with P → R^+, the associated log diamond gives a morphism of sites (Spd(R, R^+), P)^a_qpkét → (Spec R, P)^a_két; separately, for any divisible saturated chart P, (Spd(R, R^+), P)^a_qpkét ≅ Spd(R, R^+)_qproét and there is a morphism of sites to (Spec R)_ét. (4) For P fs and P_∞ divisible saturated over P, base change gives (Spec S)_ét → (Spec R, P)_két for the saturated base change (S, P_∞).

For (1)–(2), P is fs and P^gp is torsion free. Without this hypothesis the power construction can fail surjectivity, as the torsion-unit example below shows. For (3)–(4), fs charts and Huber pairs over (Q_p,Z_p); work locally with sharp charts and treat unit charts separately.

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, Proposition 7.22 (p. 75); [KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, Corollary 7.23 (p. 76).)

*Needs:* [§8.39](#layer-8-quasi-pro-kummer-etale-site), [§8.32](#layer-8-kummer-etale-site-log-scheme), [§8.38](#layer-8-stdisc-log-perfectoid).

**Proof route.** For sharp P extend it into the divisible characteristic and compute the saturated self-coproduct Q^gp/P^gp⊕Q. Under the stated torsion-free groupification hypothesis split off the free unit group, whose power-map cover is strict finite étale and surjective; passage to limits gives the infinite tower. Chart-local finite Kummer maps and saturated base change give the scheme comparison, while a divisible target chart makes quasi-pro-Kummer-étale maps strict.

**Checks.**

- P = N: T^{1/n} covers (Lemma 7.21). P trivial: the statements reduce to quasi-pro-étale covers. Excluded generality: for P = Z/2Z and n = 2, Q_p⟨P⟩ = Q_p[t]/(t^2−1) ≅ Q_p × Q_p. The power-map ring endomorphism t ↦ t^2 = 1 misses the t = −1 component on Spd, so it is not a surjective Log diamonds cover; the associated log structures are trivial because P is a group.


<a id="layer-8-kummer-etale-vs-qpket"></a>

**Kummer-étale cohomology of log schemes via log diamonds.**

Let Λ be a torsion abelian group, R a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion, (R[1/p], R^+) the associated Huber pair and P → R a map from an fs monoid. The comparison map is an isomorphism RΓ_két((Spec R[1/p], P)^a, Λ) ≅ RΓ_qpkét((Spd(R[1/p], R^+), P)^a, Λ). Consequently, for a perfect prism (A, (d)), R p-complete over A/I with bounded p^∞-torsion and P → R fs, RΓ_qpkét((Spd(R[1/p], R^+), P)^a, Z/p^n) ≅ (Δ_{(R,P)/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} functorially (and for saturated P after defining the left side as a filtered colimit of fs cases).

Λ torsion; R p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion; P fs (saturated via colimit).

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, Theorem 7.25 (p. 77); [KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, Corollary 7.27 (p. 77); [KY](#ref-ky), §7.3, proof of Theorem 7.25 (p. 77).)

*Needs:* [§8.39](#layer-8-kummer-tower-covers), [§8.34](#layer-8-affine-kummer-etale-comparison), [§8.33](#layer-8-log-scheme-vs-log-adic-kummer), `DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0`.

**Proof route.** Adjoin and saturate roots to obtain the divisible chart cover. Both Kummer sites descend along that cover and its saturated nerve. There they become ordinary étale and quasi-pro-étale sites, so arc descent identifies their cohomology and the affine comparison supplies the stated corollary.

**Checks.**

- P trivial: étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] equals quasi-pro-étale cohomology of its diamond (arc-descent). Remark 7.26: the analogous comparison for DLLZ log adic spaces (via Kummer étale cohomology of log schemes and of log adic spaces).

<a id="layer-8-global-etale-comparison"></a>

### 8.40 The Kummer-étale comparison

Let (A, I = (d), M_0) be a bounded pre-log prism with (A, I) perfect and M_0 an fs monoid; (X_0, M_{X_0}) a smooth fs log p-adic formal scheme over (A/I, M_0) with X_0 qcqs and mod p fibre of (X_0, M_{X_0}) → (Spf A/I, M_0)^a of Cartier type (equivalently, saturated in Tsuji's sense); (A, I, M_A) a saturated pre-log prism whose associated log prism is perfect, with (A, M_0) → (A, Γ(Spf A, M_{Spf A})); and (X, M_X) the base change of (X_0, M_{X_0}) to (A/I, M_A) (also (X_i, M_{X_i}) to fs submonoids M_i ⊂ M_A containing the image of M_0; underlying formal schemes unchanged). Define RΓ_qpkét((X, M_X)^♦_η, Z/p^m) := colim_i RΓ((X_i, M_{X_i})^♦_{η,qpkét}, Z/p^m). Then there are functorial isomorphisms RΓ_qpkét((X, M_X)^♦_η, Z/p^m) ≅ (RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(A, M_A))[1/d]/p^m)^{φ=1} ≅ (RΓ_Δ((X_0, M_{X_0})/(A, M_0))[1/d]/p^m)^{φ=1}. If moreover A/I = O_C (C algebraically closed, A = A_inf) and X is proper, RΓ_qpkét((X, M_X)^♦_η, Z_p) := lim_m RΓ_qpkét(−, Z/p^m) is a perfect Z_p-complex with RΓ_qpkét ⊗^L_{Z_p} W(C♭) ≅ RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(A, M_A)) ⊗^L_{A_inf} W(C♭), and similarly mod p^m. Kummer-étale cohomology is not replaced by étale cohomology of the generic fibre unless the log structure is trivial there.

Exactly the setup of KY §7.4 (perfect log prism, fs M_0, Cartier-type mod p fibre, qcqs X_0); properness and A/I = O_C for the second part.

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.4, Theorem 7.30 (p. 78); [KY](#ref-ky), §7.4, Corollary 7.31 (p. 80); [KY](#ref-ky), §1, Theorem 2(5) (p. 3).)

*Needs:* [§8.39](#layer-8-kummer-etale-vs-qpket), [§8.34](#layer-8-affine-kummer-etale-comparison), [§8.28](#layer-8-derived-vs-site), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-prismatic-base-change), [§8.14](#layer-8-perfect-log-prism), [§8.37](#layer-8-log-diamond-generic-fibre), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-hodge-tate-comparison), Layer 6, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra`.

**Proof route.** Both sides are formal étale sheaves, so compare affine fs charts using the diamond/affine Kummer comparison and the derived/site log-prismatic comparison. Cartier type makes fs base change integral, and quasicompactness places each finite subchart in the filtered system, permitting passage to the indicated colimit. Proper perfectness and the supplied perfect-complex étale comparison give the integral global statement.

**Checks.**

- Trivial log structures and smooth X this is BS22 Theorem 1.8(4) (Layer 6). For a proper semistable formal scheme over O_C with canonical log structure, H^i_qpkét of the generic fibre (Kummer-étale = étale cohomology of the smooth rigid generic fibre since the log structure is trivial there) is computed by the A_inf log prismatic cohomology after ⊗ W(C♭).

<a id="layer-8-kummer-local-systems"></a>

### 8.41 Kummer-étale local systems

Let (X, M_X) be an fs log diamond and pr: (X, M_X)_qpkét → X_qproét → ∗_proét. For a condensed ring Λ (here Z/p^n discrete or Z_p profinite), a sheaf of pr^{-1}Λ-modules F on (X, M_X)_qpkét is constant if F ≅ pr^{-1}Λ^r, and locally constant (a Λ-local system) if it is constant quasi-pro-Kummer-étale locally. Loc_Λ(X, M_X) is the category of Λ-local systems; D^(b)((X, M_X)^♦_η, Z_p) denotes the corresponding category of complexes locally constant with perfect fibres (hypercomplete when X^♦_η is quasicompact).

Condensed coefficient rings Z/p^n and Z_p; following Mann–Werner §3.

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.5, Definition 7.32 (p. 80).)

*Needs:* [§8.35](#layer-8-untilt-coefficients), [§8.39](#layer-8-quasi-pro-kummer-etale-site), `DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0`.

Prove the following API:

- `KummerLocalSystem`: Loc_Λ(X, M_X): locally constant sheaves of pr^{-1}Λ-modules on (X, M_X)_qpkét.
- `KummerLocalSystem.constant`: The constant local system pr^{-1}Λ^r.
- `KummerLocalSystem.pullback`: Pullback along maps of fs log diamonds.
- `KummerLocalSystem.tensor`: Tensor products and duals of local systems.
- `KummerLocalSystem.trivialLog`: For trivial log structure, Loc_{Z_p} agrees with quasi-pro-étale Z_p-local systems (Mann–Werner).

**Proof route.** Pull constant condensed coefficient sheaves along pr. Define local systems by local constancy for the specified topology. Take sheaf maps as morphisms and inherit the coefficient operations.

**Checks.**

- `KummerLocalSystem.constant_rank`: pr^{-1}Z_p^r is a Z_p-local system of rank r.
- `KummerLocalSystem.zero`: The zero sheaf is the local system of rank 0.
- `KummerLocalSystem.kummer_torsor`: Over an algebraically closed complete C and for n > 1, let π be the finite Kummer-étale n-th-root cover of the log disc. The linear local system π_*Z_p has rank n and nontrivial permutation inertia at T = 0, so it does not descend to a local system on the underlying diamond near T = 0. The root torsor itself is a torsor under Z_p(1) in the inverse p-power tower, not a rank-one Z_p-module local system.
- `KummerLocalSystem.trivialLog_eq`: With trivial log structure these are the quasi-pro-étale Z_p-local systems of Mann–Werner.

<a id="layer-8-p-kummer-local-systems"></a>

### 8.42 p-Kummer local systems

Fix a prime p and an fs log diamond (X,M_X). A quasi-pro-Kummer-étale Z_p-local system L is p-Kummer if, for every map (Y,M_Y)→(X,M_X) admitting compatible charts quasi-pro-étale locally, with (Y,M_Y) saturated and characteristic M_Y/M_Y^× p-divisible, its pullback is an ordinary quasi-pro-étale Z_p-local system. Equivalently it becomes constant after every such pullback with Y strictly totally disconnected; equivalently, strict quasi-pro-étale locally on X with fs chart P, pullback to the saturated p-root extension U_∞=U×_{D⟨P⟩^♦}D⟨P[1/p]⟩^♦ is ordinary quasi-pro-étale locally constant. Loc_Zp^{pKum} is the full subcategory of these objects. Apply the same chart criterion to locally perfect complexes to define D_lisse^{(b),pKum}.

X is an fs log diamond; all chart extensions and fibre products are saturated. Z_p is the profinite condensed coefficient ring. The equivalence of the three tests is KYcorr Lemma 1, not a definition of all Kummer local systems.

([KYcorr](#ref-kycorr), Lemma 1 and Definition 2, pp. 1–2; Example 3, p. 2.)

*Needs:* [§8.41](#layer-8-kummer-local-systems), [§8.39](#layer-8-kummer-tower-covers), [§8.38](#layer-8-stdisc-log-perfectoid), Mathlib `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory`.

Prove the following API:

- `PKummerLocalSystem`: The full subcategory Loc_Zp^{pKum} of Kummer local systems satisfying the universal p-divisible-chart pullback condition.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.chart_iff`: p-Kummer iff strict quasi-pro-étale locally the pullback to a saturated P[1/p] chart is an ordinary quasi-pro-étale local system.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.stdisc_iff`: p-Kummer iff pullback along every compatible-chart map from a saturated p-divisible strictly totally disconnected log perfectoid is constant.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.constant`: The constant finite free Z_p-local system is p-Kummer.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.pullback`: Pullback along maps of fs log diamonds preserves p-Kummer objects; use compatible fs charts locally and the p-root criterion.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.tensor`: The p-Kummer subcategory is closed under tensor products and duals, since the chart-local ordinary local systems are.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.trivialLog`: For trivial log structure, all ordinary quasi-pro-étale Z_p-local systems are p-Kummer.

**Proof route.** The corrected p-root lemma identifies the universal pullback, strictly totally disconnected and strict-local chart conditions. Take their full subcategory. Tensor products, duals, pullback and perfect coefficient complexes preserve those local conditions.

**Checks.**

- `PKummerLocalSystem.constant_rank`: Constant Z_p^r is p-Kummer and has rank r, including r=0.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.pPower_root`: On the geometric log disc over an algebraically closed complete C/Q_p, the pushforward of Z_p under the p^a-root cover, a≥1, is a p-Kummer local system of rank p^a: its permutation inertia has p-power order.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.primeToP_root`: For the n-root cover of that log disc, n>1 and coprime to p, π_*Z_p is a Kummer local system of rank n but not p-Kummer; its inertia image is cyclic of order n.
- `PKummerLocalSystem.trivialLog_eq`: For a diamond with trivial log structure, the p-Kummer full subcategory is the whole ordinary quasi-pro-étale Z_p-local-system category.

- The universal, strictly totally disconnected and p-root-chart conditions agree as in KYcorr Lemma 1. The positive p-power root permutation systems qualify; nontrivial prime-to-p root permutation systems fail. Trivial logs recover ordinary quasi-pro-étale Z_p-local systems.



<a id="layer-8-p-kummer-monodromy-criterion"></a>

**p-Kummer local inertia criterion.**

Let (X,M_X) be a locally noetherian fs log adic space over Spa(Q_p,Z_p) and L a Kummer-étale Z_p-local system, meaning a compatible inverse system L_n of finite free Z/p^n-local systems. L is p-Kummer on the log adic space iff every local log inertia representation at every geometric ξ has pro-p image in GL(L_ξ). This condition is equivalent to the p-Kummer chart condition for its associated local system on (X,M_X)^♦. Equivalently, the image in GL(L_ξ/p^n) is a p-group for every n≥1. In particular, on a smooth characteristic-zero adic space with normal-crossings log boundary, unipotent geometric boundary monodromy on L⊗Q_p implies this condition.

Locally noetherian fs log adic space over Q_p; geometric log points and finite free integral coefficient fibres. The unipotent sufficient criterion additionally assumes smooth characteristic-zero space with normal-crossings boundary; it does not claim an equivalence.

([KYcorr](#ref-kycorr), Definition 4, p. 3; Proposition 5 and proof, pp. 3–4; Remark 6, p. 4; [Inoue](#ref-inoue), Definition B.2, p. 66; Lemma B.3 and Proposition B.4 with proof, pp. 66–68.)

*Needs:* [§8.42](#layer-8-p-kummer-local-systems), [§8.33](#layer-8-log-scheme-vs-log-adic-kummer), [§8.33](#layer-8-fs-log-adic-kummer-foundations), Tau Ceti `TauCeti.IsProP`, Mathlib `PadicInt.toZModPow`, Mathlib `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map`, Mathlib `IsPGroup`.

**Proof route.** Compare finite-level adic and diamond local systems by the all-root site comparison, then restrict to the p-root image. A pro-p inertia image in GL_r(Z/p^n) is killed by the p^N-root chart for N=v_p(|GL_r(Z/p^n)|), proving the finite-level criterion without a single finite stage for the whole Z_p-system. Conversely p-root triviality kills prime-to-p inertia and makes each finite image a p-group; their limit is pro-p, and integral unipotent inertia satisfies this condition.

**Checks.**

- The p^a-root permutation representation has p-group inertia image, while the nontrivial prime-to-p n-root permutation representation has image cyclic of order n and fails. At each finite coefficient level the trivial representation has trivial (hence p-group) image. A nontrivial arithmetic unramified action with trivial local boundary inertia is allowed: only local log inertia is tested.

<a id="layer-8-laurent-f-crystal"></a>

### 8.43 Laurent F-crystals on the absolute saturated log prismatic site

Let (X, M_X) be a bounded fs log p-adic formal scheme and (X, M_X)_Δ its absolute saturated log prismatic site. A Laurent F-crystal is a crystal of vector bundles E over (O_Δ[1/I])^∧_p on (X, M_X)_Δ (a compatible family of finite projective A[1/I]^∧_p-modules on objects (A, I, M_A)^a with isomorphisms along maps) together with an isomorphism φ_E: φ^*E ≅ E. Vect((X, M_X)_Δ, O_Δ[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} is the category of Laurent F-crystals; D_perf((X, M_X)_Δ, O_Δ[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} the analogous category of perfect complexes.

Bounded fs log p-adic formal schemes; absolute saturated site with the strict flat topology.

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.5, Definition 7.35 (p. 81).)

*Needs:* [§8.17](#layer-8-absolute-log-prismatic-site), Layer 7, [§8.42](#layer-8-p-kummer-local-systems).

Prove the following API:

- `LaurentFCrystal`: The category Vect((X, M_X)_Δ, O_Δ[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}.
- `LaurentFCrystal.unit`: The unit object O_Δ[1/I]^∧_p with its Frobenius.
- `LaurentFCrystal.tensor`: Tensor products and duals.
- `LaurentFCrystal.pullback`: Pullback along maps of bounded fs log p-adic formal schemes.
- `LaurentFCrystal.descent`: Vect(…)^{φ=1} ≃ lim_{(A,I,M_A)} Vect(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ_A=1} over the absolute saturated site (Drinfeld–Mathew).
- `LaurentFCrystal.etaleRealisation`: The étale realization takes values in Loc_Zp^{pKum}((X,M_X)^♦_η), the full subcategory defined by the p-root-chart condition (KYcorr Theorem 7, p. 4).

**Proof route.** Form the ordinary localized-completed vector-bundle crystals with compatible Frobenius. Apply [§7.3](#layer-7-crystal-descent)’s coefficient descent on the perfect saturated log prism basis. Equip its descent data with Frobenius; the corrected realization target is supplied separately.

**Checks.**

- `LaurentFCrystal.unit_realisation`: The étale realisation of the unit O_Δ[1/I]^∧_p is the constant local system Z_p.
- `LaurentFCrystal.trivialLog`: For trivial log structure the category agrees with Layer 7's Laurent F-crystals (BS F-crystals Definition 3.2).
- `LaurentFCrystal.zero`: The zero crystal is a Laurent F-crystal of rank 0.
- `LaurentFCrystal.not_F_crystal`: Laurent coefficients are obtained by inverting the prism ideal before p-completion. The elementary inversion test at I=(p) over Z_p makes p a unit, whereas p is not a unit in Z_p. This is a test of the inversion step only: its subsequent p-completion is zero. Integral F-crystals and Laurent F-crystals have different coefficient definitions; no claim that every integral F-crystal fails to induce a Laurent object is made.

<a id="layer-8-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems"></a>

### 8.44 Laurent F-crystals and p-Kummer local systems

For a bounded fs log p-adic formal scheme (X,M_X), there are natural equivalences Vect((X,M_X)_Δ,O_Δ[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Loc_Zp^{pKum}((X,M_X)^♦_η) and D_perf((X,M_X)_Δ,O_Δ[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_lisse^{(b),pKum}((X,M_X)^♦_η,Z_p). On the left use the absolute saturated log prismatic site and Laurent coefficients; on the right use the quasi-pro-Kummer-étale site and the p-Kummer restriction. The unit realizes to constant Z_p.

Bounded fs log p-adic formal scheme, with its log diamond generic fibre. The realization target is the p-Kummer full subcategory of local systems or locally perfect complexes, as in KYcorr Lemma 1 and Definition 2.

([KYcorr](#ref-kycorr), Theorem 7 and proof, p. 4; Lemma 1/Definition 2, pp. 1–2; [KY](#ref-ky), §7.5, original Theorems 7.36–7.37 and proofs, pp. 81–82.)

*Needs:* [§8.43](#layer-8-laurent-f-crystal), [§8.41](#layer-8-kummer-local-systems), [§8.13](#layer-8-perfect-log-prisms-perfectoid), [§8.39](#layer-8-kummer-tower-covers), [§8.37](#layer-8-log-diamond-generic-fibre), [§7.9](#layer-7-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems), [§7.3](#layer-7-crystal-descent), [§8.42](#layer-8-p-kummer-local-systems).

**Proof route.** Evaluate on the perfect saturated log prism basis and apply ordinary Laurent descent. Its p-divisible characteristic permits the corrected p-Kummer objects to become ordinary quasi-pro-étale objects by KYcorr Lemma 1, without asserting divisibility at other primes. The ordinary perfectoid equivalences then glue on both sides, with the unit comparison inherited locally.

**Checks.**

- Trivial generic log structure: every ordinary Z_p-local system is p-Kummer, recovering the ordinary Layer 7 equivalences. The permutation local system π_*Z_p for a p^a-root cover of a geometric log disc (a≥1) has rank p^a and is p-Kummer, so it lies in the essential image. For an n-root cover with n>1 and gcd(n,p)=1, the rank-n permutation local system has nontrivial prime-to-p inertia and is not p-Kummer. It is outside the essential image; the unrestricted preprint theorem would incorrectly include it.



<a id="layer-8-smooth-proper-pushforward"></a>

**Smooth proper pushforward of Kummer-étale local systems.**

Let f: (X, M_X) → (Y, M_Y) be a smooth (Koshikawa's sense) proper map of bounded fs log p-adic formal schemes. Then Rf_*O_Δ is an F-crystal of perfect complexes on (Y, M_Y)_Δ and there is a natural isomorphism (Rf_*O_Δ)_ét ≅ Rf_{η*}Z_p for f_η: (X, M_X)^♦_η → (Y, M_Y)^♦_η; in particular Rf_{η*}Z_p is locally constant with perfect fibres and commutes with base change (Z, M_Z) → (Y, M_Y). Via the corrected Laurent realization, the resulting locally perfect complex is p-Kummer.

f smooth and proper; bounded fs.

([KY](#ref-ky), §7.5, Proposition 7.38 and Remark 7.39, pp. 82–84 (published Proposition 7.37); [KYcorr](#ref-kycorr), Introduction p. 1 and Theorem 7 p. 4.)

*Needs:* [§8.44](#layer-8-laurent-f-crystals-local-systems), [§8.40](#layer-8-global-etale-comparison), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-hodge-tate-comparison), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-prismatic-base-change).

**Proof route.** Use the smooth proper statement preserved by KYcorr, with the corrected realization target. Hodge–Tate and base change make Rf_*O_Δ an F-crystal of perfect complexes. On sharp fs charts evaluate on saturated perfect log prisms, apply Kummer comparison fibrewise, and use the corrected Laurent equivalence.

**Checks.**

- F the identity, (O_Δ)_ét = Z_p. Trivial log structures: the relative form of BS F-crystals Corollary 3.8 with smooth proper pushforward (Layer 7).

<a id="layer-8-etale-comparison-over-ainf"></a>

### 8.45 Étale comparison over A_inf[1/φ^{-1}(μ)]

Let C be algebraically closed with A_inf = W(O_C♭), ξ = μ/φ^{-1}(μ), μ = [ε] − 1; (X_0, M_{X_0}) an fs log p-adic formal scheme smooth and proper over (Spf O_C, M_0)^a with mod p fibre of Cartier type, base changed to (X, M_X) over a perfect log prism (A_inf, (ξ), M_A) receiving M_0; M := RΓ_Δ((X_0, M_{X_0})/(A_inf, M_0)) ≅ RΓ_Δ((X, M_X)/(A_inf, M_A)), H^i_Δ := H^i(M), T := RΓ_qpkét((X, M_X)^♦_η, Z_p). Then for every i, H^i_Δ ⊗_{A_inf} A_inf[1/φ^{-1}(μ)] ≅ H^i_qpkét((X, M_X)^♦_η, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/φ^{-1}(μ)].

As in KY §8 setup; C algebraically closed; properness; Cartier type.

([KY](#ref-ky), §8, Proposition 8.3 (p. 86); [KY](#ref-ky), §8.1 (p. 86).)

*Needs:* [§8.40](#layer-8-global-etale-comparison), [§8.30](#layer-8-log-frobenius-isogeny), [§8.30](#layer-8-log-nygaard-filtration), `AInfCohomology:AI.0`.

**Proof route.** At Witt length n use the algebraic Frobenius-module equivalence of [§8.0](#layer-8-algebraic-witt-frobenius): coherence makes the original cohomology finitely presented, Frobenius perfection makes it algebraic, and extension by zero with W_n(m^♭) gives the reverse map whose closed-point cone is almost zero. Pass through compatible p-completion to get the Frobenius-equivariant map to T⊗A_inf. The finite log-differential rank D bounds its pole by φ^−1(d)^−D; iterated Frobenius factors divide φ^−1(μ), giving a uniform power bound and hence the localized equality after the Frobenius colimit and completion.

**Checks.**

- Trivial log structures: the analogous statement of BMS1 Theorem 1.8(iii) via BS22 Theorem 17.2 (Layer 5/AI.5). For X = Spf O_C: both sides are A_inf[1/φ^{-1}(μ)] in degree 0.

<a id="layer-8-log-pd-rigidity"></a>

### 8.46 Log PD deformation and Frobenius rigidity

Fix a perfect field k of characteristic p and a sharp fs monoid P. Construct `LogPDDeformation.base`: in W(k)[P][1/p], take the W(k)-subalgebra D₀ generated by γ_r([m])=[rm]/r! for m∈P∖{0} and r≥1, and then take its p-adic completion D. The augmentation sends every positive monomial to zero and splits D→W(k); write J for its kernel. Use the compatible divided powers on (p,J), and the log chart P→D, m↦[m]. Frobenius is Witt Frobenius on W(k) and [m]↦[pm]. This is the p-torsion-free log PD deformation of the hollow chart; it is not a map from the hollow Witt chart to a nonzero parameter. If the original fs chart has units, localise at the face mapping to units and split off its unit group before taking its sharp monoid P. The associated log structure is unchanged, with the unit factors recorded in the chart isomorphism.

A positive integral height on P exists because P is sharp, saturated and finitely generated. It bounds the possible divided-power denominators in any fixed monoid degree. Thus each homogeneous part of D₀ is a finite free rank-one W(k)-submodule of W(k)[P][1/p]; D and J are p-torsion-free, and the augmentation remains split after completion. The usual sum and product formulas give the divided powers, and their p-adic continuity extends them to the completion. This constructs the p-torsion-free quotient of the compatible PD envelope of the positive monomial ideal, with its universal property for p-torsion-free p-complete PD targets. It does not assert that an arbitrary universal PD envelope is p-torsion-free. The ordinary PD-envelope and log exactification constructions are supplied by CrystallineCohomology Layers CR.0 and CR.5; the augmented monoid base and its Frobenius estimates are the targets here.

The API is:

- `LogPDDeformation.base.augmentation`: The continuous PD augmentation D→W(k) has kernel J and its specified W(k)-section.
- `LogPDDeformation.base.evaluate`: For a p-torsion-free p-complete PD algebra B over W(k), a chart P→B sending positive elements into its PD ideal induces a unique continuous PD map D→B. This is a map of log bases with the specified chart map.
- `LogPDDeformation.base.frobenius`: Frobenius commutes with the augmentation and with evaluations at rank-one charts, where φ(α(m))=α(m)^p.
- `LogPDDeformation.base.contraction`: For n≥0, φ^n(J)⊂p^e(n)J, with e(n)=(p^n−1)/(p−1). On a generator γ_r([m]), the coefficient is (rp^n)!/r!, whose p-adic valuation is r e(n). Products, sums and p-adic limits preserve the bound.

Prove `LogPDDeformation.rigidity` in the derived p-complete category. Let C be a derived p-complete D-complex with an integral semilinear Frobenius whose linearisation admits an inverse up to one fixed power p^c. Put C₀=C⊗̂ᴸ_D W(k), and assume C₀ is perfect over W(k). Then C[1/p]→C₀[1/p] admits a unique W(k)[1/p]-linear Frobenius-equivariant section, and its D[1/p]-linear extension is an isomorphism

```text
D[1/p]⊗ᴸ_{W(k)[1/p]} C₀[1/p] ≃ C[1/p].
```

Here uniqueness is for this fixed augmented Frobenius base. It is not a claim that changing a logarithmic chart or a period parameter leaves every comparison map unchanged. The section is compatible with morphisms of augmented PD bases preserving the Frobenius and the charts, and with further Frobenius iterates.

For existence, let K=J⊗̂ᴸ_D C, the fibre of C→C₀. The nth Frobenius on K is divisible by p^e(n). On the W(k)-mapping complex from C₀ to K, compose target Frobenius with inverse source Frobenius after inverting p. Its nth iterate has denominator bound p^(cn−e(n)). As e(n)−cn→∞, the geometric series for one minus this operator converges in a fixed p-power multiple of the p-complete mapping complex. Consequently all Frobenius-equivariant maps from C₀[1/p] to K[1/p], including their higher homotopies, vanish. Applying this to the fibre sequence gives the unique section. This is the contraction argument of Colmez–Nizioł, Lemma 2.4 and Theorem 2.6, pp.11–13, here for the explicitly constructed PD augmentation. In this base φ^n(J) already has the uniform factorial bound, so no unproved regularity of the chart monoid is used.

For effectivity of its linearisation, clear one fixed denominator p^a from the section and its Frobenius-equivariance homotopy, and let E be the integral mapping cone. This is possible because the source D⊗ᴸ_W(k) C₀ is perfect; its mapping complexes commute with inverting p. Enlarge a so that reduction of the integral map is homotopic to p^a·id on C₀. Its reduction E⊗̂ᴸ_D W(k) is then the cone of p^a on C₀ and is killed by p^a. Thus p^a·id_E factors through J⊗̂ᴸ_D E. The chosen integral equivariance gives E a Frobenius, still an isogeny with a fixed denominator bound by the triangle of the two end complexes. Applying its nth iterate to this factorisation and transporting back to E gives

```text
p^(a+c' n)·id_E = p^e(n)·u_n
```

for some endomorphism u_n and a fixed c'. Choose n with e(n)>a+c'n. The endomorphism 1−p^(e(n)−a−c'n)u_n is invertible by derived p-completeness, so a fixed power of p kills E. Hence E[1/p]=0. This proves the scalar-extension assertion; the factorial estimate alone would not suffice without this argument. Naturality follows from the uniqueness of the section.

Construct `LogPDDeformation.properCartierComplex` for a proper fine log smooth integral Cartier-type Y over the hollow log point (k,P)^a: take C_D(Y)=RΓ_logcrys(Y/(D,P)^a) using the completed log PD embeddings of [§8.4](#layer-8-completed-log-pd). It reduces by derived PD base change to C_W(Y)=RΓ_logcrys(Y/(W(k),P→0)^a), and base changes to every p-torsion-free p-complete PD evaluation of D. The latter assertion uses completed derived tensor; it is not an ordinary tensor assertion in the presence of torsion. Log smooth integral local lifts give p-completely flat PD de Rham models. The log Cartier argument supplies a uniform p^r inverse to linearised Frobenius, where r bounds the rank of Ω¹_{Y/(k,P)}. Reduction of C_W(Y) modulo p is the bounded log de Rham complex of Y. Proper coherent cohomology makes its cohomology finite over k, so derived completeness lifts it to a perfect W(k)-complex. This establishes the hypotheses of rigidity for arbitrary sharp fs P, rather than importing a result only about the standard rank-one log point.

The comparison inputs are Kato, *Logarithmic structures of Fontaine–Illusie*, Theorems 6.4 and 6.10, pp.219,222; Hyodo–Kato, *Semi-stable reduction and crystalline cohomology with logarithmic poles*, §§2.22–2.24, pp.239–242. Kato's derived base change applies to log smooth integral morphisms and flat crystals; properness is used here for the special-fibre finiteness. The p^r inverse in Hyodo–Kato Proposition 2.24 is uniform on the finite-level system and therefore remains an inverse up to p^r after derived inverse limit and global sections. Colmez–Nizioł's cited one-parameter theorem motivates the rigidity argument; the fs-monoid base, its universal property and the effectivity proof above are additional constructions in this subsection.

The API is:

- `LogPDDeformation.properCartierComplex.witt_fibre`: C_D(Y)⊗̂ᴸ_D W(k)≃C_W(Y), with all base charts retained.
- `LogPDDeformation.properCartierComplex.pd_base_change`: Evaluation at a positive chart in the PD ideal gives the log crystalline complex of the corresponding base change of Y.
- `LogPDDeformation.properCartierComplex.frobenius_isogeny`: A finite bound on the log differential rank supplies the uniform p-power inverse; integral Frobenius need not be invertible.
- `LogPDDeformation.properCartierComplex.finiteness`: C_W(Y) is perfect over W(k); its rational cohomology is finite dimensional.
- `LogPDDeformation.properCartierComplex.scalar_comparison`: Rigidity supplies the rational comparison with the Witt fibre, natural for the specified augmented chart and for Frobenius iterates.

**Checks.**

- `LogPDDeformation.empty_chart`: For P=0, D=W(k), J=0, and rigidity is the identity. This is the trivial-log case.
- `LogPDDeformation.one_parameter`: For P=N and p=2, φ(t)=t²=2γ₂(t), while φ²(t)=t⁴=24γ₄(t), with valuations 1 and 3. The contraction exponent is (2^n−1), not n.
- `LogPDDeformation.two_parameters`: For P=N², the two positive chart generators deform independently. Evaluation sends them to two specified PD elements; no common uniformizer or rational dependence of their valuations is assumed.
- `LogPDDeformation.nonfree_chart`: For P generated by (1,0),(1,1),(1,2) in Z², the relation [1,1]²=[1,0][1,2] remains in D and in every evaluation. The construction does not replace an fs monoid by a free monoid without imposing its relations.
- `LogPDDeformation.zero_complex`: C=0 gives the unique zero section and zero scalar extension. For C=D, the section is the W(k)-structure map and its linearisation is the identity.
- `LogPDDeformation.frobenius_bound`: On a two-term bounded free model the cone argument uses one common exponent c' in both degrees. A collection of unrelated degreewise isogenies without a bound is insufficient for the geometric series.
- `LogPDDeformation.nonzero_parameter`: Evaluation t↦[π^♭]^(p^n) is allowed once π^(p^n)∈pO_C, since the parameter then lies in ker(A_crys→O_C/p). Its image under θ can still be nonzero. No map from the zero chart over W(k) is being inserted.

*Needs:* [§8.4](#layer-8-completed-log-pd), [§8.30](#layer-8-log-frobenius-isogeny), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.0`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`, `DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1`, `EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2`, SchemeAndStackFoundations, Layer SF.2 (proper coherent cohomology and perfect complexes).

<a id="layer-8-log-hyodo-kato-isomorphism"></a>

### 8.47 Hyodo–Kato isomorphism for log prismatic cohomology over A_crys

Keep the precise §8 setup of KY: C is an algebraically closed complete extension of Q_p; M₀ is an fs monoid mapping to the global log structure of a saturated perfect log prism over (A_inf,(ξ)); and X₀ is an fs log p-adic formal scheme, smooth and proper over (O_C,M₀)^a, with mod-p fibre of Cartier type. Let (A_crys,(p),M_crys)^a be the associated log prism, with chart induced from M₀→A_inf→A_crys. Write X₁ for the base change of X₀ to (O_C/p,M_crys)^a. Prove `LogHyodoKato.prismatic_crystalline`:

```text
φ*RΓ_Δ(X₀/(A_inf,M₀)) ⊗ᴸ_{A_inf} A_crys
  ≃ RΓ_logcrys(X₁/(A_crys,M_crys)),
```

Frobenius-equivariantly, with linearised Frobenius an isomorphism after inverting p. Let k be the residue field of C, N the associated hollow log structure of (k,M₀), and Y the special log fibre. For a fixed section k→O_C/p, prove `LogHyodoKato.scalar_comparison`: there is a Frobenius-compatible isomorphism

```text
RΓ_logcrys(Y/(W(k),N)) ⊗ᴸ_{W(k)} A_crys[1/p]
  ≃ RΓ_logcrys(X₁/(A_crys,M_crys))[1/p].
```

Consequently every H^i(RΓ_Δ(X₀/(A_inf,M₀))⊗ᴸ_{A_inf,φ}A_crys[1/p]) is finite free over A_crys[1/p]. The hollow Witt log structure sends every positive characteristic element to zero and lifts units by Teichmüller representatives. The scalar comparison is an existence assertion with the choices below; no unspecified chart-independent period map is asserted.

([KY](#ref-ky), §8 setup, p.85, Propositions 8.8–8.9, pp.89–90; the log PD rigidity used to justify the nonzero-parameter case is [§8.46](#layer-8-log-pd-rigidity), with Kato Theorem 6.10, p.222, Hyodo–Kato Proposition 2.24, pp.240–242, and [Colmez–Nizioł](#ref-cn21), Lemma 2.4 and Theorem 2.6, pp.11–13.)

*Needs:* [§8.20](#layer-8-log-crystalline-comparison), [§8.19](#layer-8-log-prismatic-base-change), [§8.30](#layer-8-log-frobenius-isogeny), [§8.46](#layer-8-log-pd-rigidity), [§8.14](#layer-8-perfect-log-prism), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`, `AInfCohomology:AI.0`.

For the first assertion, ker(A_crys→O_C/p) has compatible divided powers. Apply the log crystalline comparison and completed base change. Proper log Hodge–Tate perfectness makes the A_inf complex perfect, so the displayed tensor needs no additional completion. The Cartier-type Frobenius isogeny applies after this base change.

For the scalar comparison, first choose a rank-one chart of the perfect log prism, using KY Proposition 2.39, p.21, where rank one means δ_log=0, not that the characteristic monoid has rank one. After localising M₀ at its unit face, its sharp fs characteristic P has free groupification. Lift a basis of P^gp to the rank-one chart's groupification; the lift of each positive element lies in that chart after multiplication by a chart unit. This gives a rank-one P-chart representing the same associated log structure as the original chart, with the intervening unit factors included in the isomorphism of bases. Transport X₀ through that isomorphism. Thus α(m)∈A_inf satisfies φ(α(m))=α(m)^p, and θ(α(m)) lies in the maximal ideal of O_C for m≠0. Unit factors on the special fibre are transported by their Teichmüller lifts. This reduction retains nonfree fs P and does not turn it into N.

Finite presentation, quasicompactness and the finitely many fine charts allow one common Frobenius iterate to kill all the nilpotent coefficients by which X₁ and its charts differ from the base change of Y. More explicitly, descend the finite defining and gluing data over O_C/p to the subalgebra generated over the fixed copy of k by their finitely many coefficients; their residues give the data of Y. The differences lie in the nilradical, and one p-power kills this finite collection and the finite relations witnessing the descent. Increase the iterate so that α(m)^(p^n) maps to zero in O_C/p for every generator m of P. Cartier-type saturation ensures that the fine log base changes used here retain the indicated underlying schemes. Pulling crystalline cohomology through this iterate and using its uniform Frobenius isogeny identifies the rational complex for X₁ with the rational crystalline complex of the resulting base change of Y. This is the finite-presentation step of KY Proposition 8.9; it is not yet a direct map of Witt and A_crys log bases.

Take the common augmented PD base D=D(P) of [§8.46](#layer-8-log-pd-rigidity). The fixed section k→O_C/p has a compatible perfect lift to O_C^♭, hence gives the Frobenius-compatible W(k)→A_inf→A_crys. For n as above, the chart

```text
P → A_crys,             m ↦ α(m)^(p^n)
```

lands, on positive elements, in the PD ideal ker(A_crys→O_C/p). It therefore defines the continuous PD evaluation D→A_crys. This is a genuine chart-compatible map: D has a variable monoid parameter, rather than the zero parameter of W(k). Apply `properCartierComplex.pd_base_change` to C_D(Y). Rigidity identifies it rationally with D⊗ᴸ_{W(k)}C_W(Y), and evaluation gives the desired comparison over A_crys. The rational Frobenius of C_W(Y) removes the Frobenius twist introduced by the chosen iterate. Increasing n commutes with evaluation by φ and gives the same comparison through these Frobenius identifications, by the uniqueness part of rigidity. A different common augmented PD presentation with the same chosen chart is compared by its PD universal maps, again using uniqueness. Changes of logarithmic chart carry their recorded unit factors; this argument does not silently identify period maps for unrelated choices.

Finally C_W(Y) is perfect over W(k) by [§8.46](#layer-8-log-pd-rigidity). After inverting p its cohomology is finite dimensional over W(k)[1/p]. Tensoring those vector spaces with A_crys[1/p] gives finite free modules, which proves the finiteness assertion. No semistable-DVR hypothesis or rank-one characteristic monoid is needed in this last step.

**Checks.**

- `LogHyodoKato.trivial_chart`: For P=0 the common base is W(k), and the argument recovers the trivial-log comparison of BMS1 Proposition 13.21, p.116.
- `LogHyodoKato.nonzero_parameter`: For 1↦[π^♭], there is no direct map (W(k),N→0)→(A_crys,N→[π^♭]^(p^n)) with the indicated chart map: θ sends the target parameter to π^(p^n)≠0. The evaluation from D is nevertheless defined once π^(p^n)∈pO_C, because its positive parameter is in the PD ideal modulo p.
- `LogHyodoKato.pd_contraction`: For t in the PD augmentation, φ^n(t)=(p^n)!γ_(p^n)(t), with valuation (p^n−1)/(p−1). At p=2 the first two valuations are 1 and 3. This exceeds every fixed linear Frobenius-isogeny denominator and supplies the convergence and effectivity estimates in [§8.46](#layer-8-log-pd-rigidity).
- `LogHyodoKato.point`: For X₀=Spf O_C with the base log structure pulled back unchanged, both relative complexes consist of their base ring in degree zero. The scalar comparison sends 1 to 1, and there are no relative logarithmic forms.
- `LogHyodoKato.nonfree_characteristic`: The relation 2(1,1)=(1,0)+(1,2) in the saturated cone of [§8.46](#layer-8-log-pd-rigidity) is respected by the PD evaluation. A proof using independent coordinates without that relation would not give this comparison.

<a id="layer-8-log-prismatic-bkf-module"></a>

### 8.48 Log prismatic cohomology groups are Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules

In the setting of the étale comparison over A_inf (X proper over O_C, mod p fibre of Cartier type, perfect log prism base over A_inf), for every i the Frobenius-twisted cohomology φ^*H^i_Δ = H^i_Δ ⊗_{A_inf,φ} A_inf with its Frobenius is a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module: a finitely presented A_inf-module N, free after inverting p, with a φ-linear φ_N inducing N[1/ξ] ≅ N[1/φ(ξ)]. Moreover H^i_Δ ⊗ A_inf[1/φ^{-1}(μ)] ≅ H^i_qpkét((X, M_X)^♦_η, Z_p) ⊗ A_inf[1/φ^{-1}(μ)].

As in KY §8: X proper; Cartier type; C algebraically closed.

([KY](#ref-ky), §8, Theorem 8.2 (p. 85); [KY](#ref-ky), §8, Definition 8.1 (p. 85).)

*Needs:* [Étale comparison over A_inf[1/φ^{-1}(μ)]](#layer-8-etale-comparison-over-ainf), [§8.47](#layer-8-log-hyodo-kato-isomorphism), [§8.14](#layer-8-perfect-log-prism), `AInfCohomology:AI.2/bkf-module`, `AInfCohomology:AI.5/cohomology-finiteness-from-periods`, `AInfCohomology:AI.5/p-local-freeness-from-periods`.

**Proof route.** Apply AI.2’s BMS1 Corollary 4.20 criterion to the proper perfect complex. Its étale input is the localized comparison of [§8.45](#layer-8-etale-comparison-over-ainf). Its crystalline finite-freeness input is [§8.47](#layer-8-log-hyodo-kato-isomorphism), using the original log PD deformation argument of [§8.46](#layer-8-log-pd-rigidity).

**Checks.**

- Trivial log structures: BMS1 Theorem 14.5 / BS22 Theorem 1.8 with the A_inf comparison (AI.5). X = Spf O_C: φ^*H^0 = A_inf, the unit BKF module.

<a id="layer-8-semistable-chart-application"></a>

### 8.49 Log prismatic cohomology of the standard semistable chart

Let O_K be totally ramified over W(k) with uniformiser π and R = O_K⟨x_1, …, x_d⟩/(x_1⋯x_r − π) (1 ≤ r ≤ d) with the canonical log structure given by the chart P = N^r → R, e_j ↦ x_j (j ≤ r), over (O_K, N → O_K, 1 ↦ π) via the diagonal 1 ↦ e_1 + ⋯ + e_r (the standard semistable chart of CR.5, with its actual monoid map recording π). Then: (1) (Spf R, P)^a is smooth of Cartier type over (O_K, N) in Koshikawa's sense, hence over the Breuil–Kisin prelog prism (W(k)[[u]], (E), N → u) via O_K = W(k)[[u]]/(E); (2) H^i(Δ̄_{(R,P)/(W(k)[[u]],N)}){i} ≅ Ω^i_{(R,P)/(O_K,N)}, a free R-module of rank (d − 1 choose i) with basis the wedge products of dlog x_2, …, dlog x_r, dx_{r+1}, …, dx_d (dlog x_1 = −Σ_{j=2}^r dlog x_j); (3) the crystalline comparison over (W(k), (p), N → 0), after u ↦ 0, computes the Hyodo–Kato log crystalline cohomology of the special fibre (Spec k[x_1, …, x_d]/(x_1⋯x_r), N^r)^a; (4) the de Rham comparison gives Ω^•_{(R,P)/(O_K,N)}; (5) base change along u ↦ [π♭] gives the A_inf log prismatic cohomology of R_{O_C}, whose Frobenius twist is ČK's AΩ (Comparison with semistable AΩ, on the overlap with AI.6); (6) the Kummer-étale comparison over a perfect log prism computes the Kummer-étale cohomology of the generic fibre, which is étale cohomology because x_1, …, x_r are units on R[1/p], so the log structure is trivial there.

1 ≤ r ≤ d; k perfect; the free coordinates x_{r+1}, …, x_d carry no log structure.

([K1](#ref-k1), Appendix A.1, Example (2) (p. 50); [K1](#ref-k1), §8, Theorem 8.1 (p. 45).)

*Needs:* [§8.19](#layer-8-log-hodge-tate-comparison), [§8.20](#layer-8-log-crystalline-comparison), [§8.30](#layer-8-log-de-rham-comparison), [§8.31](#layer-8-breuil-kisin-log-cohomology), [§8.24](#layer-8-semistable-aomega-comparison), [§8.40](#layer-8-global-etale-comparison), `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5`, `CrystallineCohomology:CR.6`, `AInfCohomology:AI.6`.

**Proof route.** The monoid quotient is free and the product-coordinate algebra is flat over the base, giving the integral smooth chart and its Cartier type by reduced special fibre. Log Hodge–Tate with CR.5’s explicit differentials gives the graded formula, while crystalline and Hyodo–Kato specialization give the special-fibre statement. Apply the log de-Rham, A_inf base-change/semistable AΩ, and Kummer comparisons to obtain the remaining realizations.

**Checks.**

- D = r = 1: R = O_K and all cohomology is concentrated in degree 0. d = r = 2: the semistable target O_K⟨x, y⟩/(xy − π); H^1(Δ̄){1} is free of rank 1 on dlog y = −dlog x.

### Examples

For the semistable node xy=π, the relative log differential module has rank one, generated by dlog x with dlog y=−dlog x. The diagonal chart, rather than two independent base generators, forces that relation. With the trivial monoid the logarithmic targets recover the ordinary ones; the identity section has δ_log=0 and factor 1. A chart element mapping to zero does not permit cancellation of α(m)^p, and its logarithmic delta is not forced to vanish by the compatibility axiom alone. At p=3 a boundary inertia character of order two acts by −1 on Z₃; p-power root covers do not remove it, so it is Kummer but not p-Kummer. At p=2 an order-three integral matrix action on Z₂² gives the same negative control. These examples distinguish the corrected Laurent essential image from all Kummer local systems.

## Downstream consumers

PadicHodgeTheory uses the integral comparison maps, twists, Frobenius and crystalline lattice description. CohomologyComparisons uses the relative and logarithmic period diagrams. The explicit Kisin dictionary of Layer 7 builds on FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory's Kisin modules and introduces no second theory of effective Kisin modules. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups can use the fs log adic foundations of Layer 8. Framed q-de Rham users can use Layer 5’s complete delta-base prefix, which is independent of q-de Rham–Witt theory. Trace-theoretic users may compare with the graded prismatic square of Layer 7; the square itself is stated with syntomic and derived de Rham carriers.
